│       ├── setup.ts
│       ├── drainScheduler.ts   # Lets React finish its queued work BEFORE Vitest deletes `window`. React's scheduler yields through Node's `setImmediate` (MEASURED: under jsdom it is Node's, exposed on the window too), which the jsdom teardown cannot cancel — so a concurrent render that yielded at least once can have a slice in flight when the environment dies between files, and it lands as an UNHANDLED `ReferenceError: window is not defined` **while every test reports as passed**. Exit 1 on a green suite. Wired as `afterAll(() => drainSchedulerQueue())` in `setup.ts` — `afterAll` because RTL unmounts on `afterEach` and unmounting itself schedules work, and the ARROW because Vitest passes hook callbacks a suite context that would otherwise land in `maxTurns`. Bounded on purpose (a runaway chain shortens the drain instead of hanging the suite); ~0.2 ms per file, and the full suite measured 148 s against 149 s before. **Do NOT add a second, local flush in a test file** — one was tried in `forgedImageUrl.test.ts` and it was the wrong scope AND carried a false reason (« RTL's auto-cleanup runs after this file » — it runs after each TEST); the mechanism is React's, so it belongs to every render. **THE DRAIN IS A MITIGATION AND THE RACE STAYED OPEN; WHAT CLOSES IT IS A GUARD IN THE WRAPPER.** This entry used to end « RESIDUAL, INTERMITTENT, disclosed: the drain does not always win … on a green suite that exits 1 with this signature, re-run before chasing it » — accurate, and exactly the shape of note that stops the next reader looking. A drain can only remove PRECONDITIONS: it is BOUNDED by design (a runaway chain must shorten it, never hang the suite), and work scheduled on a delay longer than the one tick `settleReactWork` spends is queued strictly after it. So a fully green suite went on exiting 1 at roughly one run in five. **The fix came from a detail of the reported stack nobody had used: the wrapper's own callback sits ONE FRAME above the crash** (`Immediate.<anonymous>` at `drainScheduler.ts`), so the leaked slice runs through code this module owns and can be stopped when it fires instead of raced to the exit. Each wrapped immediate records whether a `window` existed when it was queued and compares that when it runs; if the environment died in between, the callback is dropped and counted (`suppressedAfterTeardown`). **NOTHING OBSERVABLE IS LOST and it is NOT error suppression** — a callback firing after `window` is deleted belongs to a file that has ended, so no assertion can depend on it and running it yields a `ReferenceError` and an exit code, never a result; a genuine defect runs inside a live file, with a window, untouched. The condition is deliberately « the environment DIED », not « there is no window », so a runtime that never had one is unaffected. **The drain STAYS**: it is what lets legitimately-queued work FINISH for the file that owns it, and the guard only catches what it could not reach. **The probe is the evidence, and it is the strongest kind available here**: deleting the guard turns a one-in-five race into a deterministic failure with the identical three-frame stack — `ReferenceError` → `performWorkOnRootViaSchedulerTask` → `performWorkUntilDeadline` → this wrapper — reproduced by a case that renders a real concurrent root outside `act()` and then deletes the global under it. **DISCLOSED, and stated so nobody assumes otherwise:** React work rescheduled through `setTimeout` rather than `setImmediate` would crash the same way one frame lower, outside this wrapper. Wrapping timers too was REJECTED — every fake-timer test in the suite replaces them, so the probe would be installed over and torn out at random — and the observed signature has always taken the immediate path, which is the one React's scheduler picks when `setImmediate` exists. **ITS OWN PROBE CASE WAS FLAKY, AND THE FAILURE MESSAGE ACCUSED THE WRONG THING.** The case renders a real concurrent root, deletes `window`, and asserted after a FIXED 2 ms wait; observed once during a full suite run beside a build on a 4 vCPU box, it failed with « the React slice was let through: expected 2 to be 3 » — which reads as the guard failing and is the opposite: the count did not MOVE, i.e. the event loop had not reached the queued immediate before `finally` put the window back, so the slice ran into a live environment and there was nothing to suppress. **The diagnosis is MEASURED, not inferred** — shrinking the window to zero reproduces the identical message and the identical numbers, and 6 busy-loop CPU hogs do NOT reproduce it (a synthetic load starves arithmetic, not the event loop), so the honest statement is that the flake was seen once, under contention I created, and that the mechanism behind it is demonstrable on demand. The wait is now BOUNDED ON THE CONDITION rather than on a delay — the same rule this file states for `settle(page)`, *a fix is a CONDITION and not a longer sleep* — with the assertion untouched, so it is no weaker as a probe: with the guard deleted the case still fails AND the `ReferenceError` still surfaces (verified). **The general lesson is about the MESSAGE: an assertion that reads a counter cannot tell « the thing under test failed » from « the thing under test never ran », and it will confidently report the first.**

Its in-page toggle DERIVES the code list from the `[id^="sec-"]` blocks actually present (`codes()` in the inline script), so authoring the section is all a new language needs here.

Réparer l'application → » link: unregister every SW, delete every cache, reload. **It REFUSES when the app cannot be re-fetched, and that guard is the entry.** It purged unconditionally — and it is reached when a load has ALREADY failed, whose commonest cause is the network rather than a corrupt cache, so on a bad connection it destroyed the offline copy that was the user's only remaining way in and reloaded into nothing. Reported from the installed iOS PWA (« même si je clique sur réparer »), during a mid-deploy CDN window. **`doUpdate` was given the same guard for the same reason** (*offline, an unvisited lazy chunk fails as a module-load error, so tapping Stats on a plane destroyed the installed app*); this page never got it — the sibling-page miss, again. **`cache: 'no-store'` is what makes the probe trustworthy**: `sw.js`'s third fetch guard returns early for such a request, so it genuinely reaches the network instead of being answered by the very cache it is deciding whether to destroy. `navigator.onLine` is only a cheap short-circuit — it reports that an interface exists, not that the internet works — so the probe ALSO reads the body for `id="root"`, because a captive portal answers 200 with its own page and `res.ok` alone would wave it through. **The strictness is settled by the asymmetry**: a probe that wrongly FAILS costs one tap on « Réessayer » and deletes nothing, while one that wrongly PASSES strands the user — so it errs toward refusing, and offers a retry plus a way back rather than a dead end. Locked by `resetPageGuard.test.ts`, which EXECUTES the page's own inline script against a stubbed world (a source assertion would pass on a guard that exists and is never reached) and probes in both directions, including that the guard is not a blanket refusal. Same file also carries the two defects this page keeps producing because it sits outside doc:check's source tree: a per-language row per `LANGUAGES` code (the `pt` row was once missing on the ONE page you reach when nothing works) — read from the EVALUATED table, since a first version counted quote characters and got 5.5, the fr/it rows using double quotes precisely BECAUSE they contain apostrophes — and a `lang` attribute VALIDATED against that table (it was written verbatim, so a corrupt `cave-lang` produced `lang="constructor"`; main.jsx was fixed for this and its sibling was missed).

## Technology Stack

| Layer | Technology |
|-------|-----------|
| Build tool | Vite 8 (Rolldown bundler) |
| UI Framework | React 19 (npm, not CDN) |
| Language | TypeScript 6 (strict mode) |
| Linting | ESLint 10 + typescript-eslint + eslint-plugin-react-hooks |
| Tests | Vitest + @testing-library/react + jest-axe + fast-check (~5424 tests across 277 source test files; property-based suites multiply the effective assertion count via fast-check runs) |
| State | React Hooks (`useState`, `useEffect`, `useCallback`, `useMemo`) |
| Context | `AppCtx` / `useAppCtx()` — views receive all state via context |
| Persistence | `localStorage` (primary), IndexedDB (image cache), `sessionStorage` (OAuth token, non-iOS) |
| Offline | Service Worker (`public/sw.js`, current cache name `cave-tabac-v1-0-1`) |
| Auth | Google Sign-In (OAuth 2.0) |
| Cloud backup | Google Drive API v3 |
| AI | Anthropic / OpenAI / Google Gemini (multi-provider) |
| Image proxy | *(removed)* — the app is local-photos-only; no external image fetching, no corsproxy/allorigins |
| ZIP export | JSZip 3.10.1 (loaded dynamically on demand) |

                    #   starts quoting a new control.** Probed in five directions. **THE REGISTRY'S MASKING GAP IS CLOSED, and the measurement that shaped the fix is worth keeping.** The per-key rule asks « does this block contain the app's label ANYWHERE », so a document that quotes a control correctly in one place and WRONGLY in another passes. Not hypothetical: a full sweep of the guide found **THIRTEEN** drifts and the gate was green on every one, because each block also carried a correct mention elsewhere. Each was in exactly ONE language — the signature of translation drift, not a stale guide: en « Delete all data » against « Erase all data », es « Agente de IA » against « Agente IA », fr « Seuil de stock bas » ×2 and a truncated « Chiffrer les sauvegardes », de « Schwellenwert für niedrigen Bestand » and a truncated « Sicherungen verschlüsseln », it « Soglia di scorta bassa », « Svuota il cestino », « Liste raggruppate di default », « Peso di sessione predefinito », pt « Esvaziar reciclagem », « Peso predefinido da sessão », « Formato da data ». **The SCOPE is what makes the new rule usable and it is MEASURED, not guessed**: it scans only the settings-reference rows (`<li><strong>NAME</strong> —`, a NAME slot by convention) and only against the registry's own keys. That shape holds **561 rows across the six languages and 258 of them (45 %) match no dictionary value at all** — it doubles as a glossary, a concept list and a step heading — so a gate over ALL of them would need 258 acknowledgements and would rot; over the ~19 curated keys it reports **ZERO** false positives. A leading emoji is stripped from BOTH sides (the guide reproduces « 📦 Exporter ZIP » and drops the « 🤖 » from a section heading; without that the rule reports 12 hits, all of them that difference). **The similarity is a CHARACTER-OVERLAP ratio, not difflib's longest-common-subsequence, and the difference earned its keep on the first run**: the Python sweep this rule came from scored it « Peso di sessione predefinito » BELOW its threshold against « Peso predefinito sessione » because the words are REORDERED, and a character ratio is order-blind — so the gate found a thirteenth drift the sweep that produced it had missed. **The policy gets the same rule with a DIFFERENT scope, and the scope is the whole design.** `privacy.html` has no settings-reference list, so the row rule has nothing to scan there — but the masking is identical. MEASURED: scanning every emphasised string in the policy gives 197 candidates and TWO false positives, both the same prose turn in two languages (« lors d'un export ZIP » / « a ZIP export », naming the ACTION rather than the button); requiring a Settings BREADCRUMB within 200 characters gives **76 candidates and ZERO**. That is a principled cut, not an allowlist: the policy quotes a control precisely when it is telling the reader where to find it, and that is where the breadcrumb is. **`wrapsLabel` is the one shared exemption** — prose that WRAPS the label whole and word-bounded (« ships no catalogue », « Destination cloud ») rather than mis-naming it; verified against all thirteen real drifts before being added, none of which has that shape, and harmless to a truncation since there the candidate is the shorter string. **Both near-miss cases carry a NON-VACUITY guard, and a probe is why**: neutering the comparison silenced everything and left the case GREEN, because an empty report satisfies `toEqual([])` — so the policy case now asserts it examined at least 20 candidates. A second probe taught the older lesson again: the first attempt at it replaced a literal `→` that the source spells `\u2192`, so it changed nothing and passed. **Verify a probe APPLIED before believing it.** **A sweep over every quoted string was tried and REJECTED**: at a 0.86 threshold it reports ~57 hits per language of which one or two are real, because emoji prefixes, articles, plurals and `{n}` placeholders all read as near-misses. Curated stays the mechanism. **`public/privacy.html` IS COVERED BY THE SAME REGISTRY** — each row carries a `doc` naming which shipped file it is about. It was added after a sweep of that file found **SEVENTEEN** wrong quotations across the six languages, where an audit had reported four: all six truncated the API-key toggle, all six INVENTED a name for the ZIP export button (« Backup ZIP », « ZIP-Sicherung », « Copia de seguridad ZIP » against the app's « Exporter ZIP » everywhere), three named a different verb from the erase button's, and two got the AI section heading wrong (« Asistente DE IA » against « Asistente IA »). Nothing had ever compared that file to the dictionaries — **the guide had a check and the policy did not**, which is the whole reason the drift concentrated there. It matters more there than in the guide: this is the page a Google OAuth reviewer reads, and a policy that sends someone to a control by a name the app does not use is one they cannot verify. `dictValue` trims a leading emoji, so a Settings SECTION heading (`🤖 Assistant IA`) compares on the words prose actually reproduces — narrow on purpose, only a leading non-letter run. Probed by re-introducing each of the four drifts; each reddens its own row and names the language. **THE LAST RESIDUAL — a control quoted in the BODY of a section rather than in the settings-reference list — is closed too, and closing it cost a third exemption whose absence is instructive.** Those sentences are the ones that tell you which button to tap, so a wrong name there is as costly as in the reference list. MEASURED: scanning every emphasised string in the guide is **4044 candidates**, viable only because three exemptions absorb the classes that would otherwise swamp it. The first pass reported FOUR, of which TWO were real drifts invisible to every rule before it — it « Escludi le chiavi API dalle esportazioni » against « …da esportazioni e backup », and pt « Verificar as cópias na nuvem » against « Verificar cópias na nuvem ». **The pt one is worth knowing about: the sweep matched it against the WRONG key** (the encryption toggle, which shares most of its words) and the drift surfaced anyway — *a fuzzy rule does not have to identify the control correctly to notice that a quotation is not any of them.* The two false positives produced the two new exemptions. **`shareAWord`** — a near-miss must share a whole 4-letter word — because English « your preferences » scores 0.88 against « Preferred source » on LETTERS ALONE, sharing no word at all; verified against all fifteen drifts known at the time, every one of which shares a word, since that is what a drift IS (the same control renamed by an inserted article, a different verb, a truncation or a reordering). **`isRealLabel`** — a quotation that IS a label the app renders is correct, whichever row's loop is looking at it — because the registry is a CURATED SUBSET of the dictionary, so a fuzzy rule keyed on it necessarily meets real labels it does not know and reports them against whichever key they most resemble, *which is a report about the registry rather than about the guide*. Two shapes made it compulsory: the German tasting paragraph names BOTH sibling controls in ONE sentence, correctly (« Verkostung starten » and « ▶ Verkostung fortsetzen »), so each was reported as a near-miss of the OTHER; and the French inventory section quotes « À ne pas reprendre », the rebuy filter chip, a real label the registry has no reason to carry. **Verified against every real drift found so far — the thirteen in the guide, the seventeen in the policy and the four below: not one equals a dictionary value**, because a drift is by definition a string the app does not render. **The residual it leaves is disclosed rather than hidden**: the guide could point at control A while naming control B, with B real — a wrong CROSS-REFERENCE, not a wrong label, and no string-level rule can see it. **Turning the German false positive into COVERAGE rather than acknowledging it is what paid**: adding `tasting_title` to the registry surfaced FOUR MORE REAL DRIFTS in one stroke — the guide dropped the button's indefinite article in en, es, it and pt (« Start tasting » for « Start a tasting », « Iniciar cata » for « Iniciar una cata », « Avvia degustazione » for « Avvia una degustazione », « Iniciar prova » for « Iniciar uma prova »), in the one sentence that tells a reader which button starts a timed session; fr and de were right, which identifies it as translation drift. Same build fixed the cloud-destination row, which QUALIFIED a label the app renders bare (`lbl_cloud_provider` is « Destination » / « Destino » / « Ziel » / « Destinazione ») in five of the six — Italian alone was exact. **The body case carries its own non-vacuity guard and for a sharper reason than the policy's**: `scanned` is incremented BEFORE the exemptions, so neutering one to always-true leaves it high while nothing reaches a comparison; a separate `compared` counter is what actually fails. Probed three ways — reintroduce the Italian drift, disable `isRealLabel` (the fr + two de reports come back), force it true (the corpus-swallowed guard fires). **One performance note, because it was a real defect and not a nicety: `dictValue` did a `readFileSync` per call**, and this rule asks for a label once per candidate — ~81 000 reads, 14.4 s for one case. Memoising the dictionary source and hoisting a `split("")` out of the similarity scan took it under 3 s.
                    #   **The BUMP gate now also covers `src/i18n/`** — `^src/i18n\.ts$` is anchored,
                    #   so it matched the loader and NOTHING under `src/i18n/`, where every visible
                    #   string in the app lives. A translation fix could ship with no APP_BUILD bump:
                    #   version.json never moves, `checkVersion` never fires, and nobody receives the
                    #   corrected text. `public/help.html` stays excluded on purpose — it is served
                    #   network-first and reaches users without a build, whereas the dictionaries are
                    #   bundled into content-hashed chunks and a bump is their only delivery path.
npm run size:check  # bundle-size guard (run after build) — asserts the eager scripts stay within gzip budget (CI gate, runs before Lighthouse). There is deliberately no catalogue budget: a user's catalogue is a runtime CSV in IndexedDB, guarded by `MAX_CATALOGUE_ROWS` (20000) in userCatalogue.ts.
# `npm run catalogue:check` / `catalogue:preflight` were REMOVED
#                     with the whole Node catalogue tooling — they judged a DELIVERED
#                     master, and there is none. What judges a
#                     catalogue now is the in-app report (Réglages → Données →
#                     « Vérifier mon catalogue »). See the tombstone section.
npm run i18n:layout # OPT-IN cross-language layout check — renders the built
                    #   app across EVERY registry language × 36 screens × 2 text sizes (M + "L") × 2 widths
                    #   (360/820px) and fails on horizontal overflow / clipped text / text painted PAST a
                    #   clipping ancestor / a screen it could not reach. **The language axis is DERIVED from LANGUAGES** — it was the literal
                    #   "fr,en,es,de,it", so a default run silently skipped Portuguese in the very script whose
                    #   job includes "run it when you add a language". Narrow an axis while iterating with
                    #   `-- --langs pt --scales l --widths 360` (the I18N_LAYOUT_* env vars still
                    #   work, a flag wins). Six languages over 36 screens is 864 renders.
                    #   **IT FANS OUT — one process per language over one SHARED preview server**
                    #   (`scripts/parallelRun.cjs`), MEASURED at **~10 min against the ~55 it took in
                    #   series**; `theme:contrast` shards the same way, one process per palette, ~2 min
                    #   against ~45. **The point is not the minutes, it is what the minutes were doing
                    #   to the work**: an opt-in check that costs an hour competes with the honest move
                    #   after widening a checker (measure it), and a check nobody runs is documentation
                    #   — the `prune` lesson, which sat red for nine releases. Three properties make
                    #   the speed-up trustworthy rather than a shortcut, and `parallelRun.test.ts` pins
                    #   each: a shard must NOT fan out again (without that guard six children spawn
                    #   thirty-six — a fork bomb dressed as a slow campaign); the preview server is the
                    #   PARENT'S, adopted by every shard, because each script used to spawn its own
                    #   `--strictPort` server and six shards would mean five failures on a taken port
                    #   (it also means a `npm run preview` you already have open is reused); and **a red
                    #   shard must stay red** — aggregating six outputs must not drown a failure, or the
                    #   parallel run reports green whatever happens, which is worse than no run at all.
                    #   A shard is one AXIS VALUE (`de`, `steel/dark`), never an index, so a failure
                    #   names a thing and the sharding cannot drop or duplicate a combination the way a
                    #   round-robin over a flattened matrix can. Verified faithful, not merely fast: the
                    #   parallel contrast run reports the same 2566 elements and 11 warnings PER PALETTE
                    #   as the serial one, and the parallel layout run the same 864 renders and 85
                    #   canary rows. Narrowing to one language (or one palette) runs a single process
                    #   with no fan-out. NOT a CI gate; needs `npm i --no-save playwright-core`.
                    #   **The 35th screen brought, more usefully, a SECOND AXIS the
                    #   harness never had: whether a catalogue is loaded.** The catalogue became
                    #   the user's own file, so half the app has an empty state it never had before —
                    #   and the seed writes only `localStorage`, so every catalogue-dependent screen was
                    #   silently rendering that empty state while the run reported PASS. Four screens
                    #   degraded at once. `setCatalogue(page, csv)` now writes the fixture
                    #   (`src/__tests__/fixtures/catalogue-excerpt.csv`) into the `cave-catalogue`
                    #   IndexedDB before each screen, with `parserVersion: 0` so the app RE-PARSES it
                    #   rather than trusting a cache the harness would have to keep in step; the new
                    #   `catalog-empty` screen clears it and measures the missing-catalogue notice.
                    #   **Because `tobaccoDb.ts` caches for the whole session, the run re-navigates
                    #   whenever the catalogue state changes** — a screen that inherits the previous
                    #   screen's module memory measures the wrong state and says nothing about it.
                    #   The `catalog` screen's marker moved `catalog_title` → `catalog_results`: the
                    #   TITLE renders in BOTH states, so the old marker reported the screen reached
                    #   while measuring the empty page. That is the finding — *a green run
                    #   over an empty state is the most reassuring way to miss a screen* — one level
                    #   deeper: that finding was about the SEED being thin, this is about the MARKER being
                    #   unable to tell two states apart. **A marker must be unique to the screen AND to
                    #   the state the screen is there to measure.**
                    #   **The 34th screen is the USER GUIDE.** `help.html` is fetched
                    #   at RUNTIME, so it is invisible to anything that only walks the React views — and
                    #   it is the longest page in the app, all dense text, tables and badges. That gap
                    #   mattered the day three features were added to it: the new prose shipped
                    #   unmeasured in six languages. It is reached the way a user reaches it (Settings →
                    #   Aide → « Mode d'emploi »), so the screen also exercises `openDocFromSettings` and
                    #   the dock-hiding rule. Its marker is `btn_collapse_all`, which carries more than
                    #   arrival: that button is gated on the document having been FETCHED and PARSED into
                    #   sections for this language, so a failed fetch reports the screen unreachable
                    #   instead of quietly measuring an empty shell. Verified green in fr@M/360 and in
                    #   de@L/360 — the worst case on every axis at once. **The seed under-covered the newest surface, and that is the SECOND time.**
                    #   Before the pre-launch full run, the five screens touched were
                    #   checked against the fixture. `modal-lot` was not really covered: both seeded
                    #   sessions carried `lotId: ""`, so the "sessions smoked from this lot"
                    #   list rendered its EMPTY state in all 24 combinations — the POPULATED case
                    #   (one row per bowl, date · time · grams, the part that can overflow at 360 px
                    #   in German at "L") was measured by nothing. Verbatim the rule: **the
                    #   seed is a screen GATE**, and a fixture built from convenient data measures a
                    #   UI no user has. Three sessions are now attributed to a PINNED lot id, and the
                    #   lot's `weightG` BALANCES against them (50 − 2.5 − 2.8 − 3.1 = 41.6) — an
                    #   unbalanced lot trips `useLotIntegrityProbe` 1.5 s after load, which turns the
                    #   Settings diagnostic section oxblood and silently changes what the
                    #   `settings-app` screen measures. One session deliberately stays UNATTRIBUTED,
                    #   because an orphaned bowl is ordinary (the detach, accounting off, a
                    #   legacy row) and the journal must keep both states in view. Confirmed by
                    #   screenshot before the run — « SÉANCES DE CE LOT · 3 », three rows, the untimed
                    #   one correctly showing the date alone. `i18nLayoutHarness.test.ts` gained the
                    #   check nothing had: the seed must be a cellar `checkAllInvariants` ACCEPTS.
                    #   **When you add content to a screen the matrix covers, check the seed reaches
                    #   it — a green run over an empty state is the most reassuring way to miss it.**
                    #   **`theme:contrast` consumes the
                    #   SAME `SCREENS` list, so adding a screen here adds it there too** — run both, or
                    #   half the new coverage is asserted and half is merely assumed. The guide was
                    #   measured clean across all 6 palettes (3 themes × light/dark, 0 failures; the 66
                    #   warnings are the documented `[deliberately dimmed]` class). **That de@L run also surfaced a
                    #   PRE-EXISTING clip the matrix had not been run against: the search
                    #   modal's subtitle truncates `Virginia/Burley · Crumble Cake` at 360 px (needs 235,
                    #   box 216). **FIXED** — see `SearchModal.tsx`. It was reported and
                    #   left standing as "a layout decision on a shipped surface"; what changed the
                    #   answer is that it was the LAST standing failure of this check, and a
                    #   permanently-red opt-in check stops being read — the `prune` lesson. The
                    #   subtitle now WRAPS and the title above it still clips, which is not an
                    #   inconsistency: both halves of the subtitle are ENUM values, so the set is
                    #   closed and the maximum is computable (34 chars, `Englisch-Aromatisch ·
                    #   Broken Flake` — a worst case a later enum value created), while a blend name is
                    #   user-supplied and unbounded. The clipping string was 13% short of that
                    #   maximum, so wrapping costs one line and can never run away. Locked by the
                    #   block in `SearchModal.test.tsx`, which also re-derives the 34 and
                    #   fails if a future enum value would need a third line.**
npm run theme:contrast # OPT-IN contrast check across the SIX palettes (brass/steel/english ×
                    #   dark/light). Measures every visible text element against its effective background as
                    #   a WCAG ratio and fails below 3:1. Same opt-in terms as i18n:layout (needs
                    #   playwright-core); reuses its screens + seed so the two cannot drift apart, AND
                    #   its fan-out — one process per palette over the parent's preview server, ~2 min
                    #   against the ~45 it took in series (see the sharding note under i18n:layout).
                    #   The console report caps the warning list, so `THEME_CONTRAST_JSON=/tmp/c.json`
                    #   dumps the full set — that's how the triage grouped 313 warnings.
                    #   **It runs ONE language (fr) on purpose** — the reason is written down so the
                    #   subset stops looking frozen: a contrast ratio is a property of the colour TOKENS,
                    #   not of the words, so the same element measures identically in six languages and
                    #   the full matrix would cost 6× the runtime for identical numbers. Language-dependent
                    #   failures are LAYOUT failures and belong to i18n:layout, whose axis IS derived from
                    #   LANGUAGES. `THEME_CONTRAST_LANG` overrides it to eyeball one screen.
                    #   **THE TWO CHECKERS SHARE A SCREEN LIST AND NOT THE CODE THAT READS IT —
                    #   THREE TIMES, AND THE THIRD IS WHAT FORCED A MECHANISM.** Each time an axis
                    #   was added to `i18n-layout.cjs` and never read by `theme-contrast.cjs`, and
                    #   each time the symptom is the same and misleading: the screen reports
                    #   UNREACHABLE, which reads as a navigation problem rather than as a seed that
                    #   never arrived. (1) The CATALOGUE seed — recorded on the script's own header
                    #   at the time. (2) `markerText`: a screen is reached by finding a dictionary
                    #   value unique to it, and `list_more` is « Afficher la suite ({n}) », whose
                    #   `{n}` the app interpolates, so the RAW value appears nowhere on the page;
                    #   the helper exists for exactly that (truncate at the first `{`, with a length
                    #   guard) and this script read `dict[scr.expect]` straight. (3) The `bigList`
                    #   CELLAR swap: `inv-long` exists to render the progressive-list footer, which
                    #   needs ~98 rows against the shared seed's 18 — `bigListCellar` was exported
                    #   and **`setCellar` was not**, i.e. half a seed step, so the payload could be
                    #   built and never written. **Fixing (2) alone left the six failures standing
                    #   verbatim, which is what identified (3)**: the marker was now right and the
                    #   footer still was not there. So `inv-long` — the screen added precisely so
                    #   the footer would finally be rendered by something — had its contrast
                    #   measured by nothing in all six palettes, from the day it landed.
                    #   **The export comment in `i18n-layout.cjs` already stated the rule («  if you
                    #   add a seed step, export it and wire the other consumer in the same commit »)
                    #   and claimed `i18nLayoutHarness.test.ts` asserts both — IT ASSERTED NEITHER**;
                    #   the claim is corrected in place rather than deleted, because a guarantee
                    #   announced and absent is the failure worth recording. The mechanism is now
                    #   DERIVED rather than hand-listed: the test takes the union of keys across
                    #   `SCREENS`, subtracts the four navigation/identity fields (`name`, `dock`,
                    #   `expect`, `go`), and requires every remaining key to be read as `scr.<axis>`
                    #   by BOTH scripts — so a fourth axis is covered without anyone remembering to
                    #   add it. Probed: dropping the `bigList` wiring names the axis and the file.
                    #   `theme-contrast`'s init script also needed the layout harness's
                    #   `__harness-cellar-pinned` guard, without which the reload a swap needs
                    #   overwrites the swapped cellar immediately — the same trap, already
                    #   documented one file over. **When you add a field to a screen entry, it is a
                    #   contract with every consumer of the list, not a private note to one.**
                    #   **AND REACHING THE SCREEN EXPOSED A SECOND DEFECT THE FIRST ONE HAD BEEN
                    #   HIDING: the check was measuring text MID-ANIMATION.** With `inv-long`
                    #   finally rendered, it reported **443 unreadable combinations**, all on that
                    #   one screen — and the numbers refuted the reading before any theory did: the
                    #   SAME string over the SAME two colours measured **4.23:1, 2.28:1 and 1.51:1**
                    #   in three different rows. Identical colours cannot give different ratios;
                    #   only an ancestor OPACITY can, and the measurer folds ancestor opacity into
                    #   the foreground. That opacity is `useEnter`: every card fades in over a
                    #   460 ms CSS transition with a per-row delay capped at `ENTER_MAX_DELAY_MS`
                    #   (700), so the tail settles ~1160 ms after mount while the loop waits 700 ms
                    #   — invisible on an 18-row list and total on a 98-row one, where the whole
                    #   tail is still at or near opacity 0. **A palette verdict of 443 failures that
                    #   is really a timing bug is the worst possible output for a checker**: it is
                    #   loud, specific, and would have sent someone retuning tokens that are fine.
                    #   The fix is a CONDITION and not a longer sleep — the lesson the `help`
                    #   screen's fixed 1500 ms wait had already flaked on: `settle(page)` polls
                    #   until no **CSSTransition** is running. Filtering to CSSTransition is
                    #   load-bearing rather than tidy: the app runs INFINITE WAAPI animations (the
                    #   Spinner, the dock's brass indicator), so « no running animation » is never
                    #   true and a naive wait would burn its full budget on every screen. BOUNDED,
                    #   so a transition that never ends shortens the wait instead of hanging the
                    #   run (the `drainScheduler` trade). **Wired into BOTH checkers**, which is the
                    #   rule this same build wrote: `useEnter` animates `translateY` as well as
                    #   opacity, so a row measured mid-fade is measured mid-MOVE, and the layout
                    #   check has the same exposure through a different property.
npm run prune       # knip — dead exports / files / dependencies (a CI-style gate; ~2s)
npm run release:data # scripts/data-only-release.cjs — bump APP_BUILD and write a version.json
                    #   carrying `data_only: true`, so the running app applies the release
                    #   SILENTLY (no countdown, no banner) at the next backgrounding. For a
                    #   release with nothing for the user to react to — a wording or
                    #   translation fix, which still needs a bump because the dictionaries
                    #   ship in content-hashed chunks. `--visible` bumps without the marker.

**THE TWO BROWSER CHECKS ARE CI GATES NOW, AND THE FAN-OUT IS WHAT MADE THAT POSSIBLE.** `i18n:layout` and `theme:contrast` see what no other gate sees — a clipped label, a draggable scroller, an unreadable colour pair — and they were opt-in for one reason: ~55 min and ~45 min, so they ran a few times a year, by hand, before a release. That is verbatim the state this file names *a check nobody runs is documentation*. Sharded they measure **~10 min and ~3 min on a 4 vCPU machine — the same shape as `ubuntu-latest`** — so the FULL matrix fits in a job with no narrowing and no coverage claim to defend. They live in a SEPARATE `browser` job in `checks.yml`, on **push AND pull_request**: the convention here is to push straight to main, so a pull-request-only browser gate would fire almost never, which is the state it exists to end. **Deliberately NOT in `deploy.yml`, and that was weighed rather than skipped**: that is where a gate can hold the artifact back, but it would add ~15 min to EVERY deploy, permanently, for a class that is visible, harmless to data and re-pushable in minutes — unlike the four gates that do sit there, where shipping past them means shipping a type error or an untested build. **CORRIGÉ : elles SONT dans `deploy.yml` désormais, et la phrase qui précède annonçait sa propre inversion sans en connaître le motif.** Ce n'est pas une régression de mise en page qui a tranché, c'est la FENÊTRE : hors du chemin de déploiement, l'artefact partait, l'application arrivait sur le téléphone, et le verdict tombait ~9 min plus tard sur un build que l'utilisateur avait déjà — signalé comme gênant, donc fermé. Le raisonnement conservé de l'ancienne version est celui du COÛT, désormais MESURÉ sur le premier déploiement à passer par elles : build 2 min 48, les quatre portes 42 s, Chromium 28 s, **contraste 2 min 27**, **mise en page 9 min 57**, téléversement puis publication — **16 min 46 au total**, contre ~4 min avant. L'estimation valait ~17 min ; l'écart est nul, et le chiffre à citer est celui-ci. `upload-pages-artifact` est resté EN ATTENTE pendant toute la durée des campagnes, ce qui est la garantie observée plutôt que supposée. **PUIS LE COÛT A ÉTÉ DIVISÉ PAR DEUX, ET LA MESURE QUI L'A PERMIS EST L'ENTRÉE : un shard de langue prenait 9 min 44 d'horloge pour 20 s de CPU — environ 5 % d'utilisation.** La campagne ne calculait pas, elle ATTENDAIT, et l'attente était des `waitForTimeout` FIXES : ~1000 ms après chaque rechargement, 700 après le clic du dock, 1200 après la navigation propre d'un écran. À 144 visites d'écran par langue, cela fait ~418 s de sommeil sur 584 — **72 % de l'exécution**. Le fichier portait DÉJÀ la bonne règle, écrite pour le seul écran `help` : *« WAIT FOR THE MARKER, don't sleep and hope »* — appliquée à un endroit pendant que le reste de la navigation dormait, la forme que ce dépôt paie en boucle. Les sommeils étaient REDONDANTS et non porteurs : `settle` + `awaitMarker` tournaient juste après et attendent déjà les vraies conditions ; ce qui manquait était une condition pour ce qu'ils ne couvraient pas — que l'app ait MONTÉ avant qu'on clique son dock (`awaitBoot`), et que le nouvel écran ait COMMENCÉ à peindre pour les six pages du dock, seules à n'avoir pas de marqueur (`awaitPaint`). **L'ORDRE `awaitMarker` PUIS `settle` est ce qui rend la suppression sûre** : le marqueur attend l'ATTACHEMENT, donc il rend la main pendant que la transition tourne, et `settle` attend ensuite sa fin ; dans l'autre sens `settle` ne verrait rien tourner et rendrait aussitôt. **Résultat MESURÉ : mise en page 584 s → 251 s, contraste 139 s → 60 s, sortie IDENTIQUE À LA LIGNE PRÈS dans les deux cas** (diff sur la sortie complète, codes ANSI retirés). **LA PARTIE QUI COMPTE EST CELLE QUI A FAILLI PASSER : le contraste est descendu de 2565 à 2564 éléments mesurés.** Un seul élément — et un élément silencieusement non mesuré est exactement la perte que ce harnais existe pour empêcher. Trouvé en vidant tous les textes mesurés de l'écran dans les deux versions et en diffant : c'est `settings-data`, et l'élément est la ligne de diagnostic du contrôle multi-appareils, **différé de 4,5 s dans `useGdriveSync`** — les 2,9 s de sommeil par écran l'atteignaient PAR ACCIDENT. `awaitQuiet` (silence de mutations, borné) a été écrit d'abord et **n'a rien rattrapé** : la ligne n'arrive pas tard parce que le DOM bouge, mais parce qu'un minuteur de l'app la produit. Il est GARDÉ malgré tout — il couvre le contenu asynchrone ordinaire, comme la section catalogue dont la lecture IndexedDB rend *rien* tant qu'elle est en vol — et l'écran `settings-data` attend en plus, explicitement, son propre libellé. Coût : jusqu'à ~4,5 s sur UN écran de 36. **La leçon générale : supprimer un sommeil ne se valide pas au chronomètre mais en diffant la sortie COMPLÈTE, y compris les compteurs que personne ne regarde.** Déploiement projeté ~9 min 30 contre 16 min 46. Locked by the « the two browser checks run in CI » block in `deployGates.test.ts`, which pins the WIRING because that is what rots — the campaigns can stay perfect while a trigger quietly disappears — including that no axis is narrowed (a run over `--langs de` reports green having measured one language of six and reads as full coverage), that the build precedes them (both REFUSE a stale `dist/`), that each reports when the other failed, and that the fast lane never acquired a build step. Probed four ways; **the `!cancelled()` probe came back GREEN the first time because commenting the line out leaves the string in the file — verify a probe APPLIED before believing it, the lesson this repo has now recorded three times.**

**ELLES SONT MAINTENANT DANS LEUR PROPRE WORKFLOW, FILTRÉ PAR CHEMINS — et le chiffre qui a motivé ce changement était FAUX D'UN FACTEUR TROIS avant d'être re-mesuré.** Lancées à chaque push, elles rendaient 864 écrans sur des commits qui ne peuvent structurellement rien changer au rendu ; un contrôle vert à 100 % sur de telles exécutions apprend à ne plus le lire, la même érosion qu'un contrôle rouge en permanence. **Un premier comptage a annoncé 12 exécutions inutiles sur 20, sur une liste de chemins choisie à la main — vues, composants, i18n, thème — et cette liste était trop étroite : un HOOK peut bouger un pixel (`gdriveStatus` s'affiche dans Réglages, qui EST un écran de la matrice), `public/help.html` est un écran, une montée de bundler change l'artefact mesuré.** Avec la liste honnête, l'économie est de **4 sur 20**, toutes des commits purement tests ou documentation. Cela affaiblit l'argument et le changement a été fait quand même, sur décision de l'utilisateur — mais le chiffre corrigé est écrit ici plutôt que le premier, parce qu'une recommandation bâtie sur une mesure trop étroite est exactement ce qu'un lecteur suivant doit pouvoir repérer. **UN FICHIER SÉPARÉ PARCE QUE `paths:` EST UN FILTRE DE WORKFLOW ET NON DE JOB** — le faire sans séparer aurait demandé une action tierce pour comparer les fichiers modifiés. **LA LISTE EST ÉCRITE À LA MAIN, c'est-à-dire la classe de liste figée trouvée six fois dans ce dépôt, et son mode de panne est le pire : un workflow ignoré ne rapporte RIEN, donc il paraît vert en ayant cessé de couvrir.** `browserPathFilter.test.ts` inverse donc la charge au lieu de redire la liste : il parcourt les fichiers SUIVIS par git et exige que chacun soit couvert par un motif OU inscrit dans une courte liste d'exemptions portant sa raison — un nouveau fichier sous `src/` est couvert d'office, un septième répertoire de premier niveau rougit. Il refuse aussi une exemption MORTE (une licence dormante blanchirait le premier fichier qui tomberait dessus) et un motif d'une forme que son mini-moteur ne reconnaît pas (sans quoi une syntaxe plus riche le rendrait silencieux). Les quatre scripts qui PORTENT les campagnes sont dans le filtre malgré l'exemption large sur `scripts/` : un vérificateur élargi doit être exercé par la campagne. `deployGates.test.ts` a suivi le fichier et **le renversement est consigné sur ses assertions** — « le job est parti de checks.yml » est inversé plutôt que supprimé. **Sondé quatre fois** ; la sonde qui supprime le workflow fait sortir la suite en 1 sur un `ENOENT`, ce qui est bruyant et non silencieux. **SUITE, ET LE FILTRE A CHANGÉ DE PORTÉE : `browser.yml` ne se déclenche PLUS sur `push`.** Les campagnes sont entrées dans `deploy.yml` pour fermer la fenêtre non mesurée, donc les garder ici aussi ferait 864 rendus deux fois par commit. **Le filtre par chemins n'a PAS été porté dans `deploy.yml`, et le trou trouvé en le concevant est l'entrée** : il faudrait diffèrer contre `github.event.before`, or `concurrency: cancel-in-progress` annule les runs intermédiaires — deux poussées rapprochées, une vue puis de la documentation, laissent le run survivant ne voir que la seconde, et la vue partirait NON MESURÉE, précisément ce que la porte existe pour empêcher. **Une porte avec un trou est pire qu'une porte lente**, donc dans `deploy.yml` elles tournent sans condition. Le filtre garde toute sa valeur là où sa base est bien définie : les pull requests, où GitHub diffe contre la base de fusion. **En SÉRIE dans le job `build` et non dans un job parallèle**, parce que les deux vérificateurs REFUSENT un `dist/` plus vieux que `src/` — un job séparé devrait reconstruire, alors qu'ici elles réutilisent le `dist/` que l'étape Build vient de produire ; elles portent aussi la garde `steps.build.outcome == 'success'` de `size:check`, pour la même raison exactement (sans `dist/`, l'erreur de fraîcheur serait la DERNIÈRE du journal, donc la première lue). **Les renversements sont consignés sur les assertions** : « fires on PUSH as well as on pull_request » et « stays OUT of the deploy path, and that is a decision » sont inversés plutôt que supprimés, le second sous le commentaire qui avait prévu sa propre fin. Sondé cinq fois (campagnes après le téléversement, axe rétréci, garde `build.outcome` retirée, `push` revenu, campagnes retirées) — chacune rougit. **Une leçon de plus, la cinquième fois que ce dépôt la note : mon assertion « la voie rapide ne construit plus » rougissait sur l'en-tête HISTORIQUE de `checks.yml`, qui CITE `npm run build` pour expliquer ce que deploy.yml faisait autrefois.** Commentaires blanchis d'abord.

**The gates now GATE THE DEPLOY.** Until they were moved, `checks.yml` ran typecheck / lint / prune / catalogue:check (the last of those since retired and its tooling deleted) and `lighthouse.yml` ran size:check, both **in parallel with `deploy.yml`** and neither able to stop it: a push that failed any of them still uploaded its Pages artifact and shipped, with the red X arriving afterwards on a build users already had. An earlier release fixed *"these gates run nowhere"*; it did not fix *"they gate nothing"*, and the difference is invisible in a green dashboard, which is how it survived. The reachable case is not hypothetical — **Vite/Rolldown transpiles without typechecking**, so a `tsc` error builds and deploys perfectly happily, and a `catalogue:check` failure means shipping author notes or a non-canonical cut straight into users' cellars. All of them now run inside `deploy.yml`'s build job, after the build (size:check needs `dist/`) and **before `upload-pages-artifact`** — **FOUR, not five: `catalogue:check` stopped being a gate when the app stopped shipping a catalogue** (it now REQUIRES `--csv <file>` and is the tool a reviewer runs on a delivery). This sentence said « all five » until it was corrected, each with `!cancelled()` so one push reports every class at once; ~12 s on a ~3 min job. The duplication with `checks.yml` on a push to main is deliberate and is the cheap half of the trade: `checks.yml` gives fast isolated feedback and is the ONLY gate on pull requests, while this copy is the one that can actually hold the artifact back — **a gate in a parallel workflow cannot block a deploy**. Locked by `deployGates.test.ts`, which asserts each gate's command appears BEFORE the upload string (positional, no YAML parser — none is a dependency and adding one only for this would be flagged by knip), that the upload anchor exists exactly once so the ordering assertions can't pass vacuously, that `checks.yml` keeps its `pull_request` trigger, and that every gate step carries `!cancelled()`. Probed: moving the upload above the gates turns 6 of its 10 cases red. **`size:check` carries ONE extra condition — `steps.build.outcome == 'success'` — and it is the exception that earns itself.** `npm test` and `npm run build` share a single step, so a failing test means `dist/` was never produced; the gate then printed « dist/ not found », which is the LAST error in the job log and therefore the first thing a reader sees. That is how a flaky test in the suite came to be diagnosed as a build problem. It is NOT a weakening of `!cancelled()` — the gate stands down only when its input cannot exist, every other class is still reported on the same push, and the `id: build` the condition keys on is pinned too (without the id the condition silently evaluates to empty and the gate would never run at all, which is worse than the defect it fixes).
```

## Key Data Structures

All application state is serialized as JSON and stored under the localStorage key `pipe-cellar-v6`.

**Primary-key invariant**: every top-level entity (tobacco, pipe, accessory, session, wishlist item, lot) is keyed by a numeric `id` assigned by the app (auto-incremented counters `data.nxT` / `nxP` / `nxA` / `nxJ` / `nxW`, or `Date.now()` for lots). **No user-entered field is ever used as a key** — names, brands, descriptions, etc. are mutable and user-facing, never identity. Update functions (`updateTobacco`, `updatePipe`, etc.) always match by `id`, never by display fields. If you add a new entity type, follow this pattern: auto-assigned numeric id, mutable user fields keyed off it. **This extends to LOTS (integrity fix):** `updateLotInTobacco` / `removeLot` / `changeLotStatus` locate the target lot by its stable `id`, NOT by a positional array index — because views hold the trash-STRIPPED `liveData` lots while the store mutates the RAW (trash-inclusive) `data.tobaccos[].lots`, so a view-computed index points at the wrong lot when a soft-deleted lot precedes a live one (silent corruption + duplicate ids). A `lot-id-unique` runtime invariant (`lotInvariants.ts`) now flags any duplicate lot id within a tobacco at `save()`. Never reintroduce index-based lot mutation.

### Tobacco Entry (`BT` template)
```js
{
  name, brand, category, blend, cut,
  force,        // 0–5 (nicotine strength)
  roomNote,     // 0–5 (room note intensity)
  taste,        // 0–5 (flavour intensity)
  rating,       // 0–5 (personal rating)
  rebuy,        // null | true | false
  tastingNotes, // free text
  description,  // free text
  imageUrl,     // "local-photo-{timestamp}" (IndexedDB key) or external URL
  lots,         // array of Lot objects
  agingMax,     // string (years, optional) — max recommended cellar age; "" if unset
  tags,         // string[] (optional) — user-defined collections ("voyage", "cadeaux"…). Sanitised by migrateData (sanitizeTags: trim/dedup/cap). Personal grouping axis, NEVER an identity key.
  catalogueLock // boolean (optional) — the user pinned this fiche against the BULK catalogue pass; `planCatalogueApply` skips it BEFORE the lookup. Absent === false. Strict boolean on load (`=== true`, not `!!` — a forged "no" is truthy). STICKY across a merge: a lock propagates, an unlock does not. Carried through wishToInv. NOT a CSV column.
}
```

### Lot / Batch (`BL` template)
```js
{
  uid,            // string (optional on legacy) — stable cross-device
                  // identity (crypto.randomUUID), minted ONCE at creation,
                  // distinct from the per-device numeric `id`. Powers uid-first
                  // lot merge (two identical-acquisition tins stay distinct).
                  // Backfilled by migrateData; NOT in the BL template (minted in
                  // useTobaccoStore, one per bulk clone; makeLotDuplicate strips it).
                  // CARRIED VERBATIM in JSON / Drive / Dropbox / ZIP backups (the
                  // data blob is serialized as-is). NOT in the CSV export/import
                  // (no uid column) — a CSV round-trip re-mints the uid; CSV
                  // re-import stays idempotent via lotMergeKey, not uid.
  status,         // "cellar" | "jar" | "finished"
  originalStatus, // "cellar" | "jar" — how the lot first entered the
                  // inventory. Set once at creation (mirrors `status`
                  // except finished→cellar fallback). Migration of
                  // legacy lots infers from dateOpened presence. Kept
                  // on the record for future migrations / analytics, but
                  // no longer drives any auto-status transition (the
                  // jar→cellar auto-revert was removed).
  weightG,        // string (grams or oz per user pref) — current balance
  weightInitial,  // string — recorded original weight; seeded from weightG
                  // at creation, back-filled via migrateData for legacy
                  // lots. Used only for display (LotRow "/ Xg initial"
                  // annotation) and the cellar/jar age recap — never to
                  // trigger a status change.
  datePurchased,
  dateProduction, // MONTH precision, free text "YYYY-MM" — a `type="text"` field
                  // with a `2017-09` placeholder, NOT a date picker. A tin is
                  // stamped with a month, not a day, and a picker would force
                  // the user to invent one. It is the PIPE's production date
                  // that is year-only; these two are different fields with
                  // different precisions, which is worth knowing before
                  // "unifying" them.
  dateOpened,     // auto-filled when status → "jar"
  dateFinished,   // auto-filled when status → "finished"
  boxNumber,
  storageLocation, // string (optional on legacy lots) — free-text
                   // physical location ("Armoire A · étagère 2"). Shown on
                   // LotRow + lot detail modal, exported to CSV, matched by
                   // the inventory search (along with boxNumber).
  price,
  seller, sellerUrl,   // sellerUrl: optional seller website URL
  disposed        // boolean (default false) — true = lot was thrown/given away unsmoked. Only the "Lots finis" counter excludes disposed lots; the per-session weight (and therefore the monthly consumption chart) is still counted because those sessions were genuinely smoked at the time. **Disposing a lot NO LONGER touches the parent tobacco's `rebuy` flag. "À ne pas reprendre" (`rebuy = false`) is a deliberate, MANUAL per-tobacco judgement — a blend you didn't like and won't rebuy — NOT a mechanical consequence of physically eliminating a tin (you can toss a moldy tin of a blend you love). The earlier auto-set-on-disposal behaviour was reverted; only the manual rebuy toggle on the fiche sets it. The disposed flag still marks the lot (Éliminés filter). The tobacco card shows the shared `FINI` pill for a disposed lot (it's status:"finished") — a separate `ÉLIMINÉ` pill was REVERTED per user preference (finished + disposed both read FINI).**
}
```

### Pipe (`BP` template)
```js
{
  name, brand, shape, courbure,
  length,               // stored in whatever unit the user typed (mm or in per global lengthUnit)
  weight,               // stored in whatever unit the user typed (g or oz per global weightUnit)
  filterType,
  chamberDiameter,      // mm
  chamberDepth,         // mm
  bowlMaterial, stemMaterial,
  finish,               // one of FINISHES (Lisse/Rustiquée/Sablée/Teintée/Autre); "" if unset (v1.1 b14-15)
  datePurchased,        // YEAR only ("YYYY") since v1.1 b13 — migrated from full ISO
  dateProduction,       // YEAR only ("YYYY") since v1.1 b13
  price, seller, sellerUrl,   // sellerUrl optional
  description, notes,   // notes = personal/private notes
  imageUrl,             // "local-photo-{timestamp}" (IndexedDB key) — the COVER photo, resolved eagerly into global imgLocal on load
  photos,               // string[] (PIPES ONLY) — additional local-photo-* keys (max 6). Loaded ON DEMAND (never into the global imgLocal) — the fiche gallery / lightbox resolve each key from IndexedDB when opened, so a large pipe collection stays cheap to load. Included in backups (gatherLocalImages walks it) and protected from orphan-GC (referenced set walks it).
  rating,  // 0–5
  status,  // "active" | "finished"
  maintenance, // MaintEntry[] — pipe maintenance log ("Carnet d'entretien"). Embedded like tobacco.lots, so it rides along in every backup. Optional on legacy pipes; migrateData defaults it to [].
  tags         // string[] (optional) — user collections, same as Tobacco.tags (sanitizeTags on load).
}
```

### Maintenance Entry (`MaintEntry`)
```js
{
  id,     // numeric, Date.now() at creation (never a user field)
  uid,    // string (optional on legacy) — stable cross-device identity (crypto.randomUUID), minted in usePipeStore.addMaintenance, backfilled by migrateData. The maintenance-entry analogue of the entity/lot uid.
  date,   // "YYYY-MM-DD"
  time,   // optional "HH:MM". EMPTY on every legacy entry and clearable by hand, which is why the absence has a defined meaning rather than being a hole: an untimed cleaning reads as NOON, the same fallback `sessionStartMs` applies to an untimed session, so both sides of the reminder comparison agree on what a missing time means. It exists because the counter compares MOMENTS, not dates — a pipe cleaned and smoked again the same day used to count zero sessions since its cleaning and drop out of the reminders entirely (reported at a threshold of 1, where that is the whole feature). Labelled `maint_time_label` ("Heure"), NOT the session form's `lbl_time` ("Heure de début"): a cleaning is an event, it has a time, it does not start. Carried in every JSON / cloud / ZIP backup, since it is part of the pipe.
  kind,   // "light" | "full" | "none" — cleaning intensity; ONLY "light"/"full" feed the reminder counter (see pipeMaint.isCleaningMaint). "none" = an intervention (repair/wax) logged WITHOUT resetting the reminder. Labels via t("maint_kind_<k>").
  tasks,  // string[] of MAINT_TASKS keys checked (swab/bowl/ream/saltalcohol/stem/wax/repair/rest/other) — descriptive only, never affect the counter. Labels via t("maint_task_<k>").
  notes   // free text
}
```
**The reshape.** Earlier releases stored a single `type` (canonical FR from the old `MAINT_TYPES` enum); it was split into a cleaning `kind` (radio: léger / complet / sans nettoyage) + a multi-select `tasks` checklist. `MAINT_TYPES` + its `_EN/_ES/_DE/_IT` maps + its `ENUM_TRANSLATIONS` row are GONE — kind/task labels resolve via plain `t()` keys (`maint_kind_*` / `maint_task_*`), NOT the `xl()` enum-translation path. `constants.ts` now exports `MAINT_KINDS`, `MAINT_TASKS`, and `MAINT_LEGACY_MAP` (the type→{kind,tasks} migration table). **Reminder rule**: only `kind` `light`/`full` reset the "à entretenir" counter — `pipeMaint.lastMaintDate` filters on `isCleaningMaint`, so a `none` entry never counts. **Migration**: `migrateData` maps every legacy `type` to a COUNTING kind (Nettoyage→light, Alcool+sel/Alésage→full, Cire/Réparation/Autre→light) + the matching task, so no pipe becomes retroactively overdue; unknown kinds normalize to `light`, unknown task keys are dropped, `type` is deleted.

Lives inside `pipe.maintenance`. CRUD via `usePipeStore` (`addMaintenance` / `updateMaintenance` / `removeMaintenance`), rendered as the "Carnet d'entretien" section on `PipesDetailView` (newest first: kind badge + task pills + notes) + edited through `MaintFormModal` (kind SegmentedField + task checkbox chips + notes). Hard-delete (no soft-delete/trash — a log entry is minor). Included in JSON/Drive/ZIP backups (it's part of the pipe); NOT in the CSV working snapshot. **That hard delete STANDS, and the SILENCE around it did not.** This was the app's only irreversible one-tap delete: every other delete is a soft-delete + an 8 s undo toast + the 30-day trash, while `removeMaintenance` hard-filters the entry out, was never wrapped in `withUndo`, and `MaintFormModal` fires it straight from the bottom bar with **no confirm**. The sentence above justifies the hard delete and is still right — a `deletedAt` + trash entry for a log row would be machinery out of proportion — but *"minor"* was doing double duty: it answered "does this need a trash?" and was then read as answering "does this need FEEDBACK?", and the entry carries a free-text `notes` field. So the one delete you cannot get back was also the only one that said nothing. `withUndo` snapshots the whole cellar and restores it wholesale, so it needs nothing from the store, which is why this is the cheap fix rather than a second delete model: `removeMaintenanceU = withUndo(removeMaintenance, "maintenance", _maintLabel)` and **the ctx key keeps its name** (`removeMaintenance: removeMaintenanceU`), so no view changed. It needed an `UNDO_KIND` row too (`kind_maintenance` / `lbl_deleted`, six languages): an unknown kind renders NO overline rather than a guess, so without the row this new undoable action would have lost its label **silently** — the exact trap that entry was written for, sprung by the next person to add one. `_maintLabel` follows the other rule — that slot is a SUBJECT (`maxWidth: 240`, nowrap, ellipsis), never a sentence — so it is `date · pipe`, like `_sessLabel`. Locked by `maintenanceUndo.test.tsx`; probed by unwiring the ctx key, which reddens the case asserting the WRAPPED variant is what views get (the wrapper existing is not the fix — being reachable is).

  price, seller, sellerUrl,   // sellerUrl optional

### Session (`BJ` template)
```js
{
  date,
  time,               // v1.3: optional "HH:MM" start time (empty on legacy / retro-dated sessions). Orders same-day sessions in the journal (newest first: date desc → time desc → id desc; untimed rows sort to the bottom of their day). Auto-filled to the tasting start time on a live tasting, to the current local time on a fresh manual "+", editable in the form. Included in CSV export.
  tobaccoId, pipeId,  // references by id
  duration,           // minutes
  rating,             // 0–5
  notes,
  weightG,            // string — tobacco weight consumed (in user's preferred unit, default from user-configurable sessDefaultWeight setting)
  lotId,              // string — id of the lot deducted (lot.id from tobacco.lots[])
  aromas,             // string[] (optional) — tapped aroma-wheel descriptor keys (see src/utils/aromas.ts). Structured complement to `notes`, aggregated into the Stats "Profil gustatif". Sanitised to known keys by migrateData.
  updatedAt           // string (optional) — ISO edit timestamp stamped by useSessionStore on every add/edit. Drives multi-device merge LAST-WRITE-WINS in useImportConfirm: when BOTH the local + imported dup carry it AND the imported is strictly newer, its NON-KEY optional fields (notes/rating/lat/lng/location*/aromas) OVERWRITE the local ones. Absent on legacy sessions → falls back to fill-if-empty (never clobbers a pre-feature local edit). NEVER a key; weightG/lotId/duration/time are untouched (balance/identity).
}
```

## Enumerations

All enumerations live in `src/constants.ts` as `export var` (TypeScript `as const`).

```ts
CATS = ["Américain","Anglais","Aromatique","Balkan","Burley","Cavendish","Cigare","Dark Fired",
        "Écossais","Lakeland","Latakia","Oriental","Perique","Turkish",
        "VaPer","Virginia","Virginia/Burley","Virginia/Latakia","Autre"]
// "Anglais aromatique" added (20 values) — the English
// AROMATIC, i.e. a Latakia-bearing blend carrying a declared
// topping. Not a coinage: Smokingpipes runs a standing
// "English Aromatics" category and The Country Squire labels products
// "(English Aromatic)", so `CAT_MAP` accepts those spellings plus
// "Aromatic English" / "English/Aromatic" — the reviewer reads English
// product pages. The gap had already been MEASURED from the other
// side: 13 rows sat in `Aromatique` with Latakia in their `blend` column
// and were read closely and judged CORRECT under Family-prime, with the
// note that "the aromatic-English is a real genre". This is that genre
// getting its own value instead of borrowing one.
//   FAMILY: `cat_fam_aromatic`, per Family-prime (a declared topping wins
//   over the leaf family) and the Lakeland precedent. The counter-argument
//   is real and was weighed: the value is NAMED "Anglais aromatique", so a
//   reader scanning the grouped dropdown looks for it under
//   "Anglais & Latakia". It lost because the written doctrine beats an
//   ergonomic hunch, and because the risk is one-directional — a
//   topping-averse smoker scanning the English group could pick it by
//   mistake, whereas the word "aromatique" is in the value itself wherever
//   it is filed. Do not re-litigate without a user report.
//   COLOUR: do NOT read taxonomy into the hue. `CAT_COLORS` is a rotation
//   of distinguishable hues, not a semantic scheme (Burley is purple,
//   Cigare periwinkle), so the hue was picked on SEPARATION alone — see the
//   theme-curator note for the measurement and the candidate that failed.
// "Lakeland" added — the Kendal floral style
// (rose / geranium / tonquin top dressing, Samuel Gawith + Gawith Hoggarth).
// Added ON REQUEST for manual entry, not because the catalogue needed it: no
// row carries the label, so the usual test ("does it name an object the
// app cannot represent?") could not be answered from the data. It sits in
// `cat_fam_aromatic` because it is defined by a TOPPING, and its
// FAMILY_AGING_MAX is "5-10" — REASONED, not calibrated: the essence
// demonstrably fades over the years (old tins are described that way) so it
// cannot take Virginia's 15-25, while a pressed leaf-forward style is nothing
// like a Danish aromatic's 3. Sources: smokingpipes "A Love for Lakelands",
// the Oklahoma Briar Society on the essence. English keeps the proper noun,
// so it is an IDENTITY entry in CATS_EN and correctly ABSENT from the four
// sparse maps (doc:check gate 16).
// "Américain", "Virginia/Latakia", "Cigare" added. Adding a
// CATEGORY is never a one-line change — it touches SIX sites, and two gates
// exist because of it: CAT_FAMILIES must partition the enum EXACTLY
// (constants.test.ts), and CAT_COLORS needs a `--c-cat-<slug>` entry with a
// MODE_LIGHT override listed in THEME_VARS (catColorsLight.test.ts) or the
// label is unreadable on parchment. Also FAMILY_AGING_MAX (utils.ts).
// "Virginia/Latakia" is deliberately absent from CATS_ES/DE/IT/PT: English
// leaves it untouched, so it is jargon, and doc:check gate 16 REQUIRES the
// four sparse maps to omit it — the same rule that requires "Américain"
// (which English translates to "American") to be present in all four.
// The MAPPING was also fixed, which is where the cost was hiding: CAT_MAP
// in the Node checker (since deleted) sent "Cigare" -> "Autre", so 14 rows
// that had carried `category=Cigare` all along were shipping to users as
// "Autre". Making the category real fixed all 14 at once, and "Autre" fell from
// 15 rows to 1. CAT_MAP holds ALIASES onto canonical values — and they are not only ENGLISH ones. The row that first justified it ("Cigar", "Cigar Leaf", "American") came from a reviewer reading English product pages, but the map also folds FRENCH spellings the app itself does not store: `Périque` → `Perique`, `Americain` → `Américain`, `Anglais Aromatique` → `Anglais aromatique`. An accent or a capital is exactly what a hand-typed CSV gets wrong, so the map is the import contract for BOTH directions, not a translation table in one.
// And `scripts/validate-tobacco-db.cjs` no longer COPIES the enums: it kept a
// hand-mirrored CATS under a comment reading "must mirror src/constants.ts",
// which duly stopped mirroring it — adding Cigare made the validator reject 14
// rows the app accepts. It now parses CATS/CUTS out of constants.ts with a
// non-vacuity guard, the way the checker already did. A comment asking
// a human to keep two lists in step is not a mechanism.

CUTS = ["Broken Flake","Coarse Cut","Coins","Crumble Cake","Cube Cut","Curly Cut",
        "Flake","Loose Cut","Plug","Pressed","Ready Rubbed","Ribbon",
        "Rope","Rough Cut","Shag","Sliced","Twist","Autre"]
// "Twist" added, and its `CUT_MAP` alias onto `Rope` removed.
// Same construction as a rope — leaves layered and spun tight — which is an
// argument for the same DENSITY (0.36, the table's highest, shared with Rope)
// and NOT for the same name: the trade sells them as two products, and the
// fold left a twist unnameable in the entry form. Added on request; no
// catalogue row carries the label today.

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// CAT_MAP / CUT_MAP — the IMPORT CONTRACT, alongside the two
// enums above: the trade / retailer labels a source may write (`Cigar`,
// `Navy Cut`, `Krumble Kake`, `English Aromatic`), mapped onto the canonical
// value. They MOVED HERE from the Node checker, which the browser
// bundle cannot import, because a THIRD consumer appeared: the browser now
// normalises a catalogue CSV the user loads themselves, and it has to agree
// with the Node importer exactly. A TS copy beside the .cjs one is the drift
// this repo has paid for three times, so the checker PARSED them back out of
// this file rather than copying them — the mechanism it had used for
// CATS/CUTS — with a FATAL non-vacuity guard, because build
// 168's lesson is that a parse degrading to `{}` makes every check below pass
// while examining nothing. `enumMapsSingleSource.test.ts` asserts the two
// sides are observably EQUAL, that no literal copy has returned to the
// checker, that every map TARGET is canonical (the rule: an entry
// pointing at a non-canonical value launders a bad label past the gate it
// feeds), and that no entry shadows an already-canonical value.
//
// BOTH ARE NULL-PROTOTYPE, and here that is correctness, not house style: the
// key now comes from a USER-SUPPLIED FILE, so on a plain object a row carrying
// `category: "constructor"` resolves to a member of `Object.prototype` —
// truthy, not a category — defeating the `MAP[c] || c` fallback that
// `mapCategory` / `mapCut` are built on. An unknown label is returned VERBATIM
// so the caller can REPORT it: the catalogue gate refuses it, the browser
// importer names it to the user.
//
// **`canonCategory` / `canonCut` sit beside them and answer
// the OTHER question.** `mapCategory` / `mapCut` normalise and hand back an
// unknown label verbatim, which is right for a checker that must REPORT it.
// A writer needs to know whether the CELLAR can store the value at all, so
// these return the canonical value or **null** — fold-tolerant, because the
// catalogue is hand-filled, while the `map*` pair stays exact because the
// catalogue GATE depends on exactness. See the helpers for why null and not
// `Autre`, and `catalogueValueNotRepresentable.test.ts` for the three writers
// that needed them.

SHAPES = ["Acorn","Apple","Ball","Barrel","Bent Billiard","Billiard", ...]

BENDS = ["Droite","Semi-courbée","Courbée"]
FILTERS = ["9mm","6mm","Balsa","Métal","Hybride 6mm","Hybride 9mm","Autre"]  // + "Aucun" option in UI (Métal + the two Hybride sizes were added later)
BOWL_MATS = [...]
STEM_MATS = [...]
FINISHES = ["Lisse","Rustiquée","Sablée","Teintée","Autre"]  // pipe surface finish (v1.1 b14-15)
ACC_TYPES = ["Briquet","Blague à tabac","Bourre-pipe","Porte-pipe","Autre"]
LIGHTER_FUELS = ["Gaz","Essence","Électrique","Allumettes","Autre"]
MAINT_KINDS = ["light","full","none"]  // cleaning intensity of a maintenance entry; labels via t("maint_kind_<k>"). Only light/full feed the reminder counter.
MAINT_TASKS = ["swab","bowl","ream","saltalcohol","stem","wax","repair","rest","other"]  // checkable tasks; labels via t("maint_task_<k>"). Descriptive only.
// (The old MAINT_TYPES enum + its _EN/_ES/_DE/_IT + ENUM_TRANSLATIONS row were removed — kind/task labels are plain i18n keys, not xl(). The legacy type→{kind,tasks} migration table is inlined in migrateData.)
```

Each enumeration has a corresponding `_EN` variant (e.g. `CATS_EN`, `CUTS_EN`, `SHAPES_EN`, `BENDS_EN`, `ACC_TYPES_EN`, `FINISHES_EN`) used for the English UI translation.

## Application Views / Router

The app uses a custom `view` state string as a client-side router. No URL changes.
All views live under `src/views/curator/` and access ctx via `useAppCtx()`. Each view returns `null` when its `view` key (or required sub-state) doesn't match — `CuratorApp` mounts every view simultaneously and only one is visible at a time.

| View key | Component | Notes |
|----------|-----------|-------|
| `home`   | `CuratorHomeViewV2` | Dashboard (sole Home layout; classic HomeView removed). **Featured pipe / featured tobacco** = most-used over the **last 30 days**. Ties broken by highest rating, then by oldest record. With zero recent sessions, rotates among ALL active candidates (see next). **The top tie-group rotates every 12 h** (was a calendar day) — both featured picks call `pickDailyTie(..., FEATURE_ROTATE_MS)` (12 h, exported from `utils/suggest.ts`) so a tied set alternates twice a day. **The tie-key is the recent-USE COUNT ONLY** (rating dropped from it — it still ORDERS the sorted list so rotation starts from the best-rated). Before, the count+rating key made the common "no recent sessions" case (every candidate at count 0 but different ratings) resolve to a UNIQUE highest-rated leader → the feature was pinned and never rotated; count-only puts all equally-used candidates in one tie group so they cycle. Mirrors `suggestRestedPipe`'s rest-only tie-key rationale. The **"Ce soir ?" secondary list** also rotates on the 12 h cadence and holds back ≥ 1 candidate (`dailyWindow(pool, now, size, FEATURE_ROTATE_MS)` with `size = min(3, pool−1)`) so a modest cellar's runners-up cycle instead of showing the whole post-hero pool frozen. **The big "Ce soir ?" HERO (`rotateDailyHero`) also rotates every 12 h** (was calendar-day) — the whole home suggestions block now breathes on one 12 h rhythm (hero + secondary list + both "du moment" picks). **Two changes so the picks actually vary for a real cellar:** (1) both **"du moment" picks now rotate among the TOP TIER via `rotateDailyHero`** (pool = recently-smoked set when ≥ 2 exist, else all actives; sorted most-recent-then-best-rated, `pool = min(5, len)`) instead of `pickDailyTie` — `pickDailyTie` PINNED a unique most-used leader (size-1 tie group → `bucket % 1` never moves), so a user with one genuinely-most-smoked blend (e.g. Autumn Evening at 3 sessions) saw the SAME "du moment" forever. The user chose variety over a strict "single most-used" reading; the top pick still often surfaces (it's `pool[0]`) but the others cycle in. `pickDailyTie` stays in `suggest.ts` for `suggestRestedPipe`. (2) **a per-launch rotation axis** (`homeRotationSeed` / `cave-sugg-rot`, see the keys table) — the 12 h bucket is stable within its window, so reopening/reloading inside it showed identical picks ("toujours les mêmes"); `rotShift = homeRotationSeed() × FEATURE_ROTATE_MS` is added to the rotation clock of ALL FOUR picks so every app launch steps them forward, while in-session navigation stays stable. **Per user request ("toujours les mêmes" with many open tins): the "Ce soir ?" picks are now a RANDOM draw, and rating is dropped everywhere.** (1) The `tonight` memo calls `computeSmokeSuggestions(..., { openOnly: true, ignoreRating: true, max: 500 })` — eligibility is OPEN jar lots only (`openJarLots`: `status === "jar"` && weight > 0; sealed cellar tins excluded), `rebuy === false` still excluded, and the rating score + `favorite` reason are skipped. The render body draws hero + secondary from `seededShuffle(tonight, shuffleSeed)` (Fisher-Yates over `mulberry32`, both in `suggest.ts`) where `shuffleSeed = homeRotationSeed()×100003 + floor(now/12h) + sessionCount` — deterministic within a session, reshuffled each launch / 12 h / logged session. This REPLACED the score-ranked `rotateDailyHero`/`dailyWindow` path for "Ce soir ?" (those helpers stay in `suggest.ts` — `dailyWindow` still drives the "À surveiller" list, `rotateDailyHero` still drives "du moment"). Reason chips (trop âgé / jamais fumé / …) still render on whatever is drawn; the "À surveiller" section still surfaces aging/low-stock separately. (2) Both **"du moment" sorts drop the rating tiebreak** — ranked by recent session COUNT only (then stable date/id), still rotated among the top tier by `rotateDailyHero`. Also surfaces the interactive smoking calendar and the "À entretenir" pipe-maintenance reminder, and a footer privacy link (see the DocPageView Google/OAuth note). |

Its `SessionFormView` twin never had the bug because that one is a real `FormSection`, which owns the gutter; this block is hand-rolled and simply never got one. **`i18n:layout` structurally cannot see this class** — a block 24 px wider than its siblings but still inside the viewport overflows nothing and clips nothing, which is none of that checker's failure modes (four of them, and it is still none of them). Shortening the German was the alternative and is the one tried and reverted. **`i18n:layout` cannot see this class either: it walks TEXT NODES, and a placeholder is an ATTRIBUTE** — verified, the script never reads one.
