| (overlay) | `CuratorSearchModal` | Global search across tobaccos / pipes / wishlist / accessories / session notes. Toggled by `searchOpen`. **Also searches** the bundled reference **catalogue** (~1200 blends) via `searchCatalog()` — the DB is lazy-loaded on modal open (never cold-start), matched with `tobaccoDbSearchMatch`, shown as a "Catalogue" group; tapping a catalog hit sets `catalogSeed` (ctx) + `nav("catalog")` so `CatalogView` opens pre-filtered on the query (consumed once then cleared). **A WISHLIST hit now resolves to its CARD.** It used to `nav("inv")` + set the `wish` filter and DROP `h.id` — its own comment said so (« the user can tap the card to edit ») — so a hit opened a 16-item list scrolled to the top, on a different item, with nothing saying where the match went (reported with two screenshots). Every other kind in that handler resolves to its specific row; this was the one that did not. `wishFocusId` (ctx, same consumed-once shape as `catalogSeed`) carries the id; `InventoryListView` expands the item's brand group when the list is GROUPED and that group COLLAPSED — the card is not in the DOM at all otherwise, which is why the reveal is an effect and not a scroll call in the handler — then scrolls it so its TOP sits just under the sticky TopBar and rings it in brass for ~2.6 s. **That scroll was fixed twice, and both failures are worth knowing.** It first used `scrollIntoView({block:"center"})`, which centres the BOX — and a wish card carries the full description, so it is routinely taller than the viewport and centring pushed the photo, the brand and the name off the top, i.e. the three things that identify it (« le haut de la fiche est masqué »). The offset is now the TopBar's MEASURED height (`data-topbar`), never a constant: that bar grows with the safe-area inset and with the text-size setting. Then a single `scrollTo` still landed 2 px under the bar, and a loop that exited once the position looked settled left a mid-list card at **1598 px, entirely off screen** — because every card fades in through `useEnter` with a delay PROPORTIONAL TO ITS INDEX, so the loop finished before that card's animation had begun, and expanding a group re-lays the list out afterwards too. It now corrects across the whole ~1 s animation window and ABORTS as soon as `window.scrollY` is not the value it set, so it cannot fight a deliberate swipe. Measured after the fix: card top at 75 px against a 66 px bar, in BOTH list modes. The collapse key is the STABLE brand (`w.brand || ""`, the rule). **The destination is the CARD, never the edit form**: a wish has no fiche (the card carries the whole record) and whole-card tap-to-edit was deliberately removed from `WishCard` because users expected the read-only behaviour of the other cards and got a form (« No surprise edits ») — a search result is that same expectation. Verified in a browser in BOTH list modes, the collapsed-group case being the one that can actually fail. |

| (section) | `CatalogueStatus` (in `SettingsModal.tsx`) | The « Catalogue de référence » section in Réglages → Données — download the template, load a CSV, see what is loaded, export it back, remove it, and back it up to / fetch it from the cloud. **The SAVE action is gated on a catalogue being loaded and the RESTORE action deliberately is not** — the device that most needs to fetch one is the one that has none, so gating both would hide the button exactly where it is the answer. **It sits BEFORE « Export & Import », and that is not cosmetic**: placed after, it pushed « Effacer toutes les données » into the middle of the tab, which is the complaint one control over. **Found by RENDERING it**, not by a test. `catalogueMeta` has THREE states and the block tells them apart — `undefined` (first IndexedDB read in flight) renders NOTHING, `null` renders the hint, an object renders the counts; collapsing the first two would flash « Aucun catalogue chargé » on every open. It surfaces every count the parser reports (rows skipped for want of identity, duplicate keys, unrecognised category / cut labels kept verbatim) because **a catalogue that silently dropped a third of its rows looks exactly like one that loaded fine**. Verified end to end in a real browser through the actual file picker: « 3 blends · 3 marques », the load date, the file name and all three warning lines. Locked by `userCatalogueSection.test.tsx`, including the placement.
| (panel) | `SyncDiagView` (in `SettingsModal.tsx`) | The MERGED cloud panel — one button, one panel, doing both jobs the two former ones did (a verdict per file, plus its size and a bin). **Two wiring defects came out of that merge and neither was visible to any test**, because both live BETWEEN modules. **(a) It lost the `!gdriveConfirm` guard the old `BackupsListPanel` carried, while the comment fifty lines above went on PROMISING it** — worse than no comment, since it tells the reader the invariant holds. **The REASON first recorded here was WRONG and is corrected in place rather than deleted, because the mistake is the instructive part**: it said both panels carried a delete button over the same files, so a row binned in one survived in the other and its bin then 404'd. The picker's bin only ever rendered under `isDeleteMode`, a state whose ONLY producer (`gdriveManageBackups`) had lost its entry point in that very merge — so the conflict named was unreachable, and the correct rule had been written from the code as it USED to be rather than as it was. What the guard is really for is simpler and still holds: `gdriveConfirm` IS the restore picker, whose primary action replaces the entire cellar, so stacking a second list of the same files under it invites a tap on the wrong one. The guard is on BOTH renders. The whole delete-mode chain — `gdriveManageBackups`, the `mode` parameter, the thirteen `isDeleteMode` branches and `gdriveDeleteOption` — was subsequently DELETED as unreachable. **(b) On Google Drive no file size was ever fetched.** Drive applies the `fields` mask VERBATIM and the three listings feeding `buildSyncDiag` asked for `files(id,name,modifiedTime)` — so `f.size` was `undefined`, every row rendered sizeless and the total read "—", killing the whole file-management half of the merge. **Dropbox worked throughout, its adapter ignoring the mask**, which is exactly how a wiring gap survives a reading; and the existing panel tests build rows by hand, so they could never have caught it. The mask is now the single named `SYNC_DIAG_FIELDS` — it had been written out three times and all three forgot the field, so the fix is one source of truth rather than three corrections. Listings that only need identity (the auto-file sweep, the newer-backup check) keep their own narrower mask on purpose. `gdriveApi.ts`'s own comment claimed "the listing has always had it; this row simply dropped it" — false, corrected in place. Locked by `cloudPanelWiring.test.ts`, source-level on purpose (the guard needs two independent states set at once; the mask's effect is invisible to any hand-built fixture), comments blanked first, probed three ways. |

Shown ONLY when `duplicateCount(dataRaw) > 0` — an always-present button for a condition most users never hit is noise, and the count IS the reason to look. Groups live rows sharing brand+name (via `utils/duplicates.ts`), shows per row the lots / weight / sessions / inventory numbers / last edit, highlights a shared identifying inventory number as « probablement la même boîte », and merges into the row the user designates: lots + maintenance move over, sessions are repointed, the dropped rows go to the TRASH (30-day undo). Follows the three rules this section learned the hard way — the panel carries its OWN close ×, its result renders under its own button, and the destructive action names exactly what will move before it runs. Locked by the « duplicates utility » block in `SettingsModal.test.tsx`. |

The dock (`BottomDock`) hides on full-screen forms (`addT/editT/addP/editP/addA/editA/addJ/editJ`), on `tasting`, on the reading/doc pages, and while the wishlist form is open. **The decision is the pure `shouldShowDock(view, {showWishForm, editWishId})` in `src/utils/dockVisibility.ts`** (extracted from `CuratorApp` so it's unit-testable — `NO_DOCK_VIEWS` + the predicate are locked by `src/__tests__/dockVisibility.test.ts`). **This REVERSED an earlier decision to keep the dock on the reading pages**: the doc pages (`help` / `changelog` / `privacy` / `licenses`) now HIDE the dock again. The floating dock pill scrolls OVER the long reading content and overlapped the text (reported as "le bug du doc, sur toutes les pages"); those pages carry their own TopBar back button, so the dock was pure noise. Do NOT re-add the doc pages to the "keeps dock" set. **The doc CONTENT itself is well-formed** — `src/__tests__/docPages.wellformed.test.ts` parses the real shipped `public/{changelog,privacy,licenses,help}.html` per language and fails on any unbalanced tag / dropped section / empty `<h2>` title, locking the classic "malformed tag ejects entries" doc bug.

## AppContext Pattern

All views read App state via the React Context, avoiding prop-drilling:

```ts
// src/AppContext.tsx
import React from "react";
export type AppCtxType = Record<string, any>;
export var AppCtx = React.createContext<AppCtxType>({});
export function useAppCtx(): AppCtxType { return React.useContext(AppCtx); }
```

In `App.tsx`, all state and functions are bundled into a single context value object (`appCtx`) and provided at the root:

```tsx
var appCtx = { data, view, nav, t, xl, lang, weightUnit, /* ... all state & functions */ };
return h(AppCtx.Provider, { value: appCtx }, /* views router */);
```

In views:
```tsx
const { data, nav, t, weightUnit } = useAppCtx();
```

**Single `appCtx` consumed by every Curator view.** `data`, `nav`, `t`, `xl`, `lang`, all `*Store` actions, `pickJarLot`, `lotAgingStatus`, tasting actions, AI actions, Drive actions, etc. When adding a new ctx key, expose it in the `appCtx` object built in `App.tsx` (currently around lines 2660-2970 — the range drifts with every App.tsx edit, so search for `var appCtx = {` rather than trusting the numbers). Missing exposure is the most common source of "button does nothing" bugs (the destructure silently yields `undefined` and the guarded handler short-circuits).

**`AppCtxType` is fully typed — keep it that way (anti-regression).** `src/AppContext.tsx` is no longer `Record<string, any>`: every **callable** (store actions, setters, tasting/gdrive/ai/export functions) is typed and **required** (`(...args: any[]) => void|any` at minimum, real signatures for `t`/`xl`/`nav`/store CRUD), every **primitive/pref** has its base type, and `data`/`dataRaw` are `AppData`. Two invariants when you add or touch a ctx key: **(1)** add it to `AppCtxType` with a real type (a new callable is `required`, not `?: any` — required keys never break tests or the seed because both are cast, see below) AND expose it in App.tsx's `appCtx` — the typecheck now flags the read site if you forget either; **(2)** the `createContext` seed and the direct-`AppCtx.Provider` test literals are deliberately cast (`as (unknown as) AppCtxType`), which is what lets required keys stay churn-free — don't "fix" those casts by trying to enumerate every key. The **~34 remaining `?: any`** keys (working-copy form objects, refs, blank `B*` templates, polymorphic `tasting`/`stats`/`updateStatus`/`*Confirm` unions) are a DELIBERATE, documented tail — see the header comment on `AppCtxType`. Do NOT bulk-convert them to precise types; typing a working-copy form surfaces false-positive shape errors for no safety gain. Type one of them only if a concrete bug motivates it.

**`nav()` MUST NOT reset edit IDs or form state (a hard invariant).** The edit handlers in every detail view follow the pattern:

```ts
setXxxForm(Object.assign({}, BX, item));
setEditXxxId(item.id);
nav("editX");
```

React batches setStates in a single event handler and applies them in order. If `nav()` resets `setEditXxxId(null)` (or `setXxxForm({})`), the user's intent is silently wiped — the edit form loads but `editXxxId === null` at save time, so the store's `updateXxx` `.map()` matches nothing and the modification is lost. **The clean lifecycle is**: set by the edit handler → cleared by the form's `cancel()` or by the store's `updateXxx()` / `addXxx()` success path. Nothing else, including `nav`, should touch them.

**The OTHER end of that lifecycle: the "+" button must BLANK the working copy, and for 150 releases it did not.** The rule above is right and stays; its consequence is that a form left any way OTHER than `cancel()` keeps its working copy loaded — and that is the ordinary way to leave one, because a form the user has not modified is CLEAN, so `useUnsavedFormGuard` lets a system-back or an edge-swipe through without a word. The next `nav("addT")` then opened « Un nouveau tabac » over the previous tobacco's fields, photo, notes and rating. **It is not cosmetic**: `addTobacco` does `uid: source.uid || newUid()` and re-stamps only lots that LACK an id, so the new row inherits the edited entity's **`uid`** — the cross-device merge identity `resolveMergeMatch` matches on FIRST — and duplicates its lot ids **globally**, which is exactly what `useTrashOps` and the 30-day sweep filter on. Three invariants fire at the next `save()` (`tobacco-uid-unique`, `lot-id-unique-global`, `lot-uid-unique`); `addPipe` additionally carries `maintenance` and `photos`, `addAccessory` the same uid. **What identifies it as an oversight rather than a decision: the SAME handler in `InventoryListView` already did it right for the wishlist** (`setWishForm({...BW}); setEditWishId(null)`) — that form is an overlay and had to — while the three view-based forms never got it, and `wishToInv` builds from `BT` with an explicit field allowlist for the same reason. The three lists now each carry an `openAddTobacco` / `openAddPipe` / `openAddAccessory` used by BOTH their "+" and their empty-state CTA, so the two doors cannot drift. `nav()` is untouched — the fix belongs at the button, not in the store (a store that ADOPTS a source uid is correct for a genuine import) and not in `nav` (that is the invariant). **Note the inversion this leaves recorded: the DIRTY path was always safe** (the guard's « Quitter sans enregistrer » calls `cancel`); the CLEAN one was not. Locked by `addFormStartsBlank.test.tsx`, probed per view.

## Curator UI

- **Entry point:** `src/CuratorApp.tsx` — top-level shell rendered unconditionally from `App.tsx` once terms are accepted. Mounts every Curator view (each returns `null` unless `view` matches), the BottomDock, the modal stack (Search / Settings / Lightbox), and Overlays (DelConfirm, save error/warn, update pill, auto-update countdown, just-updated toast, **WelcomeModal**).
- **Layout / scroll model — WINDOW SCROLL (do NOT refactor without a real-device test):** the app uses plain **window/body scrolling**. `index.html` reset is `#root{min-height:100vh}` + **`body{overflow-x:clip}` (NEVER `overflow-x:hidden`: on iOS Safari `hidden` turns `<body>` into a scroll container, so the `position:fixed` dock positions against that box and floats to the middle on scroll of a tall page; `clip` clips identically without a scroll container)** (NO `overflow:hidden` body lock, NO `100dvh` shell). **iOS-PWA floating-dock guardrails (all reverted once by a roll-back, restored + LOCKED by `src/__tests__/iosPwaDockGuard.test.ts` — do NOT undo):** (1) `body{overflow-x:clip}`; (2) shell `width:100%` not `100vw`; (3) the `nav()` pinch-zoom viewport-meta swap in `App.tsx` is skipped when `IS_IOS_STANDALONE` (mutating the viewport meta recomputes the visual viewport and dislodges the fixed dock); **(4) THE decisive one — `BottomDock` is PORTALED to `document.body` via `createPortal` in `CuratorApp`. A `position:fixed` dock trapped inside the app column drops into flow the instant ANY ancestor gains a containing-block property (`transform`/`filter`/`backdrop-filter`/`contain`/`will-change`) — which the recessed-tone surfaces + the dock's own blurred pill introduce — floating it mid-page ONLY in the installed iOS PWA (Safari-browser masks it). Portaling under `<body>` makes it immune to any ancestor. NEVER un-portal it.** The test asserts these four source invariants so a future revert fails CI instead of shipping "le menu du bas qui flotte" to the installed PWA. The shell (`CuratorApp.tsx`) is `width:100%; min-height:100vh` (**`width:100%`, NEVER `100vw`** — 100vw ignores the scrollbar and overflows horizontally, which floats the fixed dock on iOS PWA) centring a `maxWidth:760` `position:relative` column (raised from 600 to 760, so iPad / large screens use more horizontal width — a strict no-op below 600px, so phones are unaffected) that grows with its content; the page scrolls the window. The `BottomDock` is `position:fixed; left:0;right:0; bottom:0` and its inner pill caps at `maxWidth:736` (= 760 column − 12×2 margin — bump this in lock-step with the column cap so the centred pill stays aligned) with `padding-bottom: max(calc(env(safe-area-inset-bottom,0px)-20px),6px)` ("au ras + compact" — was `-12px`/floor 12px; the floating pill now dips ~20px into the home-indicator safe area, leaving ~14px clearance so it stays just above the indicator bar, floored at 6px for env=0 devices). The pill is also thinner (padding `5px 4px`, radius 20) and the tabs shorter (minHeight 42, icon 17, label fs(9)). **The five `top: 0` banners now RESERVE their height, like the tasting banner always has.** The shell has carried `paddingTop: bannerH` for `CuratorTastingBanner` for a long time, with the reason written on it — *"Keeps the active view's TopBar icons tappable during a live tasting"* — and the five banners in `TOP_BANNER_ORDER` never got the same treatment. They are `position: fixed; top: 0` at z489-492 against the TopBar's `sticky` z20, so at the top of a page a banner covered it **outright**: measured at 390 px in a device harness, the export reminder is **110 px tall and hides all 65 px of the TopBar**, every one of its four buttons (search, trash, settings, +) with it. **The mechanism is deliberately the existing one, not a new one**: each banner root carries `data-top-banner`, a single `TopBannerHeightProbe` in `CuratorOverlays` measures whichever is mounted (`pickTopBanner` guarantees at most one) with a `ResizeObserver` keyed on `pickTopBanner`, and reports up exactly like `onHeight`. The height is MEASURED, never assumed — it varies with the text, the width, the safe-area inset and the user's font-scale setting. The shell **sums** `topBannerH + bannerH` rather than maxing them, because the two STACK: `CuratorTastingBanner` takes the measured height as a `topInset` and sits below whichever top banner is up, instead of painting over it at z2001. Same build **dropped that banner's stale `autoUpdateCountdown ? 44 : 0` term** — the countdown had turned from a ~15 px strip at `top: 0` into a centred `Modal`, so those 44 px had been holding space for something that no longer existed. **A test had been pinning that 44 px for twenty-two releases** and went red on the removal, which is the moment to check who is right rather than which is easier to change: `CuratorAutoUpdateBanner` demonstrably renders a `Modal` (maxWidth 380, own backdrop), so the test was locking obsolete behaviour. Its block in `TastingBanner.test.tsx` now records the reversal and asserts the opposite — that the countdown must NOT move the banner — so restoring the old term turns it red. **Validated on the INSTALLED iOS PWA before shipping** (a purpose-built harness reproducing the geometry; the user confirmed no layout jump and no scroll shift) — the rule this section states for every fixed-positioning change, honoured rather than quoted. Locked by `topBannerInset.test.tsx`, whose own first version read its explanatory COMMENTS as data and reported a phantom sixth banner: it blanks comments before every source assertion now, the same lesson doc:check's gate 15 recorded. **When you add a banner to `TOP_BANNER_ORDER`, give its root `data-top-banner`** — the test fails otherwise, because a banner the probe cannot see goes straight back to covering the TopBar.

**Any change to these values must be validated on the INSTALLED iOS PWA** — the safe-area clearance is exactly what headless can't reproduce. **A FIFTH failure mode, distinct from the four guardrails: the dock DRIFTS mid-screen while scrolling and settles at the bottom when the gesture ends.** Reported with a scrolling screenshot showing the pill halfway up the page, which reads exactly like the in-flow bug and is not it. **The triage is what separates them, and it is one question**: at REST, at the very bottom of a page, is the pill correctly ON TOP of the last content? If yes, `position: fixed` is resolving against the viewport and the four guardrails are irrelevant — verified here in a real render (dock is a direct child of `<body>`, `position: fixed`, `bottom: 0`, and ZERO containing-block-creating ancestors), plus no horizontal overflow at 360 px with twelve overdue pipes (`scrollWidth` 360 = `clientWidth` 360). What remains is the WebKit behaviour where a fixed element painted on the main thread lags behind compositor-driven scrolling. `transform: translateZ(0)` on the outer fixed strip promotes it to its own layer and fixes it — CONFIRMED on the installed PWA. **It does NOT contradict the rule above**: that rule is about an ANCESTOR gaining a containing-block property; this sits on the fixed element ITSELF, which cannot change its own containing block. **A page-height TRIGGER was proposed here and is now FALSIFIED — kept as a correction rather than deleted.** It read *"the trigger was page height, not a code defect"*, on the grounds that the Home's maintenance section had gone from five rows to every overdue pipe (2903 px at 360 px/"L" with twelve) and that this section already says the float appears "on scroll of a tall page". The drift came back on a build whose maintenance section is **capped at five again** — a SHORTER Home than the one that carried the original report — so page height is not what produces it. What survives from that paragraph is only the negative half, and it still holds: the commits blamed at the time touched no CSS and no positioning, and the dock itself is unchanged since the first public commit; do not go looking for a regression in them. **WHAT ACTUALLY CLEARED IT IS NOT SETTLED, and the first answer written here was WRONG — recorded rather than deleted, because the mistake is instructive.** The build carrying `translateZ(0)` was reported as STILL drifting, then as fixed « après avoir fermé complètement l'app ». It was written up as a delivery lesson — a PWA resumed from the app switcher does not reload, so it must have been running the previous build — and the user corrected it flatly: **they were already on the new build before closing.** So the property alone did not clear it; destroying and recreating the web view did. That leaves two readings this file cannot choose between: either the promotion is the fix and a long-lived WKWebView had to be recycled before it took hold, or the recycling alone is the fix and the property is inert. **They are distinguishable only by TIME — if the drift never returns across many launches, the first; if it comes back with no code change, the second** — so do not restate either as established. **The drift DID come back, and the record now favours the promotion.** The prediction assumed the property was IN PLACE and it was not — the wholesale revert to build 18 removed it as collateral. Tabulated: build 23 property PRESENT, drift reported then gone after a full quit; builds 24-30 property ABSENT, drift returned at 30; build 31 property PRESENT, no drift. Twice absent → drift, twice present → none, which is the first coherent correlation this bug has produced. **It is still not proof, and the confound is nameable**: both clean observations had the property AND a freshly recreated web view. Exactly one situation separates them — an IN-PLACE update, where `doUpdate` calls `location.reload()` and WebKit keeps the same web view, unlike a full quit which destroys it; if the drift stays away through a session updated in place, the property is doing the work. **A third explanation was proposed and FALSIFIED in between, recorded so nobody proposes it a fourth time**: that closing the app never fixes anything and merely DELIVERS a newer build, HTML being network-first while a resumed PWA does not reload. It fits the 23 and 30 reports and cannot explain a drift present from the first scroll of a session, which is what was reported. Retired. The plausible mechanism for the second is documented one entry over, at `main.jsx`: mutating `document.documentElement` in the installed PWA recomputes the fixed-position layer and floats the dock, and a reload (which `doUpdate` performs) keeps the same web view while a full quit does not. **The lesson that DOES survive: an explanation that fits the facts is not the same as the one that produced them, and 'the user must have been on the old build' is the shape of guess to distrust — it explains a report by assuming the reporter was mistaken.** The one risk it shipped with is CLEARED: the pill's `backdrop-filter` still blurs under the transformed ancestor (checked on the installed PWA), so WebKit does not treat this transform as a backdrop root and a compositing promotion on an outer strip is compatible with a backdrop-filter inside it — worth knowing before reaching for the same trick elsewhere. **Why window-scroll and NOT an app-shell (hard-won):** an earlier attempt tried a locked-body inner-scroll "app-shell" (`html,body{overflow:hidden}` + `position:fixed` shell + inner `overflow-y:auto` container) to stop a reported floating-dock bug. It DID stop the float, BUT a locked body under `viewport-fit=cover` shrinks the iOS *visual viewport* to the safe-area box, so the shell + dock stopped ~0.5cm above the physical bottom (a background strip showed below the app), and no `bottom:calc(-1*env(...))` overhang reliably pushed them back to the true edge on the device. The layout was **reverted to window-scroll**, which the user confirmed reaches the true physical bottom AND does not float in the installed PWA (the original day-of-changes float turned out to be unrelated to the scroll model — it was gone once the layout returned to the pre-refactor shape). Keep it window-scroll: no body `overflow:hidden`, no `position:fixed` shell, no inner-scroll container, no `src/utils/scroller.ts` singleton (removed — scroll snapshots read `window.scrollY` / `window.scrollTo` again). **CRITICAL: neither Chromium (headless or not) nor Safari-browser reproduces the iOS-standalone `position:fixed` / safe-area / body-lock behaviour — the ONLY trustworthy test for any bottom-dock / fixed-positioning / `100vh|100dvh` / `overflow:hidden`-on-body / safe-area change is the INSTALLED iOS PWA (Add-to-Home-Screen), on a page taller than the viewport so it actually scrolls.** Don't ship such a change on a headless "looks fine" alone. (The confirmed-good window-scroll layout is also tagged at the git "test" release = commit a2423fc, an instant fallback.)
- **Routing:** views route on a `view` string state. No URL change. View keys: `home`, `inv`, `pipes`, `addT`, `editT`, `addP`, `editP`, `addA`, `editA`, `addJ`, `editJ`, `journal`, `acc`, `stats`, `tasting`. The `WishFormView` is gated by `showWishForm || editWishId` (not by view).
- **Design tokens:** `src/theme-curator.ts` exports `C` (palette: brass / oxblood / sage / amber / ember / ivory / cream), `F` (Newsreader display, DM Sans body, IBM Plex Mono mono), `DOCK_ACCENT` per section, `CURATOR_CHART_COLORS`, `catColor(cat)` (which reads `CAT_COLORS` from `constants.ts` — the themed `CURATOR_CAT_COLORS` was deleted). **Fonts are self-hosted** under `public/fonts/` (see Font hosting section below); `index.html` declares `@font-face` inline against `%BASE_URL%fonts/*.woff2`. CSP enforces `font-src 'self'` only — `fonts.googleapis.com` / `fonts.gstatic.com` are no longer whitelisted.
- **Page gutter = 12px (unified at 16, then moved to 12).** Every full-page content block shares ONE horizontal gutter of **12px**: `TopBar`, `PageTitle`, `SectionHead`, the `ZoneHead`/masthead rows, every list sub-title / filter / card-list wrapper, and every detail-view section + hero wrapper. Four coexisting values (14 / 16 / 18 / 22px) were unified down to 16; **the whole gutter then moved 16 → 12 so the tiles align edge-to-edge with the bottom dock pill** (the pill sits at `margin: 0 12px`, maxWidth 736 = 760 column − 12×2 — the user saw the dock wider than the cards above it). The alignment holds at every width: tiles cap at 760 − 12×2 = 736 = the pill cap. **Keep new full-page wrappers at `0 12px …` / `12px` horizontal, in lock-step with the dock pill margin** — if one ever moves, move the other. The exceptions that intentionally keep **18px** are the MODALS (`SettingsModal`, `TrashModal`, `EncryptionPromptModal`, the Session/Tasting confirm modals) — they're narrower, so 18px reads right there. Card/chip/button INTERNAL padding (e.g. `12px 14px`, `14px 18px`) is not a page gutter and is out of scope.
- **Primitives:** `src/components/curator/primitives.tsx` — animation hooks (`useEnter`, `useWAAPILoop`, `Stagger`), entry components (`FadeIn`, `AnimNum`), Stars, IconBtn, PressCard (state-driven scale), TopBar, PageTitle, SectionHead, StatCard, GrowBarH/V, ScreenWash, EmptyState. **No `@keyframes`, no CSS file, no `className`** — all motion is state-driven CSS transitions or WAAPI.
- **Form primitives:** `src/components/curator/FormFields.tsx` — `FormScreen` (full-screen layout with brass top hair + sticky top bar + body), `FormSection` (italic-serif section title + accent bar), `TextField`, `TextAreaField`, `SelectField` (optional `groups?: SelectGroup[]` renders `<optgroup>` headers — labels resolve via `t()`. Grouped selects: pipe form Forme by `SHAPE_FAMILIES` — **Its sixth group is keyed `length`, not `long`.** It shipped as « Longues (lecture) » holding Churchwarden AND Nose Warmer, and a Nose Warmer (fr *brûle-gueule*, lit. "face burner") is the SHORTEST pipe there is — the bowl sits under your nose — so it was filed under the opposite of what it is, in a group glossed "for reading", which is a churchwarden's use and not its own. Reported by the user, who smokes them. **The grouping itself is right and the sources say why**: both shapes are defined by LENGTH ALONE and not by bowl form (smokingpipes: *"the only requirement for a pipe to be considered a Churchwarden is its length"*; *"a Nosewarmer is virtually any pipe short enough to almost warm the nose … can manifest almost any shape"*), which is exactly why they belong together and why the group must name the AXIS rather than one end of it. Now « Tuyau long ou court » / « Long & short stems », with the stem word each dictionary already uses elsewhere (tuyau / stem / boquilla / Mundstück / bocchino / boquilha) and the right agreement in each. The guide repeats these group labels in all six blocks and moved with it — nothing checks THAT (gate 23 reads enum values, not group labels), so keep them in step by hand. Two neighbours were checked and deliberately NOT moved: `Duke` sits in `billiard` because the trade describes it as confusable with the Poker and the Cherrywood, both already there; `Tavern` stays in `regional` as an 18th-century English pub style, though it was historically a long clay — a judgement worth a second opinion, not a defect. Renaming the key is safe because `dynamicGroupLabels.test.ts` resolves `"shape_family_" + key` against every dictionary; probed, and it names the missing key and the language. Tobacco/wishlist Catégorie is grouped by `CAT_FAMILIES`, pipe Foyer/Tuyau by `BOWL_MAT_FAMILIES`/`STEM_MAT_FAMILIES`, and the PipesListView shape filter by `SHAPE_FAMILIES`. Each `*_FAMILIES` const in constants.ts partitions its enum exactly — carries a `labelKey` (`t()`) per group + a shared `fam_other` for the trailing Autre — and is locked by constants.test.ts), `StarsField`, `SegmentedField<T>`, `PhotoField`. **Never wrap the root `FormScreen` div in `overflow: hidden`** — it clips content past 100vh and creates a black-screen bug. Same warning applies to every root view div (`HomeView`, `InventoryListView`, etc.) — keep them scroll-natural.
- **CheckboxField primitive:** `src/components/curator/FormFields.tsx` — a single on/off choice with an explanatory hint, added for the per-fiche catalogue lock. The forms had no checkbox until then: every boolean was a `SegmentedField` (two labelled options) or a tri-state on a fiche. A Segmented works, but it makes the user read two labels to learn a choice exists, where a checkbox states the one thing that can be true and shows whether it is. **a11y is not optional here and repeats two lessons this file already records:** `role="checkbox"` + `aria-checked` on a real `<button>` (state ANNOUNCED, not conveyed by colour — the `FilterChipSimple` fix and the Settings-toggle fix), the hint wired with `aria-describedby` rather than left as a sibling `<div>` that associates with nothing (exactly what made all six Settings toggles anonymous), and `minHeight: 44` — the house target, stricter than WCAG 2.2's 24. Being a `<button>`, Enter AND Space activate it for free.
- **Notice primitive:** `src/components/curator/Notice.tsx` — shared tinted info-banner shell used by every inline notice in the app (aging warning, cellar advisories, duplicate alerts, AI errors, orphan-lot warning, trash summary…). Locked to a 4-tier tone system: `info` (brass), `success` (sage), `warn` (amber), `error` (oxbloodHi). Out of scope: the fixed-top alert banners in `Overlays.tsx` (full-bleed positioning, different visual style). Also exports `statusToneFromMessage()` for free-form status strings (`gdriveStatus`, `backupStatus`).
- **MaturityChip primitive (absorbed AgingBadge):** `src/components/curator/MaturityChip.tsx` — THE maturity/aging badge. Four bands, three sizes: `sm` (LotRow, bordered), `md` (tobacco card), `lg` (LotFormModal banner — body font, sentence case). Colour + label + ⚠ table locked here. Callers holding a `lotAgingStatus` verdict convert via `bucketFromAgingStatus(status)` rather than re-deriving a second vocabulary — that duplication is exactly what the absorption removed.
- **ModalAction primitive:** `src/components/curator/ModalAction.tsx` — uniform action button for modal action rows. Three variants: `primary` (brass gradient + shadow, default), `secondary` (transparent + rule border), `danger` (oxbloodHi background, destructive). Pairs with `Modal.tsx` — do NOT use this in form bottom-bars (FormScreen owns its own layout). **Two silent a11y defects were fixed here**, both found by asking which other sites shared AICard's disabled-button gap: (1) `ariaLabel` was forwarded to `PressCard` as **`aria-label`** while `PressCard`'s prop is `ariaLabel`, so the documented prop was accepted by the compiler and then dropped — **TypeScript cannot catch this**, because it deliberately skips excess-property checking on HYPHENATED JSX attribute names (they can't be TS identifiers). Latent (no caller passed it yet), but the next icon-only modal action would have shipped with no accessible name. (2) `disabled` styled the button unavailable without announcing it. Both are locked by `ModalAction.test.tsx` (probed: each fails on the old code). **When you forward an ARIA prop to a curator primitive, check the primitive's prop NAME** — a hyphenated attribute typo is invisible to `npm run typecheck`.
- **StatTile primitive:** `src/components/curator/primitives.tsx` — compact key/value tile (small label above, big value below, optional `customValue` slot for a Stars render). Used in InventoryDetailView lot recap and JournalView session detail.
- **SpecRow primitive:** `src/components/curator/primitives.tsx` — label/value row separated by a dotted bottom rule. Used in PipesDetailView and AccessoryDetailView specs sections. Pass `last` to suppress the bottom rule on the final row. **Optional `href`** — when set (with a value), the value renders as a brass external link (`target=_blank rel=noopener`). Callers pass an ALREADY-sanitised href via `safeSellerHref(url)` (utils.ts) — normalises a user-typed seller/site URL (prepends `https://`, rejects non-http(s) schemes like `javascript:`/`data:`/`ftp:`), returns `""` when not linkable. Drives the new **`sellerUrl`** field (optional on Lot/Pipe/Accessory — BL/BP/BA templates, forms LotFormModal/PipeFormView/AccessoryFormView, shown as a link in InventoryDetailView lot modal + PipesDetailView + AccessoryDetailView; rides along in JSON/Drive/ZIP backups).
- **FilterControls primitives:** `src/components/curator/FilterControls.tsx` — three list-view controls extracted from per-view duplicates: `ToggleBtn` (44×44 icon-only button with on/off state and per-section accent), `ActiveFilterPill` (rounded chip showing an active filter + clear ×), `FilterChipSimple` (2-state on/off chip with text label). **The tag/collection chip rows fold away on all three lists**: the tobacco inventory keeps them inside the "Plus de filtres" disclosure, while the pipes + accessories lists gate theirs on a local `pAdvFiltersOpen`/`aAdvFiltersOpen` behind a **`ToggleBtn` placed IN the existing controls row** (next to group-by / expand-cards) — reported from the app as "ça prend trop de place". The icon placement is the point: a labelled "Plus de filtres" button of its own was built first and REVERTED, because it cost a row to hide a row and saved nothing (the shared `MoreFiltersToggle` extracted for it was reverted too — one caller is not an abstraction). **The unification was finished**: the TOBACCO list's labelled button — the last one on its own row, on the busiest page — became the same icon in ITS controls row, so all three lists now share one affordance, one place and one icon (`filter`, a funnel; the `hash` was replaced because the tobacco fold also holds the type / cut / rating dropdowns, so `#` would have promised tags only). The `on` state carries what the labelled button showed as a dot: it stays lit while a hidden filter is applied, so a narrowed list can never look unfiltered. **The wishlist has its OWN controls row**, so the disclosure had to be added there too — the tests caught that putting it only in the tobacco row made the type / cut dropdowns unreachable in wish mode. The disclosure is hidden entirely when nothing is tagged, its `on` state includes `!!tagFilter`, and the active-filter PILL stays outside the fold so a narrowed list can never look unfiltered. The fiches keep their tag chips visible: there is no existing row to host an icon there, so a disclosure would cost exactly the row it hides. Locked by the « tag chips behind the # disclosure » blocks in `PipesListView.test.tsx` + `AccListView.test.tsx`. Each accepts an `accent` prop (and `accentBase` for the 22-alpha background tint when it differs from `accent`). The richer FilterChip in InventoryListView (count badge + focus ring + arrow-key navigation between siblings) stays local to that view — its behaviour is too specific to promote without prop-bloat.
- **SettingsButton primitive:** `src/views/curator/SettingsModal.tsx` — uniform clickable row used in every Settings list. Mirrors `IconBtn` ergonomics (≥ 44px touch target) but adds the chevron + label + optional trailing badge expected in a settings list.
- **Spinner primitive:** `src/components/curator/primitives.tsx` — small WAAPI-driven rotating ring (12px / 2px default, configurable via `size` and `thickness`) used as an inline busy indicator next to button labels whose action runs async. Defaults to `currentColor` so it inherits the host button's text colour. **Implementation uses `useWAAPILoop` — NEVER replace with a CSS `@keyframes spin` rule.** The design system bans `@keyframes`; the next reviewer will revert it. First consumers: the `Restaurer` button on the Home and Overlays cloud-newer-backup banner (see `cloudRestoreBusy` in useGdriveSync).
- **EmptyState primitive + the empty-state rule:** `src/components/curator/primitives.tsx` — icon + sentence + an optional `actions` row. **An audit of all 25 empty states found exactly ONE that offered an action** (the journal's filter reset); everywhere else the app told the user there was nothing and stopped. The costly half is the three list views (Inventory — including its wishlist mode — Pipes, Accessories), which computed emptiness from the **FILTERED** array, so a user with 200 tobaccos and a forgotten chip saw the identical « Aucun tabac » as a first-run user: no hint that a filter was on, and no way back. Each now distinguishes the two cases — no-match offers `btn_reset_filters`, genuinely-empty offers the add (`btn_add_tobacco` / `btn_add_wish` / `btn_add_pipe` / `btn_add_accessory`), because the "+" is an unlabelled top-bar icon at the opposite end of the screen from the sentence saying the list is empty. **The no-match predicates EXCLUDE what does not NARROW, and that is the load-bearing part**: the tobacco STATUS chip always carries a value (`"active"`), so counting it would call every first-run screen "filtered" and offer a reset that changes nothing; `showFinishedPipes` and `showRetiredAcc` **WIDEN or SWITCH** the set rather than narrow it, so resetting them would REMOVE rows the user had just asked to see. All three exclusions are asserted by tests. Two inert imperatives got the door they name: `aroma_profile_empty` in `StatsView` → `navToJournalFiltered("")` — **NOT a bare `nav`**, so system-back returns to Stats, which is the defect fixed everywhere else — and `tasting_no_usable_tob` in `TastingView` → `nav("inv")`. **`TastingView`'s `!tasting` branch was the harshest dead end in the app**: one centred sentence, no top bar, the dock hidden by `NO_DOCK_VIEWS`, nothing to tap — the only way out was a system-back gesture, which is not an affordance. It now offers starting a tasting (seeded IDENTICALLY to `HomeViewV2`'s CTA, so the two entry points cannot drift) and going home. **NOT fixed, deliberately: `lot_no_weight_hint`** reads like a third inert imperative and is not one — it sits directly above the lot list, every row there is tappable, and an "Ajouter un lot" button closes that same list, so the path it names is already under the user's thumb; a CTA would duplicate a control 40 px away. The component was hoisted from **FOUR copies** (a local `EmptyState` in `InventoryListView` plus verbatim inlinings in `PipesListView`, `AccListView` and `JournalView`) — the same lift as `StatTile` / `SpecRow`, for the same reason: every inline copy drifts. Its `actions` row **wraps**, because two uppercase mono buttons do not fit one line at 360 px in German and that row is the last thing on an otherwise empty screen. **A pre-existing test asserted « Aucune envie » for a wishlist of TWO items filtered to zero — its own name said "when filters narrow to zero", so it was pinning the defect**; the reversal is recorded on the assertion. New keys in all six languages: `list_no_match`, `btn_add_tobacco`, `btn_add_accessory`, `btn_add_wish`, `btn_back_home`, `btn_see_journal`, `btn_see_tobaccos`. **That change introduced TWO defects of the very class it was written to remove, and both were found by an agent rather than by a check.** (a) **The journal's CTA opened a form that could not be saved.** It did a bare `nav("addJ")`, which lands on `BJ`, whose `date` is `""` — and `SessionFormView`'s `canSave` requires a date, so the only control on that screen produced a permanently greyed Save button with nothing on screen saying why, for the only audience an empty journal has. The `+` button two hundred lines up had seeded date/time/weight and says so in its own comment. **That is the drift `emptyStateWayForward.test.tsx` was written to prevent for the tasting CTA in the SAME build** — the rule applied one component over and missed here, which is the argument for the shared `openNewSession` rather than a second correct copy. (b) **The retired shelf was read as a first run.** `showFinishedPipes` / `showRetiredAcc` are BINARY (« retired ONLY », not « also retired »), and excluding them from the no-match predicate — correct for the RESET, as the paragraph above states — also selects the LABEL and the ACTION, and both are then wrong: own twelve active pipes and none retired, tap « Retirées », and the screen said « Aucune pipe » (false) and offered an add that creates an **ACTIVE** pipe, invisible in the view being looked at. On accessories the sub-header two rows above already read « 0 retirés » while the body said « Aucun accessoire ». A THIRD state now says « Aucune pipe retirée » and its way forward is the « Actives » chip, not a form (`no_retired_pipes` / `btn_see_active_pipes` / `no_retired_acc` / `btn_see_active_acc`). **The test that pinned this could not see it** — its fixture has zero pipes TOTAL, so « no pipes » was true there; it was WEAKENED to assert only the part that was ever about the toggle (no reset offered), with the reversal recorded on it. **The general lesson: excluding an input from a predicate is a decision about the RESET, and it must be re-taken separately for the sentence and for the button.**
- **SettingsTabs:** the Settings modal is split into 4 tabs — `data` (Drive + Export/Import + AI), `prefs` (units, language, sections), `app` (install + update + diagnostic), `help` (links). State is lifted to `App.tsx` (`settingsTab` / `setSettingsTab`) so external callers (`CuratorUpdatePill` → `app`, `CuratorExportReminderBanner` / `CuratorSaveErrorBanner` / `CuratorSaveWarnBanner` → `data`) can pre-position the user via `ctx.setSettingsTab(...)` BEFORE opening the modal. Persisted in `localStorage["cave-settings-tab"]`. **The tab BAR order is `prefs` → `data` → `app` → `help` (Préférences → Données → Application → Aide)** — Préférences was moved ahead of Données. **The fresh-open default tab is now `prefs`** (was `data`); external callers still pre-position via `ctx.setSettingsTab(...)` (`data` for the save/export banners, `app` for the update pill).
- **Lightbox ghost-click defense:** `src/views/curator/LightboxOverlay.tsx` uses a `closingRef` ref-based lock (NOT state — React batching can let a second close call through before the state has propagated) plus a deferred `setLightbox(null)` 260ms after the fade-out. Without this, the ~150ms ghost-click iOS/Android emit on long-press → tap landed on the trash icon underneath the lightbox X button, silently deleting the underlying object. The lightbox tests use `vi.useFakeTimers()` + `vi.advanceTimersByTime(300)` to assert the deferred close. Do not collapse the deferral to a synchronous `setLightbox(null)` — the regression test will pass even though the bug returns.
- **Modal ghost-click defense:** `src/components/curator/Modal.tsx` carries an internal `shouldRender` state. When `open` flips false the modal flips `mounted` to false instantly (so the opacity + transform transition plays) but defers the actual unmount by ~320 ms via `setTimeout`. Same mechanism as the lightbox but generalized to every `Modal` (Settings, Search, LotForm, GdriveConfirm, Encryption prompt…). The motivating case was closing Settings via its X — the synthetic ~150-300 ms click landed on HomeView's search icon directly underneath and opened the search modal. The `useDeferredFalse(value, delay)` hook in `CuratorApp.tsx` extends the same defence to the lazy-loaded `SettingsModal` and `TrashModal` mount gates (`importModal`, `trashOpen`) so the lazy chunk stays mounted during the defer window. If you add a new modal that opens from a tappable surface that overlaps another tappable surface, follow this pattern.
- **Curator-specific ESLint config:** `eslint.config.js` has a `src/(views|components|hooks|__tests__|CuratorApp.tsx|theme-curator.ts)/curator/**` block that disables `no-unused-vars`, `no-unused-expressions`, `react-hooks/rules-of-hooks`, `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect`, `prefer-const`, `no-empty` for the vendored bundle.
- **Hook-order trap:** Curator views must call **all hooks before any early return**. Any `if (view !== "...") return null;` must come AFTER every `useMemo`/`useEffect`/`useEnter` in the component. Putting the early return first triggers "Rendered more hooks than during the previous render" when the view becomes active.
- **Prefill-race trap (invariant):** a `useEffect` that writes to a user-editable text field via `setForm` / `setTasting…` / `tastingSetupUpdate` / equivalent **MUST NOT list that same field in its dependency array**. The legitimate triggers for an on-mount prefill are screen-entry signals (`view`, `tasting?.stage`, `open`) and global toggles (`accountingEnabled`, language), never the value the effect writes back. Listing `form?.weightG` (or any other text input) makes the effect re-run on every keystroke: clearing the field to type a new value (backspace → `""`) re-fires the effect, which sees an empty value and immediately re-fills with the default, racing against the user's next keystroke and silently snapping the input back. The user-facing symptom is "I can't change this field". When you need a guarded reset of a value (e.g. clearing a stale filter whose target option disappeared, like `JournalView.tsx:118-122` or `PipesListView.tsx:61-65`), that's safe **only** because the reset is gated on the value being missing from a derived list — the steady-state branch is a no-op, so user input doesn't trigger the setter. Audit any new `useEffect` whose body writes to `form.X` / `tasting.X` against the rule: the field must come out of the dep array, or the effect must be guarded so it's a strict no-op in normal user flow.
- **Welcome popup:** `src/views/curator/WelcomeModal.tsx` — shown once per user (gated by `localStorage["cave-curator-welcomed"]`). Mounted inside `CuratorApp` so it only appears after the terms gate. Briefly introduces the app and reminds the user about local-first storage + optional Drive backup. Single "C'est noté" / "Got it" dismiss button.

## Custom Hooks

All business logic extracted from `App.tsx` lives in `src/hooks/`. Each hook receives a minimal dependency object and returns state + actions, destructured at the top of `App.tsx`.

| Hook | State | Actions |
|------|-------|---------|
| `useAppUpdate` | `updateStatus`, `updateAvailable`, `newerBuild`, `silentUpdatePending`, `justUpdated`, `updatePillDismissed`, `autoUpdateCountdown` | `checkUpdate()`, `doUpdate()`, `cancelAutoUpdate()` — accepts `{ deferAutoUpdate?: boolean }` to suspend the 10s countdown (e.g. during a live tasting). **Silent data-only releases.** When `version.json` carries `"data_only": true` (strictly `=== true`) AND the build differs, the hook skips the visible countdown banner entirely and sets `silentUpdatePending` instead. A separate effect schedules `doUpdate()` at the next `visibilitychange:hidden` OR `pagehide` event (iOS Safari standalone teardown via app-switcher), with a 30 min fallback timer. `deferAutoUpdate` still wins (live tasting blocks both visible and silent paths). The user returns to a fresh catalog with no UI interruption. `npm run release:data` (`scripts/data-only-release.cjs`) bumps APP_BUILD and writes the version.json marker — `generation` included — in one shot. **KEEP IT CALLED**: nothing invoked it for a long stretch, and in that time `generation` became a required field and this writer was never taught to emit it, so it produced a file the gate rejects and nobody found out. | **THE UPDATE PATH HAS NO SILENT DEAD ENDS.** Three of them shipped together and each one looks like a perfectly healthy app from the outside, which is why they survived. **(a) Detection was hostage to the service worker**: every line of `checkVersion` lived inside `navigator.serviceWorker.ready.then(...)`, though reading `version.json` needs no SW. No SW support, a failed registration (Safari private mode, blocked storage, one transient network error on main.jsx's single `register` call) or a `ready` that never settles — it does NOT reject when nothing is registered, so no `.catch` helps — meant the app never checked for an update again, for ever. Self-inflicted, too: `doUpdate()` unregisters every SW before reloading. Detection now runs unconditionally; the `updatefound` listener is a bonus attached if and when a registration is ready. **(b) Every gate blocked the INFORMATION as well as the ACTION.** `newerBuild` is now recorded on every detection, before and independent of the anti-loop latch, the `data_only` branch and the fail-closed `lsSet`; Settings → Application renders it (it keyed on `updateAvailable`, which the silent path never sets — so a catalogue release was invisible on every screen, and so was a build the latch had stood down on). Suppression may stop us auto-reloading; it must never stop us saying so. **(c) Silent is best-effort, never a backlog**: `fireSilent` legitimately declines when offline or when the tab is never backgrounded, so after `SILENT_FALLBACK_MS` an unapplied silent update is PROMOTED to the ordinary visible banner. A catalogue refresh the user is asked about is a small annoyance; one that never arrives is a broken app. **Why the app sometimes "updates by itself" when you tap something, and it is not the updater.** Reported: *« j'ai cliqué sur la bannière, ça ne m'a pas amené sur le menu, ça a déclenché la mise à jour »*. The pill is innocent — it calls `setImportModal(true)`, and `CuratorSettingsModal` is a **`React.lazy` content-hashed chunk**. The instant a new build is deployed the OLD `SettingsModal-<hash>.js` stops existing on the server, so the first tap on Settings (or Stats / Trash / Help / a doc page — the five lazy surfaces) by a client still on the previous build gets a 404, `React.lazy` rejects, `EB.isChunkLoadError` matches, and `purgeCachesAndReload()` reloads onto the new build. **This is a de facto second update path**, it fires on the user's first tap after any deploy, and it explains a whole class of "it updated at a random moment" reports. Nothing is broken and no data is at risk — but the app called it **« Récupération en cours… »**, the vocabulary of a fault, for what is normally a successful update. Now « Passage à la dernière version… », which is true in BOTH cases: after the purge you are on the current build, whether the cause was a deploy or a genuinely stale cache. The EB tests selected on the old word, so they were updated to the new one — note they select on the string, which is the weak point: if this screen is reworded again they will need touching, and there is no role/testid to key on. **The second instance of the same class, and the likelier cause: `deferAutoUpdate` must describe what is ON SCREEN.** `lotForm` and `maintFormOpen` are modals rendered INSIDE a detail view that returns `null` the moment you leave it (`InventoryDetailView` on `view !== "inv" || !detail`; `PipesDetailView` likewise), and NOTHING clears their state on navigation — the invariant forbids `nav()` from resetting form state, correctly. So **tapping a lot and then tapping the dock left `lotForm` armed for ever**: the modal vanished from the screen while the update stayed blocked, invisibly, with no way to see or clear it. An entirely ordinary sequence, and a likelier explanation than the setup-tasting for a device that never auto-updates. Both clauses are now gated on their host fiche being open. That instance was fixed by making the state VISIBLE; here the state is genuinely gone from the screen, so it must stop BLOCKING — **the rule that covers both: this predicate describes what is on screen, and any state that changes how the app behaves must be visible somewhere.** `showWishForm || editWishId` needs no guard because `WishFormView`'s own render gate IS that expression, so state and visibility cannot diverge — asserted, so a refactor that moves it inside a view has to revisit this. `deferReason` was also made to name the EXACT source (`tasting` / `maint` / `wish` / `lot` / `form`) rather than a category: after several rounds of guessing which clause was stuck on a user's device, the honest move was to make the app say it instead of advancing a sixth hypothesis. **The state that was blocking every update was INVISIBLE, and the diagnostic is what found it.** A screenshot showed Settings saying *« En attente : une saisie est en cours »* while the user was on the Home screen with nothing open. Cause: `deferAutoUpdate` blocks on a tasting in the **`setup`** stage (correctly — a silent reload while the user is picking a tobacco was a real bug), but nothing anywhere SHOWED such a tasting: `TastingBanner` returns null unless `stage === "running"`, and `HomeViewV2`'s CTA read `tasting.stage === "running"` so it offered « Démarrer une dégustation ». A tasting abandoned at the tobacco-picking step therefore persisted in `cave-tasting-active` across relaunches and **blocked every automatic update indefinitely, with no sign anywhere** — the explanation for every "it never starts by itself" report in this series. **Two fixes: the Home CTA now treats a `setup` tasting as resumable** (same predicate `deferAutoUpdate` blocks on — `deferAutoUpdate.test.ts` asserts they cannot diverge, since divergence *is* the bug), which also gives the way out because the tasting view can cancel it; **and Settings now names WHICH surface is holding the update** (`deferReason` from App, `upd_why_deferred_tasting` / `upd_why_deferred_form` replacing the vague `upd_why_deferred`, which said « formulaire ou dégustation » and left the user to work out which). **The general rule this earns: any state that changes how the app behaves must be visible somewhere, and a diagnostic that names two possibilities is half a diagnostic.** **A three-lens audit of the whole update path, and most of what it found was MINE.** Nine fixes; the ones worth knowing: **(a) HIGH, from the previous fix: being offline was the TRIGGER for a cache-destroying purge.** `fireSilent` declines when `navigator.onLine === false` *without* latching `fired`, and that fallback read `if (!fired) setUpdateAvailable(...)` — so `!fired` was not "it never applied", it was literally "we are offline". The promotion therefore fired only offline, into a visible path with no offline guard: 10 s later every SW unregistered and every Cache Storage entry deleted, with no network to refill them. **The promotion is REMOVED, not guarded** — when online `fireSilent` simply applies the update, so the branch was unreachable; harmful in one case, dead code in the other. 105's premise was also wrong: `newerBuild` already makes a pending silent update visible, so there was no invisible backlog to rescue. **My own test blessed it** — it stubbed `onLine:false`, asserted the promotion, and stopped. `doUpdate` now refuses offline at the single choke point all four paths funnel through, and `EB.purgeCachesAndReload` got the same guard (offline, an unvisited lazy chunk fails as a module-load error, so tapping Stats on a plane destroyed the installed app; it now falls through to the manual screen and `getDerivedStateFromError` no longer claims to be "recovering"). **(b) One "Plus tard" disabled the countdown for the WHOLE SESSION**, newer builds included: the effect dep was `!!updateAvailable`, a boolean, so `A → B` never re-ran it — `checkVersion` cleared the decline latch for B exactly as its comment promised and nothing acted on it, while `explainPendingUpdate` returned `idle` so Settings printed no reason either. Dep is now the BUILD. Also: "Plus tard" now disarms the SILENT path (it never consulted the latch, so backgrounding applied the build you had just declined), and the build is `String()`-ed at both setters (a numeric `version.json` build could never match its own latch → cleared on the next poll → the regression, latent). **(c) `pagehide` was listened for on `document`; it is fired at the WINDOW**, so the iOS app-switcher hook had been inert for six releases — both tests dispatched at `document` (one at both), so neither could discriminate. **(d) The `⛔ Sauvegardez avant de continuer !` panel claimed « Vos données peuvent être perdues » — FALSE**, and `UpdateWarnPanel` is deleted: `doUpdate` touches only service workers and Cache Storage, never `localStorage` (the whole cellar) nor IndexedDB (photos), and `reset.html` runs the identical purge under help text that says « ne supprime pas vos données ». It was also MANDATORY on the manual route while the countdown, "update now" and the silent path all reload with no warning — the app alarmed the user only when they deliberately asked. `upd_warning` now says what it means for them (« L'application va se retélécharger. Votre cave n'est pas touchée. »). **(e) The Settings update notice was `tone="warn"`, which is amber + the alert diamond + `role="alert"`** — the same assertive ARIA class as a save failure, for routine news, sitting beside the stale-check notice that IS a warning. Now `tone="info"`. **(f) Three regressions from my own 108/109**: the pill (z 490) painted OVER its own dialog (z 200), outside the focus trap and still tappable through the scrim — it now stands down while the countdown runs; a stray backdrop tap called `cancelAutoUpdate` and made the DURABLE decline decision silently — `dismissCountdown` now ends the occurrence only; and the dialog had 2 px of horizontal padding because `Modal` defaults `padding` to 0 (every sibling insets 18-26). **(g) The pill's CTA was a `<span onClick>`** — no role, no tabIndex, no key handler — so a keyboard or screen-reader user could DISMISS an update but never ACT on one; a real `<button>` now. **Probed with eight sabotages, each red.** The pattern across all of it: five of the nine were introduced by the immediately preceding releases, i.e. by the fixes for the previous report — **speed of iteration on a safety-critical hook is itself a risk**, and the audit is what caught it. **The countdown is a DIALOG now, not a hairline.** Reported from the app right after 108: "it is mainly the banner that is not explicit; there should be a countdown and a bigger pop-up." `CuratorAutoUpdateBanner` was a ~15 px full-width strip pinned to `top: 0`, alive for ten seconds — on an installed iOS PWA it lands under the status bar, directly above the app's own brass masthead, **in the same brass gradient**, so the one moment the app announces it is about to RELOAD ITSELF was the easiest thing on screen to miss. It is now a centred `Modal`: the title, the pending `v · build`, the remaining seconds at `fs(52)` (the countdown is the point of the dialog, so it is the biggest thing in it), a sentence saying the app will restart, and TWO actions — **"Mettre à jour maintenant"** (`upd_do_now`, new: the strip could only decline or wait, which is a strange thing to offer for something the user may well want now) and "Plus tard". Using the shared `Modal` buys `role="dialog"`, the focus trap, Escape and the modal stack, so **system-back and the edge-swipe mean "Plus tard"** instead of doing nothing. The prominence is warranted rather than merely nicer because a reload makes the app vanish and return; `deferAutoUpdate` already guarantees it can never fire over unsaved input, so the dialog is never a trap — it just has to be SEEN. The export keeps its `…Banner` name (three call sites, one of them the mount). **The 'Later' case in `Overlays.test.tsx` failed on this change for the right reason**: it selected `container.querySelector("button")` — the FIRST button — and silently retargeted to the new primary action; it now selects by accessible name, the same lesson the trash rows recorded. **The pill said the opposite of what it meant, and nothing could explain a stalled update.** Reported from the app with a screenshot: "when an update is available I get that, and that is all. Not explicit. And it does not start after 10 seconds like you say." Both halves were fair. (a) `CuratorUpdatePill` rendered a **checkmark glyph plus the minor version** — `✓ v1.5` — and nothing else: a checkmark beside a version number reads as *you are up to date*, the exact opposite of the message, and the minor is normally the one already running (the BUILD is what changed). It now shows the circular-refresh glyph and `upd_do` ("Mettre à jour") with the pending build — words that were already in the dictionary and that this component had never used. (b) It was keyed on `updateAvailable`, which is only set on the path that intends to count down, so **the pill vanished in exactly the states where a manual route matters most**: deferred behind an open form, stood down by the anti-loop latch, or waiting on the silent path. Keyed on `newerBuild` now (the ungated record). (c) The deeper problem: **four different brakes can hold a detected update and none of them said which** — neither to the user nor to me, which is why "it is available and nothing happens" was not diagnosable from a screenshot. The pure `explainPendingUpdate()` returns one of `counting` / `deferred` / `declined` / `suppressed` / `silent` / `idle`, exposed as `pendingReason` and rendered under the Settings notice (`upd_why_*`, dynamic keys — prefix registered in the doc-check allowlist). `counting` and `idle` deliberately render nothing: one is visibly counting down, the other is about to. Same rule as the two fixes above, one level further out — **the mechanism may refuse to act, but it must say which brake is engaged.** **The chain is covered end to end by `updateChain.e2e.test.ts`** (test-only): `version.json` → banner → countdown → `doUpdate` → SKIP_WAITING → unregister → cache purge → reload, plus the silent `pagehide` path and the three brakes (Plus tard / `deferAutoUpdate` / anti-loop cap). **Its load-bearing assertion is ORDER, not occurrence** — reload must come AFTER the purge resolves, or the browser re-serves the build being replaced from the cache it was about to drop and the app returns on the SAME build having reported success (the v1.1-iOS-PWA symptom). It also asserts `indexedDB.deleteDatabase` is NEVER called: the purge runs on a path the user did not consciously choose, and it must not take the photos with it. Every link had unit coverage and the chain had none, which is how four consecutive releases each shipped a different silent break in it. Probed with seven distinct sabotages (reload before purge, an IndexedDB wipe, no cache delete, ignoring `deferAutoUpdate`, a no-op cancel, no anti-loop cap, no `pagehide` listener) — each turns it red. **The rule for anyone touching this hook: an update path may refuse to act, but it may never refuse to report.** Probed — re-gating the information fails 6 tests, putting detection back under `ready` fails 14, dropping the promotion fails 1. | **And the CHECK ITSELF can fail.** The fetch's `.catch` is empty by necessity (a transient failure must not be noise), which left the last silent dead-end: a PERMANENT failure — a broken deploy, a 404, a captive portal, a filtered network — was indistinguishable from a healthy app, for ever, at one silent retry every 120 s. `cave-version-check-ok` records the moment a check last SUCCEEDED (reached the server and got readable JSON — recorded BEFORE any verdict, since "is there a newer build" and "can this device still ask" are different questions), persisted so it survives a relaunch, and Settings → Application warns past `VERSION_CHECK_STALE_MS` (3 days). **The poll runs every 120 s while the app is open, so this is fresh within seconds on a healthy device: a stale value never means "you have not opened the app in a while", it always means "the check is failing right now", and it clears itself on the next success** — which is why a week offline is not reported as a fault. A corrupt marker degrades to null rather than a bogus age. NOTE for anyone tempted by a once-a-day timer as an extra net: it would add nothing. The existing poll is every 2 minutes while open, and while the app is CLOSED no JS runs at all, so a 24 h `setInterval` is strictly weaker than what is already there — the real gap was never cadence, it was the swallowed failure.  **`APP_GENERATION`, the epoch that makes the version renumberable DOWNWARD.** `isRemoteNewer` refuses a version downgrade, deliberately (a rolled-back or partially-deployed `version.json` drove an endless purge-and-reload loop), so the display version is a **one-way ratchet** — publish 1.0 over a 1.5 and every installed client computes `1.0 < 1.5` and never offers the release. **MEASURED before writing anything, and it is why this is a small field rather than a big worry: `sw.js` serves HTML network-first, so a relaunch while online fetches the new `index.html` and its content-hashed chunks WITHOUT consulting this comparison.** A downgrade therefore strands nobody; it only silences the in-session flow (pill, countdown, silent data-only path) until the next cold start. Small and invisible, which is the kind worth closing before it is needed rather than during. A monotonic integer in `constants.ts` + `version.json`, compared BEFORE version and build; bump it once in the release that PRECEDES a renumbering and the version is then free to go anywhere, for ever rather than once. **It is NOT a loosening of the downgrade guard** — a LOWER generation is still refused, so the loop stays closed. **The DEFAULT is the load-bearing part**: an absent or garbage generation resolves to the CALLER's, so the comparison falls through to the old rules and every earlier deploy behaves exactly as before; defaulting to 0 would make every one of them look older than the running app and silently kill the update path — the very failure the field exists to prevent. **`null` is rejected explicitly, because `Number(null)` is 0 and not NaN** — the one garbage value JS coerces into a plausible generation, and the one a templated `version.json` is likeliest to carry; that case was found by a probe, not by reading. The anti-loop latch key gained the generation too (after a renumber the same version+build on a new epoch is a different artifact), which orphans every installed device's attempt marker ONCE — harmless, an unmatched marker suppresses nothing. `version.json` is pinned to `APP_GENERATION` by **doc:check's `checkVersions`**, beside every other version-vs-version.json rule, so a build bump meets it; the vitest side asserts only the WIRING (both call sites pass it — a pure function nobody hands the value to does nothing), which doc:check cannot see. Probed eight ways, each reddening alone. **Never show it to a user: it is not a second version number.** |

Previously only a MISSING lot (`!hasLot`) was cleared, so a shared lot id kept the ref and pushed Σsessions above `weightInitial − weightG` → `lot-balance-overflow` + double-counted stock. Locked by the "orphans a session that references a SHARED/deduped lot id" test.** **Entity LWW was PER-ROW, and that silently destroyed the user's own prose.** One `updatedAt` covers the whole row, so a device that touched ONE field overwrote EVERY unprotected field, including ones it never edited. Reachable and ordinary: iPad writes a tasting note at 10:00; iPhone — whose copy of that note is a week old — changes only the rating at 10:05; a merge on the iPad replaces the whole row and the note written five minutes earlier is gone, counted as « 1 fiche mise à jour ».
