- **Tool:** `web_search_20260209` with `allowed_callers: ["direct"]` (Anthropic built-in, `max_uses: 3`) — only exposed for Anthropic; OpenAI/Gemini use their pre-trained knowledge. The `_20260209` version is the current default per Anthropic; dynamic filtering kicks in on Opus 4.6+ / Sonnet 4.6 only — on Haiku 4.5 (the current default model) it behaves like the older `_20250305` but is kept on the newer string so the day we re-evaluate a smarter model, the tool version is already right. **`allowed_callers: ["direct"]` is mandatory on Haiku 4.5** — without it the API rejects the request with "claude-haiku-4-5 does not support programmatic tool calling", because `_20260209` defaults to requiring PTC. The escape hatch is documented in the rejection message itself. If a future migration moves the default model to Opus / Sonnet, `allowed_callers` can be removed to unlock PTC's token-efficiency gains.
- **Purpose:** Auto-populate tobacco/pipe/wishlist details — for tobaccos and wishlist items: category, cut, blend, Force/Room Note/Taste, `agingMax` (max cellar age, integer or range e.g. `10-15`, empty string if unknown); for pipes: shape, chamber dimensions
- **Source priority (tobacco/wish prompt only):** the system prompt instructs the model to query, in this strict order: (1) `smokingpipes.com` — the **reference for every field** (category, cut, blend / composition, strength, room note, taste, max age, description). The official spec table AND the SP blend description prose are both authoritative; user comments on SP product pages are demoted to "confirmation only". (2) `tobaccoreviews.com` — fallback if SP is missing the info, OR to enrich the description with 1 sentence of aggregated user feedback (must NOT override an SP value). (3) `reddit.com/r/PipeTobacco` — fallback ONLY if SP and TR come up short. The 3-search budget fits exactly: SP + TR + optional Reddit. The SP priority applies to ALL fields, not just Force/RN/Taste as it once did. Pipes don't have a deterministic priority — the prompt just asks for "web search to identify the pipe" since most pipe data lives on a single shop listing.
- **Language:** `langInstr` appended to every system prompt instructs the model to write **all text fields** (description, blend, tasting notes) in the app's active UI language — **every UI language**, not just FR/EN. `LANG_PROMPT_NAME` (module-level in `useAiAutoFill.ts`, shared with `buildScanPrompt`) maps `lang`→English language name; French gets a French clause, every other language gets an English clause that *names* the target language (`"…written in Spanish/German/Italian/European Portuguese"`) so any provider complies. Fallback `LANG_PROMPT_NAME[lang] || "English"`. **It is DERIVED — `Object.fromEntries(LANGUAGES.map(l => [l.code, langAssets(l.code).aiPromptName]))`, not a literal map**, because the literal one silently made the AI write in English for any language added after it (the six-silent-fallback class; `aiPromptName` is a `LANG_ASSETS` column, so doc:check gate 13 fails when a new language has no row). Category/cut are NOT AI-translated — they're stored canonical (French) and localised in-app via `xl()`.
- **Prompt safety:** User query truncated to 200 chars before embedding in prompt to limit injection surface
- **Label scan:** `aiScanLabel(kind, file)` in `useAiAutoFill` — photo of the tin → provider vision request → brand / name (+ blend when readable) filled into the tobacco or wishlist form. Pure helpers exported for tests: `parseScanResult` (JSON extraction + refusal/clip scrub, null when neither brand nor name is readable), `buildScanRequest` (per-provider wire shape — Anthropic base64 image block / OpenAI data-URL image_url / Gemini inline_data; Gemini key in `x-goog-api-key` header, never the URL), `buildScanPrompt`, `redactApiKeys`, `aiClipStr`, `aiIsRefusal` (the last two moved out of the `aiAutoFill` closure so both paths share the scrub). `LANG_PROMPT_NAME` (module-level, shared with the autofill prompt) instructs the scan to write any extracted blend composition in the active UI language via `buildScanPrompt(lang)`. **No `web_search` tool on the scan request** — the answer must come from the image (anti-hallucination). The photo is canvas-downscaled to 1024 px JPEG (q 0.85) before upload and never persisted. Scan overwrites brand/name (the scan IS the user's intent) but fills `blend` only when empty. **Auto-chain:** a successful scan immediately calls `runAutoFill(type, qOverride)` (the extracted body of `aiAutoFill`) with a query built from the SCAN RESULT — not from the form, whose setState hasn't re-rendered yet (stale closure). The spinner stays on across both calls; `parseAndApply` / `onErr` clear it. A failed scan never fires the chained search. UI: `AICard` `onScanFile` prop (hidden `<input type="file" accept="image/*">`, NO `capture` attr so iOS AND Android offer camera + library) — passed by TobaccoFormView + WishFormView only; the pipe form doesn't (stampings too small/worn for reliable extraction).
- **Response sanitisation (extended in 206):** `stripMarkupFromString` (`src/utils.ts`) is the shared scrubber. `clipStr` in `parseAndApply` wraps it for every text field returned by every provider (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini). Two passes: (1) strip any HTML-like tag `</?[a-z][^>]*>` while keeping the inner content — Anthropic's web search wraps quoted facts in `<cite index="N-M">…</cite>`, other providers occasionally leak `<span>` etc.; (2) decode the common HTML entities (`&amp; &lt; &gt; &quot; &#39;`). Then collapses orphan whitespace. `migrateData` (utils.ts) calls the same helper on load so pre-dirty data gets cleaned without user action — covered fields: tobacco/pipe/wish/accessory name + brand + blend + description + tastingNotes + notes, and session notes. Tests: `src/__tests__/useAiAutoFill.test.ts` for the live path, `src/__tests__/migrateData.snapshot.test.ts` for the on-load scrub.
- **API key storage:** per-provider keys in `localStorage` — `anthropic-api-key`, `openai-api-key`, `gemini-api-key`; switching providers loads the corresponding key. Gemini key sent via `x-goog-api-key` header (not URL query string).
- **API key exclusion from exports:** `excludeApiKey` React state, backed by `localStorage` key `cave-exclude-apikey`. Default: **exclude** (opt-out). Set `"0"` to include. Controls `doExport`, `gdriveSave`, and `gdriveSaveQuiet`. Toggle in ⚙️ Settings → AI section.
- **CORS:** Calls go directly to provider APIs (service worker bypasses `api.anthropic.com`, `api.openai.com`, `generativelanguage.googleapis.com`)
- **Catalogue lookup (the catalogue is the USER'S OWN FILE):** the catalogue is checked BEFORE the provider API on every auto-fill, and `"local"` has been the default. The lookup module is `src/utils/tobaccoDb.ts`: `loadTobaccoDb()` reads the user's catalogue out of `catalogueStore` (IndexedDB `cave-catalogue`) once and caches it in module memory, deduping concurrent calls; `tobaccoDbInvalidate()` drops that cache after the user loads or clears a catalogue, or the module would serve the previous one for the rest of the session. `tobaccoDbLookup(brand, name, lang)` does a case-insensitive `<brand>|<name>` lookup and returns the factual attributes plus a description resolved by the shared `pickLang` (requested → en → fr → first present), so a catalogue filled in only one language still works everywhere. **`null` means « no catalogue loaded » — the ordinary state of a fresh install, NOT a failure**, which is why the surfaces render `CatalogueMissing` rather than a retry. **REWRITTEN; the paragraph that stood here described the deleted apparatus in detail** — `src/data/tobacco-db.json` and its content-hashed chunk, the per-language `tobacco-db.desc-<lang>.json` prose chunks, `ensureLangDescriptions`, `loadTobaccoCatalogue(lang)`, `scripts/translate-tobacco-db.cjs`, and gzip figures for chunks that have not shipped. What survives from it and is still true: category and cut are stored CANONICAL (French) and translated in-app via `xl()`; the composition (`blend`) is language-neutral jargon; and **the catalogue is never in a user backup** — it lives in its own IndexedDB and its own cloud file (see `GDRIVE_CATALOGUE_PREFIX`), and nothing about it lands in `localStorage["pipe-cellar-v6"]`, the JSON/CSV/ZIP exports or the cellar backups. When a lookup hits, the VALUES are copied into the user's entry and those are backed up as usual.
- **DB-first vs AI-first:** the user picks the preferred source in Settings → AI → "Source prioritaire" (`autofillSource` ctx, persisted in `localStorage["cave-autofill-source"]`, **defaults to `"local"`** — see the bullet below for why the earlier `"ai"` default expired).
  - `"local"`: DB lookup first. Hit → instant fill, fully offline, no API call. Miss → falls through to the provider API if a key is configured (legacy behaviour). Miss + no key → the more specific `ai_err_no_match_no_key` error.
  - `"ai"`: provider API first. Success → `setAiSource(aiProvider)`. Failure (timeout, rate limit, network) → silent DB fallback before surfacing the error, so the user still gets a fill if the blend is in the catalog. Pipe form bypasses the DB entirely (no pipe entries in the catalog). **With NO key configured it never reaches the provider at all** — `runAutoFill`'s AI-first branch goes straight to `tobaccoDbLookup`, so "ai" describes a preference the app can only honour when there is something to call.
  - **The option is called « Catalogue », and the sub-line no longer describes a free built-in base.** It read *« La base locale est instantanée, GRATUITE et hors-ligne »* with the option labelled « Base locale », wording written when the app SHIPPED a catalogue: "local DB" then named something the user neither chose nor owned, and "free" distinguished it from a paid API call. The catalogue became the user's own CSV, so both halves state the opposite of what the app does — reported from the app. The option is `Catalogue` in all six languages (shorter than every label it replaces, so no layout risk) and the sub-line now says the catalogue answers *instantly, offline and without a key — if it holds the blend*. The `· source: …` tag under the search button says `catalogue` too, and `ai_compare_keep_db` (« Garder la DB ») became « Garder le catalogue » — **that one was already misquoted by the help in FOUR languages** (fr « Garder la base », es « Mantener BD », pt « Manter BD » against the app's own strings), so renaming it closed a drift as well as the vocabulary. The help's six section headings said « Base locale INTÉGRÉE » / « Bundled local catalog » directly above a paragraph beginning *"nothing is bundled with the app"* — a miss, fixed in the same pass.
  - **`"local"` STAYS the default, for a better reason than the one it was set on.** It was restored because the bundled catalogue had finished being re-validated; there is no bundled catalogue now, which retires that argument and supplies a stronger one — a catalogue is the user's OWN file, so someone who took the trouble to load one certainly wants it consulted before a paid API call. With no catalogue loaded the branch costs nothing: the lookup misses, the provider is called if a key exists, and `noMatchKey()` says «aucun catalogue chargé» rather than the false «pas de correspondance dans la base locale».
  - **The DEFAULT is `"local"` again, on the user's instruction, and the `"ai"` reason had EXPIRED.** It had been flipped to `"ai"` for a stated condition — *"while the bundled catalog is being re-validated against smokingpipes"* — and the comment in `App.tsx` still carried the sentence. The re-validation was finished, so the condition the "ai" default was waiting on was met and the cheaper, faster, offline path that needs no key was the right one to land on. **That argument is itself now obsolete and the DEFAULT still stands on a better one**: the catalogue is the user's OWN file, so someone who took the trouble to load one certainly wants it consulted before a paid API call, and with none loaded the branch costs nothing. **Only devices with NO stored value move** — `saveAutofillSource` writes on change, so a deliberate pick survives (the `ai-model-auto-migrated` rule: a default may move, a choice may not). The second half of the instruction — *"si API sélectionné on y passe que si la clé est référencée"* — was ALREADY true and is now LOCKED rather than assumed, because nothing covered it and that is exactly how the defect survived for months with the underlying behaviour correct. `autofillSourceDefault.test.ts` drives the real hook: no key → the catalogue answers and `fetch` is never called; a key → the provider is called; `"local"` + a catalogue MISS + a key → it still falls through to the provider (catalogue-FIRST is not catalogue-ONLY); and the PIPE form with no key asks for one instead, since there is no pipe data to fall back to. Probed in three directions. Same build cleared the stale `~550 popular blends` figure from two comments.
  - The `aiSource` state on the hook (`"" | "local" | "anthropic" | "openai" | "gemini"`) drives a tiny `· source: …` tag under the AICard search button so the user knows where the just-filled data came from. Sage for local, brass for any provider.
- **Sage hint "Documenté dans la base":** `TobaccoFormView` and `WishFormView` each call `tobaccoDbLookupSync(form.brand, form.name, lang)` in a `useMemo` and pass the boolean result as `dbHinted` to `<AICard>`. When true (typed brand+name match an entry AND the tap would actually reach the catalogue), AICard renders a sage `<Notice>` promising an instant fill on click. **The gate was `autofillSource === "ai" → hide`, and that suppressed the offer on EVERY FRESH INSTALL.** The original reason is sound and still holds — under "ai" the tap goes to the provider first, so promising an instant catalogue fill would mislead — but `autofillSource` only describes what the tap does **when there is a key to call** (and `"ai"` was the shipped default at the time): `runAutoFill`'s AI-first branch goes straight to `tobaccoDbLookup` when `!apiKey`. So for a new user — shipped default, no key — the tap would have filled the fiche instantly from the catalogue and the banner offering it was the single thing hidden, on the only install that has no other way to fill a fiche. The gate is now `autofillSource === "ai" && apiKey`, i.e. it keys on **what the tap will actually do rather than on the setting**, and `apiKey` joined both dep arrays. Locked by `CatalogOfferFreshInstall.test.tsx`, which drives the REAL views with a mocked catalogue rather than asserting the source — a source assertion would pass on a rewrite that reintroduced the defect in different words (the placement block in `CatalogOffer.test.tsx` reads the source because layout ORDER is what it guards; a decision needs the decision exercised). Probed in BOTH directions. **The default moved to `"local"`, so a fresh install no longer reaches this gate — the cases were NOT deleted, they were renamed**: what they protect is the same defect through the door still open, "picked Agent IA and never configured a key, or cleared it later": reverting the gate reddens 2 cases, and so does dropping it entirely, since over-reaching would restore the false promise for a user who does have a key. The `dbReady` flag in each form re-renders once `loadTobaccoDb()` resolves so the hint appears on first cache load. The pipe form intentionally doesn't have this hint (no pipe coverage in the DB).
- **Synchronous short-circuit for empty form:** when the user clicks auto-fill with brand+name empty AND no API key configured, the hook returns the legacy `err_api_key` message synchronously — no async DB round-trip that would only ever return null. Locked by the "sets aiErr to 'err_api_key' when key is empty (no fetch)" test in `useAiAutoFill.test.ts`.
- **AI prompt tightening:** the system prompt now spells out the strict descriptive → 1-5 mapping (Mild=2, Mild-to-Medium=2, Medium=3, Medium-to-Full=4, Full=4, Very-Full/Extra-Strong/Overwhelming=5) so two AI calls — and the AI vs the DB — converge on the same integer instead of treating "Medium-Full" as a coin-flip between 3 and 4. The `aging_max_years` rule is also tighter: prefer explicit "ages X" / "X-Y years" / "X+ years" mentions in SP/TR prose; fall back to family defaults (the `FAMILY_AGING_MAX` table, since revised — Latakia/English shorter, Virginia/Perique longest) only when nothing explicit; never return free text. Plafond strict at 30 to catch hallucinated 50+ year claims.
- **Cross-check button:** after a DB hit, AICard renders a "Vérifier avec l'IA" button. On click the hook fires `aiCompareCheck(type)` which runs the full AI dispatch in preview mode (3rd `previewCallback` arg to `runAutoFill` and `parseAndApply`) — the AI-derived values land in `aiCompare = { type, db, ai }` instead of being written to the form. AICard then shows a compact diff (only fields that disagree) with "Appliquer l'IA" / "Garder la DB" buttons. `applyAiCompare` writes the AI values to the form (preserving any field where AI returned ""/0); `dismissAiCompare` clears the state. The DB stays the authority by default; the cross-check is opt-in per fill.

## Scroll preservation

Returning to a list view (Catalogue / Wishlist / Collection / Workshop / Journal) after opening a detail, editing an entry, or adding a new one must restore the list scroll exactly where the user was. The pipeline:

- **`scrollSaveRef`** (App.tsx `useRef<Record<string, number>>`) holds the last-known scrollY per list, keyed by: `inv` (tobaccos + wishlist when statusFilter="wish"), `pipes`, `acc`, `journal`, `wish` (the wishlist *form overlay* opening — distinct from `inv` because it doesn't trigger a view change).
- **Save sites:**
  - `ctxSetDetail` / `ctxSetPipeDet` / `ctxSetAccDet` snapshot the scroll when a detail is opened (list → detail).
  - `nav(v)` snapshots the scroll of the **leaving** view if it's a list (`inv` / `pipes` / `acc` / `journal`) — covers the `+` button and the journal's "edit session" row tap, where no detail intermediate is involved.
  - `InventoryListView` snapshots `scrollSaveRef.current["wish"]` inline at every `setShowWishForm(true)` call site (3 sites) — the wish form is an overlay, not a view change, so neither `nav` nor the detail wrappers fire.
- **Restore sites:**
  - The centralised `useEffect` on `[view, detail, pipeDet, accDet]` in App.tsx restores `inv` / `pipes` / `acc` / `journal` whenever the user lands on the list with no detail open and `scrollToTopRef.current === false`. Forward-nav (default) sets `scrollToTopRef.current = true` so the effect's early-return guard takes over and the user lands at the top — that's the desired behaviour for an intentional menu tap.
  - `useWishStore.updateWish` restores `wish` directly after the form save (no useEffect because the wish form is overlay-only — no view change to watch).
- **`restoreScrollY(targetY, maxAttempts = 20)`** (`src/utils.ts`) — shared helper. Single `requestAnimationFrame` was too early when a list view re-mounts after closing a detail: the first paint shows an empty page and `scrollTo` gets clamped to the still-tiny `scrollHeight`. The helper retries across up to 20 frames (~333 ms) until `document.scrollHeight - innerHeight >= targetY`, then commits the scroll. Capped so a legitimately shorter list (item deleted / filter changed) doesn't loop forever.
- **Bottom dock tap-active-tab = scroll to top (iOS-style):** `CuratorApp` `onNav` handler checks `id === dockId` and forces `requestAnimationFrame(() => window.scrollTo(0, 0))` when the user taps the tab they're already on. Without this, `nav()` doesn't change `view`, the restore `useEffect` doesn't fire, and the dock tap was a no-op.
- **`nav()` must NOT wipe `scrollSaveRef`:** the previous `scrollSaveRef.current = {}` at the end of `nav` silently killed the `restoreScroll: true` path used by every store (useTobaccoStore / usePipeStore / useAccessoryStore / useSessionStore) on save success. Keys are per-list so they don't interfere; forward-nav clears via `scrollToTopRef`, not by wiping.
- **`nav()` must skip the scroll snapshot while a detail panel is open:** for a time, `nav()` snapshotted `window.scrollY` into `scrollSaveRef` whenever the LEAVING view was a list — but if a detail panel was open (`detail` / `pipeDet` / `accDet` set), the scrollY belonged to the detail (which scrolled to top on open), not the underlying list. Tapping Edit from a detail therefore overwrote the position saved by `ctxSetDetail` / `ctxSetPipeDet` / `ctxSetAccDet` with 0, and the post-save restore landed at the top. The fix gates the four snapshot lines behind `!detail && !pipeDet && !accDet`. Regression locked by `src/__tests__/navScrollGuard.test.ts`.

**`history.scrollRestoration` is `'manual'`, set in `main.jsx` before React mounts.** Reported from the app: open a blend in the catalogue, close it with a left-edge **swipe**, and you land at the TOP of the 1222-row list; the × and Escape are fine. **It is not the app scrolling.** Traced in a browser: `window.scrollTo` is never called, the document never shrinks (75 030 px and 1222 rows throughout), and `Modal`'s focus restore lands on the right row with the scroll still intact at 12 000 — the jump happens AFTER every handler has run. That is the browser restoring the position recorded on the history entry being returned to, and `useBackNavigation` seeds that entry at mount, when the scroll is 0. The app already owns this (`scrollSaveRef` + `restoreScrollY` for the restore paths, `scrollToTopRef` for forward nav), so the browser doing it too is a straight conflict — and the browser wins because it acts last. **That is also why the defect is invisible almost everywhere**: most back paths navigate to a view whose scroll the app then restores explicitly, painting over the browser's 0; the catalogue merely closes a modal, so nothing re-scrolls and the 0 stands. **It MUST be set pre-mount**: `scrollRestoration` is a property of the CURRENT history entry, so setting it later leaves the entry you navigate BACK to on `'auto'` and changes nothing — measured, and it briefly looked like a refutation of the diagnosis. Feature-detected + try/catch, because the pre-mount block also seeds the theme and the language and must not abort. Locked by `scrollRestoration.test.ts` (source-level: jsdom implements neither scroll nor `scrollRestoration` semantics), which also asserts that `useBackNavigation` does NOT set it — two owners of a per-entry property is how this returns — and that nothing in `src/` sets it back to `'auto'`.

When adding a new list view: snapshot the scroll on every "leave" path (detail open + `+` button + any overlay form opening that isn't a view change), restore it via the centralised `useEffect` (add a new branch keyed by `view === "newlist"`), and pair store add/update success calls with `nav("newlist", { restoreScroll: true })`.

## Back navigation & gestures

The system-back inputs (browser/hardware back, left-edge swipe) call a single `goBack()` routine. **`goBack` is now a DYNAMIC back stack, not a fixed parent-mapping.** The earlier code hard-coded ONE parent per screen (every non-form view → home), so system-back / edge-swipe from Stats or the session form teleported to Home instead of the actual previous screen. It now tracks a real history STACK of visited screens so back returns to where the user truly came from.

**Split of responsibility:**
- **`src/utils/navHistory.ts`** — the PURE engine (exhaustively unit-tested by `navHistory.test.ts`): `NavLoc` (a screen snapshot = `view` + open `detailId`/`pipeDetId`/`accDetId` + `statusFilter`), `pushLoc(stack, leaving)` (immutable push; de-dups the top; caps depth at 40), `isFormView`/`isRestorable`/`isBareRoot`/`sameLoc`/`locIdentity`, `fallbackParent(view)` (the minimal old mapping for an empty stack), and **`decideBack(state)`** — THE routing decision as a pure function returning a `BackAction` (`close-detail`/`close-pipe`/`close-acc`/`close-wish`/`pop`/`nav`/`none`). **`pushLoc` skips non-restorable locations: forms, `tasting`, AND bare dock/main pages** (`NAV_ROOT_VIEWS` = home/inv/pipes/acc/journal/stats with NO fiche open). **Per user request: NO history between main pages** — the dock tabs are siblings under Home, not a linear stack, so leaving one is never recorded and back from any main page falls through to Home (`fallbackParent`). A dock view WITH a fiche open is a DRILL state (`detailId` set), which IS restorable — so `detail → edit → back` still returns to the fiche, and `form → back` returns to its list via `fallbackParent`. **Critical fix: `nextStackOnNav(stack, target, leaving)` RESETS the stack whenever nav() lands on a main/root page** — a dock tab is a root, not a history cran. Without this, navigating away from an OPEN fiche via a dock tab pushed the fiche as a drill state, so back from ANY later main page dumped the user onto that stale fiche ("back always returns to accessories"). Now nav() calls `nextStackOnNav` (clears on root target, else `pushLoc`), guaranteeing back from any main page → Home.
- **`src/hooks/useBackNavigation.ts`** — TRANSPORT only now: takes a single `onBack` callback, installs the `popstate` + edge-swipe listeners once, seeds `history.replaceState`+`pushState` on mount, 400 ms debounce, and calls the latest `onBack` via a ref. No routing logic.
- **App.tsx** — owns `navHistoryRef` (the live stack) + `restoringBackRef`, and the thin executors: `captureLoc()` (snapshot current screen), `nav()` pushes the LEAVING screen via `pushLoc` at its top (gated `!restoringBackRef && v !== view`), `goBack()` runs `decideBack` and executes the action, `applyLoc(loc)` restores a popped screen (`nav(loc.view,{restoreScroll:true})` then re-applies `statusFilter` + re-opens the fiche by id from `liveData`, all inside a `restoringBackRef` guard so the restore doesn't re-push).

**Behaviour:** open overlays (tobacco/pipe/accessory fiche, wishlist form) still close IN PLACE (return to the underlying list) — priority order detail → pipe → acc → wish. View-to-view moves pop the real stack: `journal → editJ →` back returns to **journal** (not home); `journal → stats →` back returns to **journal**; `detail → editT →` back returns to the **detail fiche** (nav captured the open detail). Forms + `tasting` are never a back TARGET (filtered by `pushLoc`). A drained stack falls back to `fallbackParent` (forms→their list, else→home), so the first taps of a fresh session still behave. Home with an empty stack is a no-op (root).

**Cross-fiche back:** the pairing rows ("Top pipes utilisées" on the tobacco fiche, "Top tabacs fumés ici" on the pipe fiche) cross-navigate fiche → fiche via the ctx helper **`crossOpenDetail({view, kind, obj})`** (App.tsx), which `pushLoc`s the CURRENT fiche onto `navHistoryRef` BEFORE navigating (guarding `nav()` with `restoringBackRef` so nav's root-target stack RESET can't wipe the push, and using raw `setDetail`/`setPipeDet` so no wrong list-scroll snapshot is taken). Because of that, `decideBack` now **pops to the previous fiche instead of closing the current one to its list — but ONLY when a fiche is open AND the back-stack top is itself a fiche location** (`locHasFiche`). This is the exact cross-fiche drill; the normal `list → fiche → back` still closes to the list (the stack is empty there, so the new branch is skipped). The only way a fiche sits under an open fiche on the stack is `crossOpenDetail`, so the rule is precisely scoped. Do NOT reorder `decideBack` to close-in-place before this pop check — that reintroduces "swipe-back from the paired pipe dumps me on the pipe list instead of the tobacco fiche". Locked by `navHistory.test.ts` (cross-fiche pop + the normal empty-stack close). **Session-modal → fiche:** the JournalView `SessionDetailModal` tabac / pipe blocks are tappable (when the live entity still exists) and call the SAME `crossOpenDetail`. To make back re-open the modal, `NavLoc` gained a `sessionDetailId` (captured by `captureLoc`, restored by `applyLoc`, part of `locIdentity`, and counted by `isBareRoot`/`locHasFiche`), so a `journal` loc with the session modal open is a restorable drill — back from the cross-opened fiche pops to it and re-opens the modal. A hard-deleted entity shows via snapshot with no `onOpenTob`/`onOpenPipe`, so its block stays inert. **The LIVE tasting reaches its tobacco and its pipe too.** Reported from the app (« quand je suis dans une session j'aimerais pouvoir atteindre la pipe ou le tabac en cliquant dessus »): the JOURNAL's session-detail blocks were made tappable and `TastingView` — a different component showing the same "this tobacco in this pipe" pair — never got it. Its running-stage `ComboRow`s now take an `onOpen` and render as a `PressCard` + chevron, the identical affordance, calling the same `crossOpenDetail`. **Back RETURNS to the tasting, and the earlier refusal to do that was wrong.** It shipped with the banner as the only way back, arguing that a `tasting` origin could go stale (the 95-minute auto-end clears the session while the user reads the fiche, and `nav("tasting")` on a view whose only render gate is `view !== "tasting"` paints an empty screen). The report came straight back: « le swipe back ne me ramène pas dans la session ». **The risk was real and the conclusion was not** — it is a reason to HANDLE the stale case, not to skip the feature. `pushDrillOrigin` now records `tasting` (it stays out of `pushLoc`, so it never becomes an ordinary history entry — `isRestorable` is unchanged and still asserted), and `decideBack` drops a dead tasting origin via the new `tastingLive` flag that App feeds from `!!tasting`. **DROPPING the entry rather than blocking the pop is the load-bearing choice**: back then continues to whatever origin sits underneath, or falls through to `fallbackParent`, exactly as if the tasting had never been recorded — so a stale session degrades to the behaviour instead of dead-ending. A whole RUN of dead entries is pruned, not just the top one. Verified end to end in a browser (tasting → tap the tobacco → fiche → system back → back on the running tasting, chrono intact) and probed in both directions. The test that pinned the old exclusion now records the reversal on the assertion itself, so it is not "fixed" back. A row whose entity has been deleted stays INERT — the `? : undefined` idiom drops `role` and `tabIndex`, so it degrades to plain text rather than announcing a button that does nothing. **The test for that was VACUOUS on its first pass and the probe caught it**: it looked for the blend NAME, which is absent either way once the tobacco is gone (the row renders "—"), so deleting the `selTob &&` guard left it green. It asserts on a `data-combo-row` hook now — the rows are still there, they are simply not activable — with a positive counterpart so it cannot pass by the rows vanishing. Verified in a browser, where the tap must be a KEYBOARD activation: `PressCard`'s ghost-click defence swallows a programmatic click (the lesson, one component over). **Home-tile drills return to Home (generalises 276/277):** the Home tiles that open an overlay — "Ce soir ?"/"À surveiller" rows, the featured hero, the rested pipe, both "du moment" picks, the "À entretenir" reminder, AND the **envies (wishlist) tile** — now ALL route through `crossOpenDetail` instead of a bare `nav()+setDetail`, so the origin (Home) is recorded and system-back returns to **Home** instead of dumping the user on the overlay's underlying list. Two mechanics made this work: (1) `crossOpenDetail` records the origin via **`pushDrillOrigin`** (navHistory.ts) which — unlike `pushLoc` — KEEPS bare-root origins like Home (it still skips forms/tasting), and it gained a `kind:"wishlist"` branch (sets `statusFilter="wish"` instead of a detail); (2) `decideBack`'s pop rule was **generalised** — it now pops to the stack top whenever an overlay (detail/pipe/accessory fiche OR the `isWishlist` sub-state) is open AND the stack is non-empty, dropping the `locHasFiche` restriction (that helper was removed). The normal `list → fiche → back` still closes in place (its stack is empty — the fiche was opened by `setDetail` with no push). `applyLoc` now restores `statusFilter` **unconditionally** (default "active") so popping Home clears a lingering "wish" filter. Also: the `navTo*` filtered-list helpers (`navToInvFiltered`/`navToInvByAroma`/`navToPipes*`/`navToJournal*`) set `scrollToTopRef` so a "Familles"/"Votre profil" click-through lands at the TOP of the list, not mid-page (they use `setView` directly, bypassing `nav()`'s scroll-to-top). Locked by `navHistory.test.ts` (pushDrillOrigin + the Home-origin pop + the empty-stack close-in-place). **Pipe-fiche family bar:** `navToInvFiltered` (the pipe fiche's "Familles fumées" bars, via `PipesDetailView`) records the open fiche as the origin (`pushDrillOrigin(captureLoc())`) and clears `detail`/`pipeDet`/`accDet` itself, so the filtered tabac list lands scrolled to the top AND system-back returns to the pipe fiche. **Stats drills return to Stats + the `drillOpened` gate (the important structural change):** EVERY `navTo*` filtered-list helper (`navToInvFiltered`/`navToInvByAroma`/`navToPipesFiltered`/`navToPipesFilteredByMaterial`/`navToJournalFiltered`/`navToJournalFilteredByDate`/`navToJournalFilteredByLocation`) now records its ORIGIN screen via `pushDrillOrigin(captureLoc())` — so a drill from **Stats** (its charts/heatmap/Lieux click-thrus) returns to **Stats** on back, not Home (those helpers used to record nothing, so back fell to `fallbackParent`→Home from every Stats drill). Recording those origins broke the pop heuristic ("overlay open + non-empty stack → pop"), which had relied on a normally-opened fiche ALWAYS having an empty stack: a fiche opened FROM a Stats-drilled list now had both an overlay AND an origin on the stack, so back wrongly skipped the list. The fix is an explicit **`drillOpened`** flag (`drillOverlayRef` in App.tsx, `BackState.drillOpened` in navHistory.ts): `decideBack`'s overlay-pop branch is gated on it, so it fires ONLY for a **crossOpenDetail** overlay (drill), never for a fiche opened normally from a list. The flag is set true by `crossOpenDetail` (after its internal `nav`) and by `applyLoc` when it restores an overlay location (so a cross-fiche chain keeps popping up); it's set false by `nav()`, every `navTo*` helper (they land on a LIST), and `ctxSetDetail`/`ctxSetPipeDet`/`ctxSetAccDet` (a normal fiche open). Net: Stats→filtered-list→back → Stats; Stats→filtered-list→open a fiche→back → closes to the filtered list (then back again → Stats); the crossOpenDetail drills (fiche→fiche, Home tiles, session-modal→fiche) still pop to their origin. Also: `nav()` now resets the TOBACCO `ratingFilter` too (it reset the pipe rating + every other tobacco filter but forgot the tobacco rating, so a lingering N-star inventory filter silently narrowed the Home "Tabacs" top-bar drill), the Home "Tabacs" tile drills to the OWNED (`active`) list matching its `activeRefs` count (was `all`), and the Home "Moyenne" tile drills to `stats` (was inert). Locked by `navHistory.test.ts` (Stats-drill pop, the `drillOpened`-false close-in-place, the gated cross-drill pops) + `HomeViewV2.test.tsx` (both top-bar tiles). **The three Stats drills that pass missed (the reported "swipe-back from Stats never returns to Stats, globally"):** `StatsView` had three click-throughs still on a bare `nav()`+`setDetail`/`setPipeDet`/`setRatingFilter` (NOT the origin-recording helpers), so back from them fell to Home: (1) the **ratings histogram** — worse, the new `nav()` `ratingFilter` reset silently WIPED its `setRatingFilter(s)`, so the drill lost its filter too — now goes through the new **`navToInvByRating(rating)`** App helper (records origin via `pushDrillOrigin`, uses `setView` so the rating survives, lands on the active list to match the active-only histogram); (2) **"Top tabacs"** and (3) **"Top pipes"** bars — opened the fiche via `nav+setDetail`/`setPipeDet` (fiche closed to the inventory/pipe LIST on back), now use **`crossOpenDetail`** so back pops to Stats. The now-dead `setDetail`/`setPipeDet`/`setRatingFilter`/`nav`/group-collapse ctx reads were dropped from `StatsView`'s destructure (+ `tobGrouped`/`pipesGrouped` off the chartData memo dep array). Audited globally: every other cross-navigation already records origin (`HomeViewV2` via `crossOpenDetail`, the detail views' pairing rows, the journal session-modal); the list views open fiches through the drill-aware `ctxSet*Detail` wrappers (close-in-place, correct). Locked by `StatsView.test.tsx` (the three drills fire `navToInvByRating`/`crossOpenDetail`). **The non-clickable Stats tiles (reported "certaines tuiles ne sont pas cliquables, elles doivent toutes l'être" + "le clic sur Consommation {année} doit ouvrir les séances de cette année"):** every Stats tile with a meaningful drill target is now clickable and records the Stats origin (back returns to Stats): the **year-consumption hero** → `navToJournalFiltered(String(year))` (the journal for that year); the **"Durée moyenne par séance"** tile → `navToJournalFiltered("")` (all sessions — it's a session stat); the **"Profil gustatif"** (taste) tile → `navToInvFiltered("", "")` (the owned tobaccos it's derived from); the **aroma-profile bars** → `navToInvByAroma(key)` (inventory by aroma). The genuinely analytical charts with NO 1:1 list target stay display-only by design: the **"Note par âge du tabac"** aging curve (age bands map to no filter) and the **"Dépenses"** histograms (purchase amounts, no purchases list). New i18n key `aria_stats_year_sessions` (5 langs). Locked by `StatsView.test.tsx` (block). **Leaving the wishlist re-homes the status-chip strip:** `ScrollableChipRow` (FilterControls.tsx) gained an optional `resetScrollSignal?: number` — an effect keyed on it does `scroller.scrollTo({left:0})`. The scroller's `scrollLeft` persists across re-renders, so when `statusFilter` reset `"wish"` → `"active"` (system-back / close-wishlist) the strip stayed stuck on the right-hand **Wishlist** chip instead of showing "Actifs" at the left. `InventoryListView` bumps the signal (a `useState` counter) via an effect that watches `wishVisible` with a prev-ref, firing ONLY on the wish→exit transition (not on ordinary chip taps, so tapping "Pots" doesn't jerk the row left). Locked by `FilterControls.test.tsx` (bump → scrollTo{left:0}; unchanged → no scroll). **The `drillOpened` restore keys on a `drill` flag, not "an overlay is present" (round-11 F1):** `applyLoc` used to set `drillOverlayRef` true whenever it restored ANY overlay location — but a `{inv, detailId:X}` entry reaches the stack from BOTH a genuine drill (`pushDrillOrigin`) AND a normal `nav()` push (`pushLoc`, e.g. `detail → editT`). So `Stats → filtered-list → fiche → EDIT → back → back` wrongly kept popping the chain and skipped the drilled list (jumped to Stats), while the same sequence WITHOUT the edit correctly closed to the list. Fix: `NavLoc` gained a `drill?: boolean` (METADATA — excluded from `locIdentity`/`sameLoc`) stamped ONLY by `pushDrillOrigin`; `applyLoc` now sets `drillOverlayRef.current = !!loc.drill`. A fiche restored from a plain nav-push (`drill` absent) → `close-in-place`; a fiche restored from a crossOpenDetail/tile/chart drill (`drill:true`) → keeps popping. Locked by `navHistory.test.ts` (drill-stamp + metadata-exclusion). Also: ShoppingModal's wishlist deep-link runs `nav("inv")` BEFORE `setStatusFilter("wish")` (the reset-then-set order, matching SearchModal — the reversed order landed on the Active list); `openDocFromSettings` suppresses `nav()`'s back-stack push (it returns via `setView`, so the push was a stale entry → dead back press over a non-root view); and `restoreSelectionFromTrash`'s `picks` lookup is `hasOwnProperty`-guarded (a forged `__proto__:id` selection can't crash it).

**Modal-aware back:** (1) **Doc pages** (help/changelog/privacy/licenses) opened FROM the Settings modal return to Settings on back / X, not Home. `openDocFromSettings(page)` (ctx) stashes the underlying view in `settingsReturnRef` + closes Settings + navs to the doc page; `closeDocPage()` (ctx) reopens Settings over that view (or navs Home when the doc page was reached from elsewhere — Home footer, TermsGate). goBack short-circuits to `closeDocPage()` when on a doc page with `settingsReturnRef` set; the doc-page TopBar back/X buttons call `closeDocPage()` too. (2) **Session-detail modal** (JournalView) was lifted from view-local state to App/ctx (`sessionDetail`/`setSessionDetail`) so system-back / edge-swipe CLOSES it in place (`decideBack` → `close-session`) instead of navigating away from Journal; `nav()` clears it so it can't leak across a view change. **Wishlist:** the wishlist is a SUB-STATE of the tobacco inventory (`view "inv"` + `statusFilter "wish"`), not a page, so back from it resets the filter to the tobacco list (`decideBack` → `close-wishlist` → `setStatusFilter("active")`), NOT Home. **Modals close first:** goBack closes any open modal BEFORE any doc-page / fiche / view routing, so a swipe-back / system-back always dismisses the front overlay. Two layers: (175) the App-level overlays that aren't shared `Modal`s — lightbox → search → trash → Settings, priority via the pure `firstOpenModal`; then (177) `closeTopModal()` from `utils/modalStack.ts` closes the top-most **shared-`Modal`** modal. Every open `Modal` (components/curator/Modal.tsx) registers its `onClose` on the global modal stack while `open`, so ALL view-local modals the nav layer never knew about — catalog QuickAdd/fiche, lot & maintenance modals, the cellar-confirm, the encryption prompt, the unsaved-changes confirm — are dismissed by system-back without any per-modal wiring. Locked by `modalStack.test.ts`. **Unsaved-changes guard:** after the modal check, goBack consults `formGuardRef` — the active EDIT form registers `{ isDirty, onSave, onDiscard }` via `useUnsavedFormGuard` (ctx.setFormGuard). If the form was modified, goBack opens the `unsavedConfirm` modal (Enregistrer / Quitter sans enregistrer / Annuler — `CuratorUnsavedConfirmModal` in CuratorApp) instead of leaving. Covers ALL 5 forms, add AND edit (addT/editT/addP/editP/addA/editA/addJ/editJ + wish add/edit). dirty = JSON snapshot of the working-copy `form` taken on ENTRY vs current — a fresh add form (or one pre-filled by the catalog QuickAdd / wishToInv) is only "dirty" once the user changes it after opening; the session weight-estimate prefill is gated on `form.pipeId` so it never fires on a blank add. Session form routes its post-early-return `submit`/`cancel` through refs (its save depends on cellar/draft state computed below the hook). **Debounce**: 400 ms (in the hook) — a fast double-tap can't pop two levels in one frame. **Indirection ref**: `onBackRef` refreshed every render so the once-installed listeners always call the latest `goBack` closure (state is stale otherwise). **`accDet` IS handled now** (close-acc branch) — the old gap that teleported home from the accessory fiche is closed.

**`nav(v, opts?)` API** (App.tsx):
- `nav(v)` — default forward navigation. Snapshots the leaving view's scroll if it's a list (`inv` / `pipes` / `acc` / `journal`), sets `scrollToTopRef.current = true`, then updates `view`. The centralised restore useEffect sees the flag and lets the page land at the top.
- `nav(v, { restoreScroll: true })` — used by store save-success paths (e.g. `useTobaccoStore.updateTobacco` after editing). Skips the scroll-to-top so the centralised useEffect restores the saved scrollY for `v`.
- `nav()` must NEVER reset `editXxxId` / `xxxForm` state (a hard invariant — see Curator UI section) and must NEVER wipe `scrollSaveRef` (likewise — see Scroll preservation section).

## Google Integration

- **Client ID:** `890611313186-qadhr6pqp2vk5toh0rkrpgi3qcd1e4ji.apps.googleusercontent.com`
- **Scope:** `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.appdata` (hidden `appDataFolder`, not visible in user's Drive)
- **Backup file naming:**
  - Manual: `cave-tabac-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-tN-pN-wN-aN-jN.json`
  - Auto:   `cave-tabac-auto-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-tN-pN-wN-aN-jN.json`
  - The trailing counts (`t`=tobaccos, `p`=pipes, `w`=wishlist, `a`=accessories, `j`=journal/sessions) let the restore picker display tobacco/pipe/session counts **without downloading the file**. `parseBackupCounts(name)` extracts them.
  - **An optional human-readable device-NAME slug** (`cave-device-name` → `getDeviceName()` → `makeBackupName(…, deviceName)`) is appended at the TAIL, after the counts, before `.json` (e.g. `cave-tabac-auto-<deviceId>-…-jN-<nameslug>.json`) so a backup is identifiable at a glance in Drive/Dropbox. Sanitised to `[a-z0-9]` (accents folded) + capped at 16 chars; `parseBackupCounts`' regex tolerates the optional trailing group and `autoFileDeviceId` (front parse) is unaffected. The NAME is display-only — the opaque `deviceId` stays the convergence identity; the tail placement means a device literally named "auto" can't flip `classifyBackup`. `classifyBackup(name)` returns `"auto"` if the name starts with `GDRIVE_AUTO_PREFIX` (or matches the historical singleton `GDRIVE_AUTO_FILENAME` written by older releases), `"manual"` otherwise.
- **Per-type save model:** `GDRIVE_MAX_MANUAL = 3` (user-triggered saves rotate over 3 timestamped files). **Auto-saves overwrite a single Drive file in place** — `gdriveSaveQuiet` lists existing auto files, PATCHes the most recent (or the one tracked by `gdrive-auto-fid`), and deletes the previous tracked auto file (NOT every "leftover" — see note below) so each device converges to one auto file. The historical `GDRIVE_MAX_AUTO` constant went unused and was DELETED — don't look for it. Manual saves still use `pruneByType(existingFiles, "manual", GDRIVE_MAX_MANUAL - 1, token)` after a POST. **Dropbox bugfix:** Dropbox's `cloud.overwrite` is NOT a true PATCH — it uploads a new file (new id) then fire-and-forget removes the old. `patchExisting` used to store the OLD `fid` in `dropbox-auto-fid` and passed it as `keepId` to `deleteLegacyAutos` — when the internal remove silently failed, the leftover stuck around and the user saw 2+ auto files in Settings → Voir mes sauvegardes. The fix prefers `f.id || fid` in both writes so the NEW id is tracked and the leftover is swept on the next save (self-healing). For Drive this is a no-op since PATCH returns the same id. **Multi-device safety:** the convergence promise is now **per DEVICE**, not per account. Earlier, `deleteLegacyAutos` swept "every auto file in the listing whose id isn't keepId" — which included foreign devices' auto files on a multi-device install. Device A's auto-save was silently deleting device B's auto file every cycle, breaking the multi-device guard (device B's file gone → nothing newer to flag on device A's next launch). The fix narrowed the signature to `(autoFiles, oldFid, keepId)` and only deletes the single `oldFid` this device previously tracked. Foreign auto files are NEVER touched. The cloud may therefore hold `N` auto files (one per active device) + up to 3 manual backups, and the launch check sees all of them. **The "14 auto files" fix:** that single-fid sweep had a fatal blind spot — it could only ever delete the ONE file this device tracked, so once N>1 auto files for the SAME device piled up (a lost `gdrive-auto-fid`/`dropbox-auto-fid`, a Dropbox overwrite whose fire-and-forget delete failed, a clock-skew POST, a reinstall…), each save kept the count steady at N forever (remove 1 target, add 1 new). A user reported 14 auto files. The fix: every auto filename now carries a stable device id (`cave-device-id` → `getDeviceId()` → `makeBackupName(data, "auto", deviceId)` → `cave-tabac-auto-<deviceId>-…json`). `deleteLegacyAutos` was replaced by `sweepOwnAutoFiles(autoFiles, keepId)`, which deletes every auto file whose `autoFileDeviceId(name)` equals THIS device's id OR is `null` (legacy unstamped → adopted-and-drained once during the transition), except `keepId`. Auto files stamped with a DIFFERENT device id are foreign and left untouched — so the multi-device guarantee still holds (the account may hold one auto file per active device + up to 3 manual). The reuse-target selection is also device-scoped: `gdriveSaveQuiet` only ever PATCHes/overwrites an auto file that's its own or legacy (`ownAutos`), never hijacks a foreign device's file. `autoFileDeviceId` is a pure helper unit-tested in `gdriveApi.test.ts`; the convergence + multi-device-safety behaviour is locked in `useGdriveSync.test.ts`. **Manual save also tidies:** the sweep was wired only into the auto-save path, but on iOS standalone the silent auto-save often can't refresh an expired token, so the pile never got cleaned there — and a manual save (the obvious "tidy up now" action, token-fresh on every platform) historically skipped auto files entirely. The fix extracted the sweep into the module-level `sweepOwnAutoStragglers(cloud, token, autoFiles, deviceId, keepId)` (shared by `gdriveSaveQuiet`'s inner `sweepOwnAutoFiles` and `gdriveSave`) and called it at the end of the manual save: after the manual `pruneByType`, the manual save keeps THIS device's newest own/legacy auto file and sweeps the rest, leaving foreign stamped autos + every manual file intact. So a user with a straggler pile now has a deterministic, cross-platform cleanup: tap manual save once. **Dropbox: the deletes never actually happened:** the sweeps still didn't converge on Dropbox because **Dropbox serializes writes per namespace and rejects concurrent writes with HTTP 429 `too_many_write_operations`** — Drive tolerates parallel DELETEs, Dropbox does not. The sweep fired ~15 `files/delete_v2` calls at once (`forEach` + fire-and-forget `.catch()`); Dropbox 429'd all but maybe one and the errors were swallowed, so the pile only grew (the user saw 16 auto files, including duplicate device-stamped ones because even the overwrite's own old-file delete collided). The fixes: (1) `sweepOwnAutoStragglers` now deletes **sequentially** (chained, one at a time) and returns a promise; (2) `dropboxProvider.overwrite` no longer does its own internal old-file delete (it raced the sweep) — the sweep owns all auto deletion; (3) `dropboxProvider.remove` retries once on a 429 / `too_many_write_operations`; (4) `pruneByType` (manual rotation) is now provider-aware — it takes the provider's `remove(token,id)` and deletes sequentially (it used to hard-code the Google Drive DELETE URL, so on Dropbox the manual rotation hit `googleapis.com` with a Dropbox token and always failed); (5) `gdriveSaveQuiet`/`gdriveSave` RETURN the sweep promise so the auto-save lock is held until the sequential deletes finish — serialising saves so a later upload can't collide with an earlier save's in-flight deletes (which was ALSO 429-ing the *upload*, leaving `_onSuccess`/the timestamp un-run — the "last save time didn't update" + the false "newer cloud backup" banner both trace back to that). **The same fix also closes the false multi-device banner:** `findNewerCloudBackup` takes an `ownDeviceId` arg and skips any auto file stamped with THIS device's id, so a device's own auto file is never flagged as "a newer cloud backup" even when the local last-save timestamp failed to advance. Foreign-stamped and legacy-unstamped files still qualify. **Visibility + self-heal:** the auto-save path is silent by design, so a genuinely-broken save (e.g. a failed Dropbox silent token refresh) looked identical to "nothing to save". It adds `recordAutosaveDiag()`/`readAutosaveDiag()` (single localStorage slot `cave-autosave-diag`) recording the LAST attempt's outcome at every exit of `gdriveSaveQuiet`, surfaced as a diagnostic line in Settings → Données under the auto-save toggle. It also makes the `quietSaveInProgressRef` guard **self-healing**: the ref has no TTL, so if a prior save ever died without reaching `releaseQuietLock()` the ref would wedge auto-save for the whole session — it only honours the in-progress skip while the companion `cave-autosave-lock` is fresh (< 30 s); a stale lock means the prior save is dead, so the ref is reset and the save proceeds (recorded as `ref-reset-stale`). `sweepOwnAutoStragglers` now returns `{deleted, failed}` (checking `r.ok`, which is meaningful for both providers) so the diagnostic can show `deleted N, failed M`.
- **Restore picker:** `gdriveRestore` lists all files matching the `cave-tabac-` prefix, sorts by `modifiedTime` descending, parses counts from the filename into `option.counts`, and sets `gdriveConfirm({options, sel:0})`. The picker renders counts straight from `option.counts` for new files. Old files without the count suffix fall back to the on-demand `gdriveLoadOptionPayload` lazy fetch.
- **Save type tagging:** every backup JSON includes `_saveType: "manual"` (from `gdriveSave`) or `_saveType: "auto"` (from `gdriveSaveQuiet`). The restore picker displays 💾 / 🔄 accordingly and sorts by actual date so an auto-save appears first if it is the most recent.
- **App preferences:** every export / backup also includes `_settings` — an ALLOWLIST of the user's preferences (language, theme, mode, text size, date format, currency, units, accounting, thresholds, default session weight, list grouping, wishlist sort, section visibility, AI provider + model, cloud destination, auto-save + encryption toggles). Never a sweep of localStorage: see `src/utils/appSettings.ts` for why that would leak a live credential. Applied by `useImportConfirm` on a REPLACE only, never on a merge. Stripped from the staged data before the merge, like `_apiKey` and `_schemaVersion`.
- **Schema version stamp:** every export / backup also includes `_schemaVersion` (constant in `src/constants.ts`, currently `"v6"`, kept in lock-step with the `SK` suffix). Stripped by `useImportConfirm.stageImport` before merge. Future schema migrations can branch on this field instead of guessing — the current code tolerates older backups without the stamp (treated as legacy v6 input).
- The service worker **bypasses caching** for all `googleapis.com`, `accounts.google.com`, and `gstatic.com` requests.
- **Auto-save:** toggle in Settings → `cave-autosave` localStorage flag must be `"1"` for the auto-save effects to fire. When enabled, each `gdriveSaveQuiet` **overwrites THIS DEVICE's single auto file in place** (multi-device-scoped and device-stamped): list → reuse the device's own auto file tracked in `gdrive-auto-fid` / `dropbox-auto-fid` (or, as fallback, the newest auto file belonging to this device — `ownAutos[0]`) → write → `sweepOwnAutoFiles` deletes this device's other auto files + any legacy unstamped ones, leaving foreign devices' stamped auto files untouched. The file is named `cave-tabac-auto-<deviceId>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-tN-pN-wN-aN-jN.json` (the `<deviceId>` was woven in) and gets renamed on every save so the timestamp + counts reflect the latest state. `gdrive-auto-fid` localStorage caches the file ID for fast PATCH; a 404 on stale fid falls back to POST. **This whole path is provider-agnostic** — the same `gdriveSaveQuiet` runs for BOTH Google Drive and Dropbox via the `cloud` provider abstraction (`gdriveProvider` / `dropboxProvider`) and the `AUTO_FID_KEY = isDbx ? "dropbox-auto-fid" : "gdrive-auto-fid"` switch, so the device-id convergence fix applies to Dropbox identically. Shows an amber banner when data is unsynced; saves silently on `visibilitychange` if the token is still valid. **Audit Finding #1 — mid-upload snapshot re-check:** `_onSuccess` uploads the `rawSnap` frozen at the START of the quiet save. Before it clears `pendingSync`, it re-reads `localStorage[SK]` and compares against `rawSnap`: if the data ADVANCED during the in-flight upload (an edit landed whose own quiet save hit the in-progress skip and never rescheduled), it does NOT declare "synced" — it keeps the dirty flag and re-arms a follow-up `gdriveSaveQuiet()` on an 800 ms timer, so the newer snapshot reaches the cloud and the multi-device guard compares against the right reference. Locked by the "keeps pendingSync dirty + re-arms when data changes mid-upload" test in `useGdriveSync.test.ts`.
- **Token caching:** OAuth token stored in `sessionStorage` key `gdrive-tk` (TTL ~1h) for non-iOS browsers. On iOS standalone (redirect OAuth), `localStorage` is used instead because `sessionStorage` does not survive the OAuth redirect. `tkClear()` always wipes both storages. On 401/403, both `gdriveSave` and `gdriveRestore` clear the stale token and **auto-retry once** with a fresh token — no user action required.
- **Drive backup includes photos:** local photos are keyed as `local-photo-*` in `imageUrl`; `gdriveSave` / `gdriveSaveQuiet` call `gatherLocalImages()` to collect the base64 blobs and store them in `_imageData` in the backup JSON. On restore, `doGdriveConfirm` re-populates IndexedDB from `_imageData` — only entries whose key starts with `local-photo-` and whose value matches `/^data:image\/(jpeg|jpg|png|webp|gif);/` are accepted.
- **Auto-save self-healing:** the token expires after ~1 h. On Android/desktop, `gdriveSaveQuiet` already renews silently via `initTokenClient({prompt:""})` when the cache is empty; in-place 401/403 auto-retry covers the three Drive API branches (POST, PATCH, LIST) so a server-side rotation/skew doesn't cost a sync cycle. On iOS standalone PWA the silent refresh path can't run (no popups, redirect leaves the PWA) — instead, `triggerIosAutosaveReauth()` piggybacks on **any user save action** to kick off the iOS OAuth redirect with `ac="autosave"`. The redirect bounces back immediately when SSO + consent are already in place; the dispatcher then captures the token and fires `gdriveSaveQuiet()` with NO modal / NO status banner. Two guards prevent fires from non-user contexts: (a) a module-scope `lastUserGestureTs` updated by capturing pointer/key events — the helper short-circuits when the gesture is > 2 s old (so the 30-day trash cleanup at mount can't accidentally redirect); (b) all the existing condition guards (auto-save on, no pending OAuth in flight, token expired or < 5 min left, user has engaged with Drive before via `gdrive-auto-fid` / `gdrive-fid` / `cave-autosave-ts`). The hook is wired centrally at the end of `save()` in App.tsx so EVERY data-mutating user action (form save, lot save, tasting end, status chip tap, stars, soft-delete, trash bulk, etc.) covers iOS automatically. The 9+ explicit wirings inside individual save handlers are redundant with this central hook but kept as documentation of intent. **Banner gating:** `CuratorDriveExpiredBanner` now requires `pendingSync` (or its localStorage mirror `cave-pending-sync === "1"`) to render. Pure browsing for > 1 h without a change no longer trips the banner — only an actual unsynced modification does. **Permanent mute removed:** because the banner is now both rare and genuinely actionable, the Settings → "Bannière session expirée" toggle AND the in-banner "Ne plus notifier" button were dropped. Silencing a real "you have unsaved changes that can't sync" warning is worse than putting up with it. The session × dismiss stays for transient acknowledgement. The `cave-show-drive-expired-banner` localStorage key + the `saveShowDriveExpiredBanner` setter + the `settings_drive_expired_banner` / `settings_drive_expired_hint` / `btn_stop_notifying` / `aria_stop_notifying` i18n keys are all removed.
- **Settings modal banner re-evaluation:** The inline `Notice` ("Session Drive expirée") inside `SettingsModal.tsx` reads `tkGet()` at render time. localStorage writes don't trigger React re-renders — pre-a successful Reconnect left the Notice visibly stale until the parent re-rendered for some other reason. A `setInterval` tick at the modal level (gated on `importModal` so it only runs while the modal is open) forces a re-evaluation every 4 s, matching the global `CuratorDriveExpiredBanner`. Without this, the bug from the user's screenshot — token successfully captured but Notice still showing "Session Drive expirée" — recurs.
- **OAuth diagnostic line:** `Settings → Drive` surfaces a small italic line right under the expired-session Notice showing the most recent OAuth touchpoint via `readOAuthEvent()` (`src/utils/oauthDiag.ts`). Recorded events: `redirect-start`, `return-success`, `return-no-token`, `return-error`, `state-mismatch`, `token-stored`. The action context (`autosave` / `reconnect` / `save`…) is included where relevant. Powers diagnoses like "OAuth completed but banner stayed" — if the line shows `return-success` without an action, the read-before-clear invariant is broken somewhere.
- **Reconnect always interactive:** `gdriveReconnect` calls `gdriveGetToken("reconnect", true)` → `prompt=select_account` → 1-tap picker (login_hint pre-selects the previous account). The silent path is unreliable on iOS PWA (Google's `prompt=""` routinely returns to the PWA without a token even when SSO seems valid); an explicit user tap on Reconnect = explicit intent to fix things now, so single-tap success is required. Earlier approaches used silent-first, then silent-first-with-escalation; both stranded users in the silent-fail case. The silent OAuth path is preserved exclusively for `triggerIosAutosaveReauth` (the save-tap piggyback that auto-fires on every mutation) — that path is allowed to fail silently because the banner is the fallback.

## Image Handling

- **Locally uploaded photos** (`handlePhotoUpload`): resized to max 800px JPEG 80% via canvas, then stored **directly in IndexedDB** under a unique key `local-photo-{timestamp}-{suffix}` (audit S3: the `{suffix}` is `newPhotoSuffix()` in `utils.ts` — an 8-char `crypto.randomUUID` slice, base36-random fallback — so two uploads in the same millisecond can't mint the same key and clobber each other's blob; the leading `Date.now()` digits are preserved so `gcOrphans`' `^local-photo-(\d+)` age guard still matches). The `imageUrl` field stores that key, never the raw base64. On load, the `data` useEffect resolves all `local-photo-*` keys from IndexedDB into `imgLocal` — it also walks session `tobaccoSnapshot`/`pipeSnapshot` refs so a fantôme session's frozen photo still resolves after its parent entity is purged. **Error handling:** an `img.onerror` / `reader.onerror` now raises the `photoErr` banner (`err_photo_read`) instead of failing silently, and the IndexedDB write falls back to embedding the base64 inline in `imageUrl` (so a photo is never lost if the DB write fails). Max upload size: 20 MB (guard fires before FileReader). **Round-14 HIGH (critical): `imgCache.put` RESOLVES `false` on a transaction failure (quota-exceeded / private mode / abort), it does NOT reject — it only rejects when `open()` fails.** So `handlePhotoUpload` MUST inspect the resolved value (`ok === false → cb(du, du)` inline fallback), NOT rely on `.catch` (which only catches the `open()` rejection). Before the fix, the `.then` ran with `ok===false` and still confirmed the `local-photo-*` key whose blob never persisted → the photo rendered that session then vanished on reload (silent cover-photo loss, exactly the near-quota case the fallback comment claimed to cover but didn't). The same fix protects `PipeFormView`'s extra-photo add (it already rejects a non-`local-photo-` key). `imgCache.put` also resolves `false` on `t.onabort` (some engines abort rather than error on quota) so the promise can't hang. **Any new caller of `imgCache.put` MUST treat a `false` resolution as a write failure, never trust `.then` alone.**
- **LOCAL PHOTOS ONLY (the URL feature is fully removed)**: photos are added ONLY via device upload (`handlePhotoUpload` → `local-photo-*` key in IndexedDB). The external-URL image feature was removed in stages and is now GONE as if it never existed — URL entry, the `dlImg` network fetcher + `doFetchUrl` / `fetchImgAsBase64` + corsproxy/allorigins proxies + their CSP entries, and the launch-time conversion hook `useUrlImageMigration`. **The only remaining trace is a permanent guard-rail in `migrateData` (`_clearForeignImageRefs`, formerly named `_clearExternalUrlImages`)**: any `imageUrl` that is not one of the TWO legitimate shapes — a `local-photo-*` key, or the quota fallback's `data:image/(jpeg|jpg|png|webp|gif);` URI — is CLEARED to "". It was an `^https?://` blocklist before it became an allowlist — a protocol-relative `//host/x.png` and a `data:image/svg+xml` both walked past it; `isLocalPhotoRef` in `utils/imgCache.ts` is the shared predicate, used here AND at the form preview's `<img src>` (`safeImgSrc`), the one sink `safeBgUrl` does not cover. `migrateData` runs on load AND on every import/restore path, so a restored backup can never reintroduce a URL image. It's pure + synchronous (no network, no conversion — just blank) and covers entities + frozen session snapshots; `imageUrl` is never an identity key, so clearing it breaks no reference. `isSafeExternalUrl` + `safeBgUrl` STAY (pure URL-safety helpers, no network — used by CSS `background` sanitisation + the lightbox src guard).
- **Export/backup/restore**: unchanged — once `imageUrl` is a `local-photo-*` key, `withPhotos` / `gatherLocalImages` embed the bytes, so JSON/CSV/ZIP/Drive/Dropbox backups carry only local photos (the ZIP path no longer fetches URLs — it only emits the `withPhotos`-resolved `data:` blobs).
- **Lightbox**: shows the local photo resolved from `imgLocal` (no network fetch). **For a `local-photo-*` key NOT in `imgLocal`** (an additional pipe photo — see `pipe.photos`), it resolves the blob on demand from `imgCache` (IndexedDB) so the extra photos still open full-screen.
- **Additional pipe photos (PIPES ONLY — `pipe.photos: string[]`, max 6)**: extra local photos, keyed `local-photo-*` like the cover but **never loaded into the global `imgLocal`**. `PipeExtraPhotos` (form) + `PipeDetailGallery` (fiche) each keep a small local `previews` state and fetch only the missing keys from `imgCache` when that surface is open. This keeps a big pipe collection cheap: only the cover of each pipe is eager; the gallery bytes load per-pipe on demand. `useOrphanPhotoGC` (referenced set) and `gatherLocalImages` (backup) both walk `photos` so the blobs are never GC'd and always ride along in Drive/JSON/ZIP backups.
- **IndexedDB** (`cave-imgs`, object store `i`): store for **all** local photos (keyed `local-photo-{timestamp}`). Populated by `imgCache.put(key, base64)`. Helper module: `src/utils/imgCache.ts`.
- **`imgLocal` React state**: maps `imageUrl` key → base64, populated on data load for all `local-photo-*` keys and filled on demand for URL images.
- **Export/backup**: all functions (`doExport`, `doBackupZip`, `gdriveSave`, `gdriveSaveQuiet`) call `withPhotos()` or `gatherLocalImages()` to resolve `local-photo-*` keys to actual base64 before writing output. `doExport` and `doBackupZip` embed the COVER base64 directly in `imageUrl` (`doBackupZip` also writes the covers as separate files in the ZIP image folders). `withPhotos` now ALSO attaches the FULL `_imageData` map (like Drive), so the additional pipe photos (`pipe.photos[]`) and session-snapshot photos — which the cover-only inlining misses — travel with JSON export + ZIP too (they used to be exported as bare `local-photo-*` keys with no blob → placeholders on a fresh-device restore). Drive/Dropbox backups already stored the full map in `_imageData`. The import (`_runImport`) validates + re-imports `_imageData` to IndexedDB on restore.
- **Legacy `QuotaExceededError` migration**: if an old save fails due to localStorage overflow, `save()` still migrates any remaining base64 `imageUrl` values to IndexedDB (keyed `local-photo-<type>-<id>`) and warns the user. New uploads never reach this path since photos go to IndexedDB immediately.

## Security

### Content Security Policy (CSP)

A `<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy">` tag is present in `index.html` (root level, second line after `<meta charset>`). **If you add a new external API endpoint or CDN script, you must update the CSP accordingly.**

Key directives:
- `connect-src`: whitelisted domains are `api.anthropic.com`, `api.openai.com`, `generativelanguage.googleapis.com`, `www.googleapis.com`, `accounts.google.com`, `oauth2.googleapis.com`, `api.dropboxapi.com`, `content.dropboxapi.com` (the last two added with the Dropbox provider), `nominatim.openstreetmap.org` (session-location reverse geocoding, see geo.ts). The image proxies `corsproxy.io` / `api.allorigins.win` were **removed** (local-photos-only). Any fetch to an unlisted domain will be blocked.
- `frame-src`: `https://www.openstreetmap.org` only — the per-session OSM map iframe (the geolocation work). `form-action`: `'self' https://accounts.google.com`.
- `script-src`: `'self'`, `cdnjs.cloudflare.com`, `accounts.google.com`, `apis.google.com`. No `'unsafe-inline'` — the built HTML has no inline scripts.
- `style-src`: `'self'`, `'unsafe-inline'`, `accounts.google.com` — needed for inline `<style>` tags.
- `font-src`: `'self'` only (fonts are self-hosted under `public/fonts/`). Do NOT re-add `fonts.gstatic.com`.
- `frame-ancestors 'none'`: **INERT, and kept deliberately — this line used to claim it "prevents clickjacking via iframes" and that was FALSE.** CSP Level 3 §3.3 requires a user agent to REMOVE `frame-ancestors` (with `report-uri` and `sandbox`) from a policy delivered by a `<meta>` element, so no browser has ever honoured it here — **Chromium says so in the console, verbatim: *"The Content Security Policy directive 'frame-ancestors' is ignored when delivered via a `<meta>` element."*** The header form would work and the app cannot send one: GitHub Pages serves static files with no header customisation and there is no `_headers` / `netlify.toml` / reverse proxy in front of `t-cellar.app`. It STAYS because it is the correct directive the day this is served behind something that can send headers, and because deleting it invites the next reader to "add clickjacking protection" and put it straight back — so index.html carries a comment saying it is inert and naming the real defence. **THE REAL DEFENCE IS `src/utils/frameGuard.ts`, which refuses to RENDER a framed document.** See that module for the risk analysis; the short version is that an attacker cannot READ a cross-origin frame, so nothing leaks, but they can UI-redress a frame showing the visitor's REAL cellar — and while the reset and « Vider la corbeille » sit behind `window.confirm` (browser chrome, not overlayable) and an ordinary delete is a soft-delete with a 30-day trash, the cloud-newer banner's « Restaurer » is a genuine one-click `stageImport(…, {autoApply:"replace"})` with no confirmation (recorded deliberately above). **"Do not render" is the defence and the bust-out is only best-effort** — MEASURED in a real cross-origin frame, Chromium refuses it (*"Unsafe attempt to initiate navigation for frame with URL …"*), which is exactly the drive-by case that matters; the notice's link carries `target="_top"` and works because a user CLICK grants activation. The guard lives in `main.jsx` pre-mount, NOT as an inline script (the CSP is `script-src 'self'` with no `'unsafe-inline'` — our own policy would block it, the boot-strings reasoning), and it gates the mount AND the service-worker registration (installing the offline machinery for a page the user never chose to open is not something a refused document should do). Its six strings live in the SAME `BOOT` table as the boot shell — one pre-mount language axis, already covered by doc:check gate 15; a second map is the shape a whole release was spent removing. Verified end to end in Chromium with two static servers on different ports (top level boots normally, cross-origin frame shows only the notice); probed four ways, each reddening.
- `upgrade-insecure-requests`: forces HTTP sub-resources to HTTPS.
- `object-src 'none'`: no browser plugins.
- `base-uri 'self'`: prevents `<base>` tag injection.
- `worker-src 'self'`: service worker only from same origin.
- `img-src 'self' data: blob: https:`: allows all HTTPS image sources (user-provided tobacco/pipe images can come from any domain).

### OAuth CSRF

The `gdrive-state` localStorage key holds a random token set before the OAuth redirect. On callback, the app rejects the response if either the stored state or the returned state is absent or mismatched (`!st || !expectedSt || st !== expectedSt`). Never weaken this guard to `&&`.

The pending OAuth action (`gdrive-pending`) is validated against a whitelist (`"save"`, `"restore"`, `"reconnect"`, `"list"`, or `"autosave"`) before dispatch. Any other value is ignored.

### OAuth flow — iOS standalone vs. non-iOS

**Non-iOS (popup):** uses Google's `gsi/client` `initTokenClient` (popup mode). Officially supported by Google for client-side apps. No code exchange or client_secret needed.

**iOS standalone (redirect):** uses `window.location.replace()` with `response_type=token` (implicit grant). This navigates within the PWA webview — `initTokenClient` always opens a popup which leaves the PWA, causing the callback to never fire (stuck on "Connexion..."). PKCE (`response_type=code`) also fails because Google **Web Application** OAuth clients require `client_secret` for the token exchange, which cannot be embedded in client-side code. `response_type=token` is therefore the **only viable option** for this combination (iOS standalone + Web Application OAuth client + no backend). A cryptographically-random CSRF state (from `pkceGenerateVerifier()`) is stored in `gdrive-state` before the redirect and validated on return.

**Do NOT "fix" the iOS standalone flow to use PKCE or `initTokenClient`** — both have been tried and both fail. The token is returned in `#access_token=...` and processed by the App.tsx hash handler. PKCE helpers (`pkceGenerateVerifier`, `pkceChallengeFromVerifier`) are kept for the CSRF state generation and their test suite.

### Import hardening

- `_imageData` on Drive restore (`doGdriveConfirm`) and JSON import (`doImportFile`): keys must start with `local-photo-`, values must match `/^data:image\/(jpeg|jpg|png|webp|gif);/`. Anything else is silently discarded before touching IndexedDB.
- ID counters (`nxT/nxW/nxP/nxA/nxJ`) are clamped to integers ≥ 1 in `migrateData` on every load and import.

### SSRF mitigation

`isSafeExternalUrl(url)` in `src/utils/imgCache.ts` is a pure URL-safety predicate (no network — the app makes no external image fetch at all). It's used by `safeBgUrl` and the lightbox src guard. It rejects non-HTTP(S) protocols, `localhost`/`127.x`, RFC-1918 ranges (10.x, 172.16–31.x, 192.168.x), link-local (169.254.x), and bare hostnames without a dot.

`safeBgUrl(url)` (same module) wraps a URL safely for use in CSS `background: url(...)`. Same SSRF guard plus a CSS-metacharacter reject list (`"`, `'`, `(`, `)`, `\`, `;`, whitespace). Every Curator view that interpolates a URL into a `background` style uses `safeBgUrl`. Tests in `src/__tests__/safeBgUrl.test.ts` lock this in (26 cases). (The old `dlImg.test.ts` was removed with `dlImg`.)

## Accessibility invariants

Hand-audited and locked by `src/__tests__/a11y.curator.test.tsx` (jest-axe smoke test on every top-level Curator view, WCAG 2.1 A/AA ruleset, fails CI on any serious/critical violation).

- **Focus indicators**: every `<input>` / `<textarea>` / `<select>` that calls `outline: "none"` MUST pair with `useFocusRing()` (`src/components/curator/FormFields.tsx`) — the hook applies a 2px brass `boxShadow` on focus. Never reintroduce a bare `outline: "none"` without a replacement. `PressCard` carries its own focus ring via local state.
- **Form labels**: `TextField` / `TextAreaField` / `SelectField` (FormFields) generate `useId()` and pass `htmlFor` to a real `<label>`. Standalone inputs in views (SearchModal, SessionFormView tasting-notes textarea, TastingView weight/notes, SettingsModal sessDefaultWeight + ApiKeyInput) MUST set an `aria-label`.
- **Touch targets.** **The two standards, because 44 gets quoted without its source**: WCAG **2.2 SC 2.5.8 "Target Size (Minimum)" is 24 × 24 and level AA** — the bar normally required; WCAG 2.1 SC 2.5.5 "Enhanced" is 44 × 44 and level **AAA**, which is also Apple's HIG figure. **This project adopted 44 as a house invariant**, stricter than compliance demands — so a sub-44 element is not automatically a defect, and a measurement against 44 needs saying so. `IconBtn` default `size = 44`. `ActiveFilterPill` clear button = 28 minimum. `ApiKeyInput` reveal/save/clear buttons = 36 minimum. Never drop these below the documented minima.
- **The 12 filter/sort `<select>`s, which failed even AA.** Measured across five screens at 390 px: they were **18–20 px tall inside a 36 px wrapper** that carried the border and the background. So the control LOOKED 36 px and only its middle third opened the list — `elementFromPoint` on the wrapper's padding returns the `<div>`, which has no handler. **That is worse than a small control**: a small one you aim at, one that looks twice its size you miss without understanding why. (`appearance: "none"` also disqualifies them from SC 2.5.8's "user agent control" exception — the author modified the presentation.) The fix moves the wrapper's vertical padding onto the select (`alignSelf: "stretch"` + `minHeight: 44` on the wrapper, `padding: "0 …"`), so the whole visible box is live: **42 px, top/middle/bottom all hitting the select**, verified with `elementFromPoint`. Four views: Pipes / Acc / Inventory / Journal.
- **`ToggleBtn` is `flex: "0 0 44px"`, not a bare `width: 44`** — flex-shrink defaults to 1, so on the busiest row (the tobacco list) they were squeezed to 42. **A declared 44 the layout quietly overrules is worse than no declaration: it reads as compliant in the source.** **AND THE FIX CAUSED A REGRESSION THAT HAD TO BE FIXED IN TURN** — non-shrinking toggles pushed that row past the viewport in German at the L text size (measured before/after at 360 and 390 px: no overflow before, overflow after). A flex item defaults to `min-width: auto`, so the sort wrapper beside them refused to yield the 8 px; it now carries `minWidth: 0`. **Trading a 2 px accessibility shortfall for a horizontal overflow is a bad trade** — measure the row after any change here. Locked by `tapTargets.test.ts`, whose own first version was satisfied by the fix's explanatory COMMENT and so stayed green under probe; it blanks comments now, the third time that trap has been hit.
- **Still under 24 (AA) and NOT fixed — a decision, not a backlog item**: the Home activity-calendar cells (30 × 11, ~70 of them), the maturity-band chips (49–84 × 14) and the chart bar rows (160 × 17 / 162 × 20). Each is a **density decision on a validated layout** — enlarging the calendar cells to 24 would roughly triple the calendar's height. The available fix is an invisible hit-area padding (keep the visual bar, grow the button box); it was put to the user and **declined**, so do not "finish the sweep". Re-open it only if someone asks.
- **The SETTINGS modal was measured and is CLEAN** — 90 interactive controls across the four tabs, at 390 px/M in French and 360 px/"L" in German: **nothing under 24 × 24, and no dead zones**. Worth recording because it was the one dense surface the pass never reached (the harness selector timed out), so its status was unknown rather than good. The 35 + 19 controls between 24 and 43 are the Segmented options (34 px tall), the toggle switches (26) and the numeric inputs (36–40) — under this project's house 44, above the AA bar, and each is a row of a scrolling settings list rather than an icon floating in a layout.
