Opening the edit form of an imported item therefore fired a request to the author's host: IP, User-Agent, and confirmation that the file was imported. Not code execution — an `<img>` cannot run SVG script — but a **tracking beacon inside a shared backup**, and it contradicts `public/privacy.html` verbatim (« Photos (locales uniquement) … ne transitent par aucun service tiers »). Reachable via JSON import (BOTH replace and merge — `migrateData` runs on the merge result too) and via cloud restore; NOT via CSV, which forces `imageUrl: ""`. **The fix is an ALLOWLIST, `isLocalPhotoRef`, because enumerating what is BAD is exactly what had already missed twice from one anchor**: an `imageUrl` has had precisely two legitimate shapes made the app local-photos-only — a `local-photo-*` key, or a `data:image/(jpeg|jpg|png|webp|gif);` URI, which is the **quota fallback** and must keep working (a naive `isSafeExternalUrl` guard here would have broken it, which is why the sink was left unguarded in the first place). Applied at BOTH ends sharing that one predicate — `migrateData` (renamed `_clearForeignImageRefs`, since a name that says "external URL" would now be lying) so nothing poisoned is ever stored, and `safeImgSrc` at the sink so a value arriving any other way still cannot beacon. An unresolved `local-photo-*` key is deliberately still passed to `src`: as a relative URL it 404s on our own origin, no external request, which is the pre-existing behaviour for an evicted photo. Probed three ways (restore the anchor, restore the bare `<img>`, widen the allowlist to any `data:`) — 6, 1 and 4 cases redden respectively. **A case had asserted that `migrateData` does NOT blank `"__proto__"`, with the stated reason that scrubbing it would make the downstream guards pass vacuously — that is exactly what happened, and the reversal is recorded on the assertion**: those guards are defence in depth for a caller handing over a plain map (every fixture, three form views), so they are still exercised directly, without going through the source.

**Same build — the cloud-newer banner said « synchroniser » and did a REPLACE.** `restoreCloudNewerBackup` is the app's only `autoApply: "replace"` call site: it skips the Replace/Merge picker, shows no diff and offers no undo, while all six languages' `cloud_newer_banner` said *restore it to SYNC this device* — and sync is the MERGE word. It matters most for the exact user it appears to, because `findNewerCloudBackup` compares the cloud file against **this device's last CLOUD save, not its last local edit**, so the banner surfaces precisely when there is unsynced local work to lose. The text now names the replacement in each language's own word (remplace / replaces / sustituye / ersetzt / sostituisce / substitui), and a test asserts none of them says "sync" and that there is still exactly ONE `autoApply: "replace"` call site — the wording is only honest while the action stays the one it describes. **SETTLED BY THE USER: it goes through the Replace/Merge PICKER now**, so the app has NO auto-applied replace left in production. The decision it reverses is recorded in `useImportConfirm` («the picker would just add an extra confirm step with no useful choice — there's no other reasonable interpretation»); there IS another one, MERGE, and this is exactly the banner where it matters, since `findNewerCloudBackup` compares against this device's last CLOUD save rather than its last local edit. **`setImportModal(true)` is REQUIRED alongside the staging, not decoration**: the picker is rendered by `SettingsModal`, which `CuratorApp` only mounts while `importModal` is set, so staging without opening it would leave the import pending with NOTHING on screen — a worse defect than the one being fixed. Two tests recorded the reversal on their own assertions (`useGdriveSync.test.ts`'s « the third arg requests an auto-replace, so the user never sees the picker », and the « exactly ONE call site » case, which now asserts ZERO across all three hooks with comments stripped first). The `autoApply` OPTION stays — `"merge"` has a live caller (the CSV import) sharing the same code path. Probed: restoring the auto-replace reddens 2 cases. **The size question the previous sentence left open was settled, and it is NOT "raise Restaurer to 44".** The state was: `Restaurer` at `minHeight: 44` on Home and **28 in the global Overlays copy**, with a **28 px dismiss ×** beside it in a `gap: 8` row. So the HARMLESS action was the harder of the two to hit, 8 px from a button that replaces the entire cellar — and a miss lands on the destructive one. **The house 44 exists so a control can be REACHED, not so a destructive control is easier to hit by accident**, which is why the obvious reading of the rule is the wrong fix here. The rule the two copies now share: **the DISMISS is never smaller than « Restaurer », and they are never adjacent.** The Overlays × goes 28 → 44 and a 14 px `aria-hidden` gutter separates the pair; Home was already 44 on both, so only the separation was missing there. **« Restaurer » stays at 28 in Overlays deliberately** — the smaller target of the two, recorded in a comment so a future sweep does not "complete" the house rule on it. Locked by the « cloud-newer banner: the dismiss is the bigger target » block in `Overlays.test.tsx`, which asserts the × is ≥ 44 **and ≥ Restaurer** (the relative half is the one that carries the rule) and that a gutter element sits between them; probed by reverting both, which reddens it.

**Two fixes, and which one carries the guarantee matters.** `safeBgUrl` is now TOTAL (`String()` on entry): it is the single choke point all 18 sites funnel through, so the guarantee holds **even for a caller that hands it a plain map** — which is what every test fixture does, and what three form views and `useImportConfirm` still could. `imgMap` (`Object.create(null)`) is the root-cause fix and it is DEFENCE IN DEPTH, not the crash fix: it stops a prototype member leaving the lookup at all. Note what it does NOT do — the fallback is `|| x.imageUrl`, so the poisoned string still reaches `safeBgUrl` and the card still shows an empty photo box either way. Choosing the choke point over the source is the whole lesson: **the source is nine sites and the choke point is one.**

**The nine sites are why `imgMap` exists rather than nine inline `Object.create(null)` calls**: the initial state, four updaters in `App.tsx`, one in `useImportConfirm`, and one in each of the three form views — and every one of them was `Object.assign({}, prev, …)`, which throws the prototype straight back on. `imgMapIsSafe.test.ts` sweeps them by keying on the SETTER (`setImgLocal`), never on a spelling of the rebuild, with comments blanked first and a non-vacuity case asserting the setter is still found in each file. `tabac-local/no-dynamic-index-plain-map` could not see any of this: the map is React state, not a module-level `const`.

**Probed four ways, each reddening on its own** — dropping the coercion, giving `imgMap` a prototype, reverting one of the nine sites, and the end-to-end case: rendering the REAL `InventoryListView` over the REAL `migrateData` output reproduces `TypeError: url.indexOf is not a function` on the old code and passes on the new. `forgedImageUrl.test.ts` also asserts `migrateData` still does NOT blank the poisoned value, so the guards it locks cannot start passing vacuously.

**One regression of my own, worth recording because the mock was right to break.** `useImportConfirm.test.ts` mocks `../utils/imgCache.ts` wholesale, so the new export was missing and five `_imageData` cases died. The mock now carries the REAL `imgMap`, not a stub — a stub returning `Object.assign({}, …)` would have made the suite green against a photo map that has a prototype, i.e. it would hide the defect the sibling test exists to lock.

**Open at the time of the same review and NOT fixed then** (each needed a decision, unlike this one) — **all three have since been CLOSED**, and the list is kept rather than deleted so the record of what that review found stays intact: an imported `_apiKey` was written on MERGE as well as replace, so accepting a shared file redirected your AI calls to the sender's billing and console (**since fixed**, on the user's decision); `frame-ancestors 'none'` sat in a `<meta>` CSP where the spec requires browsers to ignore it, with GitHub Pages unable to send the header (**since fixed** — the directive stays, labelled inert, and `frameGuard.ts` is the real defence); and « Effacer toutes les données » left `dropbox-rt`, the three AI keys and `gdrive-account-hint` (an e-mail address) in localStorage, harmless with one user and a mislabel for a public one (**since fixed**).


## A lot says where its grams went

**A lot now says where its grams went, and the feature was the small half of the build.** Reported: « quand je vais sur un lot j'aimerais avoir la date de chaque session avec le grammage fumé avec un lien sur la session ». The gap was real and had a shape worth naming — **the lot fiche stated what was LEFT and never what became of the rest, while the journal could be filtered by tobacco but never by LOT**, so the one screen that raises the question was the one screen that could not answer it. The lot detail modal now lists its sessions (date · time · grams, newest first), each row a real button that opens that session's own fiche.

**Three things were EXTRACTED or REUSED rather than written a second time**, which is this file's most repeated lesson. (a) `compareSessionsRecent` (utils.ts) is JournalView's inline `sortBy === "date"` comparator, moved: two of its four rungs are not re-derivable by eye — timed-before-untimed is handled EXPLICITLY because locale collation does not rank punctuation against digits predictably, and the final `id`-DESC tie-break is what keeps the order stable after a restore scrambles `data.sessions`. (b) `sessionsForLot` owns the filter, `String()`-ed on BOTH sides because the lot `id` is numeric and `session.lotId` is a string — a raw `===` matches nothing and would render an empty list on a lot that has been smoked. It refuses an EMPTY lot id rather than gathering every orphan under whichever lot is open. (c) the row's accessible name is `aria_session_card`, the key the journal cards already use, so the two doors to a session announce identically.

**`crossOpenSession` (App.tsx) is the counterpart of `crossOpenDetail` for the one overlay that is not an entity fiche, and it needed NO change to the back engine.** It records the origin with `pushDrillOrigin` and deliberately does NOT set `drillOverlayRef`: that latch means "the open OVERLAY was drill-opened" and `decideBack`'s pop branch lists only detail/pipe/acc/wishlist, so claiming it for a session modal would assert something the branch cannot see. The sequence falls out of the existing rules — first back hits `close-session`, second finds a non-empty stack and pops to the origin. The lot modal's state is deliberately LEFT ARMED on the way out: the fiche's subtree unmounts on nav so nothing is on screen, and the pop re-opens the very lot the user was reading.

**The modal moved to `capHeight`, which the rule requires the moment a modal can exceed the screen** — a 100 g tin can carry forty bowls. `capHeight` + an inner `flex: 1; minHeight: 0; overflowY: auto; overscrollBehavior: contain`, never a `vh` cap.

**A TOTAL was considered and deliberately NOT shown, and rendering it is what settled the question.** The modal already gives initial and current, whose difference IS the grams smoked; a third figure can disagree with them (a hand-edited weight, a disposed lot, rounding). In the render fixture the seven sessions summed to 17.6 g against a 19 g drop — exactly the confusion a total would have manufactured.

**THE OTHER HALF OF THE BUILD: rendering the modal found a PRE-EXISTING clip that three checkers cannot see.** In German the Close/Delete/Edit row needed **349 px in a 340 px box at the DEFAULT text size** (375 at "L") and the third button read « BEARBE », cut at the panel edge — measured identical at HEAD, so it is not from this change, and it bites an ordinary German phone at the default setting rather than at some extreme. They are single words, so a flex item at its default `min-width: auto` could only clip; `flexWrap` costs a line ONLY where the three do not fit (verified in a browser: one line in fr / en / pt, two in de) and clips nothing — the remedy for the same arithmetic on the list controls rows. **The screen IS in the checkers' list (`modal-lot`), which is what makes the gap worth recording: `i18n:layout` fails on a page-level `scrollWidth`, on `nowrap`/ellipsis text, and (more recently) on a draggable horizontal scroller — and this is none of the three.** Content simply painted past a hidden-overflow panel. **Not fixed here** (widening a checker mid-feature is the wrong moment, per the rule about refusal sets) but it is the next thing to close: an element whose `scrollWidth` exceeds its `clientWidth` inside an `overflow: hidden` ancestor is invisible to every rule we have.

**Probed in seven directions**, each reddening on its own: dropping either load-bearing rung of the comparator, keeping soft-deleted sessions, neutering the row handler, dropping `capHeight`, dropping the overscroll containment, passing every session unfiltered, and removing the wrap. **One probe came back green and the FIXTURE was at fault, not the code** — the timed-before-untimed case used ids whose DESC order happened to agree with the right answer, so the tie-break absorbed the mutation; the ids were inverted so the later rung now contradicts the earlier one. Same shape as the photo cap: *when a probe stays green, find out which layer absorbs it.* **A process note worth keeping: `git checkout <file>` was used to undo a probe on an UNCOMMITTED file and reverted the whole feature with it.** Recovered from a scratch copy. Undo a probe by restoring the copy you took, never with `git checkout`, while the work is unstaged.


## The session mechanic — which lots a session may charge

**The session mechanic audited end to end, and THREE of its findings were one root cause: two predicates disagreed about which lots a session may charge.** `pickJarLot` accepted any jar; `isUsableLot` refuses a jar carrying an EXPLICIT `"0"` (an empty tin). The disagreement is reachable and was **REPRODUCED before anything was changed**: a tobacco with a 0 g jar AND a full cellar lot is offered in both session pickers (the cellar lot makes it usable), and the auto-select then landed on the EMPTY JAR — which is absent from the picker's option list. **A `<select>` whose value matches no option displays its FIRST one**, so the screen showed the cellar lot while the state held the empty jar, and the session was capped to 0 g against it. From there the two visible symptoms follow: a live tasting could be ignited pointing at a lot that resolves to nothing, and 95 minutes later the auto-end **DESTROYED it** — `_persistSession` refuses a positive weight with no resolvable lot, and the auto path clears the tasting state whether the save succeeded or not (a stuck zombie tasting being the worse outcome), then announced « clôturée automatiquement après N min ». A whole dégustation lost, under a success sentence. **Four fixes, and they are deliberately layered rather than one clever guard**: `pickJarLot` now takes `isUsableLot` (still jar-only — that is its contract, and `_persistSession` refuses a cellar lot outright); the duplicated auto-select block became `pickSessionLot` in `lotUtils` — **best usable jar, else the oldest usable CELLAR lot — so the chosen lot is guaranteed BY CONSTRUCTION to be one the picker will list**, which is what makes the display/state divergence impossible rather than merely unlikely; `canIgnite` requires a lot that RESOLVES among the usable ones (not merely a non-empty `lotId`, since a setup persisted across relaunches can point at a lot finished since); and the auto-end says `tasting_err_autoend_failed` when the save did not happen. **The gate and the message are both needed** — one stops it happening, the other stops the app lying about it if it ever does. Three smaller ones in the same pass: the auto-end **no longer navigates** (`addSessionFromTasting(form, {navigate:false})`) because it fires from a timer while the user is elsewhere, possibly mid-form, and a direct `nav()` bypasses `formGuardRef` — only `goBack` consults it; the tasting's failed cellar-open now REPORTS itself (`tasting_open_err`) instead of silently dropping the pending state, which its `SessionFormView` twin has always done; and `fmtLotWeight` gives an absent weight ONE rendering (`—`) where the app had three (`0g` on the lot row — asserting a figure the user never gave — `—` in the detail modal, and a hole in the picker label), keeping `0g` for a lot genuinely weighed at zero so the distinction stays visible on screen. `tobaccoHasUsableLot` is also live in production at last: exported, unit-tested and DEAD since it was written, the `tobaccoHasTag` shape that knip cannot see because a test counts as a consumer. **Probed five ways; the third probe came back GREEN and was VACUOUS** — it prefixed `false &&` onto the branch while the test asserts the SOURCE contains `auto && !ok && setSaveError`, so the substring survived. Redone by deleting the branch outright, it reddens. Same lesson as the two probes above: **a probe that does not change what the assertion actually reads is not a probe.**

**FOUR readers of the untracked-weight notion were fixed and there were SIX, and the fifth one turned the fix into a silent data loss.** An audit of the whole session mechanic (live + manual), each finding re-verified before acting. **(a) THE FIFTH READER: the three weight CAPS in `useSessionStore`.** `_persistSession` and both branches of `updateSession` clamp the recorded weight to what the lot holds (`Math.min(w, safeW(lot.weightG))`) — a guard against recording more than exists — and `safeW("")` is 0, so every session logged against a lot that fix had just made offerable **recorded 0 g**. Worse than the bug it followed: the tobacco now appears in the picker, the session saves, the journal shows it, and the grams are gone with no message. **Un-correctable by editing**, since the edit path clamps the same way. All three now exempt an untracked lot — the cap protects a KNOWN balance, and there is nothing to protect when there is no balance. **(b) THE SIXTH READER: a local COPY of the predicate in `InventoryDetailView`** (`(parseFloat(l.weightG)||0) > 0`), which the fix left behind — so the fiche went on printing « renseigne le poids d'un lot pour pouvoir utiliser ce tabac dans une séance » about a tobacco both pickers were already offering. The copied-predicate failure this repo keeps paying for (the tag predicate ×4, `FAMILY_AGING_MAX`, `CATS`). **The hint is KEPT, not deleted, and REWORDED in all six languages**: the state that still warrants it is an explicit ZERO — a weight typed by hand, or a finished lot reopened at 0 — which the pickers do refuse, and « renseigne le poids » was the wrong sentence for it because the weight IS filled in. Both halves of that reversal are pinned (zero raises it, unweighed does not), on the assertion itself so it is not "fixed" back. **(c)** The cellar auto-select fallback was duplicated verbatim in `SessionFormView` and `TastingView` and read the raw weight too; both go through `isUsableLot` now. **(d) A CROSS-CHANNEL defect, found while reading the same area and unrelated to weights: the storage-full warning could be disarmed for SEVEN DAYS by a gesture that has nothing to do with it.** `saveWarn` is a SHARED channel — the tasting auto-end notice was put on it, and the `save()` QuotaExceeded migration has been on it far longer — while the banner's × wrote `cave-quota-warn-dismissed` **unconditionally**. So closing « Dégustation clôturée automatiquement après 95 min » silenced « le stockage est à 80 %, sauvegardez avant que les écritures échouent » for a week, silently. The dismissal moved into `useStorageQuotaWarning` gated on the same `raisedRef` the clearing branch has: **the hook is the only place that knows whether the banner on screen is ITS banner**, so the write belongs there and nowhere else; the banner now REPORTS the dismissal (`ctx.dismissQuotaWarn`) and a second close cannot re-arm it. Probed in all four directions, each mutation verified applied and reddening exactly its own cases.


## Bundle budget, cold start and on-demand dictionaries

**THREE CHECKS MEASURE `dist/`, AND ONE VERIFIED IT WAS THE CODE.** `size:check`, `i18n:layout` and `theme:contrast` all judge the BUILT app, and only the first had learned that existence is not enough — a `dist/` older than `src/` gives a confident verdict on the PREVIOUS bundle. **The demonstration was on me**: two full `theme:contrast` campaigns measured an hour-old bundle, green throughout, which is how a stable 2566-element count became 2565 across a rebuild with no source change in between. Probed the obvious suspect first and it was innocent — the count is 2565 with and without `awaitMarker` — so the cause was the rebuild, not the checker. **A check reporting on the wrong artefact looks exactly like one reporting on the right artefact**, which is the whole failure mode. The rule now lives in `scripts/distFreshness.cjs` and all three call it; `distFreshness.test.ts` asserts each one consults it AND stops, and that none kept a local copy (a second implementation starts right and then only one of the two gets fixed — the drift this repo pays for in a loop). Two details worth keeping: tests are excluded from the walk (they never enter the bundle, so counting them would fail every test-only commit and teach people to route around the guard), and a FILESYSTEM error is tolerated while a `ReferenceError`/`TypeError` is rethrown — that means the guard itself is broken, and it did exactly that once, silently reporting OK on a stale bundle. `staleMessage` carries no check NAME, because two of the three callers funnel through a `die()` that already prefixes one and the first version printed « theme:contrast — theme:contrast: … ».

**Bundle-size guard**. `scripts/check-bundle-size.cjs` (`npm run size:check`) runs in the Lighthouse workflow **after `npm run build`, before the LHCI step** — a fast, deterministic pre-check that fails at build time with a clear message instead of after a 3-run Lighthouse pass. It parses `dist/index.html` for the eager script set (entry + static deps) and asserts their combined gzip stays under budget. **Why it exists**: a Lighthouse job once went red because a large body of data became EAGER (per-language prose merged into the entry chunk), and a chunk that loads on the home screen counts toward Lighthouse's `resource-summary:script:size` (500 KB hard cap) — eager JS hit 855 KB. It also REFUSES to measure a stale `dist/`, which is the failure that would otherwise report the previous bundle as current. Budgets are gzip transfer sizes, mirroring how Lighthouse measures.

**Cold-start catalogue gating (the reason changed, the RULE did not).** It was about a content-hashed JS chunk counting toward the eager script budget. There is no chunk — the catalogue is read from IndexedDB — so the cost is now an IndexedDB open plus a parse **MEASURED at 0.5-1.2 s for 1594 rows on a desktop, several times that on a phone** (see `catalogueStore`), which is worse on the home screen than a download would be. So the rule stands unchanged: the consumers are gated on their surface being ACTIVE — `CatalogView` on `view === "catalog"`, `TobaccoFormView` on `view === "addT"/"editT"`, `WishFormView` on `showWishForm || editWishId`, and `useAiAutoFill` only inside a user-triggered auto-fill. **If you add a catalogue consumer, gate its `loadTobaccoDb()` behind the surface being open — never call it from a mount-unconditional effect.** Rewritten later, which found this paragraph still naming `ensureLangDescriptions` and a chunk deleted ten releases earlier.

**The catalogue loads as ONE unit (REVERSING an earlier split — and there is only one unit to load).** That split had the fetch in two — a small specs chunk on form open, the 122 KB prose chunk only once a typed blend matched — and it was undone, because on an EXISTING tobacco the brand and name are already filled, so the match fires on the first render and the « synchroniser depuis le catalogue » offer appears ~1 s before the prose lands: tapping it inside that window synced every field EXCEPT `description`, which was therefore never saved, so re-opening the fiche offered the same update again. Reproduced at 200/200 catalogued blends and reported as « je mets à jour, j'enregistre, et il me redemande ». **A partial diff presented as a complete one reads as a broken save** — the worst misunderstanding possible in a collection app. The point is now moot: the user's catalogue is one CSV, parsed once into one object, prose included, so a two-phase load is no longer even expressible. The lesson is what survives, and it generalises past this feature: **do not let a surface offer a diff it cannot yet compute in full.** Locked by `catalogueOneLoad.test.ts` (a description is available the instant the loader resolves, and applying the diff leaves nothing to re-apply). Rewritten later — the paragraph here still described `loadTobaccoCatalogue(lang)`, `descVer` and the 122 KB chunk as if they existed.

**React.lazy code splitting — narrow re-enable**. A broader split was tried and rolled back because iOS Safari hit "Importing a module script failed" on cold launch when the lazy chunk fetch raced the SW cache. The take is narrower: only four surfaces lazy-load, and **every call site is guarded** so the chunk fetch never fires on cold start. The view always initialises to `"home"` and `importModal` / `trashOpen` start `false`, so on cold launch React never tries to render `StatsView` / `HelpView` / `SettingsModal` / `TrashModal`. By the time the user navigates into one of them, the SW is fully active and cache-first serves the chunk if it was ever fetched before. The guards live in `CuratorApp.tsx` as `{view === "stats" && <Suspense><CuratorStatsView/></Suspense>}` etc. — never remove the conditional even if the Suspense wrapper feels redundant; without it React mounts the lazy and triggers the fetch on the first render. `vendor-react` manualChunk stays (React + ReactDOM, stable URL).

**EB chunk-load recovery**. Even with the cold-start guards above, a lazy chunk fetch can still fail later in the session — a stale SW cache after a deploy, a transient network blip on iOS Safari, etc. The error surfaces as `TypeError: Importing a module script failed.` (or `Failed to fetch dynamically imported module`), which used to land in the Error Boundary's generic "⚠ Erreur de rendu" UI with no way out. The EB in `App.tsx` now detects this error class via `isChunkLoadError(e)` (regex match on the message) and **auto-recovers**: unregister every SW, delete every `caches.*` entry, then `location.reload()`. The render path during recovery shows a sober "Récupération en cours…" / "Recovering…" screen instead of the harsh red error. **Anti-loop**: a `cave-eb-recovery-ts` timestamp is stamped in `localStorage` from `componentDidCatch` (single-call hook — `getDerivedStateFromError` can be called more than once per error in dev/Strict Mode, so the flag write MUST stay in `componentDidCatch`); if the same error hits again within 30 s the auto-purge is suppressed and the manual "Vider le cache et recharger" button is offered instead. A mount-only effect in App.tsx clears the flag if it's older than 5 min so a one-off failure doesn't permanently suppress future auto-recoveries. **What `purgeCachesAndReload` does NOT touch**: IndexedDB. `cave-imgs` (the photo store) is preserved across the purge — only the SW cache and SW registrations are wiped, which is the actual cause of the stale-chunk error. If you ever consider adding IndexedDB wipe to the recovery path: DON'T — that would nuke every local photo, which is a far worse outcome than re-fetching JS. Tests in `src/__tests__/EB.test.tsx` lock the three render branches (legacy unrelated error, chunk first hit → recovering UI, chunk repeat within 30 s → manual UI) + the manual retry button.

**« EN LIGNE » N'EST PAS « JOIGNABLE », ET LA GARDE HORS-LIGNE TESTAIT LE MAUVAIS DES DEUX.** `purgeCachesAndReload` refusait sur `navigator.onLine === false`, et cette propriété dit seulement qu'une INTERFACE existe — pas que le site répond. MESURÉ dans Chromium, serveur arrêté et interface debout : `onLine` reste `true`, la garde laisse passer, et **un seul tap sur un onglet jamais visité emmène l'app sur `chrome-error://chromewebdata/` — ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED — avec l'enregistrement du service worker et tous les caches supprimés.** Avant le tap `{sw:1, caches:1, root:1}`, après `{sw:-1, caches:-1, root:-1}`. La cave dans `localStorage` survit ; l'application qui sait l'afficher, non, jusqu'au retour du réseau. **Ce n'est pas un cas limite** : un portail captif (hôtel, aéroport, train), une radio mobile sans données, un échec DNS, un pare-feu d'entreprise et une fenêtre de déploiement laissent tous `onLine` à `true` — c'est la forme ORDINAIRE de « le réseau est là, le site non ». **La page sœur `public/reset.html` porte exactement la sonde qu'il fallait, et son commentaire énumère ces mêmes cas** : c'est le manque-au-voisin, une fois de plus, et cette fois dans l'autre sens (la page a été durcie, l'appel dans le code ne l'a pas été). `appReachable()` fait maintenant la même chose : court-circuit `onLine` d'abord, puis un `fetch("./?_probe=…", {cache:"no-store"})` — `sw.js` retourne tôt pour une requête `no-store` (sa troisième garde), donc la réponse vient du réseau et non du cache qu'on s'apprête à détruire — et la LECTURE DU CORPS, parce qu'un portail captif répond 200 avec sa propre page et que `res.ok` seul l'accepterait. **L'asymétrie tranche la sévérité, et elle est déjà écrite sur `reset.html`** : une sonde qui échoue à tort coûte un tap et ne supprime rien, une sonde qui passe à tort laisse l'utilisateur sans application — elle penche donc vers le refus. **Deux conséquences qu'il fallait traiter ensemble, sinon le correctif en crée deux autres.** (a) `getDerivedStateFromError` est SYNCHRONE et statique, donc il ne peut pas attendre la sonde : il garde sa supposition `onLine`, et `componentDidCatch` la CORRIGE — quand la purge refuse, il retombe sur l'écran manuel, sans quoi l'utilisateur resterait sur « Passage à la dernière version… » à attendre un rechargement qui ne viendra jamais, ce que le commentaire de cette méthode décrivait déjà comme la panne à éviter. (b) **Le bouton manuel dit désormais qu'il a refusé** (`eb_unreachable`, six langues) : cet écran n'est atteint QUE dans la situation où le refus est la bonne réponse, donc un tap silencieux y serait la règle et non l'exception — le « contrôle mort » que ce dépôt a déjà payé deux fois. Le message nomme ce qui n'a PAS eu lieu (rien n'a été supprimé), qui est la moitié rassurante et qui est vraie. Le coût du correctif est un aller-retour réseau avant le rechargement légitime, c'est-à-dire après chaque déploiement ; c'est le chemin ordinaire et quelques centaines de millisecondes y sont invisibles. Sondé trois fois : revenir à `onLine` seul rougit 6 cas, retirer la lecture du corps rougit le cas du portail captif, ne pas remonter le refus rougit celui du bouton muet. **VÉRIFIÉ DE BOUT EN BOUT dans le navigateur, avant et après.**

**« LE SERVEUR REFUSE » N'EST PAS « VOTRE SESSION A EXPIRÉ », et les huit sites de refus ne regardaient que `code`.** Google rend **403** pour les deux — un Drive plein et une autorisation insuffisante — et met le discriminant dans `error.errors[].reason`. MESURÉ en pilotant le vrai `useGdriveSync` : un 403 quota et un 403 auth aboutissaient au même endroit, **jeton JETÉ**, écran bloqué sur « Connexion… ». Ce que cela coûte : un Drive plein fait jeter un jeton VALIDE puis relancer une authentification — sur iOS standalone une redirection OAuth complète — donc l'utilisateur repasse par Google, en boucle, pour un problème sans rapport avec sa session, et on ne lui dit jamais que son Drive est plein. **Le quota gratuit de Drive est partagé avec Gmail et Photos, donc le saturer est ordinaire.** `cloudRefusalKind(err)` (gdriveApi.ts) rend `auth | quota | rate | other` et `isAuthRefusal` gouverne les huit sites. **ON NE RECLASSE QUE CE QU'ON SAIT NOMMER, et c'est ce qui rend le changement sûr** : un 401, et un 403 dont la raison n'est pas reconnue, restent `auth` — exactement l'ancien comportement — seules les raisons listées (`storageQuotaExceeded`, `quotaExceeded`, `rateLimitExceeded`, `userRateLimitExceeded`, plus les 507/429 de Dropbox) en sortent. Le message aussi : la prose du fournisseur est ANGLAISE et remontait verbatim dans `gdriveStatus`, donc un lecteur francophone lisait « Erreur : » suivi d'anglais sur le seul refus où le remède compte ; `refusalMessage` traduit les deux cas nommés (`err_cloud_full` / `err_cloud_rate`, six langues) et laisse le message brut pour le reste — inventer une traduction d'un refus non identifié dirait à l'utilisateur quelque chose qu'on ne sait pas. **Le marqueur Dropbox n'est accepté que sur les statuts que Dropbox utilise pour ça** (507 / 429), sinon un message quelconque contenant le mot serait lu comme un quota. Verrouillé par `cloudRefusal.test.ts`, dont la seconde moitié pilote le VRAI hook parce que le classifieur pur ne garantit rien tout seul — la leçon de `chooseAutoSaveTarget`, dont la fonction était testée et l'APPEL couvert par rien. Sondé trois fois : rendre le classifieur aveugle rougit 5 cas, retirer la traduction 1, faire retomber un seul site sur `code === 403` 1.

**L'AUDIT DU CHEMIN DROPBOX, et ce qu'il a trouvé n'est PAS où on l'attendait.** L'hypothèse était que Dropbox, ajouté plus tard, porterait des défauts que Drive n'a plus. Vérifié : les mécanismes LOURDS ont bien été portés et fonctionnent — convergence par appareil, balayage (mesuré : un balayage supprime le manuel le plus ancien et son propre auto, **pas** l'auto d'un appareil étranger), les deux sens du flux catalogue, la sérialisation des écritures, et le cycle de vie du refresh token (un rejet réseau et un 503 le CONSERVENT, seul un `invalid_grant` l'efface). Ce qui n'a pas suivi, ce sont les **petits correctifs tardifs écrits en pensant à Drive** — et trois d'entre eux ont la bonne version de la règle écrite un fichier plus loin. **(a) `dropboxProvider.list` ignorait `opts.retries`, qui est AU CONTRAT** (« Number of network retries (fetchRetry); 0 = single attempt ») et que Drive lit : `dbxRpc` partait droit sur `fetchWithTimeout`, donc les quatre appelants qui demandent deux essais — sauvegarde manuelle, liste de restauration, et les DEUX sens du flux catalogue — n'avaient aucun filet sur Dropbox, et une micro-coupure suffisait à perdre l'opération. Invisible aux suites existantes, qui simulent des réponses HTTP REFUSÉES et jamais une REJECTION de `fetch` ; et `retries` étant optionnel, l'ignorer ne casse ni le typage ni le contrat structurel. **Mesuré et hors périmètre : `gdriveSaveQuiet` ne passe `retries` sur AUCUN fournisseur** — c'est symétrique, donc ce n'est pas ce défaut. **(b) Le dispatcher de retour OAuth Dropbox ne lisait aucun des trois marqueurs one-shot `list`**, là où Google les lit avec la suppression en premier. Or `gdriveDeleteBackupById` écrit son marqueur **sans regarder le fournisseur** (il passe par `getCloudToken("list")`, qui redirige des deux côtés quand il n'y a pas de jeton) : une suppression que l'utilisateur venait de confirmer ne se produisait donc pas sur Dropbox — fichier toujours là, ligne intacte au réaffichage, aucun message. C'est le défaut que le commentaire du côté Google décrit mot pour mot, corrigé sur un fournisseur et jamais sur l'autre. **La décision est maintenant la fonction pure `consumeListResume(nowMs)`** que les deux dispatchers appellent, pour qu'un troisième fournisseur ne rouvre pas le trou ; l'ordre (suppression d'abord, car seule à muter), la lecture-avant-effacement et la fraîcheur y sont épinglés, et un cas COMPTE les appelants — le trou d'origine était un dispatcher sur deux, pas la logique. **Atténuation honnête** : atteignable seulement quand le refresh token est mort ou absent, sinon le jeton vient du cache. **(c) `autorename: true` faisait perdre à une sauvegarde Dropbox ses compteurs et son nom d'appareil.** `dbxUpload` l'envoie pour survivre à une collision de nom à la même seconde (un double-tap sur « Sauvegarder ») — et le fichier arrive alors en `… (1).json`, exactement là où `parseBackupCounts` et `backupDeviceName` ancrent `\.json$`. La sauvegarde qu'`autorename` venait de sauver était donc la seule que le sélecteur ne savait pas lire. Tolérance **étroite** (une espace littérale, des parenthèses, des chiffres), et les cas de non-régression le fixent : un second slug, ` (a)`, ` ()` et `.json.bak` restent refusés. **Une correction au rapport de l'audit : `autoFileDeviceId` n'était PAS touché** — sa regex est ancrée à l'AVANT du nom, donc un suffixe en queue ne la gêne pas ; mesuré avant de le croire, ce qui a évité de « corriger » une fonction saine. **RESTE OUVERT, délibérément.** (1) **Un Dropbox plein n'est reconnu que sous HTTP 507**, alors que l'`error_summary` que le code utilise lui-même en fixture (`path/insufficient_space/…`) est une erreur d'endpoint que l'API v2 délivre plutôt en **409**. Sous 409 l'écran affiche la prose anglaise brute au lieu d'`err_cloud_full` — borné (le jeton survit des deux côtés, donc pas de boucle de réauthentification), mais le remède actionnable est perdu. **NON CORRIGÉ parce que la preuve est interne** : deviner un second code de statut serait répéter l'erreur qui a créé le premier. À confirmer sur un compte réel, et si 409 est le bon il faudra le restreindre au marqueur `insufficient_space` pour ne pas avaler `path/conflict`. (2) **« Session Drive expirée » s'affiche aux utilisateurs Dropbox** (`err_drive_expired` atteint depuis les branches Dropbox), et là où Drive escalade vers une authentification interactive, Dropbox s'arrête à `getTokenSilent` : deux boutons du panneau cloud deviennent des culs-de-sac. Invisible à la parité i18n (la clé existe et est traduite) comme aux contrats d'étiquettes. (3) **Un échec RÉSEAU du refresh grant Dropbox éjecte vers dropbox.com** : `getToken` redirige sur n'importe quel rejet de `getTokenSilent`, sans distinguer « pas de grant » d'« appel réseau échoué » — `gdriveGetToken` ne fait, lui, aucun appel réseau avant de décider. **Vérifié et NE SE REPRODUIT PAS** (cette moitié vaut autant) : un jeton Google envoyé à `content.dropboxapi.com` — le repli `JSON.parse(tkGet())` en `gdriveSaveQuiet` lit bien le cache Google sur un chemin partagé, mais la garde `if (isDbx && !dbxTokenRef.current) return;` retourne avant, donc il n'est atteignable que côté Drive ; une fuite du refresh token dans un export, une sauvegarde ou un message d'erreur (`FORBIDDEN` le couvre, `wipeAppStorage` l'efface, `redactApiKeys` nettoie les messages) ; et `dropbox-pending` jamais balayé, qui ne bloque rien puisque `getToken` le réécrit à chaque tentative.

**LES TROIS RÉSIDUS CI-DESSUS SONT FERMÉS, et le premier l'a été par une RECHERCHE parce que le dépôt ne pouvait pas répondre seul.** **(1) Un Dropbox plein arrive en 409, pas en 507 — le statut d'origine était une supposition.** La chaîne `path/insufficient_space/…` venait de l'API réelle, le STATUT avait été deviné, et deux sources indépendantes le corrigent : l'API v2 rend **409 pour TOUTE erreur spécifique à un point d'accès**, et le billet d'ingénierie de Dropbox dit pourquoi — 409 n'a pas de sens défini dans la spec HTTP, donc proxies et bibliothèques clientes le relaient intact. (`www.dropbox.com` est bloqué par le proxy d'egress de cet environnement ; le refus est une réponse, pas un obstacle, et les résultats de recherche ont suffi.) **LE MARQUEUR PORTE DÉSORMAIS LA DÉCISION, PAS LE STATUT**, et c'est cette garde qui rend l'élargissement sûr : 409 est aussi celui de `path/conflict`, `path/not_found` et `path/disallowed_name`, donc un 409 sans marqueur reconnu reste `other` — épinglé dans les deux sens. 507 est GARDÉ : le retirer changerait le comportement sur un cas que rien ici ne mesure contre l'API vivante, et un `error_summary` qui dit `insufficient_space` dit exactement cela. **Même oubli sur `too_many_write_operations`, que le dépôt CONNAISSAIT DÉJÀ** — le commentaire de `dropboxProvider.remove` énumère « 429 … ou 409 (sous le tag lock_conflict) » et le classifieur ne voyait que le 429 ; corrigé dans le même bloc. **(2) Une panne RÉSEAU éjectait l'utilisateur hors de la PWA.** `getToken` redirigeait vers dropbox.com sur n'importe quel rejet de `getTokenSilent`, lequel rejette pour trois raisons indiscernables à cet endroit : pas de grant (redirection légitime), grant révoqué (légitime), ou **l'appel a échoué** — coupure, DNS mort, délai de garde de 20 s, ou un 5xx à corps non-JSON qui fait rejeter `r.json()`. Hors ligne, dropbox.com échoue aussi, et sur une PWA installée il faut fermer et rouvrir. L'asymétrie n'était pas justifiée : `gdriveGetToken` ne fait AUCUN appel réseau avant de décider, donc il ne peut pas produire ça. Le marqueur `NETWORK_FAILURE` est posé dans `tokenEndpoint`, **le seul endroit qui sait que le rejet vient du transport et non du contenu de la réponse** ; `getToken` le relance traduit (`err_cloud_unreachable`, six langues) au lieu de naviguer. Les deux cas qui MÉRITENT la redirection la gardent, et un grant révoqué est toujours effacé — épinglé, sinon un correctif trop large tuerait la ré-authentification. **(3) « Session Drive expirée » chez un utilisateur Dropbox, et deux boutons sans issue.** QUATRE sites jetaient `err_drive_expired` en dur — la vérification cloud, le diagnostic, la restauration depuis la bannière et le téléchargement différé du sélecteur — et les quatre sont atteignables sur Dropbox, donc le message nommait le mauvais service dans les six langues. Invisible à la parité i18n (la clé existe et est traduite) comme aux contrats d'étiquettes, qui comparent le guide au dictionnaire et jamais le dictionnaire au FOURNISSEUR ACTIF. Un helper `cloudExpiredMessage()` remplace les quatre copies, et un cas interdit désormais tout `t("err_drive_expired")` littéral : ce qui pourrit est le nombre de copies. **L'autre moitié — les deux boutons du panneau cloud s'arrêtaient à `getTokenSilent`** là où Drive escalade, donc avec un jeton de rafraîchissement mort ils devenaient des culs-de-sac. Ils escaladent maintenant, et **cela n'est devenu sûr que grâce aux deux correctifs précédents** : le dispatcher lit les marqueurs one-shot, donc le retour route vers le bouton tapé et non vers le panneau des sauvegardes ; et une panne réseau ne redirige plus. **LA VÉRIFICATION AU LANCEMENT N'ESCALADE PAS ET NE DOIT JAMAIS LE FAIRE** — elle part au montage, la branche Drive s'y arrête pour cette raison même (« no popups from mount »), et une redirection OAuth pendant l'ouverture de l'app serait le pire des remèdes. **Ma première assertion était trop large et aurait cassé exactement cette règle** ; elle épingle maintenant les DEUX moitiés, ce qui est le vrai contrat. Sondé quatre fois, chacune rougissant sa cible.

**LES BANNIÈRES ET LES TOASTS N'ONT JAMAIS ÉTÉ VUS PAR AUCUN VÉRIFICATEUR, ET LA MESURE RETOURNE LA QUESTION.** `i18n:layout` et `theme:contrast` partagent une liste d'ÉCRANS, et aucune des cinq bannières `top: 0` ni des quatre toasts du bas n'y figure : elles sont pilotées par de l'état React qu'une graine de stockage ne peut pas atteindre. Un build venait d'ajouter la plus longue phrase de l'app sur l'une d'elles. **MESURÉ AVANT DE CONSTRUIRE QUOI QUE CE SOIT : les CINQ bannières du haut ne portent ni `nowrap`, ni ellipsis, ni `overflow: hidden`** — ce sont des barres pleine largeur en flux normal, elles ENVELOPPENT, donc elles ne peuvent structurellement pas tronquer quelle que soit la longueur de la traduction, et aucun des quatre modes d'échec de `i18n:layout` ne s'y applique. L'inquiétude portait sur le mauvais bout de l'écran. **Trois des quatre toasts du BAS tronquent, et chacun est BORNÉ** : l'étiquette de l'annulation est une ellipsis délibérée dans une fente `maxWidth: 240` (un nom supprimé est de longueur quelconque — c'est l'ÉTIQUETTE qui a été corrigée quand une phrase entière y a été mise, pas la fente) ; le toast « à jour » porte `nowrap` sans `maxWidth` mais son contenu est « Build NN », borné par construction ; le récapitulatif d'import est `pre-line` + `maxWidth: calc(100vw - 32px)`. **D'où `overlayTextWraps.test.ts` plutôt que trois écrans de plus dans le harnais** : ce qui rend ces surfaces sûres est une PROPRIÉTÉ DÉCLARÉE, pas un rendu, donc un test jsdom la tient sur chaque commit là où une vérification optionnelle qui a besoin d'un navigateur peut rester des mois sans tourner — ce qui est exactement arrivé à `prune`. Il couvre les cinq d'un coup, y compris celles qu'aucune graine ne saurait faire apparaître, **et il épingle les trois troncatures VOLONTAIRES comme des décisions**, ce qui est ce qui empêche un balayage futur de « corriger » la fente et de rouvrir le vrai défaut. Un cas compare le NOMBRE de bannières à `TOP_BANNER_ORDER`, donc une sixième ajoutée là sans être couverte ici rougit. Sondé deux fois. **Même build : la note « diagnostic de la sauvegarde auto » du guide n'existait qu'en ANGLAIS** — vérifié par position (elle vivait entre `sec-en` et `sec-es`), alors que deux builds venaient d'y renvoyer explicitement. Portée dans les cinq autres langues, avec la clause du bandeau ambre ajoutée aux six. **DROPBOX N'ÉTAIT COUVERT QU'AU NIVEAU DU CLASSIFIEUR, et l'écart tient à un détail qui se lit comme du câblage : `cloudProviderId` est un PROP, pas une clé de stockage.** Les quatre cas qui pilotent le vrai hook posaient `cave-cloud-provider` dans `localStorage` — ce que le hook ne lit jamais (c'est App.tsx qui lit la clé et passe le prop) — donc ils mesuraient Drive en croyant tester la routage. Le chemin Dropbox est pourtant DIFFÉRENT : `dropboxProvider` lit `r.text()` puis `JSON.parse` là où Drive lit `r.json()`, et il normalise en recyclant le statut HTTP dans `error.code`, si bien qu'un 507 ne ressemble à aucun code Drive. Trois cas bout-en-bout couvrent maintenant Dropbox (507 plein, 429 débit, 401 véritable), et ils vérifient que le jeton d'accès ET le jeton de RAFRAÎCHISSEMENT survivent — jeter le second tuerait la reconnexion silencieuse, qui est la seule chose qui rend Dropbox utilisable sur iOS. Les assertions comparent à la VALEUR du dictionnaire (`toContain(t("err_cloud_full"))`) et non à un mot : une reformulation du message reste vraie, un mauvais message ne l'est pas. Sondé : neutraliser la branche Dropbox du classifieur rougit les 3.

**COMMENT TESTER LE HORS-LIGNE ICI, parce que la méthode évidente ne marche pas.** `context.setOffline(true)` de Playwright coupe le réseau de la PAGE et **pas celui du SERVICE WORKER**. Mesuré : sous `setOffline`, un tap sur Paramètres a fait arriver `/assets/SettingsModal-*.js` sur mon serveur, qui l'a servi, et le chunk s'est retrouvé dans le cache du SW — pendant qu'un `fetch` depuis la page, lui, recevait bien un 503. Comme dans cette app **tout** passe par le SW, `setOffline` ne simule donc rien : un premier passage a rapporté « aucun défaut relevé » en mesurant une application en ligne, avec trois ✓ dont deux étaient faux. Le seul hors-ligne fiable est de **couper le serveur** (et de détruire les sockets keep-alive, sinon `close()` attend les connexions ouvertes). Deuxième piège du même passage : le modal se rend PAR-DESSUS le Home, donc `body.innerText` contient les deux et n'importe quel mot cherché est satisfait par la page de derrière — **scoper les assertions à `[role="dialog"]`**, sans quoi « Paramètres s'est ouvert » se vérifie en lisant le Home. Ce que le passage corrigé a par ailleurs confirmé comme SAIN : le démarrage à froid hors-ligne, le refus de `reset.html`, et le changement de langue hors-ligne, qui reste en français, explique pourquoi et offre un bouton Recharger.

**Cold-start shell pattern**. `data` initialises to `INIT` (empty inventory) instead of `null`, and the top-level `if (loading) return <pipe-icon/>` early return in `App.tsx` was removed. The shell (TopBar + Dock + empty HomeView) renders the instant the React mount completes; a fixed-position loading veil mounted inside `CuratorApp.tsx` covers the inner viewport area (max-width 600 column) until `loading` flips to `false`. Two invariants:
- Never set `data` back to `null` — `setData(null)` would break every store consumer that no longer null-guards. If a hook needs a "reset" path, use `setData(INIT)`.
- The loading veil is `position: absolute, inset: 0` inside the centre column — NOT `position: fixed` over the entire page. It renders at `zIndex: 9000`, which sits ABOVE the whole overlay stack (the fixed banners/pills in `Overlays.tsx` live at ~475-492, the tasting banner at 2001). That ordering is harmless because the veil only mounts during cold-start `loading` — before any overlay or tasting is possible — and unmounts the moment `loading` flips false. If a future change makes a top-level fixed element (status banner, tasting overlay) appear WHILE `loading` is still true, either raise that element above 9000 or lower the veil so the element stays interactable.

**Budget baseline.** Every figure here has gone stale twice, in the same way `prune`'s "zero warnings" had: numbers asserted in prose that nobody re-measured. **`npm run size:check` PRINTS the current total and its percentage — read that, and re-measure in the same commit whenever you touch this block.** Measured with `zlib.gzipSync(level 9)` over exactly the `<script src>` + `modulepreload` set in `dist/index.html`:

| eager chunk | raw | gzip |
|---|---|---|
| `index.js` (app code) | 610 KB | **165.2 KB** |
| `vendor-react.js` | 185 KB | **57.5 KB** |
| `en.js` (the ONE bundled dictionary) | 51 KB | **17.8 KB** |
| `primitives.js` | 37 KB | 12.8 KB |
| `Notice.js` | 31 KB | 10.5 KB |
| `imgCache.js` | 3 KB | 1.1 KB |
| `languages.js` (the registry) | 1 KB | 0.6 KB |
| `rolldown-runtime.js` | 1 KB | 0.4 KB |
| **cold-start total** | | **265.9 KB / 332 KB (80%)** |

Lazy chunks (fetched on demand, outside the eager budget): the five non-English dictionaries (`fr`/`es`/`de`/`it`/`pt`, ~16–18 KB gzip each), StatsView, SettingsModal, TrashModal, HelpView.

**WHY A SIXTH — OR SEVENTH — LANGUAGE COSTS NOTHING AT COLD START.** All the dictionaries used to ship in ONE eager chunk, of which a user read a fifth; that put the cold start at 91% of budget with barely one language of headroom, and this block used to tell the next person to devise a splitting plan before adding one. Only English is compiled in now (`src/i18n.ts`) and every other dictionary is a lazy chunk, so an added language costs ~16 KB the reader of that language downloads once and **nothing** for everyone else. Do NOT undo that by adding a static import or a `manualChunks` group for `src/i18n/` — a group is emitted as ONE file, so importing any one language would pull them all back in with every test still passing (`i18nOnDemand.test.ts` asserts it). And note `primitives`, `Notice` and `imgCache` sat in `dist/` for a long time without appearing in any baseline list here: measure the SET the HTML declares, never the chunks you remember.

**Vite 8 manualChunks gotcha.** Vite 8 ships with **Rolldown** instead of Rollup. Rolldown dropped the object-form shorthand for `output.manualChunks` — the function form is the only supported shape. `vite.config.js` declares `manualChunks(id)` returning `'vendor-react'` for any `node_modules/react*` import; the previous `manualChunks: { 'vendor-react': […] }` syntax throws `TypeError: manualChunks is not a function` at build time. The function form is also forward-compatible with Rollup, so no rollback risk.

**A BUNDLER BUMP IS VERIFIED BY COMPARING THE EMITTED SET, NOT BY A GREEN BUILD.** A Dependabot vite bump carries Rolldown with it (8.2.1 → 8.2.2 moved the bundler 1.2.2 → 1.2.5), and this app's whole cold-start story is a chunk LAYOUT: `vendor-react` split out by a function-form `manualChunks`, English compiled in while the other five dictionaries stay lazy, five lazy view chunks. Every one of those is a decision a bundler could silently undo, and the build would still exit 0 — a dictionary folded back into `index.js` costs ~16 KB per language on the home screen and nothing fails. So: capture the eager set (`grep -oE '(src|href)="[^"]*assets/[^"]*"' dist/index.html`) and the `size:check` total BEFORE, then diff them after with the content hashes normalised away. On 8.2.2 both were identical — the same eight files at **265.9 KB** — which is what makes "no regression" a measurement instead of a hope. **A bumped bundler also re-hashes every chunk**, so the artifact changes even when its content does not; that is a BUMP (the hashes are the delivery), and it is not a changelog entry (a toolchain move is not something a user can notice or act on). Dev-only dependency PRs merge like this: verify locally on current `main`, push, and the PRs close themselves as superseded rather than being merged against a stale base.

**i18n ON-DEMAND dictionaries (replaces the eager chunk).** Only **English** is statically imported by `src/i18n.ts`; `fr`/`es`/`de`/`it` are reached through `import.meta.glob("./i18n/*.ts")` and fetched on demand, each its own content-hashed chunk. **Cold start 303.2 → 240.5 KB gzip**, and the eager budget went from ~29 KB of headroom to 91.5 — which is what makes a sixth language possible (it was the documented blocker). **The three rules**: (1) the phone's language wins — `detectUiLang` is unchanged; (2) **English is the fallback**, for a language that does not exist AND for one that fails to load; (3) loading is on demand, nothing pre-warmed. **Why English is the static one**: something must be compiled in or a failed import leaves the app with NO text — the one failure worse than a missing feature — and rule 2 then becomes the failure mode for free (offline with no German chunk cached is indistinguishable from "German does not exist"; both land on English, which a German speaker prefers to French). `translate()` falls back to `LANG.en`, **not `LANG.fr`** — as do the three other `LANG[lang] || …` sites (`utils.getStorageBlockedHint`, `useTastingSession.tr`, `useSessionStore.tr`). **`t()` is still synchronous**, so the dictionary must be in memory before the first render: `main.jsx` awaits `ensureLang(active)` before `createRoot().render()`, and `saveLang` awaits before flipping `lang` — a switch that fails does NOT change language (dropping a German user to English for a choice that did not take effect is worse than staying put) and raises `langErr`, whose notice renders in the language they still have, the only one guaranteed loaded. **`ensureLang` never rejects** — every caller's response to failure is identical, so a rejection would only invite an unhandled one. **OFFLINE**: the SW is cache-first and stores every chunk it fetches, so a language used once works offline for ever; the only new failure is switching, while offline, to a never-downloaded language. **ADDING A LANGUAGE IS NOW PURELY ADDITIVE** — drop `src/i18n/<code>.ts` + an entry in `i18n/languages.ts`; `i18n.ts` needs no edit (that was the point). **Do NOT re-add a `manualChunks` group for `src/i18n/`**: a group is emitted as ONE file, so importing any one language would pull all five and silently undo this while every test still passed — `i18nOnDemand.test.ts` asserts that, plus that English stays the only static import. **Tests**: `src/__tests__/setup.ts` loads every dictionary before the suite (top-level await), because ~47 tests read `LANG.fr` synchronously; that reproduces the state the app is always in by the time anything renders.

**The four failure states that change created and did not handle.** A follow-up audit found them; each was reproduced before being fixed, and each is probed to fail on the old code (`i18nOnDemand.test.ts`). (1) **A failed switch cannot be retried in-session, and the copy said to do exactly that.** A dynamic `import()` that fails is cached AS A FAILURE in the browser's module map, so re-importing the same URL re-throws with NO network request — MEASURED in Chromium: tap offline → reconnect → tap again = **one** request in total, both attempts fail; only a reload clears it. `ensureLang` is otherwise written to be retry-friendly (no sticky `failed` flag, `inflight` cleared in `finally`), which is what made this invisible. `lang_offline_err` now names the reload, and the notice carries the button. **Do not "fix" this by clearing a flag — the state is in the browser, not in this module.** (2) **`EB.tsx` fell back to `LANG.fr`**, which is `undefined` unless French happened to load — so the string table collapsed to `{}` and every label dropped to its hardcoded French literal, in precisely the case an error boundary exists for (a chunk that failed to load). A German user with German unloaded read "⚠ Erreur de rendu". Now `LANG.en`, and its `cave-lang` default is `"en"` like App.tsx's. The four `(LANG as any)[_lng]?.key` storage-error strings in `App.tsx` route through `LANG.en` for the same reason. (3) **The STARTUP failure was invisible**: `main.jsx` mounts whether or not `ensureLang` resolved true, so `lang` stayed on the stored code while `translate` served English — English UI, DE highlighted in the picker, no notice. Both `lang` and `langErr` now init from `isLangLoaded(stored)`. (4) **Concurrent switches resolved by network timing**: tap DE (slow) then IT (fast) and the DE response landed last and won. `saveLang` carries a generation counter (`langGenRef`); a superseded resolution returns early, which also stops it clearing the spinner while a later fetch runs. Plus: `translate()` guards its lookup with `isLangLoaded` — `lang` comes from localStorage, and a corrupt `cave-lang` of `"constructor"` resolved to an `Object.prototype` member (truthy, not a dictionary) so **every** key rendered as its raw name; and `TermsGate` now renders `langPending`/`langErr`, the one screen where a failed switch produced no visible reaction at all.

**Cross-platform package-lock gotcha.** Vite 8 + Rolldown + `@vitejs/plugin-react` 6 pulls in lightningcss, `@oxc-parser`, `@oxc-resolver`, `@rolldown/binding-*` — each declares ~15 platform-specific bindings under `optionalDependencies`. By default `npm install` only enumerates the CURRENT platform's binding in the lock file, but `npm ci` strictly validates that EVERY optional binding listed in package metadata is present in the lock. Mismatch = fast EUSAGE bail like `Missing: lightningcss-darwin-arm64@1.32.0 from lock file`. The repo-root `.npmrc` pins `include=optional` so any future `npm install` keeps the lock cross-platform-complete by default. **Do not delete `.npmrc`** — and if you ever regenerate `package-lock.json` manually, run `npm install --include=optional` (which the npmrc already enforces, so plain `npm install` works too as long as the file is present).

**Assertions** (in `.lighthouserc.json`):
- HARD ERRORS (fail the PR check): accessibility ≥ 0.9, CLS ≤ 0.1, JS bundle ≤ 500 KB
- WARNINGS (visible but don't block): performance ≥ 0.8, LCP ≤ 2500ms, TTI ≤ 3500ms, total resources ≤ 1.5 MB

**When you bump a heavy dependency or add a new view**: re-run the Lighthouse job locally if you can (`npx @lhci/cli@0.15.x autorun` requires Chrome installed) or just let the GH Actions job catch it. If LCP or TTI degrade past the warn threshold, audit what got added — usually a new top-level synchronous import that should have been inlined or sidestepped.

## Optional Drive backup encryption — Phase 1

Users who want their Drive backups unreadable to a third party (e.g. a Google account compromise, a casual viewer with delegated access to the `appDataFolder`) can opt into AES-GCM-256 encryption with a user-chosen passphrase.

**Architecture**:
- `src/utils/cryptoBackup.ts` — pure crypto module. `encryptBackup(json, passphrase)` returns a JSON-stringified envelope `{ _encrypted: "v1", _kdf, _cipher, salt, iv, ciphertext }`. `decryptBackup(envelopeJSON, passphrase)` returns the plaintext. `isEncryptedEnvelopeJSON(s)` is the cheap "does this look encrypted?" detector used by the restore path — fast-rejects via `indexOf("\"_encrypted\"")` before parsing. **No size cap.** The original 2 MB short-circuit was removed because encrypted backups containing photos easily exceed 2 MB (photos are base64-embedded inside the plaintext, then the whole thing is base64-wrapped again as ciphertext), and the cap silently downgraded such envelopes to the "plaintext" branch of the restore path → `JSON.parse` succeeded → no `.tobaccos` field → user saw "Fichier invalide". Don't re-introduce the cap; the indexOf prefix check is the cheap rejection for plaintext backups already.
- Web Crypto API (no third-party dep). PBKDF2-SHA256 600 000 iterations (OWASP-2023 floor). AES-GCM-256 with random 12-byte IV + 16-byte salt per encryption — same passphrase + same plaintext = different ciphertext every time.
- `src/views/curator/EncryptionPromptModal.tsx` — passphrase prompt UI. Two modes: `setup` (enter + confirm + warning) and `unlock` (single field).
- `src/hooks/useGdriveSync.ts` — `maybeEncryptPayload` wraps the save path, `maybeDecryptText` wraps the restore path. Plaintext backups still flow through both unchanged (envelope detection branches per call).

**State (App.tsx)**:
- `driveEncryptionEnabled` — persistent flag in `localStorage["cave-drive-encryption-enabled"]`. Survives reloads. Cleared explicitly by the user via the Settings toggle.
- `drivePassphrase` — **memory only** (`useState`), never persisted. Lost on reload. The user re-enters it via the unlock modal on next Drive operation.
- `encryptionPrompt` — ephemeral `{ mode, resolve }` pair; `EncryptionPromptModal` reads it and calls `resolve(pw | null)` on submit / cancel.

**UX flows**:
- **Enable encryption**: Settings → Drive section → toggle "Encrypt Drive backups" ON → setup modal (passphrase + confirm + warning) → on submit, flag saved + passphrase cached in memory.
- **Disable encryption**: toggle OFF → `window.confirm` → flag cleared, passphrase cleared. Old encrypted backups remain restorable with the passphrase; new saves are plaintext.
- **After a reload (flag ON, passphrase gone)**: Settings shows a warn Notice "🔒 Encryption active · passphrase needed" with an "Enter passphrase" button. The next manual save also prompts.
- **Manual save** (`gdriveSave`): if flag ON and no passphrase cached, prompts. On cancel, the save aborts cleanly (no upload).
- **Auto-save** (`gdriveSaveQuiet`): if flag ON and no passphrase cached, **skips silently**. The auto-save resumes the next time the user unlocks via Settings or via a manual save. This avoids surprising the user with an auto-popup while editing.
- **Restore** (`doGdriveConfirm`): downloads the file, detects envelope via `isEncryptedEnvelopeJSON`, prompts if needed, decrypts, then routes through the normal merge/replace picker.

**What this protects**:
- ✅ Drive backups are opaque to anyone who reads them without the passphrase.
- ✅ AES-GCM tag verification catches any tampering (ciphertext + envelope metadata).
- ✅ Per-backup random salt + IV — no replay analysis across multiple backups encrypted with the same passphrase.

**What this does NOT protect**:
- ❌ Local data in `localStorage` / IndexedDB stays plaintext (the user already trusts the device; encrypting locally would block every read of the entire app).
- ❌ The OAuth token to access Drive is still stored unencrypted in `sessionStorage` (non-iOS) / `localStorage` (iOS standalone) — a malicious script with same-origin access could still upload garbage. CSP locks down `script-src` precisely to prevent that.
- ❌ **Forgotten passphrase = lost backups.** There is no recovery. The setup modal warns clearly and the user must confirm before enabling.

**Out of Phase 1** (would be Phase 2 if requested):
- JSON / CSV / ZIP local exports — currently plaintext, regardless of the Drive encryption flag.
- "Change passphrase" flow.
- Persistent "session unlocked" indicator outside Settings (currently visible only when the user opens the modal).

## localStorage / sessionStorage Keys Reference

| Key | Storage | Purpose |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `pipe-cellar-v6` | localStorage | Main application data (tobaccos, pipes, wishlist, accessories, sessions) |
| `pipe-cellar-v6-bkp` / `pipe-cellar-v6-bkp-ts` | localStorage | Pre-OAuth-redirect snapshot of the main data blob (`SK + "-bkp"`) + its timestamp, written in `useGdriveAuth.ts` just before an iOS-standalone OAuth redirect so in-memory state survives the navigation; read + restored + cleared on return in `App.tsx`'s `save()` / mount path (`lsRemove(SK + "-bkp")`). Device-local, carries only the user's own already-local data, never in backups. The `setItem` lives in the OAuth-domain file so it's exempt from the `no-raw-storage-write` rule. |
| `anthropic-api-key` | localStorage | Anthropic API key |
| `openai-api-key` | localStorage | OpenAI API key |
| `gemini-api-key` | localStorage | Google Gemini API key |
| `ai-provider` | localStorage | Selected AI provider (`"anthropic"` / `"openai"` / `"gemini"`) |
| `ai-model-` (+ provider) | localStorage | PER-PROVIDER selected model (`ai-model-anthropic` / `ai-model-openai` / `ai-model-gemini`, built as `"ai-model-" + provider`). Absent → the provider default (see AI Integration table). Written by `saveAiModel` in `useAiAutoFill`; drives every AI request's model. **Normalised through `normalizeAiModel` on every read** so a legacy id stored by an older build resolves to a current option. Device-local, never in backups. |
| `ai-model-auto-migrated` | localStorage | `"1"` once the one-shot "put this device on auto" migration has run (see `isFormerDefaultModel`). Only a stored FORMER DEFAULT is rewritten to `auto`; a deliberate pick is left alone. The flag is what makes a later deliberate pick of the cheapest tier stick instead of being flipped back to auto on every launch. Device-local, never in backups. |
| `ai-model-dead-` (+ provider) | localStorage | JSON array of model ids this device has seen a "model no longer exists" 404 for, under the **auto** setting only (`deadModelsKey(provider)`, capped at the last 8). `resolveAiModel` skips them, so a model retired upstream costs exactly ONE failed call ever instead of failing for ever. A pinned model never writes here (the user must see the real error). Corrupt value → treated as empty. Device-local, never in backups. |
| `cave-exclude-apikey` | localStorage | `"0"` = include API key in exports; absent or any other value = exclude (opt-out default) |
| `cave-lang` | localStorage | UI language (`"fr"` / `"en"` / `"es"` / `"de"` / `"it"`). On first launch (key absent) it's seeded by `main.jsx` from the browser's preferred languages via `detectUiLang(navigator.languages, LANGUAGES codes)` — primary-subtag match, **English fallback**. Runs before React mounts so the lang state + `initDateFormat` + the terms gate all see it on frame 1. |
| `cave-lang-auto` | localStorage | Set by `main.jsx` (to the detected code) ONLY when the first-launch language auto-detection fired, so the app can show a one-time "Langue détectée automatiquement · Modifier" toast (`CuratorLangDetectedToast` in Overlays). Cleared the instant the user picks a language explicitly (`saveLang` — terms gate or Settings) so a deliberate choice never triggers it, and consumed (removed) by the toast when it shows. The toast waits until `cave-curator-welcomed === "1"` so it doesn't stack on the welcome modal. Device-local, never in backups. |
| `cave-weight-unit` | localStorage | Weight display unit (`"g"` / `"oz"`) |
| `cave-length-unit` | localStorage | Length display unit (`"mm"` / `"in"`) |
| `cave-currency` | localStorage | Currency symbol for every price field. Picked from a fixed preset (`€` / `$` / `£` / `CHF` / `JPY`) via Segmented in Settings → Préférences. Default `"€"`. Display-only — stored values are not converted. |
| `cave-font-scale` | localStorage | Global "Taille du texte" preference — `"s"` / `"m"` / `"l"` (default `"m"`). App.tsx maps it to a factor (0.9 / 1 / 1.12) written to the `--cave-font-scale` CSS variable on `<html>`; every font size in the app is expressed via `fs(px)` (from `theme-curator.ts`) = `calc(px * var(--cave-font-scale, 1))`, so the whole UI rescales live with NO React re-render. Form inputs use `fsInput(px)` = `max(16px, calc(...))` so the S factor can't drop them below the 16px iOS zoom-on-focus floor. Set via a Segmented in Settings → Préférences. Device-local, never in backups. |
| `cave-theme-mode` | localStorage | Light/dark **mode**, orthogonal to `cave-theme` — `"dark"` (default, the vault) or `"light"` (a warm parchment ground + dark text + darkened semantics, shared by all three colour themes; the theme only changes the accent, darkened per `THEMES[id].lightAccent`). `applyTheme(themeId, mode)` (theme-curator.ts) writes `MODE_LIGHT` + the theme's light accent (or the theme's dark vars) onto `<html>` — every colour token is `var(--c-*, <dark fallback>)`, so the whole palette (surfaces + text + semantics + decorative washes) flips with no React re-render. Seeded pre-mount in main.jsx; App.tsx re-applies on change via `saveThemeMode` and syncs the `theme-color` meta. Set via a Segmented in Settings → Préférences. Device-local, never in backups. |
| `cave-theme` | localStorage | Colour theme — `"brass"` (default, the classic gold identity), `"steel"` (bleu acier), or `"english"` (anglais, forest-green). The `brass`/`brassHi`/`brassDim` tokens in `theme-curator.ts` are `var(--c-brass*, <brass hex>)`; `applyTheme(id)` (theme-curator.ts) writes the theme's overrides onto `<html>` (main.jsx seeds it pre-mount, App.tsx re-applies on change via `saveThemeId`) so the whole primary accent identity swaps live with NO React re-render — same mechanism as `cave-font-scale`. Only the brass family is themed (semantic oxblood/sage/amber/ember stay warm so status colour-coding survives). Translucent tints use `alpha(token, "AA")` → `color-mix(...)` (not `token + "AA"` hex concat, which is invalid with a var()). Set via a Segmented in Settings → Préférences. Device-local, never in backups. |
| `cave-maint-threshold` | localStorage | Pipe maintenance-reminder threshold — a pipe is flagged "à entretenir" after this many sessions since its last maintenance-log entry. Integer ≥ 1, default `5`. Set via Settings → Préférences ("Rappel d'entretien (séances)"). Read by App.tsx into `maintReminderThreshold` (exposed on ctx with `saveMaintReminderThreshold`) and consumed by `computePipeMaintenanceReminders` / the fiche due-check (HomeViewV2 section, PipesListView card chip, PipesDetailView Notice). Committed via `saveWatchLowWeight` (clamps > 0). |
| `cave-tasting-active` | localStorage | Live tasting session state (singleton). `null` when none. Survives reload — `useTastingSession` rehydrates on mount. Cleared on `tastingEnd`/`tastingCancel`. |
| `cave-curator-welcomed` | localStorage | Set to `"1"` after the user dismisses the one-shot Curator welcome modal. |
| `cave-notice-seen` | localStorage | Id of the most recent startup-notice the user dismissed (see `useStartupNotice`). The hook compares the id from `public/notice.json` against this value; equal → no banner; different → pop-up shown via `CuratorStartupNoticeModal`. Only ONE id is tracked at a time (the last-seen) — a new broadcast always supersedes the previous dismissal. |
| `cave-thememode-notice-dismissed-v2` | localStorage | `"1"` once the user tapped "Ne plus afficher" on the display feature-announcement pop-up (`CuratorThemeModeNoticeModal` — now covers light/dark mode AND text size). The modal otherwise shows at every app open until a fixed window closes (hard-coded `EXPIRY_MS`, **brought forward to 2026-07-24 to retire the notice** — so this key is now inert unless a future announcement bumps the date + the key suffix); a plain close (backdrop / esc / primary CTA) just hides it for the session. Defers to the welcome modal (only surfaces once `cave-curator-welcomed === "1"`). The `-v2` suffix (the key was `cave-thememode-notice-dismissed`) resets the opt-out so users who dismissed the first version see the broadened notice again. Device-local, never in backups. |
| `cave-shopping-checked` | localStorage | JSON array of the "got it" checkbox keys ticked in the "Liste de courses" modal (`"restock:<id>"` / `"wish:<id>"`). Persists the shopping progress across reloads; the modal's "Décocher tout" clears it. Read/written via `lsGet`/`lsSet` + `safeJsonParse`. Device-local, never in backups. |
| `cave-help-sections` | localStorage | Which help sections the user has collapsed in the in-app `HelpView`. Default (key absent) is expanded; explicitly collapsed sections live as `{ <key>: true }`. Set via `ctx.toggleHelpSection(key)` and `ctx.setAllHelpSectionsCollapsed(collapsed, keys)`. |
| `cave-terms-accepted` | localStorage | Set to `"1"` after the user accepts the terms in `TermsGate`. Bypasses the terms screen on subsequent loads. |
| `cave-last-build` | localStorage | Last build number seen by user (used to show "what's new") |
| `cave-version-check-ok` | localStorage | The ms timestamp of the last version check that actually REACHED the server and returned readable JSON (written before any newer/older verdict). Seeds `useAppUpdate`'s `lastCheckOkMs`; Settings → Application shows a warning past `VERSION_CHECK_STALE_MS` (3 days). Exists because the check's `.catch` is empty by design, so a permanent failure was indistinguishable from a healthy app. Self-clearing (the next success rewrites it), so being offline for a week is never reported as a fault. Corrupt value → treated as never. Device-local, never in backups. |
| `cave-update-attempt` | localStorage | From an audit: anti-loop latch for the auto-updater. `{k:"<version>/<build>", n, ts}` — records how many times this device has auto-reloaded toward a given target build. `useAppUpdate.checkVersion` stands down (`shouldSuppressUpdate`) after `UPDATE_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (3) tries within `UPDATE_SUPPRESS_MS` (30 min), so a partial deploy / stale-edge version.json that advertises a build the served bundle isn't at yet can't drive an endless purge-and-reload loop. A legitimate update never accumulates attempts (after its reload the client IS at the new build). The manual "check for updates" in Settings is unaffected. Device-local, never in backups. **It counts RELOADS, not detections, and only the silent path made the difference visible.** `checkVersion` polls every 120 s and used to bump the counter on every DETECTION; on the visible path the two are ~equivalent (detect → banner → 10 s countdown → reload, all before the next poll), but the `data_only` SILENT path is designed to WAIT for the next backgrounding, up to 30 min. So about six minutes of ordinary foreground use drove a perfectly healthy catalogue release to the 3-attempt cap: the session in progress still updated (`silentUpdatePending` was already set), but the NEXT launch inside the 30-minute window hit `shouldSuppressUpdate` and armed NOTHING — no banner by design, and now no silent path either, so the release sat undelivered while the app looked idle. Reported from the app: a new build was out and the app was not offering it. Fixed with a per-session `countedTargetRef`: a reload always ends the session, so "already counted in THIS session" is exactly "not a fresh reload attempt", and the anti-loop guarantee is unchanged (a partial deploy still burns one attempt per real reload-and-redetect cycle). **When you change this counter, check it against BOTH paths** — the visible one hides this class of bug because it never waits. |
| `gdrive-tk` | **sessionStorage** (non-iOS) / **localStorage** (iOS standalone) | Cached OAuth token (TTL ~1h). `tkClear()` always wipes both. |
| `gdrive-fid` | localStorage | Google Drive file ID of most recent manual backup |
| `GDRIVE_CATALOGUE_PREFIX` | (constant) | **The catalogue is its OWN cloud stream, and `classifyBackup` gained a third kind for it.** A user catalogue measured **3.77 MB**, and the cellar backup is written on every change (the auto-save debounces 1.2 s after any edit) while a catalogue changes only when the user loads one — so embedding it would upload 3.77 MB of unmoved data every time a session is logged. **The hazard the separation creates is the whole reason this is a typed third kind rather than a prefix bolted on**: `classifyBackup` returned `"manual"` for ANYTHING not starting with the auto prefix, and manual backups ROTATE over `GDRIVE_MAX_MANUAL` — so a catalogue file would have been **deleted from the cloud by the user's own cellar saves, silently, after three**. `findNewerCloudBackup` had no type filter either, so it would have offered a CSV as a cellar backup on a banner whose « Restaurer » stages an import of the whole cellar (`stageImport` would refuse the payload, so the user would get a banner that cannot do what it says). **Four exclusions, each asserted**: the manual rotation and the auto sweep are excluded BY CONSTRUCTION (both filter on `classifyBackup(f.name) === type`), the multi-device guard and its `explainCloudBackups` mirror skip the kind explicitly, and the restore PICKER filters before its emptiness check so an account holding only catalogue files reports « aucune sauvegarde » rather than a list of unusable rows. **Widening the return type is what FOUND the consumers** — `tsc` named the two sites (`CloudBackupDiag.kind`, the backups-list type) that had to decide what to do. This is the area three earlier releases were each spent on, so `catalogueBackupStream.test.ts` probes every exclusion: dropping the classification reddens 6 cases, the guard exclusion 2, the picker filter 1. **The WRITER, without which none of the above had ever run in the field.** Four exclusions shipped with no way to put a file in the stream they guard, so in production the guarded stream was permanently empty and every exclusion was exercised only by its own test — a guard whose subject does not exist yet is a guard nobody has watched work. `makeCatalogueName(fileName?)` (gdriveApi.ts) + `catalogueCloudSave` / `catalogueCloudRestore` (useGdriveSync) close it, and three decisions carry the feature. **(a) The name carries NO device id, unlike an auto file, and that inversion is the point**: a device id exists so each device converges on ITS OWN auto file and never touches a sibling's, whereas a catalogue is ONE artefact meant to travel — the entire feature is a second device fetching the first's file, so stamping it per device would give every device its own cloud catalogue and quietly deliver the opposite. It carries an optional 16-char slug of the user's own file name instead, at the TAIL like the device-name slug, so the file is identifiable in Drive without becoming device-scoped. **(b) Restore is EXPLICIT — no banner, no launch check, nothing automatic.** The cellar has `findNewerCloudBackup` because a stale cellar is a data-loss risk the user cannot see; a catalogue is a 3.77 MB file the user chose, and fetching it unasked on a device that deliberately has none would both surprise them and change every lookup for the rest of the session (`tobaccoDbInvalidate()` runs on success, or the module would keep answering from the previous catalogue — the rule).
