The SAVE button is gated on `catalogueMeta` (nothing to send otherwise, and it says so with `cat_cloud_none`); the RESTORE button deliberately is NOT, because **the device that most needs it is precisely the one with no catalogue**. **(c) The sweep keeps ONE copy** (`pruneByType(files, "catalogue", 1, …)`, the third kind added for it): a catalogue is a current state rather than a history, and the cellar's 3-file rotation exists to survive a bad save, which does not apply to a file the user still holds locally. `catalogueStore`'s zero-blend guard covers the remaining risk — a wrong file fetched from the cloud parses to nothing and is refused rather than replacing a working catalogue. **The probe that mattered stayed GREEN first**: both hook cases staged an EMPTY listing, so `pruneByType` deleted nothing whether the sweep was wired or not; the case that earns it stages an older catalogue beside a manual and an auto file and asserts exactly one DELETE, against `cat-old`. Same lesson as before — *when a probe stays green, find out which layer is absorbing it.* **The ANSWER appeared in another Section.** Both functions wrote to the shared `gdriveStatus`, whose Notice is pinned under the CELLAR save button (deliberately) — a different `Section`, ABOVE the catalogue one — so tapping « Sauvegarder le catalogue dans le cloud » printed the result several rows up the scroll, off screen on a phone. Reported from the app with a screenshot. **This is the earlier defect verbatim, written up in the release before it in this very file** (*"it wrote to the SHARED gdriveStatus … so the answer appeared where the user was not looking"*), and the comment at the call site NAMED the conflict before shipping it, offering the section's hint as compensation — **a hint about what a button DOES is not an answer to what it just DID.** `catalogueCloudStatus` is now its own slot with its own clear timer, rendered directly under the two buttons. A separate slot rather than the `syncDiagSource` shape (one channel + a source tag) because these two live in a different `Section` from every other cloud action, so there is no ambiguity about which button a catalogue message belongs to. Locked by the « catalogue cloud status » block in `userCatalogueSection.test.tsx` — which asserts the two function bodies contain NO `setGdriveStatus(` at all, not merely that the new slot exists; probed. |
| `gdrive-auto-fid` | localStorage | Google Drive file ID of the current auto-save file (timestamped `cave-tabac-auto-*.json`, overwritten in place on each save). |
| `gdrive-state` | localStorage | OAuth state parameter (CSRF protection) |
| `gdrive-pkce-verifier` | localStorage | Legacy PKCE verifier — always cleared at the start of the iOS redirect flow; kept for test suite only |
| `gdrive-pkce-redirect` | localStorage | Legacy PKCE redirect URI — always cleared at the start of the iOS redirect flow; kept for test suite only |
| `gdrive-pending` | localStorage | Pending Drive operation across OAuth redirect (one of `"save"`, `"restore"`, `"reconnect"`, `"list"`, or `"autosave"`). `"autosave"` is the iOS save-tap workaround — see `triggerIosAutosaveReauth` in useGdriveSync. The dispatcher persists the returned token and fires `gdriveSaveQuiet()` with NO modal / NO status banner. |
| `gdrive-pending-ts` | localStorage | Timestamp (ms) stamped alongside `gdrive-pending` when an iOS OAuth redirect starts. Powers the stale-pending sweep: any marker older than 60 s (in `triggerIosAutosaveReauth` and the mount-time cleanup in App.tsx) is treated as dead and cleaned up. Without this guard, a dropped OAuth chain (user closed the tab, Google bounced without a hash) left `gdrive-pending` set forever and silently blocked every subsequent save-tap auto-save. |
| ~~`gdrive-reconnect-ts`~~ | localStorage | Removed. It was used for a silent-first-with-escalation Reconnect strategy, but the silent first tap was unreliable in practice (Google's silent path returns without a token even when SSO seems valid on iOS PWA) so the second-tap escalation became the de-facto path — at which point the silent first tap was just noise. `gdriveReconnect` now ALWAYS calls `gdriveGetToken("reconnect", true)` → `prompt=select_account` → single-tap picker. The key may linger from a previous install (harmless); the iOS OAuth dispatcher defensively wipes it on the next successful auth. |
| `gdrive-force-select` | localStorage | Force the backup picker on next restore |
| `cave-cloud-provider` | localStorage | Active backup destination selector — `"gdrive"` or `"dropbox"`. Dropbox is the default for NEW devices; existing Drive users are preserved via the migration gate in App.tsx (any one of `gdrive-fid` / `gdrive-auto-fid` / `cave-autosave-ts` present → keep `"gdrive"`). Explicit selection always wins. Routing-only: switching never migrates or deletes backups; each provider keeps its own files + fid namespace. Saved via `saveCloudProviderId` in App.tsx; exposed on ctx with `cloudProviderId`. Changing the value also resets `backupsMeta` so the "View my backups" panel doesn't show the other provider's files. |
| `dropbox-fid` | localStorage | Dropbox file id of the most recent manual backup (the `gdrive-fid` equivalent — per-provider namespace). |
| `dropbox-auto-fid` | localStorage | Dropbox file id of the current auto-save file (the `gdrive-auto-fid` equivalent). |
| `dropbox-tk` | localStorage | Cached Dropbox access token `{t, x}` (~4 h TTL, 5-min safety margin). Renewed silently via the refresh grant — plain fetch, works on every platform incl. iOS standalone. |
| `dropbox-rt` | localStorage | Long-lived Dropbox REFRESH token from the PKCE exchange (`token_access_type=offline`). Cleared by `dbxAuthClear()` (explicit disconnect) or when the refresh grant returns `invalid_grant` (user revoked the app on dropbox.com). |
| `dropbox-state` | localStorage | CSRF state for the Dropbox OAuth redirect. Fail-closed check on return (same rule as `gdrive-state` — never weaken to `&&`). One-shot: cleared on every processed return. |
| `dropbox-verifier` | localStorage | PKCE code verifier for the in-flight Dropbox OAuth round. One-shot, read-before-clear (the ESLint `no-storage-read-after-remove` rule guards it like every literal key). |
| `dropbox-pending` | localStorage | Pending Dropbox operation across the OAuth redirect. Validated against the same five-action whitelist as `gdrive-pending` (`save` / `restore` / `reconnect` / `list` / `autosave`). |
| `dropbox-pending-ts` | localStorage | Timestamp stamped alongside `dropbox-pending` — powers the same stale-pending sweep semantics as `gdrive-pending-ts`. |
| `gdrive-account-hint` | localStorage | Email of the last Google account used for Drive. Set automatically by `captureAccountHint()` (calls `GET drive/v3/about?fields=user` after every successful auth, scope `drive.appdata` is sufficient so no extra consent screen). Passed as `hint` to `initTokenClient` (popup flow) and as `login_hint` to the OAuth redirect URL (iOS standalone) on every re-auth round-trip so Google skips the account picker when the hinted account is signed in. Cleared by `hintClear()` when the user explicitly triggers the "Switch Google account" flow (`gdrive-force-select` is set in tandem). |

## Color Theme (Design System)

All colors live in `src/theme-curator.ts` exported as `C.*`. Dark vault palette, brass / oxblood / sage accents.

```ts
// Backgrounds
C.bg       = "#0e1311"   // Page background
C.bg2      = "#131a17"
C.bg3      = "#181f1c"
C.card     = "#1a221e"   // Card surface
C.cardHi   = "#202924"
C.rule     = "#26312b"
C.rule2    = "#33403a"

// Accents
C.brass    = "#d4a661"   // Primary accent (inventory section)
C.brassHi  = "#ecc789"
C.brassDim = "#8a6e3d"
C.amber    = "#e89556"   // Warnings, callouts
C.amberHi  = "#f2b183"   // bright amber, mid step of the activity-calendar cell ramp
C.ember    = "#df6a40"   // Accessories section
C.oxblood  = "#a8453f"   // Pipes section / destructive
C.oxbloodHi= "#d27b6f"   // 5.27:1 on card, 5.73 on CARD_BG — passes AA body
C.sage     = "#8fbf9c"   // Journal section / success
C.sageHi   = "#b5deba"
C.steel    = "#6f9ec4"   // the one COOL accent in the warm vault; 5.70:1 on card (fills/charts)
C.steelHi  = "#a6c9e6"   // AA-comfortable blue (9.38:1 on card) for small text (card brand label)

// Text
C.ivory    = "#f1e9d2"
C.cream    = "#e5dcc0"
C.tx       = "#dcd4ba"   // Primary text (12.65:1 on bg)
C.tx2      = "#b5ad95"   // Secondary (8.37:1 on bg)
C.tx3      = "#958e7a"   // Tertiary (was #8e8773 — 4.98:1 on card, 4.58 on cardHi; clears AA on every dark ground, but don't shrink fonts below 13px)
```

Semantic tokens (`C.good` / `C.warn` / `C.bad`) were removed: views reach for `C.sage` (success), `C.amber` (warn) and `C.oxbloodHi` (error) directly so the surfaces compose with the same hue family as the section accents.

**No hardcoded hex in the Curator UI.** Every colour must come from a `C.*` token — a scoped ESLint rule (`no-restricted-syntax` in `eslint.config.js`, on the Curator source: `CuratorApp.tsx` + `components/curator` + `views/curator`) **errors** on any hex literal, both standalone (`background: "#2a1816"`) and inside template literals (`radial-gradient(…, #2a1612, …)`). The six one-off decorative tints that used to be raw hex were consolidated into `C.*`: `panelWarn` (error/warn callout panel), `washEmber` / `washMoss` (warm/cool radial-gradient focals), `docBadgeCave` / `docBadgePot` / `docBadgeFin` (help-doc status-badge backgrounds). `theme-curator.ts` itself is exempt (it DEFINES the tokens); `EB.tsx` is deliberately theme-independent (the theme could be what crashed) and lives outside the curator scope. The same rule block also bans raw `fontSize: <literal>` (every size must flow through `fs()`/`fsInput()`).

**The hex rule had a blind spot: `rgba()` / `hsl()`.** The hex selectors never looked at functional colour notation, which is exactly how `BottomDock`'s frosted pill shipped as a raw `rgba(18,24,21,0.24)` — a dark glass that stayed dark in light mode, leaving the gold dock labels at 2.27:1. Only `npm run theme:contrast` caught it, and only because it renders; nothing static could see it. Four new selectors now cover `rgb()`/`rgba()`/`hsl()`/`hsla()` in both `Literal` and `TemplateElement`. **The rgba ban is deliberately TINTED-ONLY** (a negative-lookahead regex exempting `rgba(0,0,0,α)` and `rgba(255,255,255,α)`): a pure-neutral value is a scrim or a drop shadow and reads the same in both modes, so banning those would have forced ~24 pointless conversions — and an over-strict rule gets correct code rewritten to please it. A NON-neutral rgba is always a palette decision, and it can only be right in the one mode it was eyeballed in. It flagged exactly **2** sites on its first run, both real: `C.oxblood` written out longhand as `rgba(168, 69, 63, 0.08)` in `SettingsModal` **one line above a border that already used `alpha(C.oxblood, …)`** (so the border followed the mode and the background didn't), and a green-tinted near-black modal scrim. `hsl()` is banned outright — it has no neutral idiom here and had zero sites. Probed in both directions, including the historical dock-pill value. **Note the scrim decision**: `Modal.tsx`'s backdrop was NEUTRALISED to `rgba(0,0,0,0.78)`, not tokenised — `alpha(C.bg, …)` would be wrong, because in light mode `C.bg` is cream and the backdrop would wash the page out instead of dimming it. A scrim's job is mode-independent; use a neutral, not a token.

**Colour themes.** The `brass`/`brassHi`/`brassDim` tokens are CSS vars with the classic hex as fallback (`var(--c-brass, #d4a661)`), so the "gold" primary identity is swappable at runtime: `THEMES` (theme-curator.ts) maps each theme id to the `--c-brass*` overrides, `applyTheme(id)` writes them onto `<html>` (seeded pre-mount in `main.jsx`, re-applied on change by App.tsx's `themeId`/`saveThemeId` via `cave-theme`), and every derived palette (DOCK_ACCENT, CARD_ACCENTS, CURATOR_CHART_COLORS) holds the var() string so it follows the swap — NO React re-render (same mechanism as `--cave-font-scale`). Ships `brass` (default) + `steel` (bleu acier) + `english` (anglais — a British forest-green vault). Themed tokens: the brass accent trio, the surface family (`bg`/`bg2`/`bg3`/`card`/`cardHi`/`rule`/`rule2`), AND `title` (the large serif display titles: Home masthead + "Bibliothèque" + the emphasised word in every page title) — all var-with-fallback. `steel` swaps the whole atmosphere + depth (warm green-black vault → cool blue-slate), not just the accent. **`C.title` is separate from the accent on purpose**: the pale steel-blue accent read washed-out as a huge title, so `steel` points `--c-title` at a crisp near-white (`#dbe6f2`) while `english` uses a bright leaf-green and `brass` falls back to the gold. Use `C.title` (not `C.brass`) for any new large display title. **Light/dark mode**: a second axis (`cave-theme-mode`) orthogonal to the colour theme — EVERY colour token (surfaces, text, semantics oxblood/sage/amber/ember/steel, ink, the decorative washes) is now `var(--c-*, <dark fallback>)`. `MODE_LIGHT` (theme-curator.ts) is the shared parchment palette (cream surfaces + dark text + darkened-for-AA semantics); `applyTheme(themeId, mode)` writes `MODE_LIGHT` + `THEMES[id].lightAccent` (a DARK accent, legible on cream) in light mode, or `THEMES[id].vars` in dark. All light values WCAG-AA-validated. `THEME_VARS` lists every var to clear on each apply. **Any new colour MUST be a `C.*` token** (the no-hex rule already enforces this) so it flips with the mode — don't hardcode a light/dark value. Steel surfaces are blue-shifted at matched luminance so every text/border contrast pair carries over (`tx3` on `card` stays ≥ 4.5:1 — validated). Semantic oxblood/sage/amber/ember + the text tokens (tx/ivory/…) intentionally stay so danger/success/warn coding + readability survive the switch. **Translucent tints of a themed token MUST use `alpha(token, "AA")`** (theme-curator.ts) → `color-mix(in srgb, token AA%, transparent)`, NOT the legacy `token + "AA"` / `${token}AA` 8-digit-hex concat — that produces invalid CSS (`var(…)AA`) once the token is a var(); the sweep migrated every brass-family alpha site. **SVG fills/strokes that use a themed token must be set via `style={{fill}}`/`style={{stroke}}`, never the presentation attribute** — WebKit doesn't evaluate `var()` in SVG presentation attributes (Charts.jsx, primitives `Stars`, `Ico`/`Orn` route colour through `style`/`currentColor`). To add a theme: add an entry to `THEMES` + a `theme_<id>` i18n key ×5; to theme MORE tokens, varize them in `C` (var-with-fallback) and add their `--c-*` to the theme's `vars` + `THEME_VARS`. **Verify with `npm run theme:contrast`** — the palette is SIX combinations (3 themes × light/dark) and the app was hand-tuned in exactly one of them (dark brass), so five were never checked by anything. The script renders all six across the shared layout screens (33 of them) and measures every visible text element against its effective background as a WCAG ratio (large text 3:1, the rest 4.5:1), failing below 3:1. It found two real defects on its first run: (1) **the BottomDock's frosted pill was a raw `rgba(18,24,21,0.24)` inline in `BottomDock.tsx`** — a DARK glass that stayed dark in light mode, leaving the gold dock labels at 2.27:1; it is now the `C.dockPill` token with a light-mode value, the dark fallback byte-identical so the installed-PWA look is untouched. (2) the unthemed `CAT_COLORS` split described above — **since fixed, and the acceptance the check carried for it was deleted with it.** Two classes are deliberately NOT failures: text over a **gradient** (the backdrop is not one colour, so any ratio would be fiction — the "Ce soir ?" hero and the CTA stay a manual judgement) and text inside a **disabled control** (WCAG 1.4.3 exempts inactive components — the greyed AICard at 0.7 × 0.6 with no API key, and the form submit at 0.5 until the required fields are filled). **That second exemption was narrowed, and this is the load-bearing part**: it used to be reduced opacity ALONE (`alpha < 0.99`), i.e. any dimming claimed the exemption — which quietly reclassified a genuine defect as acceptable. The inventory card's **POT / CAVE badges** wore `opacity: 0.75` as typographic de-emphasis of the word beside its count; that cost ~40% of the contrast (3.68:1 and 3.23:1 in light mode at 11px, vs 6.44:1 / 5.27:1 at full opacity) and the check waved it through as "deliberately dimmed" on the busiest screen in the app. Reduced opacity is not evidence of disablement, so the walk now also looks for an inactive CONTROL (`aria-disabled` / `:disabled` / `cursor: not-allowed`) and grants the exemption only then; the badge opacity was removed. **Never use `opacity` to de-emphasise TEXT** — reach for a dimmer token, so the ratio stays measurable. Verified by probe (re-adding the badge opacity now reports it with NO `[dimmed]` tag). The same pass gave `PressCard` an `ariaDisabled` prop: the convention for disabling one is `onClick={cond ? undefined : cb}`, which drops `role` and `tabIndex`, so AICard's greyed buttons were announced as plain text — a screen-reader user was never told a search button existed. Its sibling, the `FormFields` submit, had carried `aria-disabled` all along. Everything between 3:1 and AA is reported as a warning to triage — **and that triage was done: 313 → 32 warnings, 0 failures, by retuning SEVEN light-mode tokens** (`--c-tx3` #726a52→#67604a, `--c-sage` #367048→#346c45, `--c-sage-hi` #3f7a52→#305d3f, brass `--c-brass` #7d5f18→#7a5c17 + `--c-brass-hi` #8a6a1f→#695018, steel `--c-brass-hi` #356a94→#2c587a, english `--c-brass-hi` #367a4d→#295e3b). Two things made that pass safe rather than a blanket darkening: the values are **computed to clear 4.5:1 against the DARKER of the two light grounds** (the page, not the card), and each is retuned **for its ROLE** — a `*-hi` token is a brighter sibling in dark mode but must go *darker* than its base in light mode, since "hi" means "more emphasis" and on cream emphasis is weight, not luminance; keeping `--c-sage-hi` lighter than `--c-sage` is what left it under AA. The **32 residuals were deliberate at the time**: 30 were `dimmed` (an ancestor `opacity` — WCAG 1.4.3 exempts inactive components) and 2 were dark-mode `tx3` on a journal card at 4.18:1 / 4.29:1 — the `tx3`-on-`card` hair's breadth the palette had always carried. **Those last two were FIXED** by raising `tx3` #8e8773 → #958e7a (4.98:1 on `card`, 4.58 on `cardHi`), so no TEXT anywhere in the app is under AA now; only the `dimmed` class remains. Re-run the check after ANY light-mode token change; a raw `rgba()` inline in a component is the one thing it can't see coming (that was the dock-pill defect).

**The checks had never rendered a fiche or a modal.** `SCREENS` (shared by `i18n:layout` and `theme:contrast`) walked lists, forms and Settings and not one detail page or dialog, in either check, ever. That is not a small gap: **four light-mode semantic tokens were under AA as text with every instance on exactly those surfaces** — `steel-hi` 3.87:1 (the "Collections" label on all three fiches), `ember` 4.22 (accessory brand; the trash kind label at 9px), `amber` 4.27 (trash + shopping status lines), `oxblood-hi` 4.34 (pipe brand, the aging Notice, both modal delete actions) — and the **trash row clipped 84% of the item name in German at the L text size**, a CLIPPED failure by `i18n:layout`'s own rule on the one screen whose purpose is telling you what you are about to delete for ever. Six screens were added (three fiches, the lot modal, trash, shopping) and both checks now pass over 20. Four things are worth keeping: **(1) the seed is a screen GATE, not decoration** — the trash indicator needs a `deletedAt` row, the cart needs a genuinely low-stock rebuy tobacco (`computeShoppingList` requires `0 < activeWeight <= threshold`, so an already-EMPTY tobacco does not qualify, which is what made the shopping screen unreachable at first), TagChipRow needs tags; `i18nLayoutHarness.test.ts` now asserts each. **(2) An `expect` marker must be exclusive to its screen.** `modal-lot` used `lbl_initial`, which the fiche can also render, so the layout run reported the screen as reached while measuring the fiche underneath — and the contrast run, at a different width, called it unreachable. Two checks disagreeing about one screen is what exposed the marker; it is now `lbl_current`, verified unconditional and modal-only. **(3) A modal opened from a card needs KEYBOARD activation.** The card tap fires through `PressCard`'s pointer path, which installs a one-shot capture listener to swallow the trusted click that follows (the ghost-click defence) — so a programmatic click on the lot row was eaten and the modal never opened. `focus()` + Enter goes through the row's `onKeyDown`, and exercises the a11y path as a bonus. **(4) Fixture STRING LENGTHS are load-bearing, and a real export settled them.** A 41-char blend name was tried and turned the run red in five places that are all by-design ellipsis (Home suggestion rows, the shopping row) — encoding that as a FAILURE would freeze a design decision as permanent red, the over-strict-guard trap. But the user's own 58-tobacco export contains `633: Virginia Flake with Perique` (32) and `Savinelli Marte Rusticated 320 KS` (33), so "41 is unrealistic" was right and "17 is enough" was not. What the real data DID expose, and the synthetic fixture structurally could not: the Home "Familles" row gives its label 66px after a 6px dot, a 26px bar and a 26px percentage, so **`Aromatique` (71px) and `Virginia/Burley` (88px) were clipped at the DEFAULT text size in French** — six of the fifteen canonical categories, on every user's home screen. Those are enum VALUES, so both are now seeded and the label wraps. The lesson generalises: a fixture built from convenient short strings measures a UI no user has.

**The rest of what the audit had already rendered.** The SIX surfaces that had findings were promoted first; the audit had rendered **24**. "Measured clean once" is not "covered" — nothing stopped the other eighteen from regressing. Nine more are now in, prioritising the FORMS (label + field + hint on every row is where German runs longest, which is why `form-tobacco`/`form-pipe` were added back earlier): the session / accessory / wishlist forms, both EDIT forms, the lot FORM modal (a different component from the lot DETAIL modal already covered — `LotFormModal`, and the one with the dense field grid), the maintenance modal, the journal's session-detail modal, and the tasting setup. **20 → 29 screens (33 later, below); both checks pass** (`theme:contrast`: 3 themes × 2 modes × 29, nothing below 3:1; `i18n:layout`: no clipping in fr@M or de@L/360). Two things this pass added to the method. **Every marker was checked for exclusivity BEFORE use**, against `src/views` + `src/components` — the `lbl_initial` defect made that a rule rather than a habit, and `i18nLayoutHarness.test.ts` now ENFORCES it: a marker shared by two screens fails the suite, with one documented exemption (`lbl_edit`, the edit-mode overline — an edit form is literally the same component as its add form, so no marker can separate them; the navigation path is what distinguishes them, and the test asserts the exemption is actually in use so it can't become dead licence). **The navigation labels are worth grepping, not guessing**: the journal's "+" is `btn_new_session`, not `btn_add` (it pre-fills date + time, so it is its own control) and the wishlist chip is `lbl_wishlist`, not `f_wish` — both wrong on the first attempt, and both surfaced as a LOUD failure (a missing key dies; an unreachable screen fails the run) rather than a silently skipped screen, which is the property that makes this list trustworthy.

**The coverage now equals what was measured.** The last three surfaces the audit had rendered and I had not promoted: the **wishlist LIST** (the inventory in `wish` mode — distinct from the wish FORM), the **catalogue**, and the **global search modal** (whose group headers only render once there are results, so typing a query is part of reaching it — correctly, since an empty search modal is just a text field). Plus one VARIANT: a **retired pipe's fiche**, the branch that hid the whole-card opacity for as long as the fixture held only active pipes. **29 → 33 screens, and both checks pass over all of them** (`theme:contrast`: 3 themes × 2 modes × 33, nothing below 3:1; `i18n:layout`: no clipping in fr@M or de@L/360). That variant forced the exclusivity rule to be stated properly rather than widened by accident: a marker may be shared ONLY when the screens are the same COMPONENT in a different state (`lbl_edit` for the two edit forms, `sec_specs` for the two pipe fiches) — there no marker can separate them and the navigation path is what does. What the rule forbids is sharing across DIFFERENT components, which is exactly the defect. `i18nLayoutHarness.test.ts` enforces both halves and asserts each exemption is IN USE, so it cannot decay into dead licence; probed in both directions.

**Guarding the tokens in `npm test`, not only in the opt-in check** (`semanticTokensLight.test.ts`): the browser check needs a browser and is not a CI gate, so it can go months unrun — `prune` had already demonstrated exactly that. The test re-derives every light-mode semantic ratio against the page ground rather than pinning hexes, asserts the four fixed tokens are above their pre-fix values (a revert that keeps the key and restores the old hex fails), asserts the fix DARKENED rather than recoloured (dominant-channel ordering must match the dark sibling, or status coding stops being status coding), asserts every token is in `THEME_VARS`, and **records the two deliberate exemptions with their reasons** — `--c-amber-hi` (2.99:1, which looks like a hard failure and is not: it is the mid step of the activity-calendar cell ramp, never text) and `--c-steel` (a chart fill). A rule with an unexplained exception invites the next sweep to "complete" it and flatten the ramp. This is also why the pairs can look inverted (a `*-hi` lighter than its base) without repeating the `sage-hi` defect: that rule is about an emphasis pair where BOTH members are text, and here only the `*-hi` ever is.


Fonts (`F.*`):
- `F.display` = Newsreader (italic serif, used for titles + cards)
- `F.body` = DM Sans (sans-serif body)
- `F.mono` = IBM Plex Mono (numerics, labels, badges)

Self-hosted as variable woff2 files under `public/fonts/` (the previous Google Fonts hosting was removed). `index.html` declares the `@font-face` block inline, with `<link rel="preload">` for `dm-sans-var.woff2` + `newsreader-var.woff2` to prioritise the LCP path. `font-display: swap` avoids invisible-text flashes if a font file is slow. CSP enforces `font-src 'self'`.

Per-section dock accent (`DOCK_ACCENT[viewKey]`):
- `home` → brass, `inv` → amber, `pipes` → oxbloodHi, `acc` → ember, `journal` → sage, `stats` → brassHi.

**`catColor(category)` (in `theme-curator.ts`) reads `CAT_COLORS` from `constants.ts`** — the ONE category palette. Before that there were TWO: this raw-hex one (bright, saturated hues) and a themed `CURATOR_CAT_COLORS` in theme-curator.ts used by **StatsView alone** — imported there *as* `CAT_COLORS`, which is exactly why the split survived unnoticed. It cost two visible defects, both found by `npm run theme:contrast`: the same family was one colour on Stats and another on Home / the fiche / journal / catalogue, and because the live palette was raw hex it did NOT follow the light/dark mode — on the parchment ground the category text rendered at 2:1–2.9:1, well under AA. **It was resolved (the user chose "keep the bright identity"):** every value is now `var(--c-cat-<slug>, <bright hex>)`, so dark mode is byte-identical while `MODE_LIGHT` substitutes a DARKENED variant per family; StatsView moved onto `catColor()`; and `CURATOR_CAT_COLORS` was DELETED, because leaving both is what produced the divergence. The 15 light values are COMPUTED, not eyeballed — same hue, saturation capped at 0.72 (parchment reads badly under fully-saturated ink), lightness reduced until the ratio clears 4.6:1 on the DARKER of the two light grounds (the page `#e7ddc6`; the card is lighter and therefore easier). **The palette is now a pair of tables joined by a slug**, which rots silently — add a category, forget its `--c-cat-<slug>` override, and it simply stays bright and unreadable on cream with nothing failing. `catColorsLight.test.ts` is that join: it re-derives every contrast ratio, checks each slug has an override AND is listed in `THEME_VARS` (an unlisted var survives a switch back to dark), flags a stale override for a removed category, and pins the dark fallbacks so the vault look can't shift by accident. **A var() cannot be hex-concatenated** — use `alpha(catColor(x), "22")`, never `catColor(x) + "22"`, and set SVG colours via `style={{ fill }}` (WebKit ignores var() in a presentation attribute); the chart helpers already do both. The ACCEPTANCE in `theme-contrast.cjs` was deleted with the fix — a live acceptance would hide the next instance of the same class. Still used by the InventoryDetailView / Home-suggestion mini-cards, but **no longer by the inventory LIST cards** (see `CARD_ACCENTS` below). Charts use `CURATOR_CHART_COLORS` (rotating brass / oxblood / sage / amber; **`C.steel` was added at index 3** — the one cool hue in the chart rotation).

**`CARD_ACCENTS` — shared list-card accent rotation.** `theme-curator.ts` exports one palette `CARD_ACCENTS = [brass, oxbloodHi, sage, steelHi, amber, brassHi, ember, sageHi]` used **identically by the list cards** — `InventoryListView` (TobaccoCard + WishCard), `PipesListView` (PipeCard), `AccListView` (AccessoryCard), and `JournalView` (JournalEntry — top bar only; the session card has no brand label). Index-rotated per card (`CARD_ACCENTS[idx % CARD_ACCENTS.length]!`, non-null asserted — modulo is provably in-bounds), so a mixed list alternates hues down the page regardless of category/type. **The same value drives the 2px card top-accent bar AND the brand label (`<Lbl>`) AND the placeholder photo icon**, so the brand text always matches its bar. (The top bar was briefly stripped in the recessed-tone pass and **restored** — the per-card colour bar is a wanted signal, distinct from the Home info-card gradient hairlines that WERE removed. The card ground is still the recessed `CARD_BG`; only the coloured bar returned.) The blue slot uses `C.steelHi` (not `C.steel`) because the accent doubles as small brand-label text and the hi shade is the AA-comfortable one. When you add a new inventory-list card type, colour its top bar + label from `CARD_ACCENTS[idx % len]` too — do NOT reintroduce a per-view fixed colour or a `catColor`/`CURATOR_CHART_COLORS` split.

**`CARD_BG` — the recessed card/panel ground.** `theme-curator.ts` exports `CARD_BG = C.bg2` as THE single source of truth for every browse-page card & panel background — a step darker than the old lifted `C.card`, matching the interior tone of the Home "À surveiller" rows. The "encaissé" pass moved every card/panel across Home + the browse pages (Inventory list/detail, Pipes list/detail, Accessory list/detail, Journal, Catalog, Stats) from `C.card` to `CARD_BG`, dropped card radii to 8, and **removed the Home info-card gradient hairlines** — colour otherwise lives in text/labels/chips/section-title ornaments. **The list-card `CARD_ACCENTS` top bar is KEPT** (restored after the recessed-tone pass over-stripped it) — it's the wanted per-card colour signal on the tobacco/pipe/accessory/wish cards. Coloured filets that remain: the list-card top bars, and the Home dashboard stat tiles' thin **left** accent bar (the `Tile` component in `HomeViewV2`). Two focal elements stay deliberately lifted (gradient + shadow, not recessed): the Home "Ce soir ?" hero and the "Démarrer une dégustation" CTA. **New cards MUST reference `CARD_BG`, never a raw `C.bg2`**, so the whole app's card ground stays retunable in one edit. Inner tracks / empty heatmap cells that sit ON a `CARD_BG` card use `C.bg` (a step darker) so they stay visible instead of vanishing bg2-on-bg2. **The alignment is now app-wide**: the recessed `CARD_BG` ground also covers `TastingView`, the form-field primitive (`FormFields.tsx` — every text/select/textarea field, so all forms follow), `SettingsModal`, `TrashModal`, the `Overlays` update pill/toast banners, `HelpView`, and `TermsGate`. `C.card` is effectively retired as a background token (kept in the palette for `linear-gradient` fades + `C.cardHi` nested surfaces only) — reach for `CARD_BG` for any new card/panel/field surface. **The layering model (keep it consistent):** page ground = `C.bg`; **the shared `Modal` panel (`Modal.tsx`) is also `C.bg`** (a page-like ground, NOT a card) so every modal's inner `CARD_BG` cards (session-detail blocks, Settings/Trash rows, lot detail…) read exactly as on a browse page instead of merging bg2-on-bg2; card / panel / FormSection = `CARD_BG` (bg2), sits on the ground; **form input fields recess to `C.bg`** (`baseInput` in `FormFields.tsx`) so they read as inset wells inside their `CARD_BG` section rather than merging with it. The one soft spot: `LotFormModal` / `MaintFormModal` place fields directly on the `C.bg` modal panel (no FormSection), so those fields are delineated by their border only — acceptable, wrap them in a `CARD_BG` panel if a future pass wants inset wells there too. `TastingView` inputs sit on the page ground, so they stay `CARD_BG` (raised) rather than `C.bg` (which would be flat-on-flat).

**Activity-calendar cell ramp — keep the two calendars in lock-step.** Both smoking calendars share one look: **brass chrome** (title / top hairline / tap arrow / total count) + a warm **amber cell ramp with an oxblood "attention" top**. The cell colours (level 1 → 2 → 3+) are `C.amber + "55"` → `C.amberHi` → `C.oxbloodHi`; empty is `C.bg` (it was `C.bg2` — the calendar cards now sit on a `CARD_BG`=bg2 ground, so empty cells dropped a step to `C.bg` to stay visible; the card's top hairline was also removed in the recessed-tone pass). The `oxbloodHi` top level is intentional — a 4+/day heavy day must still read as a warning, so the ramp escalates by HUE (amber→red), not purely by lightness. Two call sites: `HomeViewV2` renders its own inline grid (the `bg` ternary in the activity card), `StatsView` passes the same ramp as the `{empty, low, mid, high}` palette to `calendarHeatmap` (Charts.jsx) and sets the "Calendrier" Card `accent={C.brass}`. The heatmap cells were sage at first, then a semantic sage/brass/oxblood ramp on Stats specifically. **Change both together** — a divergence is the regression to avoid.

**Home "Ce soir" + "À entretenir" lists — inset rows.** The two vertical lists in `HomeViewV2` (secondary suggestions, maintenance reminders) render each row as a subtly **inset panel** (`background: C.bg2`, `borderRadius: 8`, `border: 1px solid C.rule`) inside a flex column with `gap: 5`, NOT as flush rows separated by a bottom `borderBottom` rule. Transparent rows on `C.card` made naive gaps invisible, so the rows read as "one heap" — the inset panels give each item breathing room. Keep the container `padding: 6` + `gap` model if you touch these lists.

## Service Worker Notes

- Cache name: `cave-tabac-v1-0-1` (current). In `public/sw.js`. See bumping rules below.
- Cached assets: `index.html`, `help.html`, `reset.html`, `changelog.html`, `privacy.html`, `manifest.json`, `icon-192.png`, `icon-512.png`. `licenses.html` is NOT pre-cached (served network-first like every other page). No CDN scripts — React 19 is bundled by Vite. Self-hosted woff2 fonts are fetched once and served from the SW cache on subsequent loads (cache-first per the default fetch handler).
- **Never cached** (always fetched from network): `api.anthropic.com`, `api.github.com`, `api.openai.com`, `corsproxy.io`, `allorigins.win`, `googleapis.com`, `accounts.google.com`, `gstatic.com`. Bypass check parses the URL hostname and matches exact host or `*.host` suffix — the previous `indexOf` form was flagged by CodeQL as an incomplete URL substring sanitization.
- **`self.clients.claim()` is intentionally absent** from the `activate` handler. This ensures the new SW does not take over open pages mid-session — activation only occurs via `doUpdate()` (`SKIP_WAITING` → `location.reload()`), which is called automatically after the 10s countdown banner or on explicit user action in Settings.
- **`reg.update()` must NEVER be called automatically** (no timers, no visibility-change handlers). Calling it downloads a new SW silently; once that SW enters "waiting", the browser activates it automatically the next time all clients close (e.g. user closes and reopens the app), bypassing user consent. Version detection uses `checkVersion()` only (fetches `version.json` from network — no SW installation side-effect).
- **CRITICAL — automatic update mechanism**: Any change to `sw.js` causes the browser to install a new SW in the background. That SW enters "waiting". The next time the user closes all tabs and reopens the app, the browser activates it automatically — the user experiences this as an unwanted automatic update. This is standard browser behavior that cannot be prevented once a new SW is waiting.
- **HTML pages are network-first** (this used to say *navigation requests*, and the difference was the bug): `index.html`, `help.html`, `changelog.html`, `reset.html`, `privacy.html` are served network-first by the SW, so users always get the latest version when online, and there is NO need to change `sw.js` when these files change. **The branch used to key on `event.request.mode === 'navigate'`, which is true only for a browser NAVIGATION — while the in-app doc views (`DocPageView`, `HelpView`) read those same files with a plain `fetch("./help.html")`.** That is not a navigation, so it fell through to the cache-first branch and was served the copy captured at SW install, indefinitely. The claim above was therefore false precisely where users read the docs, and the workflow rule drawn from it ("documentation-only changes do NOT require bumping `APP_BUILD`") was false with it. The branch now keys on the URL being an HTML document (`isHtmlDoc`), which makes the documented behaviour the real one. **Same build: a 5xx no longer reaches the user when a cached copy exists.** A `fetch` that receives a 500 RESOLVES — it does not reject — so the handler's `.catch` never ran on a server error and the raw error page was returned while a good cached copy sat one line away. A GitHub Pages hiccup or a half-finished deploy broke an app that is otherwise fully offline-capable. **4xx still passes through on purpose**: a genuine 404 means the page is gone, and masking it with a stale copy would hide a deploy that dropped a file.

## Development Workflow

### Running the app
```bash
npm run dev
# Opens http://localhost:5173
```

### Making changes
Application code is split across `src/`. The main entry point is `src/App.tsx` (state + hooks owner) which renders `<CuratorApp />`.
Views are in `src/views/curator/`. Curator primitives in `src/components/curator/`. Custom hooks in `src/hooks/`. Pure utils in `src/utils/`.

### After every change
Always run quality checks before committing:
```bash
npm run typecheck   # Must pass (0 errors)
npm run build       # Must succeed
npm test            # Must pass (all tests green)
npm run lint        # Check for new lint errors (0 errors, some warnings acceptable)
npm run prune       # knip — must exit 0 (a gate)
```

**Why `prune` is a gate now.** It used to be a "re-run after any non-trivial refactor" tool, so nobody re-ran it: it had been failing (exit 1) while CLAUDE.md kept asserting a zero-warning baseline — nine releases of a red check that read as green in the docs. It costs **2.0 s**, the same as `doc:check`, so the only thing that kept it optional was habit. A check nobody runs is documentation, not a check.

### Tests — mandatory on every modification

**LE BOUTON ENREGISTRER N'ÉTAIT JAMAIS TAPÉ, DANS LES TROIS FORMULAIRES.** Une campagne de mutation sur 14 vues (80 mutations, chacune vérifiée appliquée avant d'être crue) a rendu **35 mises à mort / 45 survivantes**, avec `SessionFormView` à **0 sur 10**. La cause commune de douze d'entre elles tient en un fait : `SessionFormView.test.tsx`, `TobaccoFormView.test.tsx` et `PipeFormView.test.tsx` ne contenaient **aucune occurrence** d'`addSession`/`updateSession`, `addTobacco`/`updateTobacco`, `addPipe`/`updatePipe`. Ces suites rendent la vue, vérifient des pré-remplissages et des états `aria-disabled`, et n'exercent jamais l'écriture. Ce que ça laissait passer se lit en une ligne — `(isEdit ? updateX : addX)()` inversé : **éditer CRÉE un doublon** (nouvel `id`, nouvel `uid`, donc une seconde identité de fusion inter-appareils) et **ajouter ÉCRASE**, sans qu'aucun invariant ne le voie, les deux résultats étant des données valides. Le bouton est tapé maintenant, dans les trois, avec le garde `canSave` de chacun (l'identité pour tabac/pipe, le poids positif comptabilité activée pour la séance — dont le commentaire NOMMAIT `pipeId` et le poids, les deux termes qu'aucun cas ne faisait varier seuls).

**« EFFACER TOUTES LES DONNÉES » N'ÉTAIT ASSERTÉ PAR AUCUN TEST DE VUE.** Les trois seules occurrences de `resetAll` dans la suite sont des tests de HOOK : la fonction est couverte sous toutes les coutures — cave, photos, identifiants cloud, clés API — et son APPEL ne l'était pas. La forme *the wiring is what rots*, déjà payée sur `chooseAutoSaveTarget` et `reDeductRestoredSessions`. **Le miroir compte autant que l'endroit** : un cas éprouve chaque AUTRE bouton de l'onglet et exige qu'aucun n'appelle `resetAll`, sinon un contrôle anodin pouvait être recâblé dessus sans rien rougir. Sondé dans les deux sens. **Et sans `if (btn)`** : ce fichier en contient déjà un — la forme creuse n°1 — et le seul bouton irréversible de l'app est le pire endroit où « je n'ai pas trouvé le bouton » vaudrait succès.

**UNE ASSERTION QUE J'AVAIS ÉCRITE ÉTAIT CREUSE, ET C'EST L'ENTRÉE LA PLUS UTILE DU LOT.** `deferAutoUpdate.test.ts` verrouillait le signal de la modale d'entretien par `expect(PIPES).toContain("setMaintFormOpen")` — une recherche de chaîne sur tout le fichier. La chaîne survit dans la déclaration (`const setMaintFormOpen = ctx.setMaintFormOpen`) et dans le nettoyage, si bien que **supprimer l'appel qui SIGNALE l'ouverture laissait les 17 cas verts** (sondé). Seul le nettoyage était réellement couvert, par une regex. Conséquence : la modale cesse de bloquer l'auto-update, et une release *data-only* recharge par-dessus une note d'entretien à moitié écrite. Le comportement est piloté maintenant (`PipesDetailView.test.tsx`), et l'assertion de câblage exige l'appel AVEC son argument. **Une recherche de sous-chaîne sur un identifiant qui apparaît aussi dans sa déclaration ne verrouille rien.**

**UN CONSTAT D'AGENT VÉRIFIÉ ET RÉFUTÉ, consigné parce que la couche absorbante est instructive.** Le rapport présentait la suppression de `lotId: ""` dans le patch de changement de tabac comme une dérive de stock permanente et silencieuse. La conséquence décrite est juste ; l'état ne s'atteint pas. `tobOptions` n'inscrit un tabac que s'il a un lot UTILISABLE (ou, en édition, s'il est celui déjà choisi) et `pickSessionLot` choisit parmi ces lots-là — donc tout tabac ATTEIGNABLE dans la liste se voit réattribuer un lot à lui dans la même passe, et la remise à zéro est écrasée avant d'avoir servi. C'est exactement la garantie « par construction » pour laquelle `pickSessionLot` a été extrait. Il reste UNE différence observable, le choix VIDE, épinglée comme telle. **Quand une sonde reste verte, trouver la couche qui l'absorbe — et quand un rapport décrit un dégât, vérifier que l'état se produit avant d'écrire le test.** Sondé : la mutation rougit le cas du choix vide et laisse vert celui de la réattribution, ce qui est précisément la preuve.

**LES SIX SURVIVANTES NOMMÉES SONT FERMÉES, et deux détails de MÉTHODE valent plus que les cas.** L'inversion `addMaintenance`/`updateMaintenance` (corriger une entrée la DOUBLE, ce qui remet le compteur de rappel à zéro deux fois), la cible de la suppression DURE du carnet — la seule de l'app sans corbeille, donc effacer la mauvaise entrée perd ses notes libres définitivement — le miroir `weightG ← weightInitial` à la création d'un lot (sans lui, tout nouveau lot naît avec un solde de 50 g hérité de `BL` et viole `lot-balance` immédiatement ; le garde aval `if (!base.weightG && …)` ne rattrape rien puisque `BL.weightG` est truthy), le bouton Supprimer du lot recâblable sur `onDuplicate` — ce fichier ne passait JAMAIS de prop `onDelete` — l'allumage d'une dégustation sans lot RÉSOLUBLE, et le `×` de la bannière cloud, dont la GÉOMÉTRIE était verrouillée par un test entier et la CIBLE par rien. **(a) Deux boutons de `PipesDetailView` portent `aria-label="btn_delete"`** — celui de la PIPE dans la barre du haut et celui de l'entrée d'entretien — donc une recherche globale prend le premier et un cas qui croit éprouver la suppression d'une entrée éprouve la suppression de la pipe, vert pour la mauvaise raison : **en pilotant une modale, se scoper à `role="dialog"`**, la leçon déjà consignée pour `CompareModal`. **(b) Deux sélecteurs écrits d'après le code ont échoué contre le rendu réel** : la date d'une entrée s'affiche `02.05.2026` et non `2.5.2026` (et s'y accrocher aurait de toute façon lié le cas au réglage `dateFormat`, qui n'est pas son sujet — les notes sont le bon ancrage), et `TextField` rend un `type="text"` avec `inputMode`, jamais un `type="number"`. **Vider le DOM une fois coûte trente secondes et évite deux corrections en aveugle.**

**NON MESURÉ ET DÉCLARÉ** : 15 vues sur 29 (dont `InventoryListView`, 1693 lignes), les 21 hooks, et sur les vues traitées uniquement les chemins d'écriture, de suppression et de garde — pas les rendus, la mise en page, l'i18n ni les mémos de filtrage. Les six survivantes nommées dans la première version de ce paragraphe ont depuis été fermées (voir le bloc au-dessus) ; ce qui reste non mesuré est le PÉRIMÈTRE, pas une liste de défauts connus.


Every code change must ship with the matching tests. Before committing, audit the diff and add any missing coverage:

- **New hook (`src/hooks/`):** add a `src/__tests__/<hookName>.test.ts` covering initial state, every action, persistence (localStorage), and edge cases (no-op branches, invalid input).
- **New view (`src/views/`):** add a `src/__tests__/<ViewName>.test.tsx` covering visibility (returns null when `view !==` expected), rendering of the main elements, and all interactive controls (clicks → expected callbacks fired with expected args).
- **New public helper in `src/utils/`:** add a `src/__tests__/<helper>.test.ts` covering happy path and edge cases.
- **Modified hook/view:** extend the existing test file with cases that exercise the new behaviour — never assume the existing tests already cover it.
- **Refactored shared helper exposed for reuse** (e.g. extracting a method to be called from multiple sites): add tests for the new public surface even if the original caller is still covered.
- **Bug fix:** add a regression test that fails on the old code and passes on the fix.

If a change cannot be tested in isolation (UI animation, real network call, OAuth redirect), say so explicitly in the commit message rather than skipping coverage silently. Pure logic, hook actions, and component rendering with mocked context are always testable.

**FIFTEEN CASES ACROSS FIVE FILES GUARANTEED NOTHING, AND THEY FAILED IN EXACTLY TWO SHAPES.** An audit named them; every one was PROBED before being touched (mutate the code the case claims to guard, run it, watch it stay green). The count matters less than the two shapes, because both are easy to write and invisible on a green dashboard.

**SHAPE 1 — `if (el) { …assertions… }`.** The `JournalView` delete case looked for `button[aria-label='trash']` on the ROW and wrapped its click and both assertions in that guard. The row has carried no trash icon since the delete moved into the session-detail modal — **and a case two describes further down asserts exactly that** — so `trash` was always null, the block never ran, and it passed with ZERO assertions while claiming to cover the app's delete path. `TastingBanner`'s two overtime controls did the same through a `try { getByText(…) } catch { return null }` + `if (btn)`. **The rule: a conditional around an assertion turns "the control disappeared" into a pass**, which is the one outcome a UI test must never treat as success. If the control can be absent, its absence is the failure.

**SHAPE 2 — asserting a TRANSLATED string under a key-returning `t`.** `renderWithCtx`'s `t` returns the KEY, so « Continuer », « Accueil » and « existe déjà » appear nowhere, under any code. Three `CuratorApp` dock cases asserted `not.toMatch(/Accueil.*Catalogue.*Pipes.*Atelier.*Journal/)` — a negative that held whether the dock was hidden, shown, or deleted outright (two were stale as well: the dock has said « Tabacs », not « Catalogue », for a long time). Six duplicate-banner NEGATIVES forbade only `/existe déjà|already exists/` while the POSITIVE case beside them accepted `dup_tob_pre` **because the author had hit exactly this** — so the positives worked and the negatives could not fail. **PROBED: forcing the duplicate memo to return a row for every form state left all 26 cases in `TobaccoFormView.test.tsx` green.** The rule: **a negative assertion must reject exactly what the positive one accepts.**

**Two more, worth naming for their own reasons.** `expect(text).toBeTruthy()` asserted that the page rendered *something* — and it stood in for the dock's section filtering. And the reason the dock cases were loose at all is instructive: **the dock is PORTALED to `document.body`** (the iOS-PWA float guardrail), so it is not in the render container they searched; rather than fail visibly, they were widened until they passed. `dockPortal.test.tsx` already had the right shape (`dock_*` labels, searched under `document.body`), one file away.

**A whole HOOK had never been executed: `useBackNavigation`.** Two files named it and both only read it as SOURCE. `navHistory.test.ts` covers the routing engine; the transport — the popstate listener, the re-push that keeps a back entry available, the 400 ms debounce, the edge-swipe geometry, the latest-closure ref, the teardown — was guarded by nothing. **A listener on the wrong target is precisely the `useAppUpdate` defect** (`pagehide` on `document` instead of `window`, inert for six releases). `useBackNavigation.test.tsx` drives it for real; five probes (kill the debounce, the ref, the re-push, the edge band, the vertical guard) each redden.

**When you write a view test, ask what would happen if the control vanished** — if the answer is "it passes", the test is decoration.

**A THIRD SHAPE, and this one FAILED FOR HALF OF EVERY DAY WITHOUT ANYONE NOTICING: a negative assertion on the WHOLE PAGE.** `HomeViewV2.test.tsx`'s maintenance-cap case asserted that the sixth overdue pipe « must not be on the Home » by reading `container.textContent` — but the « Ce soir ? » hero names a PAIRED PIPE (« home_pair_with Halvorsen Foxtrot »), chosen by `suggestRestedPipe` on a 12-hour rotation bucket, and the seven fixtures are equally rested. So which pipe the hero names depends on the CLOCK. **Pinned with `vi.setSystemTime` on identical code: PASSES at 11:30 UTC, FAILS at 23:30 UTC** — and it was caught by an ordinary full-suite run that happened to cross 12:00 UTC, not by anything looking for it. **The lesson is not about clocks.** A negative assertion over the whole page is answered by every sibling feature, so it stops testing what it names; the positive direction has the mirror flaw, since `toContain("Alpha")` passes on a broken section the moment the hero happens to pair Alpha. Both are scoped now, through a `maintText(container)` helper that slices at the section heading and fails loudly if the section is absent — **NOT a `data-` hook**, because `MaintRow` renders a `PressCard`, which destructures a fixed prop list and would not forward one, and wrapping it in a marked `<div>` would change a flex item on a screen the layout matrix had just certified. The sibling case that opens the modal was ALREADY scoped (`[role=dialog]`) and needed nothing, which is what identifies this as a miss rather than a convention. Probed in both directions: four clock buckets pass, and removing the production cap still reddens it. **When a view test names an entity, scope it to the section under test — the Home renders six features that can all name a pipe.**

**THE a11y SUITE AUDITED SIX VIEWS WITH AN EMPTY CELLAR, AND WIDENING THE FIXTURE FOUND A REAL DEFECT ON THE LANDING SCREEN.** Every case passed `[]` for every collection, so each list rendered its EMPTY STATE and axe examined a sentence and a button — not one card, chip, status badge, star row, photo column or filter dropdown, i.e. none of the controls a11y defects live in. The file's own header says it exists to catch *"missing labels, div onClick patterns, missing ARIA"*, and an empty list contains none of those to get wrong. **Same finding as the two browser checks, a third time: a green run over an empty state is the most reassuring way to miss a screen — the seed is a GATE, not decoration.** The fixture now exercises the branches that carry ARIA (a lot in each status, a no-rebuy tobacco, a retired accessory, a finished pipe, a rated session with aromas, a wishlist row) and the wishlist mode of the inventory list got its own case, since `WishCard` is a different component reachable only through `statusFilter`.

**What it found: the Home « Ce soir ? » hero is a `PressCard` (`role="button"`) and the paired-pipe chip was a real `<button>` INSIDE it** — `nested-interactive`, WCAG 4.1.2. The cost is concrete: VoiceOver flattens a button's subtree into its accessible name, so the chip was not separately focusable and the whole accord shortcut was unreachable to that user. **It was also fighting the platform and said so** — the chip carried `stopPropagation` on pointerdown, pointerup AND click because *"a click-only stopPropagation leaked and opened the tobacco"*, which is the tell that the nesting was wrong rather than clever. The accord row is now a SIBLING of the card (same 12 px gutter, so it stays aligned with the blend name); all three propagation handlers are gone, since outside the card there is nothing to leak into. Locked by the « the accord chip is not nested » block in `HomeViewV2.test.tsx`, whose second case asserts the hero is STILL a control in its own right — a careless fix would move the chip out and cost the card its tap target. Probed: re-nesting the chip reddens 3 cases across two files.

**A PROCESS NOTE THAT COST A RECOVERY: I restored `HomeViewV2.tsx` from a copy taken BEFORE the fix, and silently reverted it.** The rule in this file is "never undo a probe with `git checkout`, restore from a hand-taken copy" — and a hand-taken copy is only safe if it was taken AFTER the change you want to keep. **Take the copy immediately before applying the probe, not at the start of the work.**

**THE LOT-LIFECYCLE PROPERTY TEST GENERATED WHOLE GRAMS, so the deduction-grid rule was unreachable by it.** The audit called it "a re-implementation of the stores" and that is only half right, and the half it got wrong matters: it composes the REAL `applyLotWeightDelta` and `applyLifecycleDates`, so the arithmetic under test is production code and the mirror is only the orchestration — a legitimate model-based test. What HAD drifted is that the mirror stored and debited one raw value while `_persistSession` rounds through `roundWeightToUnit` and stores THAT, so the mirror modelled the already-fixed world; and every generator emitted integers, on which the rounding is a no-op. The rule whose absence produced a false `lot-balance-overflow` was therefore invisible from two directions at once. Session weights now carry 2 decimals (a hand-typed 2.55 g is the ordinary case — the form takes free text) and the mirror rounds where the store rounds; LOT weights stay integers, because the store does not round those and modelling something the app does not do is its own defect.

**Then the probe stayed GREEN and the absorbing layer was the TOLERANCE.** Grams round to 1 dp, so the worst drift is 0.05 g per session and the property's 0.15 g window covers three — while 25 ops over 8 lot ids rarely puts more than that on one lot. So the rule got a DETERMINISTIC case built for it: ten 2.55 g sessions on ONE lot, Σ asserted EXACTLY rather than within a tolerance, which is the shape of the real report (the drift only surfaced once enough >1 dp sessions accumulated on one tin). **A second probe stayed green too, and that one is recorded on the test rather than engineered around**: dropping the rounding on the EDIT path changes nothing in the model, because the mirror stores `nw` and derives the delta from that same variable — the store is exposed only because it reads the raw `sessForm.weightG`, a difference no model that derives one value from the other can express. The case keeps the half that IS expressible (an edit leaves Σ exact, so the restore/deduct pair cannot leak) and says plainly what it does not cover. **A tolerance is the commonest absorbing layer there is: when a probe survives one, add a case with no tolerance rather than widening the generator.**

### Service Worker versioning

**`APP_BUILD` in `src/constants.ts`**: bump on every build (controls the version display in Settings).

**`CACHE_NAME` in `public/sw.js`**: bump **ONLY** when one of these changes:
- `public/icon-192.png` or `public/icon-512.png`
- The SW logic in `public/sw.js` itself

**`manifest.json` was on this list and is deliberately no longer.** The rule predates the change that made `doUpdate()` purge unconditionally: it now unregisters every SW and deletes EVERY `caches.*` entry before the reload, and it runs on every build via the `version.json` flow. So a changed manifest reaches users through the ordinary build update — the SW reinstalls from scratch afterwards and re-fetches `CORE_URLS` from the network. Bumping `CACHE_NAME` for it is not merely unnecessary, it has a real cost the next bullet spells out: a byte-different `sw.js` makes the browser install a new SW in the background for everyone, which then activates on the next cold open, independently of the app's own update flow. (A user who never takes an update keeps a stale manifest — harmless: they keep a stale app too, and the manifest only supplies install-time metadata they have already consumed.) Editing `manifest.json` therefore needs the normal `APP_BUILD` bump and nothing more. Its shape is locked by the `manifest.json` block in `serviceWorker.test.ts` (valid JSON, installability fields, every declared icon present on disk, a maskable icon, and a `lang` naming a shipped UI language).

**NEVER bump `sw.js` for `src/` changes or `.html` file changes.** These files are served network-first — the user always gets the latest from the server without any SW change. Bumping `sw.js` unnecessarily installs a new SW that the browser then activates automatically when the user closes and reopens the app, which the user experiences as an unwanted automatic update.

### Editing documentation files (help.html, changelog.html, privacy.html)

These files live in `public/`. **Always fetch the current version from GitHub before editing**, using `mcp__github__get_file_contents` (owner: `yokyok71`, repo: `tabac`). This ensures edits are applied on top of the live server version, not a potentially stale local clone.

**Documentation-only changes do NOT require bumping `APP_BUILD`** in `src/constants.ts`. These files are served network-first — the browser always fetches the latest from the server. Only bump `APP_BUILD` when `src/` code changes.

#### `public/help.html` structural contract (in-app `HelpView` depends on it)

`HelpView` parses `help.html` at runtime instead of opening it in a new tab. The view assumes a specific structure — break it and entire sections render as empty title-less cards. **When editing `help.html`, you MUST preserve all of the following invariants:**

- **Language wrappers**: `<div id="sec-fr">…</div>`, `<div id="sec-en">…</div>`, and `<div id="sec-es">`, `<div id="sec-de">`, `<div id="sec-it">` at the body level. Every section h2 must be a descendant of its language wrapper. `HelpView.SECTION_IDS` + `HELP_SECTION_IDS` (doc-check) list the per-language ids; doc-check validates every language whose wrapper is present. es/de/it/pt reuse the EN suffix (`es-install`, `pt-tobacco`, …); fr keeps its own (`fr-tabac`).
- **18 sections per language, each anchored by an h2 with a stable id** — the id ↔ key mapping is locked in three places that must stay aligned: `SECTION_IDS` in `src/views/curator/HelpView.tsx`, `HELP_SECTION_IDS` in `scripts/doc-check.cjs`, and the literal `<h2 id="…">` tags in `help.html`. If you rename, add, or remove a section id you must update all three at once.
  - FR ids: `fr-install`, `fr-concepts`, `fr-cycle`, `fr-catalogue`, `fr-tabac`, `fr-lots`, `fr-inventaire`, `fr-pipes`, `fr-wishlist`, `fr-acc`, `fr-journal`, `fr-ia`, `fr-stats`, `fr-sauvegarde`, `fr-maj`, `fr-depannage`, `fr-corbeille`, `fr-parametres`. (`install` sits at the top so new users land on the install procedure first.)
  - EN ids: `en-install`, `en-concepts`, `en-cycle`, `en-catalogue`, `en-tobacco`, `en-lots`, `en-inventory`, `en-pipes`, `en-wishlist`, `en-acc`, `en-journal`, `en-ai`, `en-stats`, `en-backup`, `en-updates`, `en-troubleshooting`, `en-trash`, `en-settings`.
- **Each h2 must have non-empty text** (it becomes the collapsible card's title) and must be paired with its EN/FR sibling (a section that exists in one language but not the other will render with an empty title in the missing language).
- **Well-formed nesting in the body between h2s** — no stray `</div>` or unclosed tags. A malformed tag inside any list, table, or note will silently auto-close the wrapping `sec-fr` / `sec-en` div and eject every subsequent h2 to body level. The runtime parser is source-order-robust against this (it slices the raw HTML between h2 anchors), but the visual structure of the card breaks anyway and the cellar/journal/whatever stylings of the orphaned content may be subtly wrong.

**`npm run doc:check` enforces these invariants automatically.** It uses JSDOM to verify every id exists, is an `<h2>`, has non-empty text, and is a descendant of its language wrapper. The script fails (exit 1) on any violation — running before every commit catches the regression it was written for (a stray `</div>` on the "Sauvegarde auto Drive" `<li>` ejected the last 4 FR sections out of `sec-fr` and they rendered as 4 empty cards). If `doc:check` reports "h2 id=X landed outside `<div id="sec-Y">`", the offending tag is *before* X in the file — bisect by reading lines from the previous well-placed h2 forward.

The card UI also injects the help-body CSS (badges, notes, warns, flow diagram, table styling) from `HELP_BODY_STYLES` in `HelpView.tsx`. When you introduce a new CSS class in `help.html`, mirror its rule there or the new content will render unstyled inside the curator shell.

### After every build — mandatory checklist

After every code change that bumps `APP_BUILD`, you **must** update the following before committing:

1. **`src/constants.ts`** — bump `APP_BUILD` to the new number.
2. **`public/version.json`** — set `build` to the new build number and `version` to the current app version. Its `generation` must equal `APP_GENERATION` (doc:check enforces it) — leave it alone unless you are deliberately renumbering the version downward, in which case bump BOTH in the release that PRECEDES the renumber. This file is fetched by `checkVersion()` to detect available updates. **Never forget this — omitting it breaks the update check.**
3. **`package.json`** — when bumping `APP_VERSION`, also bump `"version"` (semver form: e.g. `1.0.0` for APP_VERSION `1.0`). The two MUST stay aligned — `doc:check` will fail otherwise.
4. **`public/changelog.html`** — **MOST BUILDS ADD NOTHING HERE.** Add an entry only if this build shipped a new feature, a new setting, or a behaviour change a user would both NOTICE and ACT on. If you find yourself describing a colour, a border, a photo, a font size, a load time, a bundle, a translation that was missing, or something that used to be broken and now works — **write no entry**. A fix-only bump is expected to leave this file untouched: `doc:check` lets the latest entry LAG behind `APP_BUILD` precisely so nobody has to invent one. When an entry IS warranted, add it at the top of **each** language section (`sec-fr` / `sec-en` / `sec-es` / `sec-de` / `sec-it`) under the current version subtitle, and fetch the current file from GitHub first (`mcp__github__get_file_contents`) to avoid stale edits. **Gate 12 of `doc:check` now enforces this**: an entry sub-titled `Correction` / `Fix` / `Corrección` / `Behoben` / `Correzione` FAILS the check, and display/implementation vocabulary raises a warning to triage — see the changelog-rules section below.
5. **`public/help.html`** — update the relevant sections (one per UI language: fr/en/es/de/it/pt) if the change affects documented behaviour (new UI, renamed fields, changed logic). Fetch from GitHub first.
6. **`npm run doc:check`** — must exit 0 before commit. The script cross-checks `APP_VERSION` / `APP_BUILD` / `version.json` / `package.json`, asserts the latest changelog entry's build number is **≤** `APP_BUILD` (loosened from `=` post-— a fix-only bump should not force a fake changelog entry; the changelog-rules section above forbids logging simple fixes), every `src/utils/` and `src/hooks/` file mentioned in CLAUDE.md, every localStorage key documented in the keys table, and i18n integrity (every `t("…")` call site resolves in the `fr` reference dictionary, and every discovered `src/i18n/<code>.ts` — fr/en/es/de/it/pt today — carries exactly the same key set as `fr`). Two anti-drift gates: (a) **privacy disclosure** — every third-party domain referenced via `https://` literals in `src/` (minus the placeholder / user-tapped-link hosts in `DOMAIN_IGNORE`) must be disclosed in `public/privacy.html`, verbatim or via a `DOMAIN_EVIDENCE` prose mapping ("Anthropic" for `api.anthropic.com`); adding a new fetch target therefore forces a privacy edit in the same commit — this gate would have caught the corsproxy.io / allorigins.win omission it was written for, and DID catch the undisclosed cdnjs.cloudflare.com (JSZip CDN) the day it landed. (b) **structure tree** — every concrete path in the CLAUDE.md "## Repository Structure" fenced tree must exist on disk (glob entries skipped); renames and deletions can no longer leave ghost files in the doc. A non-failing **test-count freshness** check counts the `*.test.*` files + static `it()`/`test()` cases and WARNS (never fails — it's a "~" approximation) when the documented "~N tests across ~M source files" figures (Tech Stack table + Key Conventions #5) drift past tolerance (±10 % files / ±20 % cases), so the hand-maintained figure gets a nudge instead of silently rotting. The file count is the reliable anchor; the static case grep necessarily under-counts vs Vitest (`.each` / property tests expand at runtime).

Documentation-only changes (help, changelog, CLAUDE.md) do **not** require bumping `APP_BUILD` — but the changelog rule about every entry living in EVERY language section (fr/en/es/de/it/pt today — `docParity` derives the list from `LANGUAGES`, so a sixth section is not optional) still applies.

**`doc:check` enforces the bump.** The script now scans every commit between the last `APP_BUILD` bump and `HEAD`. If any user-visible file (`src/views/`, `src/hooks/`, `src/utils/`, `src/components/`, `App.tsx`, `i18n.ts`, `constants.ts`, etc. — full list in `scripts/doc-check.cjs`) changed without a subsequent bump, the script fails with the offender list. This catches the failure mode where multiple user-visible commits ship to `main` without anyone realising the version display in Settings still reads the previous build.

**THE ESCAPE HATCH, AND THE RULE FOR TAKING IT.** It used to read *"`DOC_CHECK_SKIP_BUMP=1`. Use it ONLY when the staged batch is genuinely runtime-neutral"* — a clear rule, in this file, **broken twice in one session**, both times identically: the gate printed the offending files, the failure message offered the hatch on the very next line, and the hatch was taken **without the diff ever being opened**. Two things made that easy and neither was a comprehension problem. **(a) The guard is enforced NOWHERE.** `deploy.yml` and `checks.yml` both set `DOC_CHECK_SKIP_BUMP: "1"` unconditionally — legitimately, for a DIFFERENT reason: on a branch that has not bumped, comparing against the last bump commit is meaningless, and the CI checkout is shallow. So the only enforcement is a human running it locally, which is exactly what failed — the "a gate in a parallel workflow cannot block a deploy" shape, one storey further out. **(b) The hatch cost nothing to reach for.**

**So it is a mechanism now, not a sentence** (`docChecks.resolveBumpSkip`, 8 cases): a bare `1` is accepted **only when `CI` is set**, and a human must **NAME the flagged files** — `DOC_CHECK_SKIP_BUMP='src/utils/x.ts,src/views/y.tsx'` — with the names matching the computed set EXACTLY, so an incomplete list, a stale one, or a plausible-looking guess are all refused. You cannot produce that list without having read the one the gate just printed, which is precisely the step that was skipped. **It is an ACKNOWLEDGEMENT, not a correctness check** — it cannot know whether a diff is really runtime-neutral — the same shape as `// scope-ok:` and `// lang-axis-ok:`. An EMPTY offender set short-circuits silently: complaining about a redundant flag when the gate would not have fired is the over-strict mistake that gets guards routed around.

**THE RULE, in order, and the judgement is still yours:** (1) run `doc:check` with NO flag and read the file list it prints; (2) for EACH named file run `git diff <lastBumpSha>..HEAD -- <file>` and look at the hunks — **from the diff, never from memory of what you changed**; (3) the hatch is permitted only if EVERY hunk is a comment, a type annotation, a test, or a deletion with no remaining caller — anything touching a string, a number, a style value, a default or control flow is user-visible; (4) it is **per BATCH, not per file** — two qualifying files and one that does not means BUMP; (5) **when in doubt, BUMP.** The bump is two lines and needs no changelog entry (most builds add none, and the version gate deliberately lets the latest entry lag), whereas shipping user-visible change under a stale build number means `checkVersion` never fires and the dictionaries — which travel in content-hashed chunks — never reach anyone. **The bump IS the delivery mechanism.** The gate's failure message no longer advertises the hatch as an alternative, and the two workflows keep theirs.

**`doc:check` enforces i18n parity (generalised to N languages).** The dictionaries are split per language: `src/i18n/fr.ts` (`export var FR`), `src/i18n/en.ts` (`export var EN`), `src/i18n/es.ts`, `src/i18n/de.ts`, `src/i18n/it.ts`, one `key:"value"` per line, registered in `LANG` by `src/i18n.ts` (English statically, the rest on demand — see the structure-tree entry). `fr` is the reference/canonical key set. Every key used as `t("…")` in `src/` (outside tests) must exist in the `fr` reference, AND every auto-discovered `src/i18n/<code>.ts` must carry EXACTLY the reference key set. Adding a key to one language and forgetting the others is the most common i18n bug. The check parses every `.ts` / `.tsx` / `.js` / `.jsx` file under `src/`, extracts literal keys passed to `t("…")` via regex, then cross-references against every dictionary (which it parses directly for `key:"value"` pairs — the **no-space-after-colon** shape is required by that regex, so keep it). Missing keys fail CI (exit 1); keys defined in i18n but never called are reported as warnings only (they may be referenced indirectly via `xl()` or future-proofed). **Dynamically-built keys**: keys resolved via `t(prefix + var)`, a map lookup, or `L.<key>` property access (class components like `EB.tsx`) are invisible to the literal-`t("…")` scan, so they'd surface as false "never called" noise. `scripts/doc-check.allowlist.json` carries `dynamicKeyPrefixes` / `dynamicKeys` to suppress them, keeping the unused-warning at ~0 so a genuinely-new dead key stands out. **CONVENTION — when you introduce a new dynamic-key family** (a new `t(prefix + …)` group, a new enum→`maint_kind_*`-style map, a new `L.<key>` set), **add its prefix to `dynamicKeyPrefixes` in the same commit** — otherwise every member reappears in the unused warning and erodes the signal.

**`doc:check` also enforces dev-fallback parity (gate (b.2)).** The ubiquitous `t ? t("key") : "French fallback"` idiom carries a literal that NEVER renders in production (`t` is always present) — but a drifted fallback is misleading and would show wrong text in any `t`-less render path or test. The gate scans `src/` (outside tests + the dicts) for `t("key") : "literal"` and **fails** if the literal isn't byte-identical to `fr[key]` (raw/escaped form, matching how `parseBlock` stores the reference). A one-time sweep reconciled 129 pre-existing divergences (stale "Drive"→"cloud" rename, `…` vs `...`, casing, shortened labels); the gate keeps the class dead. **When you add a `t ? t("k") : "…"` site, the fallback must equal the `fr` value verbatim** (emoji, punctuation and all) or doc:check goes red.

**What is deliberately NOT translated, stated so it stops looking like an oversight.** A full pseudo-localisation sweep of all 33 screens (the mode had to be repaired first) found **zero untranslated UI strings**: 3894 text nodes, and every unmarked one is a number, a glyph (`·` `●` `★` `×` `💾`), seeded user data, a unit, a tobacco-varietal proper noun (`Burley` / `Virginia/Burley` are identical in German — `CATS_DE` is a SPARSE override map by design, listing only what differs), or a month abbreviation that coincides across languages (`Jun`/`Jul` in German). Verified by re-running the same sweep in German, where `Anglais`→`Englisch`, `Aromatique`→`Aromatisch` and `May`→`Mai` all disappear from the unmarked set. **Three things stay single-language on purpose:** (1) **the CSV export** — headers (`Marque`, `Categorie`…), the `Cave`/`Pot`/`Fini` status cells and the `=== PIPES ===` section markers are FRENCH by construction, because `parseTobaccoCsv` matches headers by FR+EN alias only (`csvImport.ts`), so localising them would break re-import of a file exported under another UI language. The two columns that DO localise (`Arômes` values via `t(aromaLabelKey)`, `Age` via `t("age_y")`) are free-text cells the parser never matches on, so they are safe — but the inconsistency is real and worth knowing before "finishing" the job. (2) **`public/manifest.json`'s `description` + `lang: "fr"`** — the Web App Manifest has no per-language values; doing this properly means one manifest per language plus `hreflang` link tags, which is more machinery than the install sheet is worth. (3) **the `<noscript>` block in `index.html`** — FR/EN only, and reachable only with JavaScript disabled, in which case the app does not run at all. **Guard fixed in the same build**: `tabac-local/no-platform-breadcrumb-out-of-i18n` matched French and English breadcrumbs only, so `Ajustes → IA` / `Einstellungen → KI` / `Impostazioni → IA` all passed — the same "comprehensive-looking guard covering a subset" shape as the `.jsx` config gap, the `scripts/` gap (36) and the six hardcoded language lists (64). Now all five, locked per language.

**The error messages users actually see.** The cloud hooks surface a caught error verbatim (`setGdriveStatus(t("err_prefix") + ": " + e.message)`), so ANY `throw new Error("<prose>")` upstream renders that prose in every language — and no lint rule sees it, because it is a function argument, not JSX text. The French ones were fixed (`"Fichier corrompu"` → a German read "Fehler: Fichier corrompu"; `"Google non dispo"`); the same defect was later found pointing the other way — **`"No token"` (×3) and `"invalid JSON"`, English technical prose shown to a French user as "Erreur : No token"**. Both directions are one defect: a literal in a language the reader may not have. `src/__tests__/errorMessagesTranslated.test.ts` locks the class over the three cloud hooks, and is deliberately explicit about what stays: a bare **HTTP status** (`"HTTP " + r.status`) is a code, not prose — it reads the same everywhere and is the one thing that helps diagnose a failing request — plus TWO documented exemptions whose reasons are asserted, not merely claimed. `"no refresh token"` is control flow (the test asserts `getToken` still catches it, since the exemption rests entirely on that); `"Web Crypto unavailable"` is a programmer-facing invariant in a module-level pure function with no `t()` in scope, unreachable in any browser running React 19 over the HTTPS this app forces, and the alternative to throwing is a predictable CSRF state. **The popups themselves are clean** — every `alert`/`confirm` argument and every modal string already routes through `t()`; the sweep of `Overlays.tsx` and the five modal components found only `×` glyphs.

**"adding a language is one click" was not true, and now fails loudly instead of quietly.** An audit that ACTUALLY added Portuguese (rather than reasoning about it) found that the on-demand work had made the DICTIONARY additive — drop `src/i18n/<code>.ts`, the glob finds it — while **six other sites still hardcoded the five codes and every one fell back SILENTLY**: `NUM_LOCALE` in primitives (French number formatting), `nominatimReverseUrl` (French place names), `monthsShort` + `heatmapDayInitials` (English months and weekdays), `DESC_LANGS` + a five-branch import chain in `tobaccoDb.ts` (no catalogue prose at all, via a bare `else return;`), and `LANG_PROMPT_NAME` (the AI writing in English). A Portuguese reader would have got all of that with **typecheck, lint, doc:check and 3569 of 3571 tests green** — a half-translated app reads as unfinished rather than broken, which is why nobody noticed. Enum labels were a seventh: 130 values rendered in stored French across cards, fiches, filter chips and chart `aria-label`s. **The fix is one table plus two gates.** `LANG_ASSETS` in `src/i18n/languages.ts` holds one row per language (`numberLocale` / `nominatim` / `monthsShort` / `dayInitials` / `aiPromptName`) and `langAssets(code)` falls back to ENGLISH, not French; the catalogue-prose chunks are now discovered by `import.meta.glob` exactly like the dictionaries. **`doc:check` gate 13** fails when a discovered dictionary has no complete `LANG_ASSETS` row; **gate 14** fails when `ENUM_TRANSLATIONS` has no entry for it. Both are pure functions in `scripts/docChecks.cjs`, tested in `docChecks.test.ts`, and both were probed by re-running the Portuguese experiment: with only steps 1-2 done, doc:check now FAILS naming the missing row; with the row added, **typecheck / lint / doc:check / all 3583 tests pass**. **If you add a seventh site that varies by language, put its data in `LANG_ASSETS` — do not start another map.**
