**The gate that finds the axis instead of naming it (gate 15).** Gates 13 and 14 each guard ONE map, so adding Portuguese for real still meant discovering its own gaps by hand and found four: `geo.ts`'s 79-row country table, `HelpView.SECTION_IDS`, `doc-check.cjs`'s own `HELP_SECTION_IDS`, and a test file that restated the five codes. `findLanguageAxisGaps` (in `docChecks.cjs`, 11 cases in `docChecks.test.ts`) guards the **shape**: any FLAT object literal in production source whose keys already include **two or more** registry codes is a per-language axis and must include them all. **Two is the threshold on purpose** — a `{ fr, en }` pair left behind by an older build is the dangerous case, while a one-code literal is normally a default or a static import (`LANG = { en: EN }` in `i18n.ts`, which must NOT be flagged and is why the threshold is not one). Nested literals are out of scope, so `LANG_ASSETS` still needs gate 13. **Deliberate subsets get an ACKNOWLEDGEMENT, not an exception list**: `// lang-axis-ok: <reason>` on the literal's line, above it, or above the enclosing DECLARATION — that last scope is what lets one line cover a table of rows (the ten `ENUM_TRANSLATIONS` rows are ten literals in one statement, and `fr` is deliberately absent from every one of them). Same philosophy as `no-unscoped-lot-read`: force a conscious re-read rather than judge correctness, because a clever guard either misses the interesting cases or gets correct code rewritten to please it. **The gate paid for itself on its first run**, finding a site that addition had MISSED — `main.jsx`'s pre-mount boot strings (loading text + repair link) were still five languages, so a Portuguese reader on a slow or failed boot read English — plus `scripts/i18n-layout.cjs`'s hardcoded `"fr,en,es,de,it"` default, which meant **the cross-language layout checker never rendered Portuguese at all in a default run**. That one is the worst place for a silent subset: a green report from a checker is what stops anyone looking further. The layout script's language axis is now derived from the registry (`registryLangs()`), locked by `i18nLayoutHarness.test.ts`, and narrowable with `-- --langs pt`. One walk-detail worth keeping: the declaration search **stops at a sibling declaration that closes on its own line** (`const OTHER = 1;`) — accepting it would let one acknowledgement leak to every literal further down the file, which is the failure the walk exists to prevent rather than cause (locked by a test that fails on the first implementation).

**Mutating the data-integrity core: the trash was the hole. A TEST-ONLY build — no production code changed, and its own commit message does not read that way.** That is worth stating first, because the message announces "the trash gave grams back for free" and lists "two silent-corruption paths", which reads as live data loss found and fixed; the diff is five test files plus this paragraph. Everything below describes what happens when a mutation is INJECTED into code that is correct — which is exactly the finding, since nothing failed. 70 mutations across the stores, the merge engine and `save()`, chosen by CONSEQUENCE rather than coverage — a gram lost, a lot duplicated, a session debited twice. 43 killed before, 65 after; 30 tests written, each proved by re-injecting the exact mutation that had survived. **The worst was `useTrashOps`: not one test touched a session's WEIGHT.** All three call sites of `reDeductRestoredSessions` could be deleted with the suite green — delete a session, restore it from the trash, and the lot keeps the grams it smoked, free grams on every round trip (the bug). Worse, dropping the `deletedAt` filter makes "Restore all" re-debit EVERY live session at once. The pure helper had a full suite; nothing checked it was still CALLED — the wiring shape again, and the second time in two releases that a well-tested helper sat behind untested wiring. Same for `assertLotInvariants(nd)` in `save()`: removing the line left 3711 tests green while every lot/session/balance invariant stopped running and the diagnostic went quiet, in the reassuring direction. Then two survivors whose CONSEQUENCE is silent corruption, on code that was already right: dropping the per-clone `newUid()` (`useTobaccoStore`) makes bulk lot clones share one `uid`, so restoring on a second device reads three identical tins as one and two vanish with the balance still consistent (the loss through the other door); dropping `updateSession`'s `roundWeightToUnit` makes it store 2.55 g and debit 2.6, drifting until Σ crosses tolerance and the diagnostic reports an inexplicable `lot-balance-overflow`. **Both had already been fixed — the finding is that undoing either fix broke nothing**, so the repairs were one careless edit from being lost. Read the two as mutations, not as bugs discovered here. **THE PATTERN IS WORTH MORE THAN THE COUNT: when a rule exists on two paths, it is almost always the SECOND that is untested** (`_persistSession` vs `updateSession`, add vs edit maintenance, the inter-lot debit vs the three other diversion sites). **The merge engine holds — 12 of 14, the best result of the pass**: uid-first identity, the ambiguity guard, the distinct-uid guard, lot dedup, `lotId` re-attribution and the balance guard each bit. The most-repaired code in the repo is also the best guarded, which is the healthy order. **5 survivors left deliberately**, each argued rather than waved away (an equivalent mutant verified byte-for-byte on the saved payload, an LWW `>` vs `>=` that only differs at an equal millisecond and loses no data, two unreachable defensive guards). **UNMEASURED and disclosed**: 15 of the 21 hooks — including `useTastingSession`, whose zombie-tasting bug is in the very list that motivated this pass — `useGdriveSync` (2 mutations over 2354 lines), the replace path of `useImportConfirm`, and all ~29 views.

**The declared-unmeasured hooks, batch one: FOUR of the five `uid` mint sites were asserted by nothing.** `newUid()` is the cross-device merge identity — `resolveMergeMatch` consults it FIRST, and the `brand|name` fallback REFUSES to act when two rows share that pair, so the imported row is ADDED, which is the documented silent doubling. The contract stated here is « minted ONCE at creation and carried in backups ». **MEASURED, over 387 cases: removing the mint from `addPipe`, `addWish`, `addAccessory` or `addSession` leaves the suite entirely GREEN**; only `addTobacco` reddens, by one case in its own suite. **WHAT ABSORBS IT, AND HOW FAR — the question this repo insists on before believing a survivor is a defect.** `migrateData._backfillUid` re-mints on the FOUR top-level collections at the next load, so for a pipe, a wish or an accessory the loss lasts one session rather than for ever. That is not nothing: the cloud auto-save fires 1.2 s after the creating save, so a backup taken in that window carries a uid-LESS row, and the two devices then mint DIFFERENT uids for the same object — exactly the doubling mechanism. It is also why the load path persists the backfill immediately (*« an export taken before the first save carried ephemeral uids »*), a fix written for this same class through the other door. **SESSIONS are the hard case and the exclusion is deliberate**: `_backfillUid` skips them, because a legacy session backfilled to two different uids on two devices would be SPLIT by the distinct-uid guard — so for a session the mint at creation is the ONLY source of a uid that exists, and losing it never heals. `entityUidMinted.test.ts` covers all five, plus a case proving two successive creations do not share one uid (a constant satisfies « a non-empty string » while making the identity useless). **Its last case INVERTS THE BURDEN rather than restating the list**: it derives the entities from `migrateData`'s own `_backfillUid(d.…)` calls — the one place that already enumerates them — and fails when one has no mint case here, so a sixth top-level entity cannot ship unguarded. Probed six ways on the code and once on the derivation (a fictional `d.blenders` reddens the coverage case by name). **What this batch measured and found SOUND, so nobody re-chases it**: `deletePipe`'s snapshot refresh, `updatePipe`'s maintenance preservation, `addMaintenance`'s forced id (the documented id:0 collision), the AND-guard in `addAccessory` (7 cases), and the soft-delete in both `deleteAccessory` and `delWish` — each reddens under mutation. **Batch three — `useGdriveSync` et `useAiAutoFill`, deux trous, tous deux du CÂBLAGE.** Onze mutations. **Deux résultats ont dû être JETÉS avant d'être crus, et c'est la partie méthodologique :** une sonde signalée « appliquée » ne l'était pas (l'ancre `cloudGuardLocalRef(isDbx)` existe TROIS fois et mon remplacement n'en touchait qu'une), et une autre était une mutation ÉQUIVALENTE (remplacer `useRef(false)` par un objet littéral se comporte à l'identique sur un seul rendu). *« Appliquée » n'est pas « pertinente » : vérifier ce que la mutation change, pas seulement qu'elle change quelque chose.* Refaites correctement, la seconde tue. **(a) `cloudGuardLocalRef` : la fonction a son propre bloc de quatre assertions et ses TROIS sites d'appel n'étaient gardés par rien** — neutraliser les trois laissait 280 cas verts, alors que son commentaire promet « single source so the three guard sites can't drift out of agreement ». Verbatim la forme `chooseAutoSaveTarget`. Ce qui manquait est un SENS : tous les cas voisins exercent « la bannière doit sortir » et aucun n'exerçait la SUPPRESSION, seule chose que la référence produit — sans elle tout fichier paraît plus récent et la bannière crie en permanence, le défaut que trois passages ont déjà corrigé. **(b) `redactApiKeys` a deux blocs de tests comme FONCTION et deux sites d'APPEL ; celui du SCAN PHOTO n'était couvert par rien** (le motif « deux chemins, c'est le second qui n'est pas testé »). **Je m'étais trompé de sens en le rapportant et la vérification l'a montré** — j'avais nommé l'auto-remplissage, qui est couvert. La conséquence est une CRÉDENTIELLE À L'ÉCRAN : le message du fournisseur est affiché verbatim, et celui qui photographie une boîte est exactement celui qui joindra une capture à un ticket. **Mesuré et trouvé SAIN** : `chooseAutoSaveTarget`, le seuil `AUTOSAVE_FAIL_ALERT`, le verrou de sauvegarde silencieuse, `resolveAiModel` consultant les modèles morts, `openaiMaxTokensField`, `isModelGoneError`.

**Batch quatre — les VUES, huit mutations, trois survivantes.** Le dossier `curator` compte 1053 cas ; une passe coûte 44 s. **Une première mesure a failli me faire annoncer deux vues « sans aucun test » : la métrique lisait un NOM DE FICHIER, pas une couverture** — `EncryptionPromptModal` et `StartupNoticeModal` sont couverts par `untestedModules.test.tsx`, écrit pour eux. Vérifié avant de l'écrire. Les trois vraies survivantes : **(a) `pipesFiltered`**, le prédicat qui décide entre les DEUX états vides — les EXCLUSIONS y sont assertées (`showFinishedPipes` élargit) et les INCLUSIONS non, donc retirer `pTagFilter` laissait 1053 verts et l'utilisateur filtrant par collection jusqu'à zéro lisait la phrase du PREMIER LANCEMENT avec un bouton créant une pipe hors filtre ; **(b) le retour de `DocPageView`**, dont le repli `nav("home")` existe pour les portes sans Réglages derrière elles — le remplacer entièrement ne cassait rien et ramenait à l'Accueil au lieu de l'écran d'origine, un contrôle infidèle plutôt que cassé ; **(c) le repli des sections d'aide**, sur ~74 Ko de prose dense, où forcer l'ouverture rend le réglage persisté sans effet. Chacune épinglée dans les DEUX sens (un prédicat toujours-vrai, un retour qui n'appelle jamais `nav`, un repli universel) — sans quoi la correction paresseuse passerait. **Mesuré et trouvé SAIN** : l'origine Stats du drill des notes, le `scope` que le Home passe à la fiche, le lien Confidentialité, le plafond de la section entretien avec son bouton, la persistance des cases de la liste de courses.

**CE QUI RESTE NON MESURÉ, après quatre lots** : le chemin *replace* d'`useImportConfirm`, les petits hooks restants, et l'essentiel des ~29 vues — le lot quatre en a sondé huit règles sur cinq vues, ce qui est un échantillon et non une couverture. Les quatre lots ont pris `useTastingSession`, `useExportImport`, `useGdriveSync` et `useAiAutoFill`.

**Batch two — `useTastingSession` holds completely, `useExportImport` had FOUR unguarded rules, and the split between them is the useful part.** Twelve mutations chosen by consequence. **`useTastingSession` killed all seven**: the auto-end capping the recorded duration at the threshold in force (rather than the wall-clock span, the ten-hour session), `tastingOvertimeMs` taking the LONGER of elapsed and pause, a soft-deleted lot counting as missing, the auto-end NOTICE, the `loading` gate on the auto-end effect, and both future-timestamp guards in `readTasting`. The most-repaired hook in the app is also the best guarded — the healthy order, the same finding the merge engine gave. **`useExportImport` is where the gaps were, and all four are WIRING rather than logic.** (a) and (b) the two re-entry latches, `busyRef.current.json` and `.zip`: neutering either left 180 cases green, and on iOS a second tap means a second SHARE SHEET, which is a broken state rather than a redundant one — the ZIP path additionally injects a JSZip `<script>` per tap. (c) `exportFailMsg`'s code→sentence mapping: `photo-store-unreadable` is deliberately a CODE and not prose (the `errorMessagesTranslated` gate admits a spaceless kebab code precisely so no English leaks on screen), and nothing checked anyone TRANSLATED it — break the comparison and the user reads the raw code. (d) the collection report's `lang:` argument: the module validates it and writes `<html lang>`, its own cases exercise the OPTION, and nothing asserted a caller passes one — remove it and the document ships with no declared language, the accessibility defect that field was added to fix. **The pattern across all four is the one this repo keeps paying for: a rule tested where it is DEFINED and unguarded where it is CALLED.** **A METHOD NOTE, because I nearly shipped a vacuous case:** my first version of (c) asserted inside `act(...).then(...)`, the assertion FAILED, and the file reported **54 passed with « 1 unhandled error »** — a rejection thrown in an `act` continuation is not attributed to the test. Assert OUTSIDE the act and wait with `waitFor`, as the A0 cases beside it already did. Each of the four new cases probed, one red case each.

**Auditing the tests an audit named: eight suspected vacuous, SIX real, and the two it got wrong are worth as much.** Each was PROBED before being touched — mutate the code the case claims to guard, run it, and see. **The worst was `smokeSoonDrill.test.ts`, whose whole subject is a control that named a set and selected a subset**: it TRANSCRIBED App.tsx's filter into its own helper and compared that against the scope, under a comment arguing "a copy is the wrong shape in production, but here it IS the subject". It is not: a hand-written copy agreeing with the scope proves only that the author can write the scope twice. Reverting App.tsx to the exact reported defect — `overaged` alone, the thing the file is named after — left all nine cases GREEN. Fixed at the SOURCE rather than in the test: App.tsx now delegates to `lotInScope`, so there is one implementation, and the case asserts that DELEGATION (sliced from the branch to the next one, since blanking a comment preserves its length and any fixed character window is either too short to reach the code or long enough to spill into the next filter). **Four more of the same family.** `maintTimeSurvivesBackup` built `Object.assign({}, imported, { id })` by hand and asserted the result still had a `time` — a property of the JavaScript language; it moved to `useImportConfirm.test.ts` beside the merge harness that can drive the real path. `gdriveDeleteBackupById`'s fid-clearing carried a comment calling itself "functional, not cosmetic" and was held by nothing (probed: `if (false)` left 118 cases green) — now pinned in BOTH directions, since always clearing it would make the next quiet save POST a second auto file, the pile three releases were spent draining. `onDeleteEntry` had ZERO references anywhere, so the two-tap confirm on a cloud file with no undo was asserted by nothing. And `MaintFormModal` had no test file AT ALL — which is the state it was in when the release before this one changed one of its labels; its new suite pins the prefill-race trap by EXERCISING it (clear the time, save, assert it stayed cleared) rather than describing it, and probing the `[open, data, form.time]` dep reddens exactly that case. **The two the audit got WRONG:** `resetPageGuard`'s `lang` assertion does guard (removing the validation reddens it) — though it was restated as MEMBERSHIP, since "not co" reads as a rule about one string and "co" is itself a real BCP-47 tag; and `nowTime` exists, my own first grep having been too narrow (`export var`, not `export function`). **The `res.ok` half WAS real and the fix is the lesson: two guards, one asserted by nothing.** The server-error fixture carried an EMPTY body, so the body check refused it anyway and deleting the status check changed nothing; the new case is a 5xx that still returns the app's HTML, which only `!res.ok` can refuse. **One probe stayed green and the ENVIRONMENT was the absorbing layer, not the test**: swapping `getHours` for `getUTCHours` is invisible at offset 0, which is what CI runs at — so `nowTime` and `today` are pinned at SOURCE for that half, and the runtime case is kept with its limit written on it. **`helpSectionIdsAgree.test.ts` closes the third edge of a triangle** — `HelpView.SECTION_IDS`, doc:check's `HELP_SECTION_IDS` and the `<h2 id>` tags are documented as "three places that must stay aligned", doc:check held gate↔html, and nothing held view↔anything: renaming one id in the view left 169 tests and doc:check green while that section would render as an empty card. A sentence asking a human to keep two lists in step is not a mechanism.

**Mutating the test suite: 297 mutations, 285 killed, and the 3 that mattered.** The suspicion behind the audit ("3711 tests over 86 releases, there must be duplication") did NOT hold: zero dead tests, zero reversed rule still locked backwards, one partial overlap. **The accumulation is coverage, not redundancy** — and several tests look redundant precisely because they lock a past regression, which is why the deletion bar here is "prove the subject no longer exists". Only one line qualified: a `dlImg` mock in `useGdriveSync.test.ts` for a fetcher since removed. **The three real survivors**: stubbing `AromaPicker` to render `null` left 3698 of 3698 green — the multi-select wheel behind both session entry points, the inventory aroma filter and `Session.aromas` had NO test file at all, which also explains why `groupLabelKey` (its only exclusive consumer) survived while its twin `aromaLabelKey` is killed by the view tests. And `getStorageBlockedHint` returning `""` was invisible, in a helper whose own comment says it exists so "the iOS↔Android parity contract is enforced at the helper level" (invariant #21) — **a contract with no test is a comment**. Both are now covered, each probed by re-injecting the exact surviving mutation. **The methodological lesson is worth more than the findings**: the audit's own harness produced false KILLED results after a timed-out batch left `countActive` mutated in the tree, so later mutations "passed" against 3 already-red files. It was caught by a stray `git diff --stat`, and replaying the contaminated batches on a clean tree revealed 4 further survivors. Any automated measurement over this repo must assert a clean `git status` FIRST — the same shape as `prune` red for nine releases under a "clean" claim. **Reported, not fixed**: four constants can change value with nothing reddening (`MAX_ROWS`, `MAX_TAGS_PER_ITEM`, `DIAGNOSTIC_MAX_RECENT`, `GDRIVE_PENDING_STALE_MS`) because their tests import the constant and compute from it — self-referential by construction; eight sibling constants ARE pinned, through `label-contracts.json` against the help prose, which is the mechanism to extend. Five exact-boundary mutations (`>` vs `>=` in the trash sweep and `lotAgingStatus`) also survive: missing precision, not missing coverage. UNMEASURED and disclosed: the 21 hooks and every view but `AromaPicker`.

**The last seven gates extracted, and the wiring test caught me doing it wrong.** An audit probed every gate and found the remaining third had its DECISION inline in `doc-check.cjs` — gates 2/3 (a module named in CLAUDE.md), 4 (a documented storage key), 9 (a called `t()` key), 11 (a defined-but-uncalled key) and 26 (test-count freshness). All bit; nothing protected their LOGIC, since the wiring test only stops a call site being DELETED and cannot notice a regex narrowed or a tolerance widened. They are now pure functions in `docChecks.cjs` with 20 cases, each probed end-to-end against the real repo (mangle the doc, expect the gate red). **Extracting them reproduced the exact defect that audit had just found**: `findMissingTKeys` was exported and never called, because `doc-check.cjs` still ran its inline compare — the `findParityGaps` shape, in the release right after, by the person who had just written it up. The wiring test failed on the same commit, which is the strongest evidence it earns its place. A second self-correction worth keeping: my first case asserted the gate-4 regex ESCAPING protects against a metacharacter in a key; it cannot be reached, because the `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+` filter drops such a key first — the test now asserts what actually protects and says why the escape stays. **Also closed**: `npm test` and `doc:check` now run on `pull_request` (in `checks.yml`, PR-only — `deploy.yml` must keep running them on push, where they gate the Pages deploy itself, and a parallel job cannot). The argument that a gate should fire before the merge was applied to three gates out of five, and the asymmetry was written nowhere.

**Auditing the auditors: deleting a whole gate's call site left 3672 tests green.** Twenty-nine control units were probed in BOTH directions — inject the exact defect each claims to catch and confirm it reddens with a useful message, then stub the pure function and confirm a test dies. All 32 exported decisions in `docChecks.cjs` / `i18nChecks.cjs` / `labelContracts.cjs` are guarded, none is vacuous, and every gate examines real data. **What nothing guarded was the WIRING**: no test executes `doc-check.cjs` itself, so removing `docChecks.checkEnumCoverage(...).forEach(err)` outright left the whole suite green while gate 16 simply stopped running — the third instance of this repo's oldest failure shape (`prune` red for nine releases under a "clean" claim; gate 14 checking that a row NAMES a language without looking at the map behind it). `docCheckWiring.test.ts` now requires every exported decision to be reachable from the call graph rooted at `doc-check.cjs`, with comments stripped first — a call deleted but still NAMED in the prose above it is exactly the case to catch, and the test asserts that property of itself. **That comment-stripping had the same hole one syntax over, and my own change is what exposed it: a name surviving in a STRING also counted as wired.** The bump gate's failure message ends `"See docChecks.resolveBumpSkip."` — good practice, since a gate that names its own decision function is followable — so deleting the call left the name in the file and the search kept finding it; the probe stayed GREEN with the mutation verified as applied (5 call sites → 4), which is the only reason it was caught. **TWO NARROWER FIXES WERE TRIED AND REJECTED, both measured on the real repo rather than reasoned about.** (1) Blanking string literals as well as comments: a hand-rolled scanner mistakes an apostrophe inside a regex literal for a string opener and swallowed whole regions, **losing 20 genuine references**. (2) Requiring a call shape (`name(`) for everything: **six exports are CONSTANTS** (`RATIO_THRESHOLD`, `FIX_HEADINGS`, `NON_FUNCTIONAL_TERMS`…) which are never followed by `(`, and `parseDictSource` is a function legitimately BOUND as a value (`const parseBlock = i18nChecks.parseDictSource`). Both would have reported a false "unreachable" — the over-strict failure this file keeps recording, where a guard gets correct code rewritten to please it. What holds: **a FUNCTION export must be called or bound; a DATA export keeps the plain word search.** No parsing, and it asks what the file is about — not "is the name mentioned" but "is the decision used". Probed in three directions (unwire the new gate, unwire an old one, break the alias binding), each reddening and naming the right export. Same pass found `findParityGaps` **tested but never called**, while the parity gate kept its own inline copy: the tested function guarded nothing and the running one had no test, two halves of one mistake that `knip` cannot see (a test file counts as a consumer). **Still unguarded and reported, not fixed**: seven gates whose decision is written inline in `doc-check.cjs` (utils/hooks/keys/`t()`/unused/test-count, plus the `tobacco-db` validator) — the wiring test protects them from DELETION, nothing protects their LOGIC; extracting them is the same argument applied to the remaining third. Also disclosed: `npm test` and `doc:check` run only on push to `main`, not on `pull_request`, while `checks.yml` argues in its own comment that a gate should fire BEFORE the merge — defensible under the always-push-to-main convention, but the asymmetry was written nowhere.

**The failure modes, rendered rather than reasoned about.** Fifteen states in Chromium: a corrupt `cave-lang` (`"constructor"`, `"__proto__"`, a JSON blob, `""`), a blocked chunk at startup and on switch, an offline switch to a never-downloaded language, and the terms gate in each. The guards hold — no raw keys on screen, no blank screen, no two-language mix, no dead button, and the offline copy ("reconnect, then reload") is literally accurate, since a second tap provably issues no request (the browser caches a failed dynamic import as a failure). Three real defects: **(1)** an unknown code produced the amber "this language must be downloaded once" notice **permanently, on every launch, on the terms gate and in Settings** — there is nothing to download and reloading changes nothing. The on-demand change merged "unknown language" and "chunk unavailable" into one boolean, right for choosing which language to SHOW and wrong for choosing what to SAY; `isKnownLang()` now separates them, and the path that matters is a language RETIRED from the registry, which would give every user on it a false permanent banner. **(2)** `<html lang>` took the raw stored value (`lang="constructor"`), and on a failed chunk announced English prose as German — an invalid tag is worse than none for a screen reader; `main.jsx` validates against the registry and falls back to `en`, still a single pre-mount write so the iOS constraint holds. **(3)** `Segmented` conveyed its selection by BACKGROUND COLOUR alone — six identical buttons to a screen reader, in the control that carries every preference in Settings (language, text size, theme, units, currency); `aria-pressed` now, the same fix made to `FilterChipSimple`.

**Reading the help prose found what no gate could, and one gate found what no reading could (gate 21).** The dictionaries had been read natively; the ~74 KB of help prose per language never had. Four defects, and the shape of each is the lesson. **(1) All 30 internal links of the Portuguese help block, table of contents included, pointed at `#en-*`.** The translation prompt said to change the `<h2>` id prefixes and said nothing about `href`s, so the anchors were copied faithfully. Nothing could see it — the prose reads perfectly, every id named exists somewhere in the file, the anchor gate checks that the h2 ids are present and correctly wrapped, and a proof-reader follows words, not link targets. `HelpView` renders ONE block at a time, so every one of those links went nowhere. **Gate 21 (`checkAnchorLanguage`) closes it**, reporting each foreign language once rather than each link. **(2) `privacy.html` over-declared a REMOVED feature in all six languages** — the "update place names" batch button, since deleted, still described as a Nominatim call the user can trigger from Settings, in the page a Google OAuth reviewer reads. Its prose contract fingerprints `geo.ts`, but the button lived in Settings, so the fingerprint never moved and the gate never asked for the re-read: **a contract can watch the right service and the wrong call site.** **(3) The URL-image field** was still documented in three help sections × six languages while section 13 of the same page said the feature was removed — the page contradicted itself, and `PhotoField` exposes only `onPickFile`/`onClear`. **(4) The language list said five languages**, so a Portuguese reader was told *in Portuguese* that the app offers five, not including theirs. Then the per-language findings: German had three `sie`/`es` gender errors on `das Los`, and Portuguese had drifted to Brazilian register in the help (`Apagar`/`Anular`/`endereço` where its own dictionary says `Eliminar`/`Desfazer`/`morada`) — pt concentrates the defects because it is the newest and the only help block never re-read, which makes the diagnosis clean rather than subjective. **Left as decisions, not corrections**: the "finished" status word diverges in es/de/it and **the app itself is split** (es badge `Acabado` vs chip `Lote terminado`; de `Aufgeraucht` vs `Fertiges Los`), so the fix belongs in the dictionary, not the help; and sections 4 and 11 contradict each other on the auto-fill default in all six languages — the code settles it (`cave-autofill-source` has defaulted to `"ai"`, so section 4 is the wrong one), but rewriting it is an editorial choice in six languages. **RESOLVED — and the follow-up is worth more than the finding.** Section 4 was rewritten in the very next release, so by the time anyone came back to this note the contradiction it names was gone; the note kept sending readers at an already-fixed line, and it said "section 4 is the wrong one" when section 4 had become the RIGHT one — **a stale to-do is not merely useless, it points the next fix backwards.** Re-reading section 11 to confirm then found the LIVE defect one paragraph away: the "local catalogue" block described the app under **`Base locale`**, which stopped being the default. Three of its claims were false under the shipped default — "the answer arrives instantly, offline, no network request" (the provider is queried first), "a green panel appears as soon as you type a recognised brand + name" (`dbHinted` in `TobaccoFormView`/`WishFormView` opens with `if (autofillSource === "ai") return false`, so the offer is SUPPRESSED by default), and "the Search button does exactly the same thing" (it does not, which is why the `· source: …` line beneath it exists at all). What was true and stayed: with no API key the catalogue answers directly (`useAiAutoFill`'s AI-first branch falls to `tobaccoDbLookup` when `!apiKey`). Rewritten in all six languages so every claim is conditioned on the setting. **The lesson for this file: when a note records a decision to defer, whoever later resolves it must come BACK here** — and re-read the surrounding prose rather than only the line the note names, since a stale note is evidence that this area has not been looked at in a while.

**The first NATIVE read of es/de/it, and four gates for a seventh language (17-20).** Portuguese got a native review when it shipped; Spanish, German and Italian never had one — machine-translated and unread since, while every gate checked that a key EXISTS, differs from French and is a plausible length, and none that it means the right thing. Reading all 1070 keys of each against `fr` found **21 defects and no more**, which is itself the useful result: the failures are narrow and dull, not broken sentences. The instructive ones: **`age_mo`** was ` mes` / ` mesi` / ` meses` — `fmtLotAge` CONCATENATES it onto a count (`Math.floor(d/30) + t("age_mo")`), so it rendered "5 mes" and "1 mesi", wrong in three languages in two opposite directions. **The plural sweep structurally could not see it**: that sweep followed `{n}` placeholders, and this key has none — the number is glued on by the caller. `de`/`en` were already abbreviated (` Mon.` / ` mo`), which is the shape the other four now use. Then a French gender carried onto an English loanword (es «marcan **la** briar» → *el brezo*), a word from the wrong domain (es `Hornillo` = a camping stove → *Cazoleta*; it `scatola` = a box → *latta* for a tin), a plural slot holding a singular (it "3 ritirato"), German's only two `Sie`-imperatives in a `du` file, and **`Fiche` — an untranslated French noun — 21 times in German prose**. **What was NOT changed is the other half of the result**: `es ficha/entrada/tarjeta` and `it scheda/voce` look like drift and are considered distinctions the help makes identically; `de Karte` for a record reads ambiguously against Karte = map but the help uses the same phrasing, so changing it would have BROKEN agreement. The threshold held was "a native reads it as an error", not "I would phrase it differently" — the over-strict-guard lesson. **Gates 17-20** close the seventh-language residue, and each was probed in both directions with a test that dies if the gate is stubbed: **17** label-contract coverage (the contracts name dictionaries by PATH, a language axis gate 15 structurally cannot see, since it reads literals of language CODES); **18** doc-page blocks, GRADED — `privacy.html` fails (one page, legally meaningful), `changelog.html` warns (~80 historical entries, so a hard gate could only be satisfied by pasting English, which is what the fallback already does); **19** a dictionary that is a copy of `en.ts` — the identical-value gate compares each language to FRENCH, so an English copy passes in silence; whole-file at ≥50%, since individual English values are legitimate (highest real overlap today is fr at 7.3%); **20** catalogue prose, warn-only (generating a chunk is a paid AI run that legitimately lags).

**Gate 14 checked the ROW, not the MAP (gate 16).** `ENUM_TRANSLATIONS` rows name a language; the maps behind them are deliberately SPARSE, since a value identical in French needs no override. Gate 14 verified the row names every dictionary — and stopped there. Probed by emptying them: **ten `= {}` maps leave `doc:check` fully green** while every category, cut, shape, material, finish, accessory type and fuel renders in stored French, which is exactly the defect the whole enum machinery exists to prevent. `checkEnumCoverage` closes it, and **the EN map is the oracle**: a value English had to TRANSLATE is language-bearing and must exist in every other map; one English left alone (`Flake`, `Billiard`, `Latakia`, `Cumberland`, `Morta` — ~110 of them) is jargon and correctly absent everywhere. That test is what makes the gate possible without a human judging 130 values per language: it asks the one map that has already made every one of those judgements. `fr` is skipped (canonical) and so is `en` (it IS the oracle). Probed both ways — green on the real repo, red naming the four missing values on an emptied `CATS_DE`.

**The second shape, and the half that was worse.** An overflow audit reported the gate's blind spot: it matched keyed objects only, so a bare **ARRAY** of codes (`["fr","en","es","de","it"]`) went straight past it. That shape had frozen **six guards** on five languages — `docParity` (a changelog entry present in five sections and missing from the sixth would NOT have been caught), `helpCatalogueBrands`, the layout harness's marker parity, the shipped-dictionary rules, the label contracts, and `detectUiLang`'s supported set — plus one user-facing defect: **`TermsGate`'s language toggle offered fr and en only, unchanged since es/de/it landed**, on the FIRST screen a new user sees. It looked deliberate, which is why it survived three language additions. Gate 15 now reads both shapes (a list must be codes and NOTHING else, or every two-string array would read as a language axis). **Bringing tests into the gate was tried and REVERTED in the same build**: it reported 45 sites, ~30 of them legitimate two-language fixtures for a pure function, and a guard needing thirty acknowledgements to stay quiet is one people learn to silence — so the test side is closed by `languageAxisTests.test.ts`, which looks only at a MODULE-SCOPE list (indent zero) that drives a suite, and reports zero fixture noise. **The frozen guards were the worse half**, because a green suite is precisely what stops anyone looking further — the same shape as `prune` failing for nine releases while this file asserted a clean baseline, and as the six silent fallbacks with 3569 of 3571 tests passing. Two consequences worth knowing: the **label contracts now guard `pt.ts` and the pt help block** (7 dictionary + 8 help patterns, each verified to match the shipped file before being added — a pattern that never matches makes the gate permanently red), and **`detectUiLang(["pt-BR"])` now returns `pt`**, which is wanted (the app ships one Portuguese, and pt-PT beats the English fallback for a Brazilian reader) and is asserted so the consequence is recorded rather than rediscovered.

**The hardcoded languages NO gate can see, and the shapes that make them invisible.** Gates 13-15 and `languageAxisTests` between them cover keyed objects, flat arrays of codes, and the two named maps. A sweep of everything OUTSIDE those shapes — `lang === "x"` comparisons, TS unions, regex alternations, glob patterns, `public/*.html`, `sw.js`, `manifest.json`, the build scripts, the ESLint rules — found **five more frozen lists, every one failing silently**. (1) **`public/reset.html`'s message table stopped at `it`**, so a Portuguese reader hit `L[lng] || L.en` and read ENGLISH *on the one page you reach when nothing else works*; the file sits outside doc:check's source tree, so no gate had ever looked at it. (2) **`useStartupNotice`'s "any slot present" fallback tail** was the literal `["…","en","fr","es","de","it"]`, so a broadcast authored ONLY in Portuguese was invisible to every other reader while an fr-only one reached everyone — and `RawNotice` refused a `pt` slot outright, so it could not be authored without a cast. Gate 15 structurally cannot see this one: the array mixes a VARIABLE (`lang`) with codes, and the gate only reads lists that are codes and nothing else. It is derived from `LANGUAGES` now (duplicates are harmless — the loop stops at the first slot with content). (3) **`TobaccoFormView` + `WishFormView` called `tobaccoDbLookupSync(brand, name, lang === "en" ? "en" : "fr")`** — a two-language clamp predating v1.3. Every OTHER caller passes `lang` straight through, so the catalogue description the `CatalogOffer` diff was judged against was the FRENCH one for four of the six languages; `pickLang` already owns the requested → en → fr ladder, which is the correct one. (4) **`i18nChecks.test`'s identical-value loop** was the literal `["en","es","de","it"]` — one line under a map the sweep had already DERIVED, inside a test claiming "in any language" — so Portuguese drift went unchecked from the day it shipped (probed: making a `pt` value identical to `fr` now turns it red; it was green before). `languageAxisTests` cannot see this one either: it reads MODULE-SCOPE lists only, and this one lives in an `it()` body. (5) **`docPages.wellformed`'s "languages the fr/en-only archive cannot offer back" list** (the toggle guard) had frozen at `["es","de","it"]` — so the newest language, the one likeliest to be narrowed away by an untested path, was the single case nobody checked. **The lesson is the shape, not the count: a frozen list is invisible in exact proportion to how ordinary it looks**, and the four gates only see the two shapes someone thought to describe. **Two deliberate subsets that had no stated reason now carry one** (an unexplained subset is indistinguishable from a frozen one, and gets "completed" by the next sweep): `theme:contrast` runs ONE language because a contrast ratio is a property of the colour TOKENS, not the words — the same element measures identically in six languages, so the full matrix would cost 6× the runtime for identical numbers, and language-dependent failures are LAYOUT failures belonging to `i18n:layout`; and `buildCsvLines` is French by construction (see the note). **Gate 15 also stopped reading PROSE as data**: comments are blanked before the scan (length-preserving, so line numbers still point at the real file) after the gate reported its own explanatory comment — one quoting `["es","de","it"]` — back at itself. A false positive is not benign here: it gets correct code rewritten to please the guard, which is the failure this whole family of gates exists to prevent.

**The pt-PT glossary, written down because it cost a native review and will otherwise be re-litigated.** Portuguese is **European (pt-PT), not Brazilian**, and the two are far enough apart in everyday computing vocabulary that a Brazilian word reads as a machine translation to a reader in Portugal. The settled terms: **ecrã** (not tela), **ficheiro** (not arquivo), **gerir** (not gerenciar), **guardar** (not salvar), **aceder** (not acessar), **utilizador** (not usuário), and **AO90** spelling (`percetível`, `ativo` — no mute consonant). The catalogue prose keeps the glossary already settled on this project: **picante** not apimentado, **fumado** not defumado, **alperce** not damasco, **maçaroca** not sabugo (measured over the shipped `tobacco-db.desc-pt.json`, counting each term with its inflections — `\b(picante|fumad[oa]|alperce|maçaroca)s?\b` — picante 79 / fumado 405 / alperce 16 / maçaroca 2, against **zero** for all four Brazilian alternatives counted the same way. The method is stated because the figures differ by an order of magnitude depending on it: `fumado` alone, exact, is 21). **Pipe jargon stays in English**, as it does in every other language of this app — `CUTS_PT` overrides only `Autre`, because Flake / Ribbon / Plug / Ready Rubbed / Coins are what Portuguese smokers actually say; the tobacco FAMILIES keep the adjectival form agreeing with *tabaco* (Inglês / Aromático / Escocês), matching how es and it do it. **The one structural trap: `o cachimbo` is MASCULINE**, where *la pipe* / *la pipa* / *la pipa* are feminine in fr/es/it — so curvature is **Reto / Semicurvo / Curvo** and finish is **Liso / Rusticado / Areado / Tingido**, NOT the `-a` forms. Copying the Spanish or Italian row's shape (the obvious shortcut when filling a new `ENUM_TRANSLATIONS` column) misagrees on every pipe fiche, in the two enums most visible there. **Two bowl/stem materials were corrected against Portuguese trade and forum sources (.pt), not a dictionary**: Bruyère is **Briar** (the lusophone trade sells "cachimbos de briar"; "raiz de urze" appears only as a gloss and *urze* alone names the shrub, Erica — and each language already uses its own trade word: Briar / Bruyère / Brezo / Radica, so Portuguese using "briar" is the pattern, not an untranslated string), and Meerschaum is **Espuma do mar** (real .pt sources write "cachimbo em espuma do mar"; collectors understand the German word but it is not the usual label in Portugal). **Checked and deliberately KEPT — do not redo this search**: "Torga" rejected for Bruyère (it is *Calluna vulgaris*, a different species); "Areado" kept for sandblasted because "jateado" is attested only on Brazilian sites; **Corno, Ebonite, Calcador, Milho, Esteatite, Bordo, Cana** each verified; "Bolsa de tabaco" kept over "tabaqueira", which in Portugal reads as the national tobacco company. Two dictionary findings were also rejected on evidence: **FEITO stays** in the finished badge (all five siblings use their own "done" word there and TERMINADO would clip), and **"blends" stays untranslated** because the rest of the pt catalogue copy does.

**Adding a language (the infra is prepped, so it's mostly content).** The `ADD A LANGUAGE` checklist lives in `src/i18n/languages.ts`. In short, for Spanish `es`:
1. `src/i18n/languages.ts` → add `{ code: "es", label: "ES" }` to `LANGUAGES` (BOTH switchers read this list — Settings, and the `TermsGate` one — so the toggle option appears automatically).
2. `src/i18n/es.ts` (`export var ES = {…}`) with the **same key set** as fr/en. **Nothing to wire** — `src/i18n.ts` reaches the non-English dictionaries through `import.meta.glob("./i18n/*.ts")`, so the new file is picked up and emitted as its own chunk automatically. Do NOT add a static import: that would pull the language into the cold start and undo the change.
3. `src/constants.ts` → add the `_ES` enum maps (`CATS_ES`, `CUTS_ES`, …) and an `es:` entry in each `ENUM_TRANSLATIONS` row (the ONLY place enum-label translations wire in — `xl()` resolves them by lang, keyed off the English map, so no `xl(…)` call site changes).
4. Doc pages: author `<div id="sec-es">…</div>` in `public/{changelog,privacy}.html`, and the `es-…` `<h2>` anchors in `public/help.html` + `es:` ids in `HelpView.SECTION_IDS` + the ids in `HELP_SECTION_IDS` (doc-check). `licenses.html` is English-only legal text — `extractBody` serves it to all languages, nothing to do. **Also `public/reset.html`'s `L` message table** (it sits outside doc:check's source tree, so NO gate looks at it, and a missing row silently serves English on the one page you reach when the app itself is broken).
5. **`LANG_ASSETS` in `src/i18n/languages.ts` — a row of five values** (`numberLocale` / `nominatim` / `monthsShort` / `dayInitials` / `aiPromptName`). **Not optional**: `doc:check` gate 13 FAILS without it, which is the whole point — those five used to live in five separate maps that each fell back SILENTLY, so a new language got French number formatting, French place names, English months and weekday initials, and AI-written text in English, with every check green.
6. Catalog descriptions (optional but recommended): `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=… npm run translate:tobacco es` — AI-translates each blend's English description into `description.es`, idempotent, on-demand/token-costly. Until it runs, `es` users see the English catalog description (via the `pickLang` fallback); category/cut already translate via `xl()`. Then bump build + rebuild so the enriched chunk ships.

**Enum DISPLAY invariant.** Enum values (category, cut, shape, courbure/bend, filterType, bowlMaterial, stemMaterial, finish, accessory type, fuel) are STORED canonical (French) and MUST be run through `xl(value, XXX_EN)` at every render site — never interpolated raw into JSX. Raw renders silently stay French in every non-French language (es/de/it at the time of the bug, es/de/it/pt today — and `en` too for any value the `_EN` map actually rewrites) (the enum-render bug: tobacco card / detail category·cut, Home featured tobacco+pipe, pipe-detail shape header, accessory-card fuel, and every SearchModal subtitle were rendering the stored value directly). `searchAll()` (SearchModal, a pure non-component fn) takes `xl` as its 4th arg since it can't reach ctx. When you add a new view that shows an enum field, wrap it in `xl(…)` and import the matching `_EN` map; a bare `{item.category}` is a translation bug, not a style choice. **`xl()` and `catColor()` must not resolve a forged label to a PROTOTYPE MEMBER.** Every `_XX` map is a plain object literal, so `m["__proto__"]` is `Object.prototype` — an OBJECT, and TRUTHY, so the `|| v` fallback never fires — and `m["toString"]` is a function. Handed to React as a child an object **THROWS** (« Objects are not valid as a React child »), which the error boundary turns into the full-screen failure page. **Reachable made the catalogue the user's own file**: `parseCatalogueCsv` keeps an unrecognised taxonomy label VERBATIM on purpose, so a row saying `category: __proto__` is loaded, indexed and rendered. **And ONLY in a non-French UI**, because `xl` returns early for French — the kind of asymmetry nobody stumbles on by testing. `catColor` never crashes: it puts an object into a CSS colour, which the browser drops, so the label silently loses its colour. Both now use `hasOwnProperty` + a string check, at the READER rather than by null-prototyping ~50 maps — the map arrives as a PARAMETER, so one guard covers every caller and every future map (the `safeBgUrl` argument: many sources, one sink). **`effectiveAgingMax` and `CUT_DENSITY` already had this exact guard; these are the two sites that pass missed**, which is why `forgedEnumLabel.test.ts` re-asserts all four together. It also PINS the exposure itself (a plain map really does resolve `__proto__`), so the day someone null-prototypes `constants.ts` the case fails and says the guards became belt-and-braces rather than the only defence. Probed in both directions. **This is now enforced by `tabac-local/no-raw-enum-render`** (see the custom-ESLint-rules index) — a bare enum rendered as JSX text blocks CI instead of shipping French to every language but French.

`doc:check` **auto-discovers** every `src/i18n/<code>.ts` (2-3 letter code) and enforces parity against the `fr` reference across ALL of them — no edit to the check. The in-app doc views (`DocPageView`/`HelpView`) resolve `sec-<lang>` / per-section ids dynamically via `docPage.ts` (`extractLangSection` / `pickLang`) with a requested → en → fr fallback. **The "handful of inline `lang === "en" ? … : …` strings fall to the FR branch" claim that stood here is STALE and was deleted**: an audit found ZERO user-visible two-language ternaries left in `src/`; every surviving comparison is logic (plural rule, date format, decimal separator, chunk paths). Run `localStorage.setItem("cave-lang","pseudo")` (pseudo-loc mode) to surface every string that bypasses `t()` before translating — **and note that this mode was silently DEAD for a stretch**: the `isLangLoaded` startup guard did not know `pseudo` has no dictionary, so `lang` fell to `"en"` and the `lang === "pseudo"` branch became unreachable while this paragraph kept recommending it. Measured: 0 of 938 marked nodes before the fix, 1706 of 3650 after. `_langUsable` now exempts it, and `i18nOnDemand.test.ts` pins that.

**`doc:check` enforces LABEL TRUTHFULNESS (gates 10-11).** Parity gates prove a label EXISTS in every language and that its dev fallback matches — never that it is still TRUE. Six user-facing claims had silently drifted (the merge description, the privacy policy's photo + AI paragraphs, the device-name hint, the diagnostic's "repair" offer, two lot hints); each was code moving while prose stood still, and one had survived 20 builds. The registry + full rationale live in **`scripts/label-contracts.json`**; two gates attack the problem from both ends of what a machine can actually verify:
- **(a) numeric contracts** — a claim quoting a NUMBER is mechanically checkable. Each entry reads the value out of the code (`source` + `match`, capture group 1, optional `divide`), renders each `patterns` string with `{n}`, and asserts it appears in the doc. Change `TRASH_RETENTION_DAYS` without touching "30 jours" and CI names both sides. Patterns are listed per language **only where that wording was verified to exist** — a pattern absent on day one makes the gate permanently red and therefore worthless; partial coverage still catches a constant change. **26 contracts**. **Eight of them target CLAUDE.md rather than a shipped doc, and they close a class the others could not see**: a family of CAPS — `MAX_ROWS`, `MAX_TAG_LEN`, `MAX_TAGS_PER_ITEM`, `DIAGNOSTIC_MAX_RECENT`, `GDRIVE_PENDING_STALE_MS`, `MAX_CSV_ISSUES`, `MAX_CATALOGUE_ISSUES`, `MAX_CATALOGUE_ROWS` — whose values appear in NO user-facing prose, only here, and whose tests all IMPORT the constant and compute from it, so they are self-referential by construction. **MEASURED across the whole suite: with four of them mutated at once, only three cases went red, and two of those were fixtures the absurd value happened to truncate** — a realistic drift (50000 → 40000, 20 → 15) reddened nothing anywhere. `docText` returns raw content for a non-HTML target, so CLAUDE.md needed no new mechanism. Probed one by one: each of the eight now fails doc:check on a plausible change. The remaining 18 are checked against `public/help.html` and — for the 7 whose number is also worded in the UI — against **every** `src/i18n/*.ts` dictionary (the `pt.ts` row was added to all 7 and a `pt` pattern to the help block; before that the Portuguese translations of those claims were unverified) — the same numbers live in both, and for three claims (photo cap, search minimum, tasting auto-close total) the dictionaries are the ONLY place they appear: trash retention, pipe rest target + 24 h minimum, maintenance threshold, tasting overtime + auto-close, passphrase minimum, max extra pipe photos, default low-stock grams, the catalogue floor, and three CEILING claims — the Home "À surveiller" window, the "Ce soir ?" secondary list, and the 3 rotating manual cloud backups. **A ceiling is `exact`, not `atLeast`**: "jusqu'à 3" is wrong whether the cap rises OR falls, whereas a floor claim ("plus de 1200") only breaks downward. Writing those three contracts is what exposed two more drifts — "À surveiller" had displayed 3 at a time while the help still said 5, and "Ce soir ?" shows a featured pick PLUS 3 others, not 3 in total. That last one uses `mode: "atLeast"` — the pattern carries a `(\d+)` and the number found in the DOC must be ≤ the code's, so "plus de 1200 blends" stays green (**1225 today**, 25 of margin — and note the catalogue has both SHRUNK and grown, 1221 → 1215 through merges, then 1219 and 1225, so `atLeast` guards a floor approached from ABOVE, not a growing number) but fails the day a bad importer run ships fewer than advertised. Source can be `source`+`match` (regex over text), `sourceJson`+`jsonArrayPath` (collection length), or **`sum: [term, term]`** for a DERIVED claim — "auto-ended after 95 min" is really `OVERTIME_THRESHOLD` (90) + `OVERTIME_AUTO_END` (5), so reading both terms means the claim breaks if EITHER moves; pinning 95 to one of them would silently miss a change to the other.
- **(b) prose contracts** — prose semantics can't be compared to code, so the gate detects that the described behaviour MOVED and forces a human re-read. A code region delimited by `// LABEL-CONTRACT:start <id>` / `:end <id>` is fingerprinted (whitespace-normalised, so a reformat is not a false positive); when the hash drifts, doc:check fails, prints the entry's `why`, and lists the labels to re-read. If they are still accurate, acknowledge **explicitly**: `node scripts/doc-check.cjs --accept <id>` (or `--accept all`) rewrites the stored fingerprint. That extra step is the point — re-reading must be a conscious act, never a default. **13 couplings**. **A prose entry's `labels` are the list of strings to RE-READ, and many of them still end "(5 languages)" — that parenthetical is a stale COUNT, not a scope**: every one of those paragraphs exists in six sections, and the fingerprint fires regardless of how many. Read it as "in every language section"; fix the count in `label-contracts.json` when you next touch an entry. `makeBackupName` → device-name hint/help/CLAUDE.md, `gatherLocalImages` → privacy photos paragraph, `aiScanLabel` → privacy AI paragraph, `applyEntityLww` → `import_merge_desc`, `lotAgingStatus` → the "en cave uniquement" claims, plus the three NETWORK-FLOW paragraphs (the category where drift is most expensive, since it means under-disclosing what leaves the device): `reverseGeocode` → the Nominatim promises, the JSZip CDN loader → the cdnjs disclosure + licence attribution, `gdriveGetToken` → the `drive.appdata` scope paragraph a Google OAuth reviewer reads, `buildDropboxAuthUrl` → the App-folder confinement claim, and `dropboxProvider` → the two transfer hosts. **`AI_MODEL_DEFAULTS` + `AI_MODEL_OPTIONS` + `AI_MODEL_ALIASES` → the help's "Choix du modèle" note (5 languages) + the CLAUDE.md provider table** — vendor line-ups now move every few months, and one refresh showed what that costs: `gemini-2.0-flash`, the app's own Gemini DEFAULT, had been shut down for four months with every Gemini auto-fill failing. What kept the help note TRUE through that refresh is that it names model FAMILIES only (Haiku / Sonnet / Opus), never versions — the `why` tells the next reader to check that property first. The region deliberately includes the ALIASES: an alias silently remaps a user's remembered choice, which is itself a claim the note makes (qualified accordingly — "si un modèle est retiré, l'app le remplace par l'équivalent actuel", a sentence my own model refresh had just made necessary). **`ensureLang` → the help's "Langue" bullet (5 languages) + the two CLAUDE.md i18n entries + `lang_offline_err`/`lang_offline_reload`/`lang_loading`** — the on-demand loader made a language change something that can FAIL, and the help went on promising it "à tout moment" with no caveat, in all five languages, for three releases; that is the exact gap this gate exists to close. **`CUT_DENSITY` + `DEFAULT_CUT_DENSITY` + the shape-taper tables → the help's session-weight note (5 languages) + the CLAUDE.md `bowlEstimate.ts` entry, which reproduces the whole density table value by value.** Those numbers already moved three times. Two of the help's claims there are ORDERINGS, not quoted numbers — "a dense flake outweighs an airy ribbon at equal volume" and "a conical chamber holds less than a straight one" — so they are asserted mechanically in `bowlEstimate.test.ts` under a describe block named for the help: a density pass that inverts one of them goes red BEFORE the fingerprint asks for a re-read, which is the stronger guarantee of the two. Use that pattern whenever a prose claim happens to be checkable. **The gate for a claim about the catalogue's CONTENTS, not its size**: `helpCatalogueBrands.test.ts` reads the example brands out of every `"…1200…(A, B, C…)"` paragraph of the shipped `public/help.html`, per language, and asserts each has blends in `tobacco-db.json`. The numeric contract only ever checked the COUNT, so a brand could be advertised in the guide while the catalogue held none of its blends — leaving a reader who looked for it to conclude the catalogue was broken. **The resolution rule is the load-bearing part**: a first version compared the advertised name to the brand KEY for equality and wrongly flagged a brand the catalogue stores under a longer key with the advertised name as an explicit alias — an over-strict guard is worse than none, because it forces correct prose to be deleted (it did: the name was removed before a user caught it). The test now walks the same ladder as the app — exact key, then the brand's aliases, then a substring of the full brand name — and asserts BOTH directions: an absent brand still fails, an aliased one still passes. The extraction requires the parenthetical to be NEAR the figure and to be a real enumeration (≥ 2 commas) — a wider window jumped to an unrelated parenthetical — and the test refuses to pass vacuously (it asserts it found a list, and that the catalogue is non-empty).
**`public/changelog.html` is DELIBERATELY NOT covered by the label-quoting registry, and the reason is not that nobody looked.** Measured: the file quotes ZERO Settings breadcrumbs and exactly FOUR control names — the `home_pair_accord` word in fr/es/it/pt, all four currently correct. So the subject is almost empty, and the part that exists is HISTORICAL: a changelog entry records what a past release did, so an entry naming the label the app used AT THE TIME stays a true statement after a rename, where the guide and the policy describe the app NOW and become false. Adding a gate here would guard four words and would fight the file's purpose. **Do not "complete the sweep" onto it.**

- **(c) domain coverage** — the scheme's last blind spot was that nothing forced anyone to CREATE a contract: a new endpoint could ship dutifully disclosed in the policy and completely uncoupled, so the next time its behaviour moved no gate would ask anyone to re-read that paragraph. Gate 8 already computes every host `src/` talks to; this reuses that set from the other side — **every request target must be claimed by exactly one prose contract** via `domains: [...]`, and a claimed host the app no longer contacts is flagged too (stale bookkeeping, and the paragraph may now over-disclose). All 12 current hosts are claimed. A host that is a placeholder or a user-tapped link belongs in `DOMAIN_IGNORE` instead, with a comment.
- **HTML docs are matched on their TEXT layer**, not their source (`docText`): a claim is routinely split by inline markup (`jusqu'à <strong>3</strong> sauvegardes`), which a source-level substring match misses even though the sentence reads fine. Script/style bodies are dropped so a stray literal there can't satisfy a claim; `raw: true` opts back into source matching.

The gate logic lives in **`scripts/labelContracts.cjs`** — pure, `readFile` injected, so it is unit-tested by `src/__tests__/labelContracts.test.ts` (42 cases). **The i18n gates got the same treatment**: their DECISIONS moved to **`scripts/i18nChecks.cjs`** (pure — dictionary parsing, the allowlist shape, what counts as a suspicious identical value, the length-ratio outliers, parity gaps), leaving `doc-check.cjs` to read files and report. Tested by `src/__tests__/i18nChecks.test.ts` (25 cases). **The same was done for three more gates** — **`scripts/docChecks.cjs`** (`src/__tests__/docChecks.test.ts`, 131 cases — the figure said 18 for a long time, having never followed gates 13→22) holds the structure-TREE parser (a directory stack across lines, globs skipped, inline comments stripped), the privacy-DOMAIN disclosure decision (verbatim host or a mapped prose name like "Anthropic"), and the BUMP gate's user-visible predicate — where the load-bearing detail is that NEVER-visible WINS over visible (`src/utils/x.test.ts` matches `^src/utils/`; flipping it would fail every test-only commit and train people to reach for `DOC_CHECK_SKIP_BUMP`). Each was mutation-probed: flipping the precedence, dropping the tree's directory stack, and short-circuiting `domainDisclosed` to `true` each turn the suite red. **A third pass finished the job**: the version/changelog cross-check (`checkVersions` — asymmetric on purpose: an entry may LAG behind `APP_BUILD` because a fix-only bump must not be forced to invent changelog noise, but never overshoot it), the help-anchor validator (`checkHelpAnchors` — including the landed-outside-the-wrapper case that is the whole reason it exists: a malformed tag auto-closes `<div id="sec-fr">` and HelpView then renders those sections as empty title-less cards) and the dev-fallback parity gate (`findFallbackMismatches`) all moved into the same module, +17 cases. Probed the same way: making the changelog rule symmetric, dropping the wrapper containment check, and stubbing the fallback comparison each turn the suite red. The motivation is the same as for the contracts: `doc-check.cjs` had grown to ~15 gates with NO tests of its own, and the identical-value gate had just been rewritten (flat allowlist → per-language) with nothing but two manual probes behind it — a gate whose own correctness is unverified prints "doc:check OK" just as confidently after it has silently stopped checking anything. The cases lean on the negative side (what must still be flagged, what must never be silenced), including that the legacy flat array is REJECTED rather than honoured, and they re-run the real rules over the real dictionaries so a data regression also shows up in `npm test`. Those tests lock the FAILURE behaviour specifically: a guard that silently stops firing is worse than no guard, because it reads as "verified" while verifying nothing. They also assert the real registry isn't empty and that every prose entry carries a recorded fingerprint, a region, labels and a `why`; `doc-check.cjs` separately errors if either list is empty, so the gates can't pass vacuously.

**When you add a claim that quotes a number, or move logic a sentence describes, add the contract in the same commit.** The markers also pay off at the code site: whoever edits a marked region sees which sentence documents it.

**`doc:check` also runs two i18n quality warnings.** Both are non-failing — they surface candidates for human review:
- **Identical values across a language pair** — likely a forgotten translation. Checked for every pair (fr/en, fr/es, fr/de, fr/it). The script auto-skips pure-symbol strings (emojis like `📊`), ≤3-char codes (`min`, `lot`), and entries on the `identical` allowlist in `scripts/doc-check.allowlist.json` — which **now** maps each key to the LANGUAGES the match is by design in (`"catalog_title": ["en"]`, or `"*"` for a value identical everywhere by nature). The previous flat key list silenced a key across all four pairs at once, so allowlisting `catalog_title` for fr/en also hid a future Italian left as "Catalogue"; the loader now REJECTS the old array shape with a migration message rather than honouring it silently. The allowlist covers legitimate cognates — `Description`, `Notes`, `Wishlist`, brand names, English `Journal`/`Latitude`/`Floral`, German `Vanille`/`Anis`, Spanish `Miel`/`Combustible`/`disponible`, Italian `Access.`. Add only the language you verified — that precision is the point. When you add a key whose translations legitimately match, append it so the warning stays actionable — the 27 that had accumulated were verified and listed (plus dropped two genuinely dead keys, `tags_none` + `warn_url_kept_as_is_long`, the latter left over from the URL-image removal), taking both the identical and the unused warnings back to **zero**.
- **A translation > 1.4× the FR length** (FR ≥ 3 chars) — may overflow tight layouts (button labels, card chips, dock tabs). Per language, measured: 100 de / 79 it / 73 es / 56 pt / 30 en — far too many to re-read on each commit, so **the question is answered by RENDERING instead**: `npm run i18n:layout` (`scripts/i18n-layout.cjs`) drives the built app in a real browser at 360 px with a seeded cellar and FAILS on (a) horizontal document overflow, (b) text wider than its box that cannot be shown (`nowrap` / `overflow:hidden` / ellipsis), (c) text PAINTED PAST a clipping ancestor (see the end of this bullet), or (d) a screen it could not reach. **It was widened on the two axes that were missing.** SCREENS: the six dock pages were the easy ones — the dense surfaces are the FORMS and SETTINGS (label + field + hint per row, where German runs longest), and neither is reachable by a dock click, so the first version never looked at them; it now navigates to add-tobacco, add-pipe and all four Settings tabs (12 screens at the time; 33 — see the notes). TEXT SIZE: the whole matrix runs at M **and at the "L" setting** (`cave-font-scale` 1.12), which multiplies every string by 12% on top of the translation's own length — a German label at 1.4× the French rendered 12% larger is the real worst case. **A third axis was added — VIEWPORT**: 360 px is the phone the app is designed for, and 820 px clears the 760 px column cap so the two-column Home grids, the wide Stats charts and the centred dock pill are exercised at full width (no automated check had ever looked at that layout). `I18N_LAYOUT_SCALES=m` / `I18N_LAYOUT_WIDTHS=360` narrow the matrix while iterating. **The harness's own assumptions are unit-tested without a browser** (`src/__tests__/i18nLayoutHarness.test.ts`, 22 cases): the script exports its `SCREENS` / `SEED_KEYS` / `DATA`, and the tests assert that every screen's `expect` marker key AND every key it navigates by (`btn_add`, `btn_settings`, `tab_*`) still exists in EVERY dictionary — `LANGS` there is derived from `LANGUAGES` (it was the five literal codes, so a marker missing from a newly-added language would have passed; two `it()` TITLES still read "all five", which is the stale number and not the check) — that the seed keeps suppressing the two states that once broke the run, and that the seed still exercises what is measured (jar + cellar + finished lots, a no-rebuy tobacco for the third badge, canonical French enum values). Because the check is opt-in and needs a browser, it can go months without running — these fail in `npm test` the moment a key is renamed out from under it. Selectors come from the DICTIONARIES (the script parses `src/i18n/<lang>.ts` and looks up e.g. `btn_settings`), so it clicks the right control per language and a renamed key fails the run instead of silently skipping a screen. It is opt-in — **not a CI gate, and Playwright is deliberately NOT a dependency** (`npm i --no-save playwright-core` for the run); the check only means something when the UI or the dictionaries change shape, so run it when you add a language, add a dense surface, or before a release. `-- --shots` also writes per-screen PNGs. ****Last full-matrix result — the build-59 run: PASS, and the FIRST one sharded.** 6 languages × 36 screens × 2 text sizes × 2 widths (864 renders, **~10 min** — one process per language, see the fan-out note above): no overflow, no clipped text, no stray horizontal scroller, nothing cut off by a hidden-overflow ancestor. It is the first full run since the flat lists gained their `inv-long` screen, since the grouped lists were capped, and since two builds added cloud prose. **The canary behaved EXACTLY as the note below predicts, which is itself a check on the note**: French **0**, English **10 and all at `l`**, es/de/it/pt at both sizes (20/15/20/20), and **all 85 rows at 360 px, none at 820**. Those 85 are ONE card footer seen through FIVE doors — `inv`, `inv-long`, and the three modals that render the inventory list behind them — not five defects. It reproduces the serial run's output exactly — 85 canary rows, the same tobacco-card footer through the same five doors — which is what makes « faster » a measurement rather than a hope. Previous run (in series): **the build-57 run: PASS**, same matrix, ~55 min. Before that: **the build-43 run: PASS.** 6 languages × 35 screens × 2 text sizes × 2 widths (840 renders, ~55 min): no overflow, no clipped text, no stray horizontal scroller, nothing cut off by a hidden-overflow ancestor. It is the run that covers the builds where the Home changed shape (the accord row moved OUT of the « Ce soir ? » PressCard) and where seven views started rendering POPULATED data in the a11y fixture. **The canary behaved exactly as predicted below — French never, English only at "L", es/de/it/pt at both sizes, and only ever at 360 px — with ONE figure to correct: the English row measures 203 px of 206 here, not the 206 recorded below.** It still wraps, because the row's 8 px gap is what pushes it over (203 + 8 > 206), so the reading is unchanged; the 3 px is font-metric variance between machines, and the rule this file states about numbers applies to its own — **the figure a reader should trust is the one the last writer produced.** 68 informational rows, all four screens being the SAME card seen through `inv` plus the three modals that render the list behind them. **The previous PRE-LAUNCH run: PASS** — 6 × 34 screens × 2 × 2 (816 renders, ~50 min). **It was the first full run on the CORRECTED SEED** — the fix that gave `modal-lot` three sessions attributed to a pinned, balanced lot — so the populated lot-session list is now measured rather than assumed, which is the whole point of that fix (a green run over an empty state is the most reassuring way to miss a screen). The only output is the documented tobacco-card footer canary, and it behaves exactly as the note below predicts: es/de/it/pt at both text sizes, **English at "L" (206 px of 206, the arithmetic to the pixel)**, and French never — which is what identifies it as a row sitting at its limit rather than a translation defect. **It now also reports under `modal-trash` / `modal-shopping` / `modal-search`, and that is ONE row seen four times, not four defects**: those screens render the inventory list BEHIND the modal, so the same card footer is still in the DOM. Do NOT "fix" it by shortening translations — that was tried exactly on the Italian and reverted. Previous full-matrix result: PASS, the first clean full matrix and the first full run at all; it confirmed the search-subtitle wrap in all six languages, and that the guide prose and chip relabelling introduced nothing. Before that — the first run covering all SIX languages (792 renders: 6 × 33 screens × 2 text sizes × 2 widths, ~2 h): it FAILED, on two Italian defects, and both are worth knowing.** (1) `modal-maint`'s title was clipped at 360 px / "L" — "Nuova manutenzione" needs 158 px in a 148 px box — fixed by letting the TITLE wrap (the title set is bounded, two strings × six languages, so wrapping cannot run away; the brand overline above keeps nowrap+ellipsis because a brand can be any length). Abbreviating the Italian would have bought 10 px and a vaguer word, which is the BARATTOLO trade rejected earlier. (2) **Four `acc-retired` screens became UNREACHABLE because of a correct translation fix**: it changed the Italian `acc_retired_lower` from "ritirato" to "ritirati" (it sits in a count slot — the header read "3 ritirato"), and the harness clicked `getByText("Ritirati", {exact:false})`, which is case-insensitive, so `.first()` silently moved from the chip to the now-matching count line and clicked something inert. The harness uses `getByRole("button", …, {exact:true})` there now: **a selector must target the CONTROL, not the text, or a correct fix elsewhere can make a screen stop being measured** — and an unreachable screen is a loud failure here precisely so it cannot pass as "clean". After both fixes Italian re-ran green over its 132 renders. Do not restate this result as current after adding a language or a screen — re-run it. — the wrapping layouts absorb the slack, so the doc:check warning is advisory, not a defect list. What the script REPORTS without failing is the tightest row in the app — the tobacco card's footer (`space-between`: weight left, status badges right, ~206 px usable, French 152). Every language except fr/en wraps it in some configuration at the default text size (it 222-246 px; es 207 and de 199 + the row's 8 px gap once a third badge like the ✕ no-rebuy marker appears) — and at the **"L" text size EVEN ENGLISH does** (206 px of 206), so this is a row sitting at its limit, not a translation problem: the row is `flexWrap`, so nothing clips and the card is just ~29 px taller. **Do not "fix" this by shortening translations** — Italian `BARATTOLO` → `BARAT.` was tried and reverted, because at 199 + 8 > 206 it still wrapped and so bought no layout gain, only a vaguer word. If the single line is ever wanted back the honest lever is the layout (the 8 px gap or the badge letter-spacing). **THE 36th SCREEN IS `inv-long`, AND IT EXISTS BECAUSE THE SEED COULD NOT REACH A CONTROL.** The flat lists render a bounded prefix now (`useProgressiveList`, 60 rows) with an « Afficher la suite (N) » footer under it — a mono uppercase label with letter-spacing, in six languages — and the shared seed holds **18 tobaccos**, so that control had never been rendered by either browser check. Same rule the seed keeps re-teaching, one notch out: *a green run over a state the seed CANNOT REACH is the most reassuring way to miss a control.* `scr.bigList` swaps in a cellar of 98 tobaccos for that screen alone and swaps it back after, mirroring the per-screen catalogue mechanism. **The clones each carry ONE BALANCED LOT, and both halves are load-bearing**: a lot-less tobacco is filtered out of the default « Actifs » list (`countActive` needs a non-finished lot) so it would never reach the list at all, and an unbalanced one trips `useLotIntegrityProbe` 1.5 s after load, which turns the Settings diagnostic oxblood and silently changes what a later screen measures. **Two harness defects came out of adding it, and each is the same shape as one already recorded here.** (1) **`addInitScript` runs before EVERY page load in the context**, so the reload a cellar swap needs immediately overwrote the swapped cellar — and the screen reported as *unreachable*, i.e. a seed that never arrived, dressed as a navigation problem, which is precisely the diagnosis this harness has been fooled by before. The init script honours a `__harness-cellar-pinned` flag now. (2) **A marker carrying a placeholder can never be found**: `list_more` is « Mehr anzeigen ({n}) » and the app interpolates the count, so the raw dictionary value appears nowhere on the page. `markerText()` truncates at the first `{`, **with a length guard** — a value beginning with its placeholder would leave a prefix short enough to match half the page, turning « screen reached » into the vacuous pass this whole marker mechanism exists to prevent. Both are pinned in `i18nLayoutHarness.test.ts`. **Result at 360 px / « L » in German — the worst case on every axis — PASS**, the footer measured and clean; the only output is the documented tobacco-card canary, which now also reports under `inv-long` because it is the same card seen through one more screen. **The seed is load-bearing, and two of its entries were learned the hard way**: (1) lists are grouped-and-collapsed by default, so without `cave-default-grouped=0` no card renders and the check would pass having measured nothing — it counts the seeded entities it actually saw and fails at zero (that guard fired on the very first run); (2) a cellar that has never been exported shows the **export-reminder banner**, which is `position:fixed` at the top and COVERS the TopBar — it swallowed the "+" and the gear, and the Settings modal even opened on the wrong tab because the tab click landed on the banner, so the seed sets `cave-last-export-ts` to now. **Each navigated screen also proves it arrived** by finding a string that exists only there (`expect`, resolved through the dictionary): counting inputs was NOT enough — the inventory list has filter `<select>`s, so a form that never opened still looked "reached", while the App and Help tabs have no inputs at all and looked broken.

  **The FOURTH failure mode: text PAINTED PAST a clipping ancestor.** The three older rules ask whether the DOCUMENT slides sideways, whether a text leaf clips its OWN text (`nowrap` / `pre` / `overflow-x: hidden` / ellipsis), and whether some container became draggable (the unmarked horizontal scroller, `data-hscroll` acknowledging the deliberate ones). **A case was met that is none of the three** — and it is what MOTIVATED the fourth rule below, not something still outstanding: the lot modal's Close/Delete/Edit row needed 349 px in a 340 px panel in German at the DEFAULT text size and the third button read « BEARBE ». **RESOLVED — it carries `flexWrap: "wrap"`, and the fourth rule then found its byte-identical twin in `JournalView`'s session-detail modal** (see the list of three below). CONFIRMED EMPIRICALLY by the build-43 full matrix: `modal-lot` is in the screen list, German ran at both text sizes with the fourth rule active, and nothing was reported. **The phrase « left open » stood here after the fix and cost a re-investigation** — it was carried forward into a status report as an outstanding defect, forty lines above the paragraph recording its repair.
