That is the stale-to-do failure this file already names one subsystem over: *a note that has been resolved does not merely go useless, it points the next reader backwards.* **When you fix a case a paragraph opens with, close it in that same sentence.** The row is not a text leaf, so the clipped rule skipped it; it has no `overflow-x: auto`, so the scroller rule skipped it; and **the shared `Modal` panel is `overflow: hidden`, which both swallows the excess and leaves `document.scrollWidth` unchanged** — so the screen WAS in this checker's list and passed. The failure it hides is the worst kind: a control the user can neither read nor reach, on a page that looks perfectly composed.

  **It is measured as GEOMETRY against the real clipping boundary, never as an element's own `scrollWidth`** — the leaf carries the text, the ANCESTOR decides whether the overflow is reachable. For each text LEAF the walk goes up to the first ancestor that settles the question: `auto` / `scroll`, or a `data-hscroll` marker, means the content is reachable by dragging and therefore belongs to the scroller rule, so those **CLEAR** the element instead of accusing it; `hidden` / `clip` is the clipping boundary, and the leaf's right edge is compared against `cr.left + clip.clientLeft + clip.clientWidth` (`clientLeft` skips the border, `clientWidth` excludes it and any scrollbar). **Leaves only, and only leaves with TEXT**: a decorative gradient bleeding out of a rounded `overflow: hidden` card is the intended use of that property, and reporting it would be the over-strict mistake this file keeps recording — what is never intended is a WORD cut in half.

  **A `text-overflow: ellipsis` ancestor EXEMPTS the element, and that clause was learned by measurement rather than reasoned in.** The first version flagged 7 catalogue search rows: the search TITLE is a `nowrap` / `hidden` / `ellipsis` div wrapping an italic `<span>`, so the SPAN is the leaf and lays out at its natural width, past the parent's edge. An ellipsis renders a "…", i.e. the truncation is **SIGNPOSTED** — and whether a signposted truncation is the right call is an **EDITORIAL judgement the checker must not make**. It was decided BOTH ways inside one component: wrong for the search subtitle (two enum values, a closed set, a computable maximum — so it wraps) and RIGHT for the title above it (a blend name is user-supplied and unbounded). A rule that flagged both would force the second to be "fixed" into unbounded wrapping.

  **It found three real PRE-EXISTING defects on its first two runs**, all verified on a clean tree, none caused by the probe. **(a)** `JournalView`'s session-detail modal carried the Close/Delete/Edit row **byte-identical** to the lot modal's row as it stood BEFORE the lot modal was fixed — `display: flex, gap: 10`, no `flexWrap` — so German « BEARBEITEN » was painted 27 px past the panel and read « BEARBE », at the DEFAULT text size: one twin was fixed and the other never looked at, the copied-shape failure this repo keeps paying for. **(b)** `StatsView`'s category-donut legend: the label span had `flex: 1` and no `minWidth: 0`, and **a flex item defaults to `min-width: auto`**, so at 360 px the donut (160) plus the gap (14) left ~132 px, « Virginia/Burley » needed more, and the VALUE beside it was pushed past the card's `overflow: hidden` edge and cut by 13 px — **the trap for the FOURTH time**; fixed with `minWidth: 0` + `softBreakSlashes`, which is exactly the shape `HomeViewV2`'s "Familles" row has carried for that same list of labels. **(c)** `HomeViewV2`'s `Tile` label: « CONSOMMATION » is a single 12-character word carrying 19 px of letter-spacing in a 105 px box, cut by 2 px in **FRENCH** at the "L" text size inside an `overflow: hidden` tile — neither a space nor a slash to break at, which is precisely the case `overflowWrap: anywhere` is reserved for as the last resort. **The full matrix above ran under the three older rules and therefore says nothing about this class** — do not read that PASS as covering it.

**Pseudo-localization mode.** A hidden third "language" `pseudo` lives inside the `t()` function in `App.tsx`. It re-uses the EN block at runtime and runs each string through `pseudoize()`: wraps with `⟦ … ⁂⟧` and replaces vowels + some consonants with accented variants (`a→å`, `e→é`, `i→î`, etc.). `{placeholder}` syntax is preserved so interpolation still works. Activate via DevTools:

```js
localStorage.setItem("cave-lang", "pseudo"); location.reload();
```

Reveals truncation, overflow, missing `t()` calls, and brittle layout assumptions when adding a new language. Not exposed in the language switcher UI — the switcher renders `LANGUAGES` (fr/en/es/de/it/pt today) and nothing else; `pseudo` is for design/QA passes only.

**Custom ESLint rules — index.** The canonical roster of the `tabac-local/*` rules (all in `eslint-rules/*.cjs`, each with a self-test `src/__tests__/eslint-<rule>.test.ts`). This table is the single source of truth for **name + severity + test-override**; the full rationale / history for each lives in the linked prose — update BOTH the table row and the prose when a rule changes, but the table is what a reviewer scans first. When you add a rule, add a row here — **and its self-test**: `no-platform-breadcrumb-out-of-i18n` was found to have shipped without one (11 tests for 12 rules), which matters because a lint rule's failure mode is SILENCE — one that stops matching reports nothing, indistinguishable from a clean codebase. The same build removed `eslint-rules/` from the global ESLint `ignores`, so the rule sources are now linted like any other code: their characteristic decay is a helper defined but never wired into `create()`, which `no-unused-vars` catches and nothing else did. (Four rules are additionally OFF for `scripts/**/*.cjs` — `string-only-method`, `number-only-method`, `no-dynamic-index-plain-map`, `no-raw-storage-write` — each for a reason stated at that block; see the note below the footnote.)

| Rule | Sev | Off in tests? | Catches | Full rationale |
|------|-----|---------------|---------|----------------|
| `string-locale-compare` | error | no | `.localeCompare` on a non-`String()` receiver (crash) | ↓ "coercion tripwires" |
| `string-only-method` | error | yes | `.trim`/`.toLowerCase`/`.startsWith`/`.replace`/… on a non-string (warn→error) | ↓ "coercion tripwires" |
| `number-only-method` | error | yes | `.toFixed`/`.toPrecision`/`.toExponential` on a non-number | ↓ "coercion tripwires" |
| `no-raw-storage-write` | error | yes | raw `localStorage`/`sessionStorage` `setItem`/`removeItem`/`clear` — use `lsSet`/`lsRemove` | `appStorage.ts` structure entry |
| `no-storage-read-after-remove` | error | yes | `removeItem(K)` then `getItem(K)` in one function (the OAuth read-before-clear bug) | § Security → "OAuth read-before-clear" |
| `no-hardcoded-lang-ternary` | error | yes¹ | `lang === "x" ? "UI text" : "UI text"` (two-language leak to es/de/it) | ↓ "guardrails" |
| `no-hardcoded-jsx-text` | error | yes¹ | bare JSX UI-text literals (`<span>Bonjour</span>`) | ↓ "guardrails" |
| `no-fs-in-input` | error | no | `fontSize: fs(...)` on a JSX `<input>`/`<textarea>` — use `fsInput()` (iOS zoom-on-focus floor) | `theme-curator.ts` `fs`/`fsInput` entry |
| `no-scrolling-focus` | error | yes¹ | a bare `.focus()` — must pass `{ preventScroll: true }`, since focus moves the viewport and none of this app's focus moves is a navigation the user asked for | ↓ "focus rule" |
| `no-dynamic-index-plain-map` | error | no | dynamic index into a module-level **string-keyed** plain-object lookup map (`M[userKey]` fall-through to `Object.prototype`) — build with `Object.assign(Object.create(null), {…})` | ↓ "prototype-safety rule" |
| `no-unscoped-lot-read` | error | n/a — ON for 2 files only | a `.lots` read in the two inventory views without a `// scope-ok: <reason>` acknowledgement | ↓ "lot-scope rule" |
| `no-raw-enum-render` | error | no | a bare enum field (`{item.category}`) rendered as JSX text instead of `xl(value, XXX_EN)` — silently shows French to es/de/it | ↓ "enum-render rule" |
| `no-hex-alpha-concat` | error | n/a — design-system scope | a 2-hex alpha concatenated onto a colour (`token + "22"`, `${token}22`, `${token}${c?"55":"25"}`, or via a local const) — the palette is `var()`, so it yields invalid CSS the browser drops SILENTLY | ↓ "hex-alpha rule" |
| `no-platform-breadcrumb-out-of-i18n` | warn | — | inline "Settings → X" / "Safari"/"Chrome" breadcrumbs outside i18n (invariant #21). **Does NOT fire on a `t ? t(k) : "fr fallback"` literal** — doc:check gate (b.2) pins that byte-identical to `fr[k]`, so it cannot drift | ↓ end of this section |

¹ off via the rule's own internal allow-list (tests + i18n dicts + rule files), not the per-folder override. The per-folder test override (`src/__tests__/**`) explicitly disables `string-only-method`, `number-only-method`, `no-raw-storage-write`, `no-storage-read-after-remove`; `string-locale-compare` stays on everywhere.

**And no border around the photo column either.** The last two lines of the polaroid frame, `borderRight` + `borderBottom` in `C.rule`. They read as a sensible photo/text separator only while the photo FILLED the column; under `contain` a wide photo (a churchwarden is ~3:1 against a 100×110 column, so ~30% of the height) leaves those two edges closing a mostly-empty box **in a colour distinct from the card**. Reported from the app. Removed on all four list cards; `listPhotoNoFrame.test.ts` now asserts the column carries no border at all. **Note what is NOT ours and cannot be fixed here**: with `contain`, an extreme aspect ratio leaves the PHOTO'S OWN studio background as a visible band (white, on a dark card). Nothing in this codebase draws it and no CSS can remove another image's ground — the only lever is cropping the image before import. That trade is the deliberate price of showing the object whole.

**A photo is shown WHOLE and never has a ground of its own (the settled rule).** One rule, seven surfaces: the four list cards (tobacco / wishlist / pipe / accessory) and the three detail heroes. `center/contain` + a transparent ground, so the whole object is visible and the card shows through the leftover area. **It took five passes because each one fixed half the rule.** One drew a deliberate "polaroid" frame (`contain` + 8px padding + a coloured ground); two more kept fixing the frame's COLOUR (`C.cream` inverted to near-black on parchment → a token that kept cream for dark → that token made white); a fourth finally asked whether the frame should exist and removed it — but did so with `center/cover`, which fills the box **by cropping**, so a tall tin or a long pipe could never be seen whole. Reported from the app with a cropped Cornell & Diehl tin. **The two halves must hold together: `contain` (whole object) AND no ground (no frame).** Asserting only one is exactly how this half-regressed four times, which is why `listPhotoNoFrame.test.ts` checks BOTH on all seven sites and not a colour — a colour assertion passed at every wrong step. It strips comments before matching (its first version failed on the comment explaining the fix) and is probed in both directions. Scope note: the small identifying thumbnails elsewhere (Home tiles, journal rows, search results, the extra-photo galleries) deliberately keep `cover` — a thumbnail identifies, it is not a viewer, and the galleries open a lightbox.

**No ground behind a list photo at all (this is the settled state).** The 12 px of pixels around a list-card photo was wrong three times: `C.cream` inverting to near-black on parchment, then a dedicated token that KEPT the historic cream for dark, then that token made white. All three answered the wrong question, and the user's asked the right one: *why is there a background on the list and none on the fiche?* Because **both declare one** — you never see the fiche's, since it uses `center/cover` and the photo covers it, while the list combined `center/contain` with an `8px` padding to draw a "polaroid" frame on purpose. That pass removes the frame: `cover` + no padding on all four cards (tobacco, wishlist, pipe, accessory), so the photo fills its 100×110 column and no colour is reachable. The `photoMatte` token is DELETED, not left dangling (knip is a gate since 36). The trade accepted knowingly: `cover` crops ~5 px each side of a square photo, which is what the fiche has always done. **Locked by `listPhotoNoFrame.test.ts`, which asserts the LAYOUT (cover + no conditional padding + no conditional background) and not a colour** — a colour assertion would have passed at all three wrong steps. It strips comments before matching, because its own first version failed on the comment explaining the fix.

**The photo matte, wrong twice in opposite directions.** Reported from the app with screenshots. The list cards letterbox a photo (`center/contain`, the "polaroid" intent) so the matte shows as a band around it; the FICHES use `center/cover`, where the photo fills the box and no matte is ever visible — which is why the two surfaces looked different and why only the lists can reveal a mistake here. An earlier fix corrected the light-mode half (`C.cream`, a TEXT token, mapped to near-black on parchment) but **deliberately preserved the historic cream for dark mode**, on the stated reasoning that "the validated dark look must not move by one byte". That reasoning was wrong: dark was also wrong. Most tin photos carry their own white studio background, so a cream band around a white photo reads as two mismatched whites, while the fiche already looked white. `photoMatte` is now **white in both modes** — the fallback for dark, an explicit `MODE_LIGHT` entry for light so the intent is visible in the table a reader would check. **Preserving an existing value is only conservative when that value was right**; "don't change what was validated" quietly assumes it was. Locked by `theme.test.ts`, probed against BOTH historical defects.

**The three blind spots a four-agent audit surfaced, and the one shape they share.** A parallel read-only audit (four lenses: tool coverage / cross-site consistency / theming / i18n-outside-JSX) produced ~22 findings, every one I re-verified turning out real. Three were systemic, and all three are the SAME shape as the `.jsx` and `prune` gaps: *a guard covers one channel, one folder, or one data path, and everything outside it is presumed clean because nothing looks at it.*

1. **THE GATES DID NOT EXIST.** `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` and `npm run prune` were in **no workflow at all** — CI ran only `npm test` / `build` / `doc:check` / `size:check`. Meanwhile CLAUDE.md called typecheck "the canonical CI gate", `dependabot.yml` called lint "a CI gate", and `eslint.config.js` said its error-level rules "block CI". So every `tabac-local/*` rule — written specifically to stop hardcoded French strings, raw enum renders and mode-blind colours reaching users — had **zero enforcement**: a commit with a `tsc` error or a French label merged and deployed green. Fixed by `.github/workflows/checks.yml` (typecheck + lint + prune, on `pull_request` as well as push, each step `if: !cancelled()` so one run surfaces every class). **If you promote a check to a gate, put it in a workflow in the same commit** — the local checklist is discipline, not enforcement.
2. **The design-system rules were not registered on the one module that is pure styling.** The `no-restricted-syntax` block (no-hex, the tinted-`rgba()` ban, `fontSize`→`fs()`) plus `no-raw-enum-render` were scoped to `src/components/curator/**` + `{ts,tsx}` — so `src/components/Charts.jsx` missed on BOTH axes (wrong folder, wrong extension) and had **never** been checked by them, while `StatsView`, which delegates its entire visual output to it, was fully covered. `main.jsx` and `App.tsx` were uncovered too, and App.tsx carried a live violation: the light page ground `#e7ddc6` hand-copied into the `theme-color` meta (that literal is CLAUDE.md's own reference ground for every computed light value). The glob now covers `src/components/**` + `App.tsx` + `main.jsx` with an explicit `ignores` for the two documented exemptions, and the meta tint is **derived** from `MODE_LIGHT` via `THEME_COLOR_META` so a light-ground retune carries the status bar with it. This is the `.jsx` config gap one layer deeper: those files DID match a config — just not the design-system one.
3. **Both browser checks only ever walked the happy path.** The fixture shared by `i18n:layout` and `theme:contrast` held no retired pipe, no retired accessory, no orphaned lot and no paused tasting — so **four of seven theming defects lived in states the checks could not render**, including a whole-card `opacity: 0.55` putting retired-card text at ~2.3:1 in all six theme×mode combos (below the 3:1 FAILURE floor, not merely a warning). Adding the data is not enough: both lists default to active-only, so the `pipes-retired` / `acc-retired` screens that tap the filter chip were added too. **When you add a state with its own rendering branch, add it to the fixture AND a screen that reaches it** — `i18nLayoutHarness.test.ts` now asserts both.

Two of that file's own guards were themselves hardcoded lists and broke on correct changes — the nav-key list did not see a new screen's keys, and the seeded-key check read five remembered files so it failed when a duplicated key was correctly centralised. Both now derive from the source (with non-vacuity assertions), and both were probed: a renamed nav key and a genuinely stale seed key still fail.

**A rule only protects the files ESLint actually reads.** Every config block in `eslint.config.js` was keyed on `**/*.{ts,tsx}`, so the two `.jsx` sources — `src/components/Charts.jsx` and `src/main.jsx` — **matched no block and were skipped entirely** ("File ignored because no matching configuration was supplied", visible only with `--no-warn-ignored`). Not one of the 11 custom rules, nor `no-hardcoded-jsx-text`, had ever run on the chart helpers: that is how `donutChart` shipped the hardcoded French centre caption "total actif", rendered verbatim in all five languages, and it never appeared in any report. A `files: ["src/**/*.{js,jsx}"]` block now brings them in scope; the first run flagged the two strings, two raw `localStorage.setItem` calls in `main.jsx` (→ `lsSet`) and three unused `catch (e)` bindings. **When you add a source file with a new extension, add it to a config block in the same commit** — and treat a lint report that has never mentioned a file as a claim to verify, not evidence of cleanliness.

**`scripts/` had the same gap, one level worse, and `npm run lint` is now `eslint src/ scripts/`.** The build/check scripts matched the recommended config but NO block declared the Node environment, so every `require` / `process` / `console` read as an undefined global: 310 problems, ~300 of them that noise — in a directory the lint target never even visited. Declaring the environment is what makes it lintable; the remaining 7 findings were all real and all fixed: two dead locals in `doc-check.cjs` left over from the extraction into `i18nChecks.cjs` (`identicalAllowed`, `HAS_LETTER` — the live copies are there), a dead accumulator in the xlsx exporter, a `no-regex-spaces` hit in the structure-tree parser (3 literal spaces → `{3}`; that regex is load-bearing, `depth = length / 4`), and a deliberate control-char strip that now carries an `eslint-disable` naming its reason (XLSX rejects those chars in a shared string). **Four `tabac-local` rules are OFF for `scripts/`, each for a stated reason** — the coercion tripwires and the prototype-safety rule guard against a SILENT crash or a forged key in a user's browser, whereas a build script throws in front of whoever ran it and only ever parses the repo's own files; and `no-raw-storage-write` fires on `localStorage.setItem` inside a Playwright `page.evaluate()` seed callback, whose body runs in the PAGE where `lsSet` does not exist. **The override block MUST stay after the main rules block** — flat config lets the last matching block win, and an earlier placement left every one of those overrides silently ineffective (caught only by re-running the probe, not by reading).

**Hardcoded-UI-string guardrails.** Two custom ESLint rules (both `"error"`) backstop the i18n sweep by blocking the two shapes of hardcoded, un-`t()`-ed UI text from re-entering `src/`:
- `tabac-local/no-hardcoded-lang-ternary` (`eslint-rules/no-hardcoded-lang-ternary.cjs`) — flags `lang === "code" ? "UI text" : "UI text"` ternaries whose branches read like user-facing text (whitespace or a Latin accent). A two-language ternary silently shows French/English to es/de/it. Allow-listed files: `src/i18n.ts`, `src/i18n/`, `src/hooks/useAiAutoFill.ts` (AI-prompt clauses are intentionally bilingual), tests, and the rule files. Self-test: `src/__tests__/eslint-no-hardcoded-lang-ternary.test.ts`.
- `tabac-local/no-hardcoded-jsx-text` (`eslint-rules/no-hardcoded-jsx-text.cjs`) — flags bare JSX text literals (`<span>Bonjour</span>`) that read like UI copy (a real 2+ letter word AND whitespace or accent). Single-symbol glyphs (`×` `—` `✕`) and `{t("…")}` expression containers are not flagged. Escape hatch for genuine version identifiers etc.: `{/* eslint-disable-next-line tabac-local/no-hardcoded-jsx-text -- reason */}` (used on the `v … · build N` version lines). Self-test: `src/__tests__/eslint-no-hardcoded-jsx-text.test.ts`. A runtime pseudo-loc DOM scan (Playwright) empirically confirmed zero leaks across home/inv/pipes/acc/journal/stats/add-form/settings before the rule shipped at `"error"`. UI text must go through `t("key")`; enum labels through `xl(value, XXX_EN)`.

**Runtime-safety coercion tripwires (all `"error"`).** Three custom ESLint rules block calling a type-specific method on a receiver the type system can't prove is the right primitive (these throw at runtime on a string/undefined/number-typed value):
- `tabac-local/string-locale-compare` (`eslint-rules/string-locale-compare.cjs`) — forbids `.localeCompare` on a non-`String()`-coerced receiver (caught a real crash). Stays on everywhere, including tests.
- `tabac-local/string-only-method` (`eslint-rules/string-only-method.cjs`) — the broader String-only-method family (`.trim`/`.toLowerCase`/`.startsWith`/…). **Promoted from `"warn"` to `"error"`** once the whole codebase was wrapped in `String(...)`; any NEW unsafe receiver now blocks CI. Escape hatch: `String(x)` at the call site, or a scoped `eslint-disable` (e.g. the `window.location.replace` case in `useGdriveAuth.ts`).
- `tabac-local/number-only-method` (`eslint-rules/number-only-method.cjs`) — companion for `.toFixed`/`.toPrecision`/`.toExponential`; wrap the receiver in `Number(...)`. The recognizer exempts arithmetic expressions / `Number()` / `Math.*` / `parseFloat` / numeric literals so the many `(a/b).toFixed()` sites aren't touched; `.toLocaleString` is deliberately excluded. `"error"` from the start.

`string-only-method` and `number-only-method` are disabled in the per-folder test override (tests operate on controlled fixtures); `string-locale-compare` stays on everywhere, including tests. Also `"warn"`: `tabac-local/no-platform-breadcrumb-out-of-i18n` (`eslint-rules/no-platform-breadcrumb-out-of-i18n.cjs`) — backstops the iOS/Android parity invariant #21 by flagging platform breadcrumbs ("Safari" / "Chrome" navigation paths) outside the i18n dicts + utils.ts allow-list.

**Prototype-safety rule (`"error"`).** `tabac-local/no-dynamic-index-plain-map` (`eslint-rules/no-dynamic-index-plain-map.cjs`) consolidates the finding class that audit rounds 8-12 kept surfacing ONE site at a time (`resolveCanonicalBrand`, `computeAgingSweetSpot` maps, `AccListView`/`AccessoryDetailView` `TYPE_COLORS`/`TYPE_ICONS`, `TrashModal` `KIND_*`, `THEMES`, `DOC_PAGES`, `toggleCollapseKey`…). It flags a DYNAMIC (non-literal) computed index `M[expr]` into a MODULE-LEVEL `const` plain-object lookup map whose KEY type is runtime-forgeable — `Record<string, …>`, `Record<any, …>`, a `{ [k: string]: … }` index-signature literal, or no annotation. On a plain object a key equal to a prototype member (`"__proto__"`, `"constructor"`, `"toString"`…) resolves to the value on `Object.prototype` — a truthy non-value that defeats the ubiquitous `M[key] || fallback` guard. The fix is a null-prototype map: `Object.assign(Object.create(null), { … })` (or `Object.create(null)` for a mutable one). **Deliberately NARROW to keep false positives ~0**: (1) module-scope `const` only (a local `{}` accumulator is a different animal); (2) the initializer must be a bare `ObjectExpression` — the null-proto forms + `new Map()` are recognised and skipped; (3) **closed-union-keyed maps are SKIPPED** — `Record<MaturityChipSize, …>` / `Record<IcoName, …>` / `Record<WatchKind, …>` can only be indexed by a value TypeScript already proves is in-set, so they're not prototype-forgeable AND wrapping them would also drop the object literal's exhaustiveness check (the rule reads the key type off the declarator's TS annotation to tell the two apart); (4) WRITE targets (`M[k] = v`) and `delete M[k]` are skipped. Escape hatch: `// eslint-disable-next-line tabac-local/no-dynamic-index-plain-map` for a map whose keys are a provably-closed safe set the rule can't see. Self-test: `src/__tests__/eslint-no-dynamic-index-plain-map.test.ts` (14 cases). **When you add a module-level lookup map indexed by a data-derived string, build it null-proto from the start** — the rule will otherwise block CI.

**NARROWING (1) — "a local `{}` accumulator is a different animal" — WAS WRONG FOR THE CASE THAT MATTERED, and it cost the harshest failure this app can produce.** `ghosting.ts` builds FOUR function-local accumulators, two keyed by `tobacco.id` and two by `tobacco.category`, and `migrateData` coerces a category to a string without ever validating it against `CATS` — so a JSON import or a cloud restore carries `category: "__proto__"` straight in. `counts[cat] = (counts[cat] || 0) + 1` then reads `Object.prototype` (TRUTHY, so `|| 0` never fires), writes through the `__proto__` SETTER (which ignores a non-object, so the key is never stored), and leaves `total` at 1 with `Object.keys(counts)` empty — `families[0].count` throws. **THAT THROW IS A BRICK, NOT A GLITCH**: `CuratorApp` mounts `CuratorPipesListView` unconditionally and its `pipeFamily` memo sits ABOVE the view's own early return (the hook-order rule REQUIRES it), so it fires on the first render after `data` loads **whatever screen the user is on**; `_runImport` calls `save()` before any render, so the row is already on disk; the error boundary replaces the whole tree, so Settings — and « Effacer toutes les données » — is unreachable; and **neither recovery path clears localStorage** (`EB.purgeCachesAndReload` and `public/reset.html` both stop at service workers and Cache Storage). The only way out is clearing site data or deleting the PWA, with the user's own cellar stranded. Verbatim the already-fixed `imageUrl: "__proto__"` brick, through a different key. **What identifies it as a MISSED SITE rather than an oversight of principle: `utils.ts` builds the same kind of tally with `Object.create(null)` and carries a comment describing this exact mechanism, and `prototypePollution.test.ts` covers five functions without ever importing `ghosting.ts`.** Locked by `ghostingPrototype.test.ts`; probed per map.

**Three more sites in the same class, and the CATALOGUE one is the reason the sweep was worth doing.** `CatalogView`'s brand grouping (`groups[bk].push` → `push is not a function` → the error boundary takes the whole app) and its `collapsed` map, both keyed by the catalogue's own `brand_key` — which `parseCatalogueCsv` keeps VERBATIM by design, correctly. The `collapsed` one is the quieter half and the more instructive: the read resolves to `Object.prototype` so `!== false` keeps the group shut, and `toggleGroup`'s write goes through the `__proto__` setter, so **the group can never be expanded however many times it is tapped** — a control that is not broken, merely inert, which is the hardest kind to report. Note `toggleGroup` had to rebuild onto `Object.create(null)` too: a bare `Object.assign({}, prev)` hands the prototype straight back. And `useExportImport`'s `tobMap`/`pipeMap`, keyed by entity id on the write and by `session.tobaccoId` on the READ: a forged id returns a FUNCTION, TypeScript cannot see it (the index is `any`), the CSV cell reads `function toString() { [native code] }` — **and it SHORT-CIRCUITS the snapshot fallback three lines below, which exists precisely so a session whose entity is gone still exports an identifiable label.** The export loses the very information that fallback was added to preserve.

**THE OTHER 23 CANDIDATES WERE JUDGED AND ARE INERT — recorded so the next sweep does not redo the reading.** A scan for a local `{}` written through a dynamic key found 27 sites. The three StatsView `catByTob` maps and `PipesListView`'s `pipeFamily` feed a `Set` and then `CATS.filter(c => present.has(c))`, or compare with `===`, so a prototype member is simply never in the enum; `SettingsModal`'s `tobById`/`pipeById` read `.brand`/`.name` off the result, which are `undefined` on a function, so the label degrades to `""` exactly as a genuine miss does; `sanitizeAromas`' `seen` is gated by `isValidAroma` on the write and read back over the fixed `ALL_AROMAS`; the two `byDay` heat-map tallies are keyed by a date string and read back only at real day keys, so a forged date costs at most one unit of `total`. **The pattern that separates the dangerous four from the inert 23 is worth stating: a map is dangerous when the value it returns is USED — dereferenced, arithmetic'd, or returned as a label — rather than merely COMPARED against a closed set.** Extending the ESLint rule to function-local maps was considered and is the obvious next step; it would demand 23 free but noisy edits, so it is deliberately left as its own change rather than folded into a fix for a live brick.

**Hex-alpha rule (`"error"`).** `tabac-local/no-hex-alpha-concat` (`eslint-rules/no-hex-alpha-concat.cjs`) forbids concatenating a 2-hex-digit alpha suffix onto a colour. Before theming, `C.brass + "22"` produced a valid 8-digit hex; varizing the palette turned the token into `var(--c-brass, #d4a661)`, so the same expression now yields `var(--c-brass, #d4a661)22` — **not a colour, and browsers drop an invalid declaration silently**, leaving no background / no border and no error anywhere. The replacement is `alpha(token, "22")`. **Why it needed a rule and not more discipline**: the migration swept this class, CLAUDE.md documented it in two places, and a later audit agent explicitly CLEARED the category — and five live sites were still shipping (MaturityChip background + `sm` border, AICard card + button borders, AgingBadge background + border). Each survived because every sweep grepped ONE spelling; the shapes actually in the wild were `token + "22"`, `token + (c ? "22" : "1c")`, `` `${token}22` ``, `` `${token}${c ? "55" : "25"}` `` (split across two interpolations — invisible to a `${C.x}AA` grep, which is why it lived longest) and `colour + someLocalConst`. MEASURED in Chromium before the fix: every maturity chip rendered at `backgroundColor: rgba(0,0,0,0)`. The rule is **positional, not value-based** — it asks whether a 2-hex string sits in a concatenation slot, and deliberately does NOT judge whether the receiver "looks like a colour" (that judgement is what the greps got wrong). It resolves a local `const` to its initializer, because the AgingBadge instance hid behind exactly that indirection and a literal-only first version stayed green on it. Scoped to the design-system files (same set as the no-hex / no-raw-fontSize selectors). Self-test: `src/__tests__/eslint-no-hex-alpha-concat.test.ts` (21 cases; all five real shapes pinned as invalid fixtures, plus `${x}ffset` as a valid one so the word-boundary guard can't be dropped). `MaturityChip.test.tsx` carries a runtime counterpart asserting the rendered `background` is a `color-mix()`.

**Focus rule (`"error"`).** `tabac-local/no-scrolling-focus` (`eslint-rules/no-scrolling-focus.cjs`) requires `{ preventScroll: true }` on every `.focus()`. **Why it needs a rule and not discipline: the defect is invisible in BOTH engines this repo can run.** jsdom does not lay out or scroll at all; and Chromium focuses a `div[tabindex=0]` on tap — so a focus restore lands back on the row — and treats `document.body.focus()` as a no-op. **iOS Safari does neither**: it does not focus non-form elements on tap, so `Modal`'s recorded "last active" element is `<body>` there. A bare `.focus()` can therefore be added, measured green in every harness available here, and still lose the user's place — which is exactly how one half of a two-part report came to be declared sound on the strength of a Chromium run. Flags a member call ending in `.focus` with no argument, or with an object argument lacking `preventScroll: true` (an options object that says nothing is the shape a half-applied fix leaves behind; `preventScroll: false` is flagged too, so asking to scroll gets a reason attached via the disable comment). A variable or spread argument is ACCEPTED — the rule cannot see inside it and guessing produces the false positives that get guards switched off. **OFF in `src/__tests__/**` and `scripts/**`**: a `.focus()` there SIMULATES what the browser does when a user taps or tabs, and the browser scrolls, so opting out would model something that never happens. Self-test: `src/__tests__/eslint-no-scrolling-focus.test.ts` (19 cases, incl. the wiring and both exemptions). **Its first run flagged 13 sites, every one in tests or scripts and none in production** — the rule confirming the sweep was complete.

**Lot-scope rule (`"error"`, two files only).** `tabac-local/no-unscoped-lot-read` (`eslint-rules/no-unscoped-lot-read.cjs`) flags EVERY `.lots` read in `InventoryListView.tsx` + `InventoryDetailView.tsx` unless it carries a `// scope-ok: <reason>` comment. **Why a rule at all**: when the list is filtered to a lot-level slice, every figure on the card and the fiche must describe the lots in that scope — that leak was fixed seven times and the final systematic sweep still found five more sites, two of them SORT ORDERS (invisible as text, so unreachable by fixing what the user could see). The discipline was then written into CLAUDE.md as prose, which is exactly the state in which the five leaks existed: nothing enforced it. **It is deliberately dumb — an ACKNOWLEDGEMENT rule, not a correctness rule.** It makes no attempt to judge whether a given read is correctly scoped: that judgement is the thing a human keeps getting wrong, and a clever rule that guessed would either miss the interesting cases or force correct code to be rewritten to please it (an over-strict guard is worse than none, because it gets correct work deleted). Same philosophy as the label contracts: force a conscious re-read at the moment someone touches lot-derived data. **The annotation attaches to the ENCLOSING STATEMENT** (the comment block directly above it, or a trailing comment on the read's own line), NOT a line window — the first version matched within 3 lines and a probe (inject a leak into the real view, expect red) showed a new unscoped read placed right below an annotated one silently inheriting its license. One statement, one acknowledgement; a contiguous run of `//` lines is one annotation so a long reason needs no reflowing. Writes (`tob.lots = …`, `delete`) and object-literal keys are skipped; computed `tob["lots"]` is flagged. Self-test: `src/__tests__/eslint-no-unscoped-lot-read.test.ts` (15 cases, incl. that false-negative case and an assertion that the rule stays WIRED to both views and isn't file-disabled). **Eight reads are annotated today** — the chip counts (they label the filter chips themselves, so they must see every lot), the two `scopedLots` scope routes, the deliberately-unscoped `nFinished` / `finishedCount` (both consumers are gated on there being no scope), the lot list (`visibleLots`, whose second filter IS the scope), and the raw `indexOf` the store mutations key on. **When you add a figure to either view, route it through `lotInScope` / `scopedHeldWeight` / `scopedOldestAgeDays` — or say in one line why it doesn't need to.**

**Enum-render rule (`"error"`).** `tabac-local/no-raw-enum-render` (`eslint-rules/no-raw-enum-render.cjs`) enforces the enum DISPLAY invariant (see that section) in the Curator source: a bare `{item.category}` rendered as JSX TEXT is flagged; it must go through `xl(value, XXX_EN)`. **Why it needs a rule**: the stored value is canonical FRENCH, and it usually reads fine in English too (`Ribbon`, `Flake`, `Billiard`), so the leak is INVISIBLE to anyone testing in fr or en while showing French to es/de/it — which is how SIX sites shipped at once (tobacco card + detail category·cut, Home featured tobacco and pipe, pipe-detail shape header, accessory-card fuel, every SearchModal subtitle). Every current site is correct, so it ships at error level. **The rule asks "is this value rendered as text?" and every step of the walk from the read to the JSX container must be a rendered position** — that inversion is what stopped it misfiring: a CallExpression ARGUMENT is never rendered (the call's RESULT is), which silences `xl(v, CATS_EN)`, the local alias `tr(v, SHAPES_EN)` in `PipesDetailView`, and the colour lookups `catColor(fam.category)` in ONE rule instead of three hand-written excuses — an excuse-list version flagged two of them wrongly. Skipped: JSX **attributes** (`<SelectField value={form.category}>` MUST pass the canonical value or the option stops matching and the save breaks; `key=` wants identity), the left operand of `&&` (a guard — but NOT of `||`/`??`, where the left IS what renders: `{tob.cut || "—"}` is flagged), a conditional's test, statements inside a `.map()` callback (only its returned value renders), and the `{xl ? xl(v, X_EN) : v}` dev-fallback idiom. Caught: the bare read, both halves of `{cat} · {cut}`, template literals, a HALF-translated line (`{xl(p.shape, SHAPES_EN)} · {p.finish}`), and `map(f => f.category)`. Verified by re-injecting two of the real leaks into `AccListView` and `PipesDetailView` and confirming both go red. Self-test: `src/__tests__/eslint-no-raw-enum-render.test.ts` (22 cases, incl. the two false positives as permanent fixtures + a check that the field list covers every translated enum). **When you add a translated enum to `ENUM_TRANSLATIONS`, add its field name to `ENUM_FIELDS` in the rule** — a field missing there is silently unguarded.

|------------|----------|---------------------|
| Inline tinted "notice" banners → shared `<Notice>` primitive | `src/components/curator/Notice.tsx` | 10 sites: aging warning, cellar advisories (SessionFormView + TastingView), duplicate banners (TobaccoFormView + WishFormView), AICard error, orphan-lot warning, TrashModal summary, SettingsModal status |

**Anti-regression coverage** (added after the sweep): `src/__tests__/curator/{Notice,ModalAction,FilterControls}.test.tsx` (+ `MaturityChip.test.tsx`; the AgingBadge suite retired with the component) — snapshots that lock the rendered output of every primitive so a future refactor of the size/tone tables can't silently desync the design system.

**When extending the design system**: prefer adding a new variant to an existing primitive over re-rolling an inline style block. The migration history above shows that every inline copy drifted: ten different "tinted banner" implementations existed before the extraction. Promote early — three similar sites is already enough to extract.
