### Clickable Stats — drill-down to filtered lists

Every chart and aggregate on the Statistics page is a one-tap entry point into its source list. The wiring lives in three layers:

**1. App-level state.** Three journal filters were lifted out of where they used to live in `JournalView`'s `useState` into `App.tsx` ctx so any view can pre-select them: `journalFilterPipe`, `journalFilterTobacco`, `journalFilterYear` + their setters. A fourth was added: `journalFilterDate` (ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`) for day-precise filtering from the calendar heatmap. Two more followed: `journalFilterCommune` / `journalFilterCountry` for the "Lieux" (location) stats click-thru. Two new pipe filters cover the bowl / stem material click-thrus: `pBowlMaterialFilter`, `pStemMaterialFilter`. All are reset on `nav()` like every other list filter.

**2. Navigation helpers** (App.tsx, mirror the existing `navToInvFiltered` / `navToPipesFiltered` shape — clear shadowing filters, set the targets, jump via `setView` not `nav()` so the new filter doesn't get wiped on the way):

- `navToPipesFilteredByMaterial(material, kind)` where `kind` is `"bowl" | "stem"`.
- `navToJournalFiltered(year, pipeId?, tobaccoId?)` for the year-level click-thru (monthly / yearly histograms — month label `"YYYY-MM"` is sliced to `"YYYY"` at the StatsView call site). Clears `journalFilterDate` so the two don't fight.
- `navToJournalFilteredByDate(date)` for the day-level click-thru from the calendar heatmap. Clears `journalFilterYear` (the date already implies the year) so the active-filter chip row stays uncluttered.
- `navToJournalFilteredByLocation(kind, value)` for the "Lieux" stats click-thru, `kind` ∈ `"commune" | "country"`. Sets just the chosen location filter and clears every other journal filter for a clean drill-down. JournalView surfaces each active location filter as a removable 📍 chip and AND-composes them in its session memo (strict `String(s.locationCity)` / `String(s.locationCountry)` equality). The "Lieux" section sits under the smoking-calendar heatmap in StatsView (it's session-derived).

**3. StatsView wiring** (`src/views/curator/StatsView.tsx`). Every clickable bar / cell carries an `item.onClick` callback (the chart primitives in `Charts.jsx` already supported this — no architectural change). The heatmap info line under the calendar transforms into a tappable button (`DD.MM.YYYY · N séances →`) when `calSel.count > 0`, calling `navToJournalFilteredByDate(calSel.date)`. Hover polish on `hBars` (Charts.jsx): the bar opacity bumps 0.88 → 1.0 on hover via inline `onMouseEnter/Leave` + a `data-hbar` selector; the label color already brightens tx2 → ivory for clickable rows (that predates this pass). Pure inline-style implementation, no CSS file.

**Year / date exclusivity invariant.** The journal's date and year filters are mutually exclusive on entry — setting one through the helper clears the other. JournalView's `sessions` memo still AND-composes both (so if a state-machine bug lets both through, the more restrictive wins) but the helpers enforce the cleaner UX. The Date chip surfaces at the very top of the JournalView (above the three regular dropdowns) so the user clearly sees it's the narrowest active filter.

**Tests.** `src/__tests__/statsClickthru.test.ts` locks the material AND-filter contract + the `"YYYY-MM" → "YYYY"` slice rule + the strict day-equality filter rule. `src/__tests__/curator/JournalView.test.tsx` was adapted with a stateful wrapper so `fireEvent.change`-driven assertions still work after the ctx-driven refactor (renderWithCtx doesn't run App.tsx so setters need real React useState behind them).

### Strict-TS promoted to main

The two strict flags — `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` and `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` — are now part of the main `tsconfig.json`. Background:

- `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` — `prop?: T` is distinct from `prop: T | undefined`. Catches code that spreads `undefined` into a field documented as optional.
- `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` — `arr[i]` and `record[key]` return `T | undefined` instead of `T`. Forces explicit handling of out-of-bounds / missing-key cases.

**History:** introduced as an opt-in (`tsconfig.strict.json`) with ~240 errors. Migrated incrementally — utils.ts, then App.tsx + InventoryListView, then useGdriveSync + useAiAutoFill + JournalView, then the full src/ production sweep (24 → 0), and finally the test files (168 → 0 via mostly `mock.calls[N]![M]` non-null assertions on RTL queries and Vitest mock state). The opt-in tsconfig and its `:strict` npm script were deleted — the main `npm run typecheck` is now the strict gate.

**For new code:** the patterns to internalize are
- `arr[i]` is `T | undefined` — capture with `const item = arr[i]; if (!item) return …;` OR assert with `arr[i]!` when the bound is provably satisfied.
- `prop?: T` in an interface means "may be absent OR `T`, NOT `undefined`". Don't pass `cb ?? undefined` to a `?:` prop — use conditional spread `...(cb ? { cb } : {})` or change the interface to `prop?: T | undefined` if the caller pattern requires it.

### Dead code discipline

`tsconfig.json` runs with `noUnusedLocals` + `noUnusedParameters`. Any local, parameter, or destructured field you stop using **must be removed in the same commit** — the typecheck refuses commits otherwise. This rule extends to:
- `import { x }` lines where `x` is no longer referenced.
- React state pairs `const [x, setX] = useState(...)` where neither side is read or both are dead.
- Destructured ctx vars (`const { x } = useAppCtx()`) where `x` is no longer used in the component.
- i18n keys in `src/i18n.ts` that no caller passes to `t("...")`.
- Functions/components/types exported but with zero call sites (verify with grep before deleting).

If you touch a file for an unrelated reason and notice obvious dead code, remove it in the same commit. Don't grow the dead-code backlog.

### changelog.html rules

- **NO CATALOGUE REFERENCES.** The changelog carried ~40 bullets about the catalogue across every language section — how many blends it held (1000 → 1160 → 1215 → 1225 → 1371), which families had been rechecked, where its buttons had moved. Every one of those became FALSE when the app stopped shipping a catalogue: a reader scrolling the history was told about a reference base they do not have. Removed on the user's instruction, and the rule stands: **do not announce the catalogue in the changelog.** Eleven entries were deleted outright, nine kept their other bullets and lost the catalogue ones, four were RETITLED (their heading named the catalogue beside a feature the entry still announces — pipe rest, wishlist sorting, geolocated sessions, the AI model refresh), and seven bullets were reworded. Three of those seven were FALSE POSITIVES worth knowing about: v1.1/1 and v1.2/5 used « Catalogue » as the OLD NAME OF THE INVENTORY TAB (they now say « Inventaire », which is also the accurate word), and v1.5/16's « les catalogues des fournisseurs » meant the AI vendors' model line-ups. Verified afterwards: zero lines matching `catalog|catálog|katalog` in any section, and all six sections lost exactly 40 `<li>`.
- **Five language sections** — `public/changelog.html` has one section per UI language: `<div id="sec-fr">` / `<div id="sec-en">` / `<div id="sec-es">` / `<div id="sec-de">` / `<div id="sec-it">`, with a language toggle button identical to `help.html`. Every entry must appear in **all five** sections. (`doc:check` enforces only the `sec-fr` latest-build number, but the other four must stay in lock-step by convention.)
- **Features and important changes only** — include new features, new settings, significant UX improvements, and important behaviour changes (e.g. update mechanism changes). **Never include simple bug fixes** (display glitches, field resets, minor text corrections, etc.). **This is now a `doc:check` gate (12), because prose alone did not hold it.** **15 of the 25 entries** in the current version's section broke the rule and were deleted: photo framing, light-mode contrast, tap targets, bundle size, and six entries literally sub-titled `Correction`. Three patterns produced them, and they are the ones to watch for. **(a) The changelog was used as a build log, reverts included** — five consecutive entries were about the same photo frame, each undoing the last, so a user reading top-to-bottom watched an internal debate; another five do the same for light-mode contrast. *An iteration series is one decision, and usually one the user should not have to witness.* **(b) Audit-tool output was mistaken for UX work** — `theme:contrast` and `i18n:layout` phrase their findings in user language ("unreadable", "clipped"), and the diffs touch visible surfaces, so a contrast retune FEELS announceable. It is not: the user never noticed the old value and cannot act on the new one. **A build whose origin is a checker finding defaults to NO entry.** **(c) The checklist read as one-entry-per-build** while the exception lived two sections away — step 4 above now says the opposite first. The gate itself (`docChecks.checkChangelogIsFunctional`, tested in `docChecks.test.ts`) is deliberately split by certainty: a self-declared fix heading FAILS (the entry has already classified itself, no judgement needed), while display/implementation vocabulary only WARNS and needs two distinct terms — a real feature can legitimately mention colour, and an over-strict guard gets correct prose deleted. **When it fails, delete the entry — do not reword the heading.** In practice: `doc:check` enforces this by ALLOWING the latest changelog entry to lag behind `APP_BUILD` — a fix-only bump should leave the changelog untouched. The check still fails if the latest entry's build number is *higher* than `APP_BUILD` (no time travel).
- **Structure** — each build entry uses `<h2><span class="tag">vX.Y · Build N</span> Title <span class="date">Month YYYY</span></h2>` with `<h3>` sub-heading (Nouveau / New feature, Amélioration / Improvement, Important) and a `<ul>` of bullet points.
- **Version prefix in the tag (mandatory)** — the `class="tag"` chip MUST read `vX.Y · Build N` (the minor version, then `·`, then the build), NOT a bare `Build N`. Build numbers **reset to 1 at every minor version** (each minor version has its own second build…), so a bare `Build N` is ambiguous once the changelog spans several versions. The version prefix disambiguates at a glance. Do NOT repeat the version again inside the title text (the old `Build 1</span> v1.3 — Title` shape is retired — the first build of a version reads `<span class="tag">vX.Y · Build 1</span> Title`, version only in the tag). `doc:check` parses the latest build number with `/(?:v[\d.]+ · )?Build (\d+)/` so the prefix is tolerated but the `vX.Y · ` form is the required convention for new entries.

### End-of-task proactive suggestions

After every significant task (bug fix, feature, security change, release), always close with a short **"Et ensuite ?"** paragraph proposing the natural next layer: security, maintainability, monitoring, documentation, or UX. Keep it to 2–4 bullet points maximum. The user decides whether to act on any of them — the goal is to surface what a senior engineer would think of next, not to impose extra work.

### Git conventions
- **Always push to `main`** — all commits go directly to the `main` branch.
- Commits: brief English messages describing what changed.
- Main branch: `main`
- **NEVER put a `Claude-Session:` URL in a commit message.** The default
  convention appends one; on this repo it must be dropped. It is a link into a
  private tooling session published in the history of a PUBLIC repository, it
  is useless to every reader of that history, and it cannot be taken back once
  pushed — a rewrite leaves the old commit reachable by SHA. `Co-Authored-By`
  stays; it names an author, which is what a trailer is for. Set by the user,
  standing: *« enlève l'url et ne remets jamais ceci — pas utile »*.

## Key Conventions for AI Assistants

1. **Multi-file architecture** — Code is organized across `src/views/curator/` (~29 views + overlays), `src/hooks/` (21 hooks), `src/utils/` (`lotUtils`, `imgCache`, `lotInvariants`, `diagnostic`, `cryptoBackup`, `oauthDiag`, `oauthReturn`, `stats`, `gdriveApi`, `cloudProvider`, `dropboxAuthCore`, `rotation`, `suggest`, `watchlist`, `geo`, `tobaccoDb`, `docPage`), `src/components/Charts.jsx`, and `src/components/curator/` (icons, primitives, FormFields, Modal, BottomDock, AICard). `App.tsx` is the state + hooks owner and renders `<CuratorApp />`; it delegates all business logic to hooks. Do not add code to App.tsx that belongs in a hook.
2. **TypeScript strict mode** — `tsconfig.json` has `"strict": true`. All new code must be type-safe. Use `any` sparingly and only for genuinely dynamic values (context, external APIs, schema migrations on imported data).
3. **Build tools** — Vite + npm. Run `npm run dev` to develop, `npm run build` to produce `dist/`. No CDN dependencies in source; all imports go through npm.
4. **READ THE EXIT CODE OF EVERY GATE — never a piped summary.** This rule already existed for vitest (« a run can be GREEN and still exit 1 ») and the general form was learned the hard way: build 46 was pushed with a commit message asserting « Gates: typecheck, … » while `tsc` was **failing on four `TS18047` errors in a test file added after the last typecheck run**. Two mistakes compounded. (a) A gate was run BEFORE the last file was written and not re-run — the sweep must come after the final edit, always. (b) The habit of `npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | head -3; echo TSC_OK` and `npx knip 2>&1 | tail -1` **discards the exit code**: a pipeline reports the status of its LAST command, so `head`/`tail` returns 0 whatever the gate did, and `echo OK` then prints unconditionally. That is how a red gate read as green locally and the deploy died on `main`. It also sent the first diagnosis to the wrong gate entirely (knip, whose step merely ran after the failure). Run each gate bare, or redirect to a file and echo `$?` — `set -o pipefail` if a pipe is unavoidable. **A claim about a gate is only true if its exit code was seen.**

5. **ESLint** — Run `npm run lint` before committing. **Zero errors required.** **Read the whole summary, not `| tail -1`** — that truncation is how two releases shipped a `no-undef` and had their DEPLOY blocked by the gate (which is the gate working; missing it locally was not). `npx eslint . | grep -cE "  error  "` answers the only question that matters.

   **The warning budget: 7, all `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps`, all deliberate.** It was 20, then 9. Nine were **dead `eslint-disable` directives** — a suppression that no longer suppresses anything is worse than none, because the next edit to that hook gets its real dep problem silently swallowed; they were read one at a time and removed. **Do NOT run `eslint --fix` on them**: one of the nine (`useAppUpdate.ts`) was not dead but MISPLACED — `disable-next-line` sat above a comment block instead of the dep array 15 lines below, so it disabled a comment while the warning it was written for stayed live, showing up as two unrelated notes at opposite ends of the file. `--fix` would have deleted it and left the warning. Moving it removed two warnings at once.

   **Two more went when the LOT modal was taught to report itself.** `PipesDetailView`'s twin effect had been written `[!!maintForm, setMaintFormOpen]` and drew TWO warnings at once — a missing dep and "a complex expression in the dependency array" — and copying that shape for the lot modal would have made it four. Hoisting the boolean to a named `const` above the effect satisfies the rule exactly (the dep becomes statically checkable) while keeping the behaviour the inline `!!` was there for: fire on OPEN/CLOSE, never on a keystroke inside the modal. **When an effect keys on "is this modal open", name the boolean** — the inline coercion buys nothing and costs two warnings.

   **The remaining 7 are judgements and must stay warnings.** Each is a dep deliberately omitted (`Modal`, `useSessionStore`, `useStartupNotice`, `useStorageQuotaWarning`, `DocPageView`, `InventoryListView`, `PipesListView`). Adding what the rule asks for is exactly the change this file documents as the **prefill-race trap** — an effect that writes a user-editable field must NOT list that field, or clearing it to type re-fires the effect and snaps the value back, and the user reports "I can't change this field". Blanket-fixing them trades a clean count for real bugs.
6. **Test suite** — `npm test` runs ~5424 tests across 277 source test files with Vitest (re-measured; `doc:check` warns when they drift past ±20 % cases / ±10 % files). **A run can be GREEN and still exit 1** — see `src/__tests__/drainScheduler.ts` for the one way that happens and the hook that closes it; read the exit code, not the summary (incl. fast-check property tests on lot lifecycle). All tests must pass before committing. Add tests for new view components using `renderWithCtx()` from `src/__tests__/viewTestUtils.tsx`. Automated a11y smoke tests run via `jest-axe` in `src/__tests__/a11y.curator.test.tsx` — they catch missing labels, removed focus rings, missing modal ARIA, etc.
7. **Inline styles** — The project uses CSS-in-JS (inline `style` props). Do not add CSS files or CSS-in-JS libraries. Colors come from `src/theme-curator.ts` via the `C.*` tokens; fonts from `F.*`. Never reach for hardcoded hex values in views.
8. **French language** — UI strings, labels, and AI prompts are in French. Keep new UI text in French. Add each key to EVERY dictionary in `src/i18n/` (`fr,en,es,de,it,pt` today — aggregated as `LANG` by `src/i18n.ts`); `doc:check` AUTO-DISCOVERS them and enforces parity against `fr`, so fr+en only fails CI.
9. **localStorage schema** — The key `pipe-cellar-v6` must remain stable. If a schema change is needed, migrate data in `load()` and bump the version suffix.
10. **Service worker cache** — Bump `APP_BUILD` in `src/constants.ts` on every build, **and** update `public/version.json` to match (used by `checkVersion()` for update detection). Bump `cave-tabac-vXXX` in `public/sw.js` **ONLY** when icons (`*.png`) change, or when SW logic in `sw.js` itself changes — **not** for `manifest.json` (see the CACHE_NAME section: `doUpdate()`'s unconditional purge delivers it without an SW churn). **NEVER bump `sw.js` for `src/` or `.html` file changes.**
11. **API keys** — Never hardcode API keys. Keys are entered by the user and stored per-provider in `localStorage` under `anthropic-api-key`, `openai-api-key`, and `gemini-api-key`. By default they are **excluded** from exports and Drive backups (opt-out model); set `cave-exclude-apikey=0` to include them.
12. **Image storage** — `handlePhotoUpload` always stores base64 in IndexedDB under `local-photo-{timestamp}` and sets `imageUrl` to that key. Never store raw base64 in `imageUrl`. All export functions resolve these keys via `withPhotos()`/`gatherLocalImages()` before writing output. IndexedDB (`imgCache`) holds both local photos and URL-fetched image cache. Always call `isSafeExternalUrl(url)` before any proxy fetch.
13. **Lot lifecycle** — Lots always flow `cellar → jar → finished` (one direction only); reactivation goes back to `cellar` or `jar`. Both `changeLotStatus` and `updateLotInTobacco` auto-fill `dateOpened` on `jar` and `dateFinished` on `finished`. `changeLotStatus` always clears `dateFinished` when going to a non-finished status. When reactivating a 0g finished lot via the Réactiver button, the form is pre-filled with the target derived from **`originalStatus`** (`originalStatus === "jar" ? "jar" : "cellar"`) — **Round-15 lifecycle MED-1: the SAME rule as the weightG>0 branch, NOT `!!dateOpened`. A legacy finished lot that migrateData stamped `originalStatus:"jar"` (finished with no dateOpened) used to land in `status:"cellar"`+`originalStatus:"jar"`, an impossible state that trips the `cellar-not-jar-origin` invariant; the two Réactiver branches now agree.** When the target is jar, `dateOpened` defaults to today in the prefill (invariant #4). **Round-15 lifecycle MED-2: `applyLifecycleDates` clears `disposed:false` on the manual JAR branch too (not just cellar) — a jar lot is active and can't be "disposed"; a manual reactivate-to-jar used to leak `disposed:true` onto an active lot.** When `status === "finished"`, the edit form shows a **✓ Consommé / 🚮 Éliminé** toggle (field `disposed`). `disposed: true` excludes the lot from the **Lots finis** counter only; sessions logged against that lot before disposal still count in the monthly consumption chart (they were genuinely smoked at the time). **Auto-revert removed**: `applyLotWeightDelta` used to auto-revert a jar lot to cellar when a positive delta (session edit/delete) brought its weight back to `weightInitial` AND `originalStatus === "cellar"`. In practice the migration heuristic infers `originalStatus = "cellar"` for almost every legacy jar lot (any jar with a `dateOpened`, i.e. effectively all of them), so deleting a session silently demoted an opened pot back into the sealed cellar. The product invariant is now: **an opened jar NEVER auto-reverts to cellar**. `stepCellarRevert` and its tests were removed. The user can still flip the status manually from the lot edit modal. Auto-reactivation of a finished lot whose weight comes back to >0 still fires (finished → jar via `stepAutoReactivate`) — **EXCEPT for a `disposed` lot: a lot the user physically threw/gave away NEVER auto-reactivates on a session delete/edit that credits weight back; it stays finished+disposed (weight restored, shown only under "Éliminés", never counted as usable stock). A finished-but-not-disposed lot still reactivates. This supersedes the earlier "reactivate + clear disposed" behaviour — not reactivating a finished lot means it's never held stock, which also resolves that behaviour's double-count concern. Round-13 weight/lot MED-1.** **Initial weight bookkeeping**: every lot still carries a `weightInitial` field plus an `originalStatus` ("cellar" | "jar"). They're now purely informational — `weightInitial` powers the LotRow "/ Xg initial" annotation when it differs from current; `originalStatus` is kept for future migrations / analytics but no longer drives any status transition. **Same-lot edit** in `updateSession` still collapses the restore+deduct into a single net delta — the rationale shifted from "avoid spurious revert" to "the intermediate balance is meaningless and the cap is cleaner" but the code shape is unchanged. `weightInitial` and `originalStatus` are surfaced in the UI only in `LotFormModal` (input + segmented field, edit mode only for `originalStatus`) and `LotRow`. `LotFormModal` hides the `weightG` field at creation — only `weightInitial` is shown and `weightG` is mirrored at save; the status picker mirrors into `originalStatus` only when `!isEdit` so a later status flip in edit mode doesn't silently rewrite history. Existing data is migrated by `migrateData` (utils.ts) — `weightInitial = weightG` for every legacy lot; `originalStatus` is inferred from current status + dateOpened presence (jar/finished without an opening date → "jar"; everything else → "cellar"). CSV export includes both columns; JSON/Drive backups carry the fields verbatim. **Runtime invariants**: `src/utils/lotInvariants.ts` exports `checkLotInvariants`, `checkSessionInvariants`, `checkPipeInvariants`, `checkAccessoryInvariants`, and the combined `checkAllInvariants` + `assertLotInvariants`. The assertion is called from `save()` (App.tsx) on every persist; violations are routed to `src/utils/diagnostic.ts` which keeps a persisted counter + last-20 trail in `localStorage["cave-diagnostic-v1"]`. Surfaced in Settings → Diagnostic section (sage when clean, oxblood when violations exist) with **Copy / Download / Clear** action buttons. **Auto-repair removed**: the previous "Réparer auto." button and its `src/utils/dataRepair.ts` helper were removed entirely. They operated on `liveData` (which already filters trashed rows), so a save() of the repaired payload could wipe the trash without warning. The helper also re-cleared session `tobaccoId` / `pipeId` / `lotId` in direct violation of the immutable-sessions policy. Diagnostic now is inspection-only. A **threshold toast** (`CuratorDiagnosticToast` in `Overlays.tsx`) was historically mounted as a fixed bottom banner but **was removed from the UI** (the user found it noisy); the component is still in the file for the existing tests but is no longer rendered by `CuratorOverlays`. The Settings → Diagnostic section still surfaces the counter + last 20 violations for power-user inspection. The session orphan rule `session.lotId === "" || lot exists` is locked by both a unit test and a fast-check property test (`src/__tests__/lotLifecycle.property.test.ts`).
14. **Always verify changes** — After editing source files, run `npm run typecheck` to confirm the change is type-safe. Run `npm run build` to confirm it compiles. Merge conflicts can silently revert edits.
15. **Auto-update with countdown** — When `checkVersion()` detects a new build, `useAppUpdate` starts a 10-second countdown (`autoUpdateCountdown`) and then calls `doUpdate()` automatically. A fixed amber banner shows the countdown with a "Plus tard" button that calls `cancelAutoUpdate()` and stops the timer (the update pill in Settings remains available). `self.clients.claim()` must remain absent from `public/sw.js` (prevents mid-session SW takeover). **`reg.update()` must NEVER appear in timers or event handlers** — it silently installs a waiting SW the browser then activates on next open. Use `checkVersion()` (version.json fetch) for version detection only.
16. **Weight unit setting** — The global `weightUnit` React state (`"g"` or `"oz"`, stored in `localStorage` key `cave-weight-unit`) controls all weight label suffixes throughout the app. It is a **display-only preference**: stored values are NOT converted — only the suffix label changes. Never hardcode `+"g"` in display code; always use `+weightUnit`. Applies to tobacco lot weights AND pipe physical weight. The setting is toggled in ⚙️ Settings → Préférences. When the unit changes, `saveWeightUnit` also converts the two unit-scoped stored weights (`sessDefaultWeight` + `watchLowWeight`). **Round-15 HIGH: that conversion goes through the pure `convertWeightUnit(raw, fromUnit, toUnit)` (utils.ts) — do NOT reintroduce an inline `parseFloat(x) || N` + 1-dp-oz version.** The old inline code corrupted small values: a `|| N` fallback replaced a legit small/zero value, and 1-dp oz rounding collapsed anything < 1.4 g to `"0"`, so a 1 g default became **85 g** and a 1 g low-stock threshold became **1418 g** on a g→oz→g round-trip. `convertWeightUnit` returns `null` (leave the stored value UNTOUCHED) for empty/garbage/no-op — never substitutes a fallback — rounds oz to **3 dp** and accepts a comma decimal. Locked by `convertWeightUnit.test.ts`. **The oz precision has been raised TWICE, for the same reason each time, and only the second raise makes the round trip the IDENTITY.** At 1 dp came the corruption above; at 2 dp nothing exploded, but the grid stayed COARSER than the gram side — MEASURED over the 2000 one-decimal gram values from 0.1 to 200.0, **1295 did not survive g→oz→g**, drifting by up to 0.10 g, and 0.1 g still went to `"0.00"` and back to `"0"`, which greys the session form's Save for ever with nothing on screen saying why. At 3 dp: **0 of 2000 fail**. It matters because these two values are PREFERENCES THE USER TYPED: toggling the display unit and back must give them their own number, not a nearby one. Neither sits on the DEDUCTION grid (`roundWeightToUnit`, 1 dp g / 2 dp oz) — the default is a prefill re-rounded at save, the threshold is only ever compared — so the third decimal never puts an unrepresentable weight near a lot. **RESIDUAL, disclosed:** oz→g→oz still drifts one gram-grid step (0.1 oz is 2.835 g, stored `"2.8"`, read back 0.099 oz), because the GRAM side stays at 1 dp — the grid the whole app deducts on, which is not this function's to move. g→oz→g is the direction a preference actually travels. Three pre-existing cases pinned the 2 dp grid and each records the reversal on its own assertion. Conflict resolution in `pickJarLot`: "round" means multiple of 50 in g mode, whole number in oz mode. **No per-pipe `weightUnit` field** — the global `weightUnit` is used everywhere.
17. **Length unit setting** — The global `lengthUnit` React state (`"mm"` or `"in"`, stored in `localStorage` key `cave-length-unit`) controls the length label suffix in the pipe form and detail view. It is a **display-only preference**: stored pipe length values are NOT converted — only the label changes. The setting is toggled in ⚙️ Settings → Préférences. `parseAndApply` converts AI-provided `length_mm` to the user's preferred unit before storing. **No per-pipe `lengthUnit` field** — the global `lengthUnit` is used everywhere.
17b. **Currency setting** — The global `currencySymbol` React state (`"€"`, `"$"`, `"£"`, `"CHF"`, `"JPY"`, stored in `localStorage` key `cave-currency`) controls every price label in the app. **Display-only preference**: stored numeric values are NOT converted — only the symbol changes. The setting is toggled in ⚙️ Settings → Préférences via a 5-option Segmented field. Default `"€"`. Consumed by `ctx.currencySymbol` everywhere a price is rendered: tobacco / pipe / accessory form labels and detail views, lot price columns, Home top-bar totals, Pipes-list header total, Stats price aggregates, and the CSV "Prix" column header. Do NOT hardcode `"€"` in display code — always read from ctx. **No per-entity currency field** — the global `currencySymbol` is used everywhere.
18. **Session weight deduction** — When `weightG > 0` in a session, the weight is deducted from the tobacco's lot (identified by `lotId`). **Default weight**: on a NEW session (`addJ`) or a tasting setup, once a pipe is picked, `weightG` is ESTIMATED from the pipe's chamber size × the selected tobacco's cut density — `estimateSessionWeight(pipe, tobacco, sessDefaultWeight, weightUnit)` in `src/utils/bowlEstimate.ts` (chamber volume = cylinder from `chamberDiameter`×`chamberDepth`; density from the `CUT_DENSITY` table keyed by the canonical CUTS value, `DEFAULT_CUT_DENSITY` 0.25 for Autre/unknown; grams→oz converted; rounded 1 dp g / 2 dp oz). When the pipe has NO chamber dimensions, it falls back to the global `sessDefaultWeight` setting. Applied via a `useEffect` keyed on `form.pipeId`+`form.tobaccoId` / `tasting.pipeId`+`tasting.tobaccoId` (NOT on `weightG` — prefill-race rule) in BOTH SessionFormView and TastingView, so changing the pipe OR the tobacco re-estimates, and the user's manual edit sticks until they do. Edit mode keeps the recorded weight; accounting-off forces `weightG="0"`. (A per-pipe `smokeWeight` field was briefly stored; it was replaced by this session-time estimate and `migrateData` drops any leftover value.) **UI hints**: the session weight field shows an "estimé · modifiable" sub-line (`weight_estimated_hint`) whenever the value IS a chamber×cut estimate (picked pipe has chamber dims, add-mode, accounting on); Settings → default session weight carries a matching fallback sub-label (`sess_default_weight_hint`) explaining it applies when the pipe's chamber dims are missing. **In EDIT mode only**, a "↻ Appliquer le poids par défaut (N g)" button (`btn_apply_default_weight`) re-applies the current estimate to an OLD session's weight on tap (add mode auto-applies it, so the button is edit-only). Edit: old weight is restored first, then new weight is deducted. Delete: weight is restored. **Round-15: the recorded session `weightG` is rounded to the deduction grid (1 dp g / 2 dp oz) via `roundWeightToUnit(w, weightUnit)` (lotUtils.ts) in BOTH `_persistSession` (`w`) and `updateSession` (`ow`/`nw`) — so the stored session weight and the lot debit are byte-identical. The session used to store the raw hand-typed value while the lot rounded, so Σ(sessions) and (weightInitial−weightG) drifted by sub-grid amounts and, after enough >1 dp sessions on one lot, crossed the balance tolerance → a false `lot-balance-overflow`.** If `lotId` is stale/missing, `pickJarLot` auto-selects the best jar lot. The session tobacco dropdown shows **tobaccos that have at least one usable lot** (jar OR cellar with positive weight) for `addJ`; in `editJ` mode, the currently selected tobacco is always included even if it has no usable lots. The lot picker appears when the selected tobacco has >1 usable lot and now lists jar AND cellar lots side-by-side, each prefixed with its status (`Pot` / `Cave` in FR, `Jar` / `Cellar` in EN). **Cellar → jar confirm flow**: when the picked lot is in cellar status, the form shows an advisory note and intercepts the Save action with a `Modal` confirming the cellar→jar transition. Accepting calls `changeLotStatus(tobId, idx, "jar")` (which auto-fills `dateOpened`); because `addSession`/`updateSession` close over the previous render's `data`, the actual save is queued via a `pendingPostOpenSave` state and fired from a `useEffect` once React has re-rendered with the lot in `"jar"`. Do NOT collapse this back into a synchronous `setTimeout(0)` — the closure issue was the reason this is split. **Orphaned sessions** (lot deleted via `removeLot`): `lotId` is set to `""` — restore is skipped on delete (`deleteSession` still has `&&sess.lotId` guard), and the weight field is locked read-only in the edit form with a ⚠️ warning. **Finished-lot auto-reactivation**: when editing a session reduces weight so the lot is no longer empty, `applyLotWeightDelta` auto-reactivates the finished lot to `"jar"`. The weight field is locked (read-only) only when `lotId` is explicitly set (non-empty) but the referenced lot no longer exists (deleted). Sessions with `lotId === ""` created before lot tracking (no `weightG`) are never locked.
19. **Tasting mode (live session) — invariants**: `useTastingSession` manages a singleton "live" session persisted in `localStorage` key `cave-tasting-active`. Two stages: `setup` (pick tabac + pipe + lot + initial weight) → `running` (timer started). **Cellar-lot parity**: the setup view accepts cellar lots like `SessionFormView` does — the tobacco dropdown lists every tobacco with at least one usable lot (jar OR cellar with positive weight), and the lot picker exposes both statuses tagged `Pot/Cave` (FR) or `Jar/Cellar` (EN). If the picked lot is in cellar status, `tastingIgnite` is intercepted by a confirm modal: accepting calls `changeLotStatus(... "jar")` and queues `tastingIgnite` via a `pendingPostOpenIgnite` effect so the closure sees the lot already promoted. Mirrors the SessionFormView cellar-confirm flow line-for-line so the two entry points stay behaviourally identical. The timer is **derived** from `Date.now() - startTs - pausedAccumMs`, not an incrementing counter, so it stays accurate across reloads, backgrounding, and sleep. A 1s `setInterval` only triggers re-renders. Pausing stores `pauseStartTs`; unpause adds the delta to `pausedAccumMs`. **Background behaviour**: the user can navigate to any other view while a tasting is running — state is preserved and a fixed gold banner appears on every non-tasting view (showing live elapsed time + "▶ Reprendre" button). On `tastingEnd`, the elapsed time is rounded to minutes (min 1), and a normal session is created via `addSessionFromTasting()` (`useSessionStore`), which reuses the standard `_persistSession` path for weight deduction. **Wake lock**: `navigator.wakeLock.request("screen")` is acquired while running and not paused, released on pause/end. No fail loud if the API is missing. Cancel from the tasting view requires confirm; cancel from setup is silent. **Overtime guard (`OVERTIME_THRESHOLD_MS` = 90 min, `OVERTIME_AUTO_END_MS` = 5 min)**: once elapsed ≥ threshold, a fixed red banner (App.tsx, `tastingOvertimePrompt()`) replaces the gold "in progress" banner on every view (including the tasting view itself) with "Continuer" / "Terminer" buttons. After `OVERTIME_AUTO_END_MS` more elapsed time, `tastingEnd()` auto-fires from the tick-effect — session is saved normally. "Continuer" calls `tastingPostponeOvertime()` which bumps `overtimeThresholdMs` by another 90 min. **Critical**: because the overtime check is elapsed-based (not wall-clock), pausing the session also pauses the countdown — this is intentional (paused user is engaged with the app). The Home screen exposes a permanent "Démarrer une dégustation" CTA card under the mini-strip; it switches to "▶ Reprendre la séance" (and a brass gradient) while a tasting is running. Starting a tasting also remains accessible via the Journal toolbar flame button. **Running-stage controls**: the full-width "Terminer la séance" label button was replaced by a square **stop icon button sitting next to the pause button**, each with a small caption below (Pause/Reprendre, Terminer) — new `stop` glyph in `icons.tsx` (filled rounded square), i18n keys `tasting_btn_pause` / `tasting_btn_stop` / `tasting_btn_resume` / `aria_pause_tasting`.
20. **Security invariants — never regress these:**
    - **CSP**: the `<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy">` tag must remain in `index.html`. Adding a new external API or CDN requires updating `connect-src` or `script-src` in the same commit. `unsafe-inline` must NOT be re-added to `script-src`.
    - **OAuth CSRF guard**: the state check in the OAuth callback must remain `!st || !expectedSt || st !== expectedSt` (fail-closed). Do not change to `&&`.
    - **OAuth action whitelist**: `gdrive-pending` must be validated against `["save", "restore", "reconnect", "list", "autosave", "restore-cnb", "cat-save", "cat-restore"]` before dispatch (`restore-cnb` = the cloud-newer-banner one-tap restore; `cat-save`/`cat-restore` = the CATALOGUE's own cloud stream; the Dropbox flow has the same eight). **THE TWO CATALOGUE ACTIONS ARE THE FIX FOR THE THIRD INSTANCE OF ONE DEFECT, AND THE SHAPE IS WHAT MATTERS.** Both catalogue buttons BORROWED a cellar action — `getCloudToken("save")` and `getCloudToken("list")` — and on iOS standalone a missing token means a REDIRECT whose return dispatcher routes on the action string ALONE. So « Sauvegarder le catalogue dans le cloud » resumed as `gdriveSave`: a full CELLAR backup, manual-file rotation, `cave-autosave-ts` stamped, `markExported()`, and « ✓ OK » shown under the OTHER button — with the 3.77 MB catalogue never uploaded. « Récupérer le catalogue » resumed as the backups panel. The dispatcher's own comment enumerates *"FOUR buttons can now issue a 'list' redirect … each of the three non-default ones leaves a fresh one-shot marker"*; the catalogue restore was the FIFTH and left none. The two earlier instances were the 🗑 resuming under `"restore"` (which opened the DESTRUCTIVE restore picker) and « Vérifier les sauvegardes » resuming under `"list"`. **A DISTINCT ACTION, NOT A FIFTH MARKER**: the markers exist because three buttons genuinely share the "list my cloud files" operation and differ only in what they do with the result, whereas a catalogue save is not a cellar save with a flag on it — `"restore-cnb"` is the precedent, added for exactly this reason. Overloading an action and disambiguating it out-of-band is the shape that produced all three. **WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT: all nine hook cases in `catalogueCloudStream.test.ts` pass `"tok"` as `preToken`, so `getCloudToken` is never reached at all** — the token-acquisition path was covered by nothing. The new cases drive the REAL dispatcher through `__PENDING_GDRIVE_*`, and read the uploaded file NAME out of the Drive multipart `FormData`, which is the only place it appears. **Two lessons from writing them.** The first version asserted that Settings stays SHUT on a catalogue resume and was wrong: `useGdriveAuth`'s capture opens it for every action but `reconnect`/`autosave`, and for the catalogue that is RIGHT — the panel and its `catalogueCloudStatus` line live in Réglages → Données, so the user must land where the answer appears. And the fetch mock had to be discriminated BY URL rather than by `mockResolvedValueOnce` ordering: mounting the hook can fire the launch cloud-check or the silent refresh, and a `once` queue silently hands those responses to the wrong caller. **The lock-step test between the two providers was itself a fake guarantee** — `dropboxAuth.test.ts`'s « matches the gdrive whitelist values exactly » compared against a hand-written literal and never read the Drive list, so an action added on the Drive side alone left it green; it DERIVES the Drive list from source now (comments blanked, non-vacuity asserted), which is both a real lock-step check and one that never needs hand-editing again. Probed in both directions. Locked by `src/__tests__/processOAuthReturn.test.ts` (each canonical value verified individually) AND by `src/__tests__/oauthWhitelist.property.test.ts` — a fast-check property test that fuzzes 500 random strings against the dispatcher in BOTH the implicit-grant and PKCE paths, plus 200 near-miss variants (capitalisation, whitespace, suffixes). Any future relaxation of the comparison (case-insensitive, substring, trim) fails the property test on the first counterexample.
    - **OAuth read-before-clear**: in `processOAuthReturn` (and any future variant of the OAuth-return handler), the `gdrive-pending` action MUST be read into a local variable BEFORE any `removeItem` cleanup of the same key. An early cleanup was once added at the top of the handler for the failure case, and the success-path read further down silently became a no-op (always returned `null`), so every fresh token from Google was dropped without dispatch. Symptoms: Reconnect never made the banner disappear, iOS auto-save piggyback stuck. Locked at THREE levels: (1) the runtime test in `src/__tests__/processOAuthReturn.test.ts` — Proxy-wrapped localStorage asserts `getItem` precedes `removeItem` on `gdrive-pending`; (2) the static ESLint tripwire `tabac-local/no-storage-read-after-remove` (eslint-rules/no-storage-read-after-remove.cjs) at "error" level — flags ANY `localStorage.removeItem("K")` (or `<ident>.localStorage.removeItem("K")`) followed by `localStorage.getItem("K")` of the same literal key in the same function scope across the whole codebase, blocking the bug from re-entering production code at lint time. The rule is scope-per-BlockStatement with `return`/`throw`-aware propagation: a `removeItem` inside a block that ends with `return` or `throw` doesn't pollute the tracking of mutually-exclusive branches, which keeps the PKCE / implicit-grant split in `oauthReturn.ts` free of false positives; (3) the rule's own self-test in `src/__tests__/eslint-no-storage-read-after-remove.test.ts` (23 fixtures including IIFE, arrow functions, `window.localStorage`, mixed `w.localStorage` + bare, and the branch-with-return mutual-exclusion case).
    - **iOS standalone Drive auth**: MUST use `window.location.replace()` + `response_type=token`. Do NOT switch to PKCE (`response_type=code`) or `initTokenClient` — both have been tried and both fail (see "OAuth flow — iOS standalone vs. non-iOS" section). The CSRF state check (`!st || !expectedSt || st !== expectedSt`) must remain fail-closed.
    - **imageData filtering**: `doGdriveConfirm` and `doImportFile` must always validate `_imageData` keys (`local-photo-` prefix) and values (`/^data:image\/(jpeg|jpg|png|webp|gif);/` regex) before writing to IndexedDB.
    - **Counter clamping**: `migrateData` must always clamp `nxT/nxW/nxP/nxA/nxJ` to `Math.max(1, parseInt(x)||1)`.
    - **SSRF guard**: the app makes no external image fetch; `isSafeExternalUrl(url)` remains a pure URL-safety predicate used by `safeBgUrl` (CSS background sanitisation) + the lightbox src guard. `migrateData._clearForeignImageRefs` blanks any `imageUrl` that is not a `local-photo-*` key or an allowed `data:image/…` URI — an ALLOWLIST, because the previous `^https?://` blocklist missed the protocol-relative and `data:` forms (no fetch either way).
    - **Token storage**: OAuth token uses `tkGet()`/`tkSet()`/`tkClear()` helpers — never access `gdrive-tk` directly via `localStorage` or `sessionStorage`.
    - **Auto-update gate**: `useAppUpdate({ deferAutoUpdate })` must be called AFTER `useTastingSession` **and after `useWishStore`** (it was moved there; nothing between them consumed its return) so both can suspend the countdown. Do not regress to an unconditional countdown. **`deferAutoUpdate` is THE protection for unsaved work, and it is the only one** — the update does NOT wait for the user to agree: the visible banner is a 10-second veto window that fires `doUpdate()` by itself, and the `data_only` silent path fires with no banner at all, so there is no second gate behind this predicate. It must list every surface holding input a reload would destroy: an active tasting (**both** stages — a silent update firing on `visibilitychange` during `setup` reloaded mid-setup), the eight full-screen form views, the lot modal, the **wishlist overlay** and the **pipe maintenance modal** (both added later). The last two had been "accepted residuals": the wishlist because `showWishForm`/`editWishId` were composed after the hook — a routing detail, not a reason, since it is a full add/edit form that even registers with `useUnsavedFormGuard` — and the maintenance modal because it was "lower-stakes", which is not the test (a reload discards a half-written note just as completely, and the silent path gives no chance to object). `maintForm` is local to `PipesDetailView`, so it reports itself via `ctx.setMaintFormOpen` and **must clear on unmount**, or leaving the fiche with it open would block every update for the rest of the session. **Add every new form-bearing surface here**; locked by `deferAutoUpdate.test.ts`, which reads the predicate out of `App.tsx` because what rots is the LIST, not the mechanism. Note the tasting itself is persisted (`cave-tasting-active`) and survives a reload — it is in the list to avoid interrupting the user, whereas every other entry is there to avoid losing data. **The predicate was right and NOTHING CLEARED THE STATE ON THE WAY OUT, so a BLANK setup blocked every automatic update for ever.** `decideBack` routes `tasting` through `fallbackParent` to home without cancelling, so `cave-tasting-active` survives relaunches carrying `{stage:"setup"}` and this clause goes on returning true on a screen the user left days ago — silently, since the silent path has no banner to notice. **A NEW USER reaches it unaided**: the Home's CTA is « Démarrer une dégustation », the setup needs a tobacco AND a pipe, and a fresh install has neither, so the screen is genuinely unusable for them and a system-back is the natural exit. This same state was met from the other side — such a tasting was made VISIBLE and resumable, which is the way out — and did not stop it being created. `goBack` now cancels it, and **ONLY when nothing has been chosen** (`!tasting.tobaccoId && !tasting.pipeId`): that is not work, there is literally nothing in it, and a setup where the user picked either one is preserved exactly as before. **The narrowness is the whole safety of the fix** — discarding a partly-filled setup would be the opposite defect, and a silent one. The setup-stage rule is untouched: this removes the EMPTY state, it does not stop deferring on a real one, and `deferAutoUpdate.test.ts` asserts both halves so neither can be "simplified" into the other.
21. **iOS / Android parity — mandatory check on every change** — The app targets both iOS Safari (often added to Home Screen as a PWA) and Android Chrome (browser + PWA). Whenever a commit adds, edits, or removes platform-specific code or documentation, you MUST audit both platforms in the SAME commit:
    - **Code**: any behavior gated on `IS_IOS`, `IS_IOS_STANDALONE`, `navigator.standalone`, `matchMedia('(display-mode: standalone)')`, `userAgent` checks, or `Webkit*` CSS prefixes must either apply correctly on both platforms or be explicitly justified as an intentional asymmetry (see the documented list below). New platform branches require a matching path or a one-line comment explaining why the divergence is correct.
    - **help.html**: any feature that behaves differently on iOS vs Android needs both platform's path/instructions in BOTH the FR and EN sections. A single-platform note is a regression — fix it in the same commit.
    - **Error messages / status banners**: never hard-code "Safari", "Réglages → Safari", "Chrome → Paramètres" or any platform-specific navigation path in a user-visible string without `IS_IOS` (or equivalent) branching for the other platform.
    - **OAuth / storage / file pickers / lightbox / save-to-photos**: these touch native OS conventions that differ; verify the user can complete the equivalent task on both platforms.
    - **Maintenance ritual**: when you write or modify a platform-gated branch, grep the codebase for sibling references (`IS_IOS`, `IS_IOS_STANDALONE`, `Safari`, `Chrome` in user-facing strings) and confirm the help / runtime / error message stack stays symmetric. If you discover an asymmetry while working on something else, fix it in the same commit when it's safe to do so, or open a follow-up task.
    - **Known intentional asymmetries — do NOT "fix" these**:
      - `IS_IOS_STANDALONE` controls redirect OAuth on iOS standalone vs popup OAuth on Android/browser. Extending it to Android PWA (`matchMedia display-mode: standalone`) would break Android Drive auth by forcing redirect instead of popup.
      - `gdrive-tk` stored in `localStorage` on iOS standalone (survives redirect), `sessionStorage` on all other platforms (tab-scoped, cleared on close).
      - `safe-area-inset-bottom` applies to iOS notch; `env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0)` fallback to 0 is correct for Android.
      - `WebkitTouchCallout:"default"` on the lightbox: enables iOS "Save to Photos" long-press menu. Android Chrome shows its own context menu natively — no additional code needed.
    - **The tab icon existed for iOS only, which is this invariant failing in the most visible place there is.** `index.html` declared `apple-touch-icon` and **nothing else**, so every non-Apple browser (Android Chrome, every desktop one) had NO declared icon and fell back to requesting `/favicon.ico`, which this site does not serve: a 404 on every page load, and a blank tab. An iOS-specific affordance with no equivalent for the other platform is exactly what this invariant forbids, and the tab icon is the FIRST thing a visitor sees — before they install anything. **How it was found is worth recording**: an Android-emulated Chromium probe (the user has no Android device). **Neither `page.on("response")` nor `ctx.on("response")` reports the favicon request — it is issued by the BROWSER itself, not by the page**, so what found it was probing the served paths directly; and note that everything else there returns 200 only thanks to `vite preview`'s SPA fallback — `favicon.ico` has an extension, so it escapes the fallback and tells the truth. Locked in `src/__tests__/serviceWorker.test.ts`, which asserts BOTH halves: a non-Apple icon link exists, AND it points at a file that actually ships (otherwise the 404 merely moves). **What that emulated probe DOES and does NOT establish, since the honest limit is the point of running it**: it establishes that the app boots and renders under an Android UA, that `IS_IOS` / `IS_IOS_STANDALONE` are both false so it takes the popup-OAuth + `sessionStorage` branch, that `sessionStorage` is writable, and that nothing overflows the document; it CANNOT establish the real Google popup round-trip, PWA install / standalone display-mode, or true touch input. Worth knowing alongside it: **the whole vitest suite already runs on that same non-iOS branch** (jsdom has no `navigator.standalone` and a non-iOS UA), so the Android code path is continuously exercised.
22. **Third-party licenses — both files must stay in sync** — when integrating any new third-party code (bundled npm dependency, runtime-loaded library, or external SDK), update **both** of these in the same commit:
    - **`LICENSE`** (repository root) — the canonical plain-text file shown on GitHub. Append the full license notice and copyright to the **Third-Party Notices** section.
    - **`public/licenses.html`** — the in-app HTML page (English, styled like privacy/help/changelog), linked from ⚙️ Settings → *Licence & crédits* (key `btn_licenses`). Add a styled `<h3>` section with the licence tag, a one-line description, and a `.license-card` block reproducing the same notice.

    Cover the legally relevant cases the same way in both files:
    - **Bundled dependency** (in `dist/`, e.g. via `npm install`): full license text + copyright required for MIT/BSD/Apache.
    - **Runtime-loaded library** (e.g. JSZip from cdnjs, Google Identity Services): attribution + link required.
    - **Dev-only tool** (Vite, ESLint, etc.): a single-line entry in the build-time section is enough — not redistributed.

    `public/licenses.html` is served network-first, so updating it does not require bumping `CACHE_NAME` in `sw.js`. Skipping either file silently breaks MIT/BSD compliance for the corresponding distribution channel (GitHub vs. the live PWA).

23. **Soft-delete / Trash (extended in 159)** — every top-level entity (Tobacco, Pipe, WishlistItem, Accessory, Session) AND every Lot (sub-entity inside `tobacco.lots`) carries an optional `deletedAt?: string` ISO field. The five top-level store delete actions (`deleteTobacco`, `deletePipe`, `deleteAccessory`, `deleteSession`, `delWish`) and `useTobaccoStore.removeLot` all STAMP this field instead of removing the row. `useSessionStore.deleteSession` still restores the lot weight via `applyLotWeightDelta` even when soft-deleting. `removeLot` no longer orphanises sessions — the lot stays in storage, so the session's `lotId` remains valid; restoring the lot re-attaches them cleanly. App.tsx exposes `data: liveData` to ctx (raw arrays minus rows with `deletedAt`, plus each tobacco's lots stripped of deletedAt lots) so views, stats AND the four `filtered*` memos all see the live world; the raw state is exposed as `dataRaw` for the Trash UI in Settings → Corbeille. **Critical**: `liveData` must be the source for every consumer that drives the UI — its definition was lifted above the `filtered`/`filteredPipes`/`filteredSessions`/`filteredAccessories` memos so they all read from it. Reading from raw `data` in any of those would resurrect the bug where deleted tabacs/pipes stayed visible in their list. Helper functions on ctx: `restoreFromTrash(kind, id, scopeTobId?)` clears `deletedAt` (kind `"lot"` is scoped to its OWN tobacco — a lot id is unique per tobacco, not globally; the others key on `data[key]`), `restoreSelectionFromTrash(selection)` clears `deletedAt` on every row whose `"kind:id"` string is in the Set, in ONE atomic save (the per-row loop the TrashModal used dropped all but the last save because each call read stale `data` from its closure), `restoreAllFromTrash()` clears `deletedAt` on every entity AND every lot in one save (no confirm — restore is non-destructive), `permanentlyDelete(kind, id, scopeTobId?)` removes the row (and for `"lot"` also orphanises referencing sessions like the old hard `removeLot`, scoped to that tobacco), `emptyTrash()` wipes every soft-deleted row in one go (including lots, with the same orphan handling — keeps a `window.confirm` because it sidesteps the 30-day safety net). A startup cleanup (App.tsx effect, 6 s deferred) hard-removes rows AND lots whose `deletedAt` is older than `TRASH_RETENTION_DAYS` (30, in `constants.ts`); orphan sessions get `lotId=""` when their lot is purged. The purge computation is the pure `sweepExpiredTrash(snap, cutoffMs)` in `utils.ts` (unit-tested by `sweepExpiredTrash.test.ts`); the effect only does the loading-gate + scheduling. **Critical fix:** this effect (and `useLotIntegrityProbe`) were mount-only `useEffect(fn, [])` reading `data` from the mount-time closure — that closure is bound to the empty `INIT` (load() is async), so the 30-day retention NEVER purged anything (soft-deleted rows lived forever in localStorage + backups) and the probe kept clearing a live diagnostic. Both now gate on `loading === false` and read the latest data via a ref — the SAME closure fix as `useOrphanPhotoGC` (locked by `lotIntegrityProbeGating.test.tsx`). **Any new startup effect that reads `data` must follow this loading-gate + ref pattern** — a `[]` dep reading `data` directly is bound to `INIT`. `assertLotInvariants` (in both `save()` and the startup integrity probe) ignores trashed rows AND trashed lots so deletedAt items can't inflate the diagnostic counter. The Trash UI lives in a dedicated `CuratorTrashModal` (`src/views/curator/TrashModal.tsx`, opened via `ctx.trashOpen` / `ctx.setTrashOpen`, mounted in `CuratorApp.tsx`). The modal supports a **selection mode** (atomicity fix in 168) — tap "Sélection" / "Select" to flip each row into a checkbox row, pick a subset, then tap "Restaurer la sélection (N)". The CTA delegates to `restoreSelectionFromTrash(selection)` so the whole pick lands in ONE save (the per-row loop the modal originally used dropped all but the last picked item — React batched the setData calls). Per-row Restore / × buttons and the Tout restaurer / Vider la corbeille bulk row are hidden in selection mode; the contextual Restaurer la sélection / Annuler pair takes over. Selective permanent-delete is intentionally not offered — the user asked for restore-only, and a destructive bulk action against a freely-picked subset deserves its own dedicated UX. It lists soft-deleted lots only when their parent tobacco is NOT trashed (restoring a lot before its parent is meaningless). The old `TrashSection` inside `SettingsModal` was removed — don't reintroduce it; Settings stays focused on settings. **No delete confirmation dialogs**: tabacs / pipes / accessoires / envies / séances / lots all soft-delete immediately when the user taps the trash icon. The 8 s undo-toast is the instant safety net; the 30-day Trash is the long-tail safety net. The styled `CuratorDelConfirmModal` and `delConfirm` ctx state were removed — don't reintroduce a confirm prompt on a soft-delete path. The "Empty trash" CTA inside `CuratorTrashModal` is the lone exception that keeps a `window.confirm` — it's the irreversible bulk action that sidesteps the 30-day safety net. **Trash indicator (simplified in 161, extracted to shared component in 163)**: `CuratorTrashIndicator` in `src/components/curator/TrashIndicator.tsx` — an amber trash IconBtn that surfaces when `dataRaw` contains any entity or lot with `deletedAt`. Tap opens `CuratorTrashModal` via `setTrashOpen(true)`. Mounted in every list-view TopBar trailing slot: HomeView (left of the cloud icon), InventoryListView, PipesListView, JournalView, AccListView. Returns null when the trash is empty so it never decorates a clean app. **Start-session gate**: the "Démarrer une session" CTA on `InventoryDetailView` is hidden when the tobacco has no usable lot (i.e. all lots are finished). A finished lot can't back a session, so surfacing the button would be a dead end. The undo-toast snapshot-based undo still works on every soft-delete (snapshot restores the pre-delete data wholesale, which has no `deletedAt`). **Backup vs CSV**: JSON / Drive backups serialize the raw `data` so soft-deleted rows survive a restore — the user keeps the 30-day safety net across reinstalls. `buildCsvLines` (in `useExportImport`) is the only export path that filters `deletedAt` rows (top-level rows AND lots inside live tobaccos): the CSV is a working snapshot of the live inventory, not an archive. **Sessions immutable on permanent delete (replaces the earlier sanitisation policy)**: `permanentlyDelete("tobacco"/"pipe", id)`, `emptyTrash`, and the 30-day cleanup all leave session fields untouched. Sessions keep their `tobaccoId` / `pipeId` as fantôme ids; the journal renders via the snapshot. Before purging the entity, `refreshSnapshotsForRemoval(sessions, deletedTobs, deletedPipes)` (pure helper in `src/utils.ts`, was in App.tsx originally) refreshes every referencing session's `tobaccoSnapshot` / `pipeSnapshot` with the entity's current `{brand, name, imageUrl}` — so the journal photo + label match what the user was seeing right before they confirmed the deletion. **Same refresh on SOFT-delete** — `useTobaccoStore.deleteTobacco` and `usePipeStore.deletePipe` both call `refreshSnapshotsForRemoval` BEFORE stamping `deletedAt`. Reason: as soon as the row carries deletedAt, `liveData` filters it out and the journal's `tobOf(id)` / `pipeOf(id)` lookup returns undefined → the entry falls back to the snapshot. If the user had renamed or re-imaged the entity between session save and deletion, the snapshot was stale. Refreshing here locks in the latest state. Re-creating an entity later (new id) does NOT auto-link to old sessions: ids are immutable. The `sanitizeSessionRefs` helper and its trash-path wiring were REMOVED — sessions no longer get their ids cleared on any trash op. The kind `"lot"` branch in `permanentlyDelete` still explicitly clears `lotId` on referencing sessions (lots have no snapshot — they're abstract — and `deleteSession`'s weight-restore guard `&& sess.lotId` relies on empty lotId). The three cross-ref invariants (`session-tobacco-exists`, `session-pipe-exists`, `session-lot-exists`) were dropped because dangling refs are now an expected state, not a bug. **Diagnostic banner removed**: `CuratorDiagnosticToast` (the floating bottom banner that surfaced when the violation counter crossed `DIAGNOSTIC_TOAST_THRESHOLD`) is no longer mounted in `CuratorOverlays`. The component stays in `Overlays.tsx` for tests but isn't reachable from the UI. The Settings → Diagnostic section still surfaces the counter + last 20 violations for power-user inspection. **Image GC closure bug fix (critical, a regression)**: the mount-only `gcOrphans` useEffect in App.tsx used to capture `data` at the time the effect ran — which was BEFORE `load()` had populated it (load is async). The closure was stuck on `data = null`, so `referenced` was always empty and `gcOrphans` deleted every `local-photo-*` IndexedDB entry older than 5 minutes on every cold start. The fix gates the timer on `data` first becoming non-null (deps `[data]` + `gcRanRef`) and reads the latest data through a ref inside the setTimeout callback, so `referenced` always reflects the live inventory. **A re-fix (critical, a regression from the instant-shell change)**: that change switched the initial `data` state from `null` to `INIT` (empty inventory). That re-broke the gate: `data` was truthy from frame 0, the effect flipped `gcRanRef.current = true` immediately with empty arrays, and the 4-second timer fired before `load()` had finished on slower devices — sending an empty `referenced` set to `gcOrphans`. Result: every `local-photo-*` older than 5 minutes nuked on cold start (especially visible on the wishlist, where photos aren't refreshed by re-editing the entity). The re-fix gates the effect on `loading === false` (the signal that `load()` has actually completed) and changes the dep array from `[data]` to `[loading]` — the timer only schedules once the real inventory is in state. Lesson: any change to the initial `data` state needs to audit every `useEffect` that conditions on `if (!data) return` — those guards became no-ops after that change. Users who lost photos can restore the latest Drive backup to repopulate IndexedDB.

24. **Duplicate detection on tobacco + wishlist entry** — `TobaccoFormView` and `WishFormView` both show an amber warning banner when the typed `brand + name` (case- and whitespace-insensitive, via the shared `dupKey` from `useImportConfirm`) matches an existing **live** row. The tabac form checks against `data.tobaccos`; the wishlist form checks against `data.wishlist` first ("identical wish already exists") and falls back to `data.tobaccos` ("you already own this — no need to wish"). Both skip the check while brand or name is empty, both skip the entity currently being edited (`form.id` / `editWishId` match), both skip trashed rows (`!deletedAt`). **Warning only — never blocks save**: a brand+name dup can be a legitimate re-listing (a different vintage, a refurbished tin, etc.). **Only tobaccos and wishlist items get this** — pipes and accessories can legitimately exist in multiple copies (a user can own two Peterson Sherlocks); duplicating the detection there would be noise, not signal.

25. **Adding features / fixing bugs:**
    - **Business logic** (hooks, utils, ctx values): change once. Add the test in the existing `src/__tests__/` file for that hook/util.
    - **UI change**: edit the Curator view in `src/views/curator/`.
    - **New ctx key** (e.g. a new action from a store): expose it in `appCtx` (search `var appCtx = {` in App.tsx) — otherwise the destructured value in views is `undefined` and the feature silently no-ops.
    - **`help.html` updates**: ship in the same commit as user-visible behaviour changes.

26. **Web requests — SEARCH, do not crawl. Binding on this assistant and on
    every agent it spawns.**
    - **Reach for `WebSearch` first, always.** A search result is served by an
      engine that publishers have opted into; it answers most questions from the
      snippet alone.
    - **`WebFetch` only when a snippet is genuinely ambiguous, and only on a host
      that welcomes it.** Respect `robots.txt`. Many sites — retailers and
      review sites in particular — disallow crawlers, and a 403 from one of them
      is that policy speaking.
    - **A refusal is an answer, never an obstacle.** If a fetch is refused
      (`robots.txt`, 403, a bot wall, or the agent proxy), report the blocked
      host and work from the search result instead. Never retry it, never route
      around it, never fabricate a different user agent. This is the same rule
      the environment already applies to its own proxy.
    - **Never automate a sweep of a third-party site.** Repeated fetches to
      build a dataset are a crawl whatever the tool is called, and this project
      has no reason to run one.
    - **What this does NOT cover, stated so nobody assumes it does**: the
      internal behaviour of the fetch tool is not something this file can
      enforce or audit. The rule binds which tool is reached for and what
      happens on refusal — that part is a decision, and it is the part that has
      gone wrong before.
    - **The app itself is already compliant by construction** and must stay so:
      the AI auto-fill uses the provider's server-side `web_search` tool, makes
      no direct request to any third-party site, and the CSP `connect-src` does
      not whitelist one. Do not "improve" it into a fetch.
